incident_description:
RISK OF INFANT DEOXYGENATION AND SUFFOCATION:

I observed an infant in a mobile carrier such as a car seat completely covered by a pink Cozy Cover for over an hour without any access to air external - outside of the tightly covered seat.  The specific cover is an accessory with elastic around the entire rectangular edge which tightly captures the seat.  It has two V configured zippers for baby placement and removal from the seat.  And it has a head-hole that is fully covered by a flap.  This model Cozy Cover completely covers the infant and its face when zipped and the flap is down - which is the natural resting position.  The cover is designed to fully cover the infant including its face.  In this case, I thought the infant was removed and the seat was empty and sealed.  However,  ordering and eating a full meal (well over 1hr) the parents/caretakers peeked into the head-hole and said their infant was sleeping "the entire time!".  

Complete entrapment coverage risks the child re-breathing the same air to the point of deoxygenation.  In addition, the Cozy Cover rests concave down due to gravity pulling on the material - so it droops inward towards the nose and mouth.  Larger infants and those under a drooping or improperly installed Cozy Cover are at high risk of suffocation due to occlusion of the nose and mouth by the Cozy Cover material.    There are more than one Cozy Cover model.  This model does not have ventilation material and covers the child's face entirely when closed.
justification: The infant was at high risk of suffocation due to complete coverage by the Cozy Cover, but no injury or death occurred in this instance.

incident_description: In 2017, I purchased a Tommee Tippee brand "Closer to Nature" bottle and cap to feed by baby.  On March 17, 2018, when my baby was 7 months old, I fed my baby with the Tommee Tippee bottle and placed her in bed for a nap.  At the time, she was teething and liked chewing on the cap of the bottle, which is like a plastic cup that fits over the top of the bottle, similar in shape to one-half of a hollow ball.  When I put her down, she was holding on to the cap.  Later that morning when I rolled her over to wake her, the cap of the Tommee Tippee bottle was attached to her face by suction, covering her mouth and nose.  I removed the cap and realized she was not breathing.  I immediately began chest compressions and a friend called 911.  The police and EMTs arrived and she was taken to the hospital, where she was later pronounced dead. I had no idea this cap could suffocate my baby. Nothing in the packaging or instructions warned about the risk of suffocation from the cap. My baby's death could have been prevented with air holes, vents, or other features that prevented a suction from developing when a baby inhaled. I believe this product has a hidden dangerous and should be recalled.
justification: The incident resulted in the death of a baby due to suffocation caused by the bottle cap, which is the highest severity level.

incident_description:
I had stepped into the kitchen (several feet away) for a moment when I heard one of my twin toddlers and it seemed they were too close to me through the dining room.  I came around the corner and one of my toddlers was standing there in the dining room (to which they do not have access) and behind him our Regalo baby gate/fence was in pieces.

Turns out, the metal sections are essentially just friction-fit (with a detente rather than a full catch) into the plastic segment couplers.  Further, we have 2 of the 8-section gate assemblies, and at least 3 of the "welds" (which they're obviously not) between the vertical and horizontal metal pieces have failed, leaving movable vertical members and chisel-sharp "weld" material.  Third, one of the "internal" pieces of the upper panel junction has had its coupling part (a small circle that fits inside of the adjacent panel's coupler to connect the two) snap off as it is only attached via an unnecessarily skinny plastic neck.

This represents two gross engineering failures and one failure (on repeat) due to extremely poor quality control and workmanship.  Obviously there are not ISO quality controls in place to ensure that weldments are consistently having proper joint fusion, the plastic-to-metal joints in the panel assemblies are designed to prioritize cost over reliability, and the design of the plastic panel couplers themselves is being done by someone with little or no engineering knowledge including the ability to reduce stress risers and weak points in such a part.

I have since used high-strength zipties and sheet metal screws to turn the remaining panels into what should be a reliable fence for our toddlers, although the possibility of a failed plastic connector still exists, but I think that may have been a secondary failure after the panels were allowed to move out of alignment due to the plastic-to-metal joints coming apart elsewhere.
justification: The incident involved a toddler accessing an unauthorized area due to a faulty baby gate, but no injury occurred.

incident_description:
My 6 month old fell out of an Ergo Baby Sport carrier whilst I was placing him into the back carry position. He broke his femur (thigh bone). I followed their instructions exactly and have attached a copy of it, you can see from the photo that in steps 3 and 4 the baby is vulnerable to falling and thats is what happened to my child. Although I have used this carrier for 7 years with 3 different children on this occasion when I buckled the waist band and put the left shoulder strap on, then looped his left left through the straps, the next step would be to put on the right shoulder strap. At this point he is partially restrained, when he started squirming out of the carrier while his left leg was still trapped and I was still holding his left thigh. He fell backwards on the the bed at an angle twisting away from me, with his left thigh trapped and it snapped. He ended up with an diagonal fracture of the femur.
The orthopedic surgeon said they have heard of other babies falling out of the ergo baby carrier whilst trying to be put in. The ergo baby carrier is not safe for back carry unless there is an extra person there to hold the baby until all the straps are in place. I reported this to the Ergo baby company right away but they claimed they had never heard of it happening. Looking online I see a lot of other fractures occurring as a result of this carrier.

"Name of product:
Baby Einstein Musical Motion Activity Jumpers
Hazard:
The "sun" toy attachment on the activity jumper can rebound with force and injure the infant, posing an impact hazard." ([REDACTED]/)

incident_description:
I own a day care.  Last year I bought a full-size crib to use in my day care.  Our licensing rules state the crib must be full-size if children are sleeping over night. I bought a standard crib mattress.  I thought it was okay to use the crib.  Until I was inspected.  Luckily I didn't have any children currently using it or I would have been in violation.  The state worker showed me that if the mattress were to shift there would be over an inch gap in areas.  We measured the opening of the crib where the mattress would fit.  It measures 53 x 28 1/2 inches.  I called the crib manufacturer.  They wanted me to send them photos.  I sent them several photo's showing the gaps where an infant could get trapped.  They also said that this crib was manufactured to to be 53 x 28 1/2 opening.  When the licensing consultant shifted the mattress there was over an inch gap almost 2 inches in areas.  Mattresses are suppose to be tight fitting.  The manufacturer told me to buy another mattress to see if that helped.  However, you probably know they don't make them bigger.  I took the mattress I had over to my daughter's house.  My mattress fit her crib with no issues.  It was tight fitting.  I've made several email communications to the crib manufacturer and they haven't responded. 

Below is a document from the State of Michigan Childcare licensing:
R 400.1916 Bedding and sleeping equipment.

 (5) Infants, birth to 12 months of age, shall rest or sleep alone
in an approved crib or porta-crib. A crib shall have all of
the following:
(a) A firm, tight-fitting mattress.
Technical
Assistance

Any rectangular shaped portable crib labeled by the manufacturer as a
portable crib is acceptable if it complies with subrules (5)(a-f) of this
rule.

Note: Under the federal crib standards, non-full-size baby cribs must
be sold with the mattress. The mattress, when inserted in the center of
the crib, must not leave a gap of more than 1/2 inch at any point
between the perimeter of the mattress and the perimeter of the crib.
When the mattress is placed flush to one side and end of the crib, the
resulting gap must not exceed 1 inch. These measurements must be
taken with no sheet covering the mattress. If the non-full-size crib mattress
was sold with the crib and meets these requirements, it will be in
compliance with subrule (5)(a) of this rule.
 

Note: Under the federal crib standards, full-size baby crib mattresses

must measure 27 1/4 inches by 51 5/8 inches with a thickness not

exceeding 6 inches.
justification: No children were using the crib, so there was no injury or incident, but the potential for harm was identified during inspection.

incident_description:
I am reporting the Halo Bassinett Swivel Sleeper. The bassinett after use develops a steep incline so that if a baby was placed in it in a specific position, it would be a choke hazard/ suffocation risk. The bassinett is designed to swivel 360 degrees around a center support system. The bassinett also features a collapsible side so that when parent is in bed, they can reach into the bassinett and remove baby. This collapsible side operates on a spring system which is a very tight spring. The problem I believe arises after continued use of the collapsible side which places uneven pressure on the bassinett, which base is not often centered, so that the pressure is more exaggerated on the bassinett that is not evenly supported underneath. This literally causes the support to bend thus making the bassinett unlevel. After the first few weeks of use, we notice this happening. It was not until my infant was sleeping one night and the incline was pointing downwards, towards his head, that I noticed him shifting drastically towards that side. I was very thankful that he did not spit up while his head was in the position because he could have easily choked. IÃÂm also thankful I noticed him shifting before it became too drastic that his neck and chin became compromised and he couldÃÂve suffocated. 
I reported this to the company who said ÃÂmovementÃÂ is normal, it meets the allowable ÃÂinclineÃÂ for sleep areas and that this bassinet is not meant to be ÃÂrigidÃÂ. I have to strongly disagree with all of these comments - there should be zero incline when abiding by the AAPÃÂs recommendation for a firm, flat surface, and if your product is advertised as such then it should be. And if there is any product i expect to be ULTRA rigid, it would be my sleep area for my infant. The company also blamed my baby for moving around too much. I can assure you this is not the case as it began happening with him only a couple weeks old, and he is swaddled during every sleep so it is impossible for him to move within the bassinett. When the were not receptive to my complaints and I threatened to report them, they quickly dismissed me and retracted their offer to issue a replacement (in my opinion, because they knew the same issue would happen and it would further expose them). I demanded a replacement of a different style (a non swivel) which they refused and then promptly, without notice, issued me a refund check, presumabley to shut me up. Their response to my complaint leads me to believe they are aware of the issue and unwilling to address it therefore are guilty of gross negligence. 
I want to reiterate - you will not notice this issue with an out of the box bassinett. The defect of level ness comes after repeated use of the collapsible side, which places uneven pressure on the uncentered support, causing it to lean in either direction. 
I also found that this product was recalled in Canada and IÃÂm curious of this is why.
justification: The incident describes a potential suffocation risk due to the bassinet developing a steep incline after repeated use, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Good afternoon, 
My name is [REDACTED]. I am a [REDACTED] for the Albany County Department of Health, in upstate New York. I work in the [REDACTED] as an EPA certified Lead Risk Assessor. On June 26, 2017, I conducted a risk assessment with my co-worker, [REDACTED], at a home where a child was lead poisoned. Interior and exterior lead paint hazards were identified, however, they were relatively minor in nature. Upon completion of required remediation, we returned to the home and took clearance dust samples. This was done on August 4th, 2017. The dust samples passed the EPA clearance levels. Typically, when lead hazards are remediated, a child's blood lead level should begin to decrease. However, in this case, the child was tested again, and his levels continued to rise. [REDACTED] and I returned to the home on September 1, 2017, to investigate further. (We had tested some of the toys in the home during the first inspection, but were unable to find anything positive for lead). 
On September 1, I re-tested toys in the home, this time testing virtually everything, including the crib. During conversation with the child's mother, I determined that the child was spending a lot of time in the family vehicle when they would travel to visit relatives. I asked if I could check the interior of the car. Inside I found a toy that the child regularly mouths (it is a teething toy). When I tested it with our XRF analyzer, it registered at 12.9 mg/cm2. This toy is built by "The First Years." It is called a "My Phone." We brought the toy back to the office and took it apart so we could determine whether the positive reading was coming from the plastic casing, or if it was coming from the electronic components within. When I opened it up I noticed a metal disc which showed obvious areas of corrosion. I tested the disc with the XRF and it registered at 18.2 mg/cm2. The disc is located within the plastic, however, there are several small holes that would easily allow corroded metal dust to escape into the child's mouth when they mouth the surface. This morning, I bought a brand new version of this toy at a local [REDACTED]. It was also positive, with almost identical readings. After bringing this to my supervisor's attention, as well as our Commissioner, we agreed that it would be best to make you aware of this toy; that it may be found to be dangerous for children and that it may require a recall. Thank you for your attention to this matter! I am available via email [REDACTED] if you have any further questions. 
Sincerely, 
[REDACTED]
justification: The child's blood lead levels continued to rise despite remediation, indicating injury from lead exposure via a contaminated toy.

incident_description:
I work for a Fire Department in Los Angeles, CA.  Pomona, CA to be exact.

We responded to a reported structure fire in a mobile home unit, with reported elderly person trapped, popping electrical sounds and smoke.  Upon arrival, we found no persons home (after kicking in and severely damaging two doors) and no smoke or fire, fortunately.

What we did find was a completely melted and unidentifiable remnant of a solar night light hanging on the back of the unit, about six feet from another just like it (presumably).  The homeowner was VERY lucky his siding didn't catch on fire and also that he had nothing directly above it that would carry the fire to the rest of the house.  

I took pictures of it and have contacted customer service of the manufacturer and have received no reply.  Upon Googling this product, there are SEVERAL complaints about this exact problem on line.  The light has the name ""Everbrite" on it.
justification: The incident involved a melted solar night light with potential fire risk, but no actual fire or injury occurred.

incident_description:
Fisher Price Infant to Toddler Rocker is the name of the product.  

On 04/23/2017 at approximately 1000hrs my baby one year old female ([REDACTED]) who is approximately 18.5LB  was rocking in this product when this product tipped completely frontward dropping my baby's whole body on the tile floor where she hit head first.  The product is completely unstable and will tip over at the drop of a dime.  The product was poorly built and designed it is to narrow as well as too high. 

On 04/25/2017 at approximately 1330hrs my child was sitting in the chair, I personally placed the front legs on the chair on the floor so that my child could not rock at all, so that the chair stood only in place. I rushed my child to the nearest emergency room located at Florida Heartland Hospital in Sebring, FL.  Where she received treatment for extreme head injury pertaining to the incident.

I witnessed both incidents both events happened so fast that I was powerless to do anything but watch my one year old daughter be injured by this dangerous chair. incident_description: We bought this bed for my 1 year old in 2013. When we potty trained him he had a few accidents and we took the outer cover off to wash. On the inside I found food bits and water had accumulated and begun to rot. Absolutely disgusting. There are several small holes in the tray top that allow food, water, and beverages to drip in.  I called evenflo to inquire if there was a fix, or recall, or substitute tray. The service representative said all their trays have those holes to prevent drowning. 

If the holes are a safety feature, then they should drain freely, not into an enclosed space that creates a mold hazard. Or at least make the tray easier to disassemble to clean thoroughly.

incident_description: Almost a year ago when my daughter was four months old I purchased the "Berkley crib and changer by Sorelle" crib. I followed all assembly instructions and was satisfied with my purchase until now. I put my daughter down for a nap, she usually fusses for a few minutes and then puts herself to sleep. I could hear her quiet down and assumed she was beginning her nap time ritual of making herself comfortable by cuddling with her blanket or teddy bear. Instead she started screaming crying, not the usual whining cry, but she sounded like she was in pain. When I opened the door I saw her throwing her body weight away from the changer side of the crib. Because this is a combo crib there is a slot between the changer top and storage area and my daughter had reached her arm through and gotten stuck. As she is only one year old, she attempted to get it back by bending her arm, only further wedging it in. By pushing herself away from it she was actually further wedging her arm in. She was screaming in pain and fear and was crying tears of pain. I was able to remove her arm by picking her up with one arm and making it so her arm was level with the opening while using my other arm to pull her arm straight and then carefully I pulled her arm out. It had swollen from being wedged and at one point I feared I would have to either lubricate her arm somehow to slide it out or break the crib. While the extraction only took a minute she suffered bruising all over her upper arm and right below her elbow. She was terrified as was I and she is lucky that she didn't break her arm or dislocate her shoulder or elbow. Crib slats must be a certain distance apart to keep children safe, but this slat was not the same width and obviously is not safe. I immediately disassembled the crib and returned it to the Babies R Us from which it was purchased. I was in tears as I described the horrifying situation, they said they would not recommend the crib to any person who took interest in buying it and attempted to remove the floor model but were told by corporate that they had to leave it out. I given a full refund and offered a compensatory 20% off a new crib, but declined because the majority of the selection there was the same brand. I will never in my life buy a piece of Sorelle furniture and especially not a crib. I will warn any friend who has children who use a crib to avoid the brand. My entire day was ruined and instead of going to a birthday party we spent the day in tears disassembling the unsafe crib and removing it and purchasing and assembling a new crib. It was a horrific experience as a mother and I can say that it ended in a best case scenario compared to how bad it could have been. Luckily I have the resources and ability to replace the crib, but for families who don't have that luxury it would be terrifying to have to trust leaving your child alone in a crib like that.
justification: The child suffered bruising and pain, indicating an injury (severity 3). The incident is unlikely to recur frequently given the specific circumstances described.

incident_description:
We ordered a Graco Foam Mattress off of Walmart.com and had it shipped to our local WalMart. We purchased the mattress on 6/22/2016.  We put the mattress on the bed and put the sheet over it. My son was born on 7/72016. For the first few months he slept with us, then we started putting him on his mattress with the sheet. He spit up on the sheet so we removed the sheet and washed it. We just placed him on the mattress at this point. I started noticing these small, long, shiny, brittle fibers on his clothes and on my own. After about a week, I asked my husband if he noticed them and he said they were all over his and my daughters clothes. I googled what the fibers could be and it popped up fiberglass from a baby mattress in the search. 

I called the manufacturing company StorkCraft. They asked me what the model number and the date of manufacturing was. I told them April 2016. She asked if it was sold with a plastic cover and I responded no. She said, "Oh." She then asked me to send them pictures of the matress and of the receipt. I went and looked at the mattress again and realized the mesh cover had a different tag than the mattress. I opened the mesh cover  and the mattress manufacturing date of January 2015 with the model number that matches the model numbers of the recalled mattresses. At the time we were on the phone, I did not know it matched. 

I asked to speak to someone about these fibers and how to get them off of everything. They're on my households' clothes, my carpet, my couches, my washer, and my dryer. She transferred me to [REDACTED] in Customer Service but it went to voicemail. I left her a message. I called back and asked when she would be available and the woman said maybe later today maybe tomorrow. 

I then called Graco. The woman I spoke to asked me when I had talked to Storkcraft and I told her today but they sent me to voicemail. I told her it was terrible customer service. She called them and told me they would be in contact with me. She offered me a coupon. I asked her how they were allowing Storkcraft to sale a recalled product in their boxes? She told me they were not responsible, that the manufacturing company was. I told her that they, as a company, should ensure that the company they do business with isn't putting a recalled product in their boxes. She gave me more excuses as to why they weren't responsible because StorkCraft was a licensing company of theirs. I told her they should be making sure this isn't happening to anymore of their consumers. She looked at the recall and the only thing she could tell me is why it was recalled and what they were doing to resolve the issue. 

I spoke to [REDACTED] and she asked me to send photos and the receipt. She also asked me where it was manufactured and I told her where in China. She asked me when I noticed the fibers and I said about a week ago. I explained what they looked like and how they were everywhere and I couldn't get them off and that they had spread to everything. She said she would have to contact the company in China. She asked me if I knew where they were coming from: the mesh liner or the mattesss. I said I wasn't sure because if it was one or the other they're poking out and easily spread so it is hard to determine where. I did tell her I took a clean, black sock and ran it over the mattress with the mesh cover and it was completely covered in the fibers. I specifically asked her to find out what they were and how to get them off of everything.

I received this email from StorkCraft:

Dear [REDACTED], 

Thank you for sending photos of your Graco Deluxe Foam Crib and Toddler Mattress-in-a-Box. They have been reviewed.

As per the technical department, it was not sure or confirmed  where the fibers  are coming from . It would be difficult identify  what those fibers are and how to remove them. We sincerely apoloigize as we are unable to assist regarding the fibers .


For your concern regarding the recall, only those mattresses that were missing the mattress fire barrier (Models 06710-100 or 06710-200 and a manufactured date between August 2014 and January 2015)  are affected.   In those instances we only send this missing fire barrier cover. 

We have gone ahead and submitted order [REDACTED] to send you a new mattress barrier cover for your mattress . 




**Please keep this entire thread when responding**

Thank you,

Customer Service TE (Replacement Parts)

Stork Craft Manufacturing Inc. 
Suite 200 - 12033 Riverside Way
Richmond, BC, V6W 1K6
Local Calls: 604-275-4242 
Toll Free: 1-877-274-0277

Obviously, they have admitted to selling me a recalled mattress which is illegal under the Consumer Product Safety Improvement  Act of 2008. I do not believe that they have manufactured a mattress but they have no idea what they have put in it. 

I collected all of the clothes in my house that were contaminated. When I had done this, my eyes began to itch and it felt like sand was under my eyelids. It took me an hour of flushing my eyes with saline solution to make them feel better. My son has been sick. He had an eye infection, a runny infected nose, and had difficulty breathing with fluid in his lungs. He has been sleeping with us ever since I discovered the fibers were coming from the mattress. The doctors have not confirmed yet whether it was from the mattress. I am making my son and I an appointment with an opthamologist on Monday. I will also be looking to send off these fibers to a lab to determine what they are.

I saw on WalMart.com a review a woman had written. She had bought the mattress for her Great Dane. When it got dirty, she washed the mesh liner and  the other liner that covered the foam. She dried it on air only. When she opened the dryer, the liner exploded and fiberglass went all over her face and everything. She just threw it away. 

I intend to email StorkCraft back and demand that they figure out what it is and how I get rid of them as well as reminding them that it was illegal to sale me the mattress to begin with.
justification: The incident involves exposure to potentially harmful fibers causing health issues like eye irritation and respiratory problems, indicating injury.

incident_description:
The Prince Lionheart brand weePOD Basix toilet seat caused my daughter severe rashes on the back of her thighs and buttocks. We have used this seat as directed over our regular toilet seats since my daughter potty trained. About a year ago she developed what we thought was an eczema rash. For the past almost year, we have been to numerous doctors, put her on numerous steroid creams and non steroid creams, spent countless amounts of money on new and different lotions and soaps all to no effect. She had been tested for bacteria, fungus, and virus and all came back negative. At the worst, she had over a dozen open sores and scabs from the rash and all the scratching and itching and pain that it caused her. The dermatologist had suggested a biopsy when it dawned on me while she used the bathroom one day that all of these spots were where her skin touched her toilet seat. We immediately got rid of the toilet seats and over the past two weeks her legs have almost completely healed. She still has skin discoloration where she had sore for so long that will take some time to go away. 

While searching the internet ("Contact Dermatitis Prince Lionheart") we came across numerous Amazon reviews for the exact same product of other people whose children developed rashes after using this toilet seat. We also came across an article of a child in the U.K. Who was taken to the hospital because of her rash from this product and this article shows that the company knows about this issue. 

We want this product recalled due to the risk of severe rash it poses, so we can protect other people from going through what we went through and so those who are going through it now can get an answer and stop their child's suffering. 

Daily Mail Article: http://www.dailymail.co.uk/health/article-3300918/When-nappy-rash-really-sign-allergy-Baby-wipes-cleaning-sprays-potty-training-seats-blame.html

incident_description:
I have been using a high chair manufactured by "4moms" and purchased at Giggle.com for $299.00.
I purchased this high chair in September of 2016 and began using this high chair in November 2016. 

The 4moms high chair is a new high chair model that was released in 2016. The high chair has a latch that is located underneath the tray. The latch is a bar that releases the tray when the bar is pushed up and out. The latch is unique in that it uses a magnet to engage the latch and can be used with one hand. 

My 8 month old baby is able to push on the latch with his feet and release the tray causing it to fall off of the high chair. The first time he did this I was across the room and had to run to catch him to prevent him from falling as his restraint straps were on but not tightened down completely.  Over the course of the past month he has been able to remove the tray by pushing on the latch with his feet on a regular basis. I have stopped using the high chair because it is unsafe and additionally very inconvenient when the contents of the tray fall on the floor. 

My 7 month old nephew has been using the same high chair model purchased from the same vendor and he is also able to remove the tray on his high chair by pushing on the latch with his feet. There is at least one other online review on 4moms website where a consumer indicates that her 6 month old baby is able to remove the tray by pushing on the latch with her feet. I mention this because I don't believe it is an isolated issue with my specific high chair. 

I have used video to document my son removing the tray with his feet. I also have video of the latch mechanism operating as the manufacturer intended. I have been in contact with 4moms as well as the vendor, Giggle. I sent them the video footage. 4moms responded by indicating that: "the tray latches do appear to be functioning properly. It appears that your little one may be at a height right now where they are pushing up and pushing out on the latch underneath the tray to disengage the latches." 4moms refused to refund my money and failed to indicate that they would look into this problem. 

Based on my research of safety guidelines a child should not be able release the tray either intentionally or by accident. The fact that I spent $300 on a high chair that isnÃÂt safe for our baby is a concern. However a larger concern is that in my opinion this high chair has a design flaw and can pose a danger to babies and children using it. At a minimum there should be a warning label on the chair informing parents that it is possible for their child to remove the tray with their feet. Parents should be aware of this before they invest $300 in a high chair that canÃÂt be returned as well as use a high chair that could easily cause injury. Furthermore per 4moms response there is no information on this high chair that indicates it is not appropriate for a little one at a certain height. If I had known there was a height restriction that would prevent my 6-8 month old from safely using the chair, I would have purchased a different high chair. 

Please let me know if you need any additional information from me. I am happy to share the video footage of the problem with the high chair tray. 

Thank you,

[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involves a design flaw allowing a child to release the tray, posing a risk of falling but no actual injury reported.

incident_description: I purchased a replacement night light with incandescent bulb from Wal-Mart (Great Value Soft White Incandescent, item number 1038, made in China but said to be designed by Meridian Electric Company of St. Louis). Both the replacement and the original are new items purchased this year. The problem with the 1st one is that if the two prongs are fully inserted into the duplex receptacle, the light is always on and the switch does not work. The switch works if there is about 1/8 of an inch of metal exposed on the prongs but it is not fully inserted. It is as if the outlet squeezes the switch contacts together leaving it in an always on condition. Since the outlet is to the right and above a bathroom sink, I decided to buy another one. As soon as I plugged the new night light into the receptacle, it exploded with a loud bang! Fortunately the plastic shield in front of the night light prevented me from eye injury as I was not wearing glasses. The GFCI circuit breaker also tripped. I am not an electrical engineer but I do have a doctorÃÂs degree in physics so I carefully removed the duplex receptacle from the wall. The hot, neutral, and ground wires were all firmly and properly attached to the receptacle. I reset the breaker and found the outlet functional so I KNOW the problem is with the night light. I made several pictures of the exploded bulb. I will return the repackaged item to Wal-Mart.
justification: The incident involved an exploding night light, but no injury occurred due to the plastic shield preventing harm.

incident_description: On the date of the incident an infant child had her two lower teeth damaged from a crib utilized at the school in the infant room. Subsequently when the child was picked up her teeth were pulled out and down. The family was notified immediately and CPS was notified by self reporting procedures. The crib was approved for use by licensing prior to installation in the infant room. The components responsible for the incident were removed to make the crib in line with other cribs without this feature. In addition a safety stand down and changes to current safety procedures are being revised to include process improvement and composite risk assessment. The incident is still pending investigation and the teacher is on administrative leave until further notice. An investigation by the school is currently under way and it is being checked for recall of this item or any safety notifications. All manufacturer's warnings were followed and there was no instructions dealing with these components.
justification: The infant suffered dental injury from the crib incident, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is rated as rare (1) given the specific and unusual circumstances described.

incident_description:
My 6 month old Granddaughter's airway was blocked when using the Sophie the Girafe! 
Sitting on the floor with my Granddaughter in my lap I introduced Sophie the Girafe to her for her to put in her mouth as she is teething, it was obvious she loved the soft sensation on her gums. After putting one of the legs in her mouth I heard a  little gasp, no air was coming out, I gave a quick pull the leg was out, she was breathing fine, thank God! 
My granddaughter's longest finger measures one and a half inches long, the giraffe's leg measures two and a quarter inches long. Her little fingers are also very small around, where not only is the giraffe's leg is larger around, the hoof is so much larger than a baby's fingertip. I believe it is the hoof of the giraffe that was lodged in her airway. 
I was very concerned that this could happen to another baby I reached out to the US Safety Product Safety Commission as well as the toy Company. 
The toy company states this toy stimulates the five senses, Taste: "Sophie the Girafe is made of 100%  natural rubber and food paint, and is completely safe to chew, just like a feeding bottle teat. Her soft texture and numerous chewable parts (ears, horns, legs) make her perfect for soothing a baby's sore gums during teething". 
The toy company's response to me stated their company meets legal European and worldwide standards and does not create a risk of choking or oppression. They perform tests to simulate the throat and trachea of a child and concludes the giraffe cannot cause a child to choke and is not a choking hazard. Also to provide a child with parental supervision. Also they compared what happened to my granddaughter as: "When a baby puts their fingers in their mouth, they may be able to regurgitate themselves and/or emit choking sounds that can frighten parents. This may also occur when a child puts Sophie la giraffe in their mouth. This is not a loss of breath, which can arise when respiratory tracts are blocked, but regurgitation."
My Grandaughter's airway was blocked! We are the voice for our precious babies. We need more thorough testing to keep our babies safe and hol the toy companies accountable. The US Consumer Product Safety Commission has been notified.
justification: The incident involved a blocked airway but no injury occurred, and the child resumed normal breathing after intervention.

incident_description:
I am a pediatrician and worked for 4 years in a neonatal intensive care unit. 

I am concerned about the Crescent Womb - a sleep hammock marketed towards infants. 
https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/1727087541/crescent-womb-infant-safety-bed

This infant sleep hammock increases the risk of infant death as the hammock promotes a chin-to-chest position (as shown in the manufacturer's own pictures of the product - http://www.crescentwomb.com/uploads/7/0/3/3/70333151/s687171726677863482_p2_i7_w2560.jpeg ).

There is also a risk of entrapment and/or strangulation as depending on the size of the crib used, the baby could roll and get its head stuck between the hammock and the side of the crib. 

This product falsely claims to decrease the risk of SIDS, when in reality I am worried it will only increase the risk.
justification: The product promotes a dangerous chin-to-chest position and risks entrapment or strangulation, which could lead to infant death.

incident_description: I'm concerned with the product "crescent womb." It is pictured spread over an open sided crib. An infant could easily roll out of it onto the ground. In addition, a "sling" like that may promote asphyxiation from a "chin to chest" position. It should not be advertised as a safe place for an infant to sleep. The AAP is clear that infants belong in a crib on a flat surface with a well fitted sheet on their back.
justification: The product design poses risks of falls and asphyxiation, which could lead to severe injury or death, as per AAP guidelines.

incident_description: The crescent womb claims to be a safe sleeping environment and also claims to reduce the risk of SIDS.  This product goes against all AAP sleep standards and everything recommendation to reduce the risk of SIDS.  It has babies sleep in an elevated hammock versus flat on their back.  This leaves babies at risk of positional asphyxiation, becoming entangled in the hammock, or falling out of the hammock and becoming injured.  This product needs to be stopped before it causes a baby to die.  According the the company, QVC has picked up this product.  Please look into this product.
justification: The description highlights potential risks of positional asphyxiation, entanglement, and injury, which could lead to death, indicating a high severity level.

incident_description: On multiple occasions, both my infant child and I have been pinched very very hard by one of the activity toys on her bright starts bounce bounce baby activity center. It is green and yellow, with a blue cloth seat cover, it has a yellow adjustable platform underneath for the child's feet to stand on. It spins around 360 degrees, and the toys that are around the seat include a blue ball that slides up and down a post, underneath which is a ring and then an accordian like flexible plastic structure that can be compressed when pushed down, I guess the idea is that you push down on the ball on top and compress the accordian thing and then when you let go the ball jumps up the post from the release of the pressure on the bottom thing. Almost everytime I have tried doing this, from every angle or possible holding position, my fingers have gotten pinched between the parts on the balls way back up after trying to let go. I tried it many times to ensure it wasn't just a fluke, or could only happen if you do it a certain way, almost every time it pinched my finger, and thus couldn't possibly be considered safe by any standard.One incident brought blood it pinched so hard, and although it wasn't difficult to get my finger free (you have to pull the ball back down) and I realize the cut was caused by my trying it over and over, if it had been my child that was pinched that hard it could have very well done much greater damage. I discovered this when my little one started crying hysterically while playing with the toy, she had jerked away from the pain and had already freed her little hand (it got her in the webbing between her thumb and pointer finger), I checked her out and noticed a purple rounded pinch mark on her hand. I immediately took her out of the bouncer and investigated the issue myself, and after determining it would most certainly do it to her again if left as it was, I cut the accordian like thing off and have had no further issues.

justification: The child's head was wedged in the crib, causing indentations and a dangerous position, but no suffocation or lasting injury occurred.

incident_description: I was gifted a brand new IKEA Sundvik crib for our son. We have used the crib for the past four months (since he was two and a half months old). I just noticed that the bottom board of the crib that supports the mattress is bowed in the middle. It is bowed even when he is not in the crib, but when I put him in it the mattress support bows even further. My son weighs 22 pounds, which is less than half of the maximum load weight. I contacted IKEA customer service to report the issue and was told that although this sounds like a quality issue, they are unable to assist me because I do not have a receipt (since this was a gift). I inquired about the safety of continued use of the bowed crib, and the representative told me that she cannot give me any information on the crib's safety. From what I understood, IKEA stands behind their products and the safety of their products, but they are not willing to stand behind this product even when it is deemed to be a "quality issue."
justification: The crib's bowed support poses a potential safety risk, but no injury has occurred yet.

incident_description: My baby used the mam pacifier to sleep but last night she woke up crying with red eyes and face desperate with the pacifier stuck inside her mouth. I pulled it out carefully. She was inconsolable, after this she still cried and sobbed sleeping. Im really angry!
justification: The baby experienced distress and physical discomfort with the pacifier stuck in her mouth, indicating an injury level incident.

incident_description: The DG (dollar general) brand baby teether was being chewed on by my 11 month old son. While chewing on it, the ring broke, causing the beads to come off, one of which got caught in his throat. I had to preform the heimlich maneuver to dislodge the bead. This product is extremely unsafe, and broke under a small amount of pressure put on it by my son. Because this product is advertised as a teether for infants, it most certainly needs to be taken out of circulation. The product is still being sold online and in stores.
justification: The incident resulted in a bead getting caught in the child's throat, requiring the Heimlich maneuver, which constitutes an injury.

incident_description: A Piece came off as my daughter was chewing on it. I could have choked her, glad I caught in time. As I checked over the rest of the product I realized many of the parts are becoming loose.
justification: A piece came off during use, posing a choking hazard, but no injury occurred as it was caught in time. Multiple loose parts indicate a recurring issue.

incident_description: There is a gap between the crib and mattress I have for my son. The mattress came with the crib as a set. The mattress will slide from side to side. When centered it is a little less than 1 inch on each side, but when it slides it creates an almost 2 inch gap. He has gotten his arms and legs stuck in between the rails and mattress. In one occasion his head has become wedged. I have contacted the company and they say the gap, which is roughly 2 inches, is recommended and that crib mattresses are not to be snug. They will not remedy the situation. My son is 9 months old and I am afraid of what would happen to a smaller infant.
justification: The description indicates that the child has gotten limbs and head stuck, which constitutes injury, and the issue is recurring.

incident_description: I purchased the rumparooz all in one pocket cloth diapers from amazon.com. The cloth diapers are listed as being for babies from 6 to 35+ pounds. At 13 pounds my son was only in the 19th percentile at 4 months. The elastic band around where the diapers go around the thighs are very tight. They left welts and blisters on my babies thighs. I took pictures of the marks that they left. I stopped using the diapers a month ago and he still has scars on his thighs from them. At $24 a diaper I would expect to have a product that wont injure my child.
justification: The diapers caused welts, blisters, and lasting scars on the baby's thighs, indicating an injury.

incident_description: The sun hit our 6 month old in the face and left him with a bruise. we were using it properly. we checked with the manufacturer, and our model ob3 was not recalled.
justification: The incident resulted in a bruise, which qualifies as an injury, but there was no death or severe harm.

The mfg is Delta Children's Products, the M# 23004-983, po#256285, lot#js13006, made in Taiwan, DOM: 03/2013, Desc: LX High Chair.

incident_description:
I bought a box of size 5 Kirkland brand diapers for my 2 year old. I had noticed that she kept getting diaper rashes for no apparent reason. All of a sudden 2 weeks ago, she had a 1st degree burn that was so bad, cold water made her cry out in agony. And, she was only wet, not dirty.

We determined that these diapers were not wicking away the moisture and have since quit using them.
justification: The child suffered a 1st degree burn due to the diapers not wicking moisture, which constitutes an injury.

incident_description: my daughter was playing, laying on the play gym her foot was resting on one of the gym pools and as she pushed off to reach for a toy the gym folded in half covering her face and chest.
justification: The incident involved the play gym folding over the child's face and chest, but there was no mention of injury.

incident_description: My 9 month old fell out of the HC144BZF (Casablanca),  high chair falling 27" to the tile floor. She was rushed to the ER, at which time they did a CAT scan to ensure that her jaw was not broken. She suffered a large bruise on the chin area as well as two bruises to the knees.

incident_description: Fisherprice Rock and play Sleeper has mold on the back of it. This was purchased in February 2016.

incident_description:
We purchased the Little Einstein Bouncer for my son when I was pregnant with him, upon him turning 4 months he was finally able to use the product as he feet could completely touch the ground, and he had the strength to bounce as well. Once he began to teeth, she showed much interest in the "sun" toy that is next to the blue cloud toy on his jumper. Numerous times he has actually pushed it down to where is flung back and smashed him in the face. Mind you he isn't too tall right now so it was literally right it his face. He has probably done this 3-4 times already, each time startling him quite a bit and causing him to cry. However this time he did it again and actually cut his  upper lip when it flew back. At this point, we can't even let him play in his jumper (which he loves) unless we are actually sitting on the floor to make sure he does not go for the sun. 
In addition, he managed to pull off the bar that is attached to the musical mirror and actually managed to break it off completely! I am very disappointed as this product was not cheap and had so many good reviews before purchasing. After pulling off the bar and being kept from playing with the sun toy. There are not many options left for him besides just bouncing. Very disappointed in the quality of our product so far.
justification: The incident resulted in a cut to the child's upper lip, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) as the child has repeatedly hit his face with the toy and the issue persists without intervention.

incident_description: I purchased the Ikea Stuva crib for my daughter and at only 10 months old in just a 2 minutes she was able to chew through a side of the crib- each short side is just a paint covering and particle board of the crib and actually ingested some of the particle board. It easily dissolved in her mouth. After fits of vomiting and a call to poison control, she is fine now thank god. I called customer service immediately and put in a claim. The representative was very kind and concerned about my daughter. She informed me that a person from the store would be calling me back to arrange the return and refund of the product. I received a call today from a very rude man from my local San Diego store who informed me that they came to the decision that it is not a fault of the product but of my "lack of supervision" of my child and that they will not honor the warranty or return the item. Cribs are the one place that your baby should be safe. As parents we buy our cribs thinking that they will be safe and not be sickened or even worse, she could have choked.
justification: The child ingested particle board and vomited, indicating injury (severity 3), but the likelihood of this happening is unlikely (2) given the specific circumstances described.

incident_description: My son has been used MAM pacifiers since the day he was born.  We have never had any issues.  About a week ago he got his paci out of his crib...crawled up on the couch beside me and handed me the tip of the paci.  He had chewed it off.  I contacted MAM and they apologized and have been great to deal with. They sent him a teether and an envelope requesting me to send it back to them so they can test it in the lab (I have already sent it back).  We have since weened our son from the pacifier because of the awful safety risk.  I just wanted to report this because in my opinion even if a child chews on the pacifier...they should not be able to chew through it.
justification: The child chewed off the tip of the pacifier but no injury occurred, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: My toddler was playing with one of the balls that came with this toy - http://www.amazon.com/Earlyears-Roll-Swirl-Ball-Ramp/dp/B004IZWQYQ, and it split open letting the tiny little balls inside the bigger ball fall all over the floor.  This would be a significant choking hazard for my infant and my toddler.

incident_description: My daughter was playing in the bouncer when the strap broke. It is frayed and none of the other straps look frayed.
justification: The strap broke but there was no mention of injury, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: On April 27th I put my 22 month old son down for a nap in his Graco Lauren Crib. Not long after, i heard a loud noise over the baby monitor and went in the room to find he had pushed up the trim across the top of the back of the crib. This exposed small wooden pegs that were loose and 4 of them were laying around him in his crib. This is a part that came pre assembled and was barely attatched. This crib is still being sold, probably through different distributors. We purchased our crib in Spring 2014 from Wal Mart.

incident_description:
The safety pins included in the Kidco Safeway Gate for installation at the top of stairs are completely inadequate.  In the installation instructions they list the use of these pins to stop the gate from swinging out over the stairs.  However they are improperly positioned and sized in order to perform this function.

Last evening my 3 year old son went to close the gate in our home, located at the top of a stair case.  When he pushed the gate shut it jumped the latch and swung out over the stairs.  Since he was pushing the gate my son began to fall when the gate swung out.  Thankfully I was standing there with him and was able to catch him before he fell down a full flight of stairs.

This product needs to be adjusted as it is unsafe when installed as detailed in the instructions.
justification: The incident involved a near-fall due to a faulty gate, but no injury occurred as the child was caught in time.

incident_description: baby regularly uses pampers [REDACTED], babysitter put pamper drymax on her yesterday and we ended up in St Barnabas ED with diagnosis of 2 degree burn of left buttock/flank.  Child protective services was notified!  I found literture stating that P&G paid claims to 59 people related to allegations of this diaper causing harm, and yet never issued a recall.  I find this to be appalling.

incident_description: I took the pad off my sons rock n' play sleeper made by fisher price to find black mold growing. I am so disgusted that this company knew about the problem back in 2013 but have nothing to try and prevent the problem.
justification: The presence of black mold is an incident with potential health risks, but no actual injury is reported.

incident_description: My newborn son (5 days old) was sleeping in the snug a puppy sleeper and I looked over at him and his mouth was blue, he was not able to get good oxygen flow due to his poor head and neck control at an angle.  According to the American Pediatrics Association, babies should sleep flat on their backs.  This sleeper is unsafe and may cause sids.  I gave my son mouth to mouth and rushed him to the hospital.  Thank God he is healthy.
justification: The baby's mouth turned blue due to poor oxygen flow, requiring mouth-to-mouth resuscitation and hospitalization, indicating an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is high (4) given the unsafe sleeper design and the baby's vulnerability.

incident_description: It was in the middle of the night and pitch black in my bedroom. My newborn infant was sleeping beside me in a Kolcraft bassinet. She was fussy and I put a pacifier in her mouth. She suddenly screamed a bloodcurdling scream I'd never heard from her before. I reached quickly for her and grabbed her ankle right before she fell. The bassinet collapsed in a vertical position and she was sliding head first onto the hardwood floor. I caught her, but just barely. The next morning my husband latched the bassinet again and said he thought he fixed it. I didn't dare to use it again and thank goodness  I didn't. My two year old daughter put her baby doll in it and it collapsed again. It was the 2011 model; not listed on the recall list. Earlier models of the same bassinet have been recalled for very similar issues. I am still shaken at the tragedy that could have happened.
justification: The bassinet collapsed twice, nearly causing injury to the infant, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description:
I have several night lights in my home, all are the same make and model. AmerTac model 71055 auto turn on night lights.  I have had these for approximately 10 years.  I have recently had two of them fail.  It starts out with an acrid smell in the house that I can't immediately identify where it is coming from.  I then discover the white plastic housing near the photo eye on the nightlight is turning brown.  In both instances it appears the photo eye is melting inside the housing.  Both times the nightlight continued to operate so it wasn't immediately apparent that something was wrong with it.  It should be noted that I do understand basic electricity concepts and I always use the proper sized light buld in all fixtures.  I believe if I would have been out of town when this happened  these highlights could have started a fire. I will take pictures of what it looks like and will be happy to mail the product in for inspection.  

Once again I had two identical products fail in the same way within a year of each other.
justification: The incident involved melting components and potential fire risk, but no actual injury or fire occurred.

incident_description: Pacifier found lodged in my baby's throat, choking him.
justification: The baby was choking due to a pacifier lodged in the throat, indicating a serious incident with potential for injury or death.

incident_description:
I was holding my almost 6 month old baby in my arms. She had her pacifier in her mouth.  She can now grab the pacifier and put it on her mouth on her own.  While I was looking at my other daughter, my baby stuck the whole pacifier in her mouth. The was no visible part outside of her mouth and she was chocking. 

If she hadn't been with me, she probably would have chocked to death.  She sleeps with the pacifier and has it in her crib. This is why I decided to file a report. My daughter could have done this on her own in the middle of the night and might have choked.  I do not reccommend this pacifier at all. 

It is the Acent pacifier that has green or blue part in the center. The rest of the pacifier is transparent.
justification: The baby choked on the pacifier but was not injured due to immediate intervention, though the potential for death was present if unsupervised.

incident_description:
Ingenuity 3 in 1 Deluxe High Chair, #60634 NA

Tray unlock mechanism requires squeezing a handle into the tray. Infant's feet and toes became trapped between this mechanism while attempting to remove the tray while infant was in the high chair. The mechanism also has unnecessarily sharp plastic edges, which severely bruised infant's toes.
justification: The infant's toes were severely bruised due to sharp plastic edges and trapping in the mechanism, indicating an injury (severity 3). The description suggests this could happen frequently during tray removal (likelihood 4).

incident_description: My son has been diagnosed with "Right Torticollis" and "Mild positional plagiocephaly." He now has to have physical therapy to fix the tightening of his neck muscles on his right side. The physical therapist said that this is due to the way that gravity pulls the heavy infant head down while sleeping in the Fisher Price Rock & Play. He now favors turning his head to one side due to the tightening of the muscles and thus has developed a mild flat spot on the back-right side of his skull. My first son also used the Fisher Price Rock & Play sleeper and had SEVERE Brachycephaly; he had to have a helmet to correct the shape of his head from this. I had no idea at the time that the Rock & Play could cause Brachycephaly, plagiocephaly and torticollis or I would NEVER have used it for either son. We ended up paying $1,200 AFTER 80% insurance coverage of my first son's helmet. FIsher Price should not market this Rock & Play as a safe infant sleeper due to the extensive medical issues that it can and does cause. I know that I am not alone in my frustration with this product-please see other reviews from Amazon and other verified retailers.
justification: The description details physical injuries (torticollis and plagiocephaly) requiring medical intervention, indicating a severity level of 3.

incident_description:
The tinylove take along mobile can be used in 3 different ways. Directly attached to the baby's carseat, attached to the baby's stroller canapy with a provided claw device, or attached the to baby's pack and play with the provided arm clamp. I am concerned about the arm claw as it is provided in order to hold a mobile over a baby's head while he or she sleeps. I hadn't had it but for a week or two when i found it in the bottom of the pack in play broken. If my baby had been under it, he could have been hurt from the object falling on him. There is also a concern that pieces of it could have choked him if chewed. 
  The design of the clamp is flawed as it is 2 pieces of cheap plastic bonded together somehow. It makes certain parts of the plastic cery thin and unable to withstand pressure. The design itself is supposed to handle pressure as you tighten the clamp to the pack and play in order to support the weight of the arm. Without a strong clamp design this is doomed to break and i'm worried that many children may be hurt by this.
justification: The description indicates a potential for injury from the broken clamp falling on the baby or from choking on broken pieces, though no actual injury was reported.

incident_description:
I bought the Vyssa Vinka baby crib at the end of July 2016. The mattress had previously been recalled: http://www.ikea.com/us/en/about_ikea/newsitem/011315_recall-VYSSA-crib-mattresses 

The one we bought was manufactured on 7/7/2015, which was after the recalled ones were manufactured and supposedly ok. After my baby had been sleeping on the crib for 3 months I noticed a sizable gap between the end of the mattress and the crib (the reason for the previous recall). I took the mattress back to Ikea and when they measured it, they were surprised to find that it measured the same length as the recalled ones.  It is not long enough for the crib and poses a serious threat of entrapment for babies. They told me they are investigating the problem and have stopped sale of the mattress.

We should have returned the damn thing then, but the high chair was a gift and we didn't know when it had been purchased or where.  Twice, he popped the tray off and fell face first out of the thing.  The first time he busted his face up pretty well.  The second time, i was sitting at the table next to him an literally caught him by the bib before he hit the floor.  Since then, the damn thing has been in the garage.  I can't imagine how dangerous this could be or what may have happened to kids sitting in it that were hurt worse than my son.

He was on the verge of falling out. The only thing keeping him in was the buckle. This all happened within seconds. He was not injured just had some very scared and angry parents. incident_description:
We had purchased the Disney Baby Finding Nemo Sea of Activities Jumper approximately 5 months ago.  Our son was jumping in it the morning of 2-28-16 at approximately 9:15 AM and one of the four nylon straps broke while he was jumping in it.  While he was in the seat jumping the platform with our son seated in the seat of the platform fell towards the corner that had broken, leaving his legs stuck in the seat and him face down on the ground. 

Upon inspection of what caused the break, there is a metal buckle on all four corners where the straps are held at the underside of the platform the baby sits in.  This is a stamped piece of steel which leaves one side with sharp edges.  This is a factory pre-installed part and is not adjusted or moved when assembling the product.  The intended jumping motion in this product over time would appear to cause wear on the nylon strap from the sharp edges of the steel buckle against on the nylon strap, eventually wearing through and cutting the nylon strap causing a break.
justification: The incident resulted in the child being stuck face down on the ground, indicating potential injury from the fall and entrapment.

incident_description:
Our daughter is 6 weeks old and approximately 11 lb. She is of average size for her age and is well within the age and weight limits recommended for use of this product. She is not able to sit up, pull up, or roll over on her own. After eliminating other possibilities, we believe that she recently was injured by a combination of factors inherent in the design of this product.

Our baby had slept in the bassinet through the night, except for when being fed and changed. At her first feeding the next morning, it became apparent that her forehead was covered in what resembled a deep purple rash or petechiae. We sent photos to our pediatricianÃÂs office and were told to take our baby to the emergency room immediately, for fear of a serious underlying medical cause. However tests and evaluation revealed no apparent cause. This was validated by a follow up visit to another pediatrician the following day, who again found no concerning underlying medical issues. He believed this to be an injury from some outside factor in the babyÃÂs immediate environment and recommended further investigation. The babyÃÂs environment immediately preceding the problem was the HALO Bassinest Swivel Sleeper, which we believe was the primary cause due to two factors.

The first factor is that the bassinet will not always stay level, allowing a squirmy baby that is not otherwise mobile to eventually slide into the mesh sides of the bassinet. This is well documented in online reviews of the product, to which HALO has responded that tilt up to 5 degrees is allowable under safety regulations.

The second factor, and an apparent design flaw, is part of the so-called ÃÂSoothing CenterÃÂ of the ÃÂPremier SeriesÃÂ bassinets. This is a small battery-powered device attached to the side of the bassinet that offers a nightlight, vibration, music, sounds, and a nursing timer. Four round head screws hold on the plastic back plate of the ÃÂSoothing CenterÃÂ, one at each corner. The bottom two screws sit below the top level of the mattress and behind the fabric trim of the mesh sidewalls. However the top two screws are separated from the babyÃÂs sleeping area only by the mesh sidewalls. The screw heads protrude from the surface of the soothing center back plate, posing a blunt injury hazard to the baby.

We have concluded with reasonable certainty that during the night our baby slid into the side of the bassinet nearest the ÃÂSoothing Center, with her forehead area near the exposed screw heads. While she cannot roll over or pull up, she does root, peck, and bob her head, sometimes with considerable force. This is normal for a baby of her age and size. However, these types of movements while near or pressed up against the ÃÂSoothing CenterÃÂ allowed her to bang her head repeatedly into the screw heads, causing the purple marks discovered on her head the next morning. The size and shape of the injuries are consistent with the screw heads. The location of the injuries is consistent with her position in the bassinet that morning.

Our recommendation is for a recall and redesign of the ÃÂSoothing CenterÃÂ to modify the back plate attachment to a method that protects the baby from injury.
justification: The baby sustained injuries consistent with banging her head against exposed screw heads, requiring medical evaluation.

incident_description:
I recently picked my 2 year old son up from his morning preschool program, and I noticed that he smelled like he just had a BM. His teachers change him before pick up, so I suspected that it had just happened. I did not have any diapers with me, so I figured he would be okay until I got home, as it's a very short drive. As I was putting him in his car seat, he started squirming and crying. By the time we were half-way home, he was literally screaming as if in pain and writhing in his car seat. I could not do anything but get him home as quickly as possible. When we got in the door, I immediately took off his pants and discovered that he was wearing a Pampers-brand diaper. I also saw that he barely had any poo in it. (I thought that sitting in the poo on the way home was causing him discomfort, although this has never happened before.) When I tried to wipe him, he started crying even harder, so I had to quickly put him in the tub. He also had a bright red mark on his bottom, like a diaper-rash that remained for approximately a week.

My son has never worn Pampers brand before. The diapers that we leave with the preschool are a different (eco-friendly) brand, and his teachers must have run out of those diapers. If I had known that he was wearing a different brand, I could have removed the diaper on the way home and just let him dirty his pants, but I had no idea what the issue was. Concerned about this, I did a quick search on the diapers and discovered that many parents have complained that Pampers Dry Max diapers have caused chemical-like burns on their children. I see that Proctor and Gamble denies it and says that the parents are miffed that the company changed their design. Snopes shows that it has never been proven that the diapers have caused the rashes. Since I have never purchased these diapers, I would have had no idea about a change in design; however, my son has never screamed and cried (almost hyperventilating) from a dirty diaper. He also did not eat anything out of the ordinary that would have caused a rash. After being home for about an hour, my son would still not sit down due to the pain and chose to eat his lunch either squatting or standing up. 

I realize that P&G settled this in the courts, but it would be remiss of me as a parent to not file a report. Meanwhile, parents of infants/toddlers do not have the time and energy to complain to a company over a "change in design". While some children may be immune to harm from these particular diapers, others are obviously affected by a harmful component in them.
justification: The child experienced significant discomfort and a rash lasting a week, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
The consumer's daughter is eight months old and weighs fourteen pounds. The walker was a gift for his child's baby shower. 09/30/2015 - The consumer's daughter was sitting in the walker when it collapsed and, as it turned out later, she suffered a fractured left femur. The child was in her grandfather and mother's care at the time of the incident. 

The child's mother informed the consumer that his daughter did not cry a lot when the incident happened. When the consumer arrived home a couple of hours later, he noticed that, although with no apparent bruises, he noticed his daughter's left thigh was a little swollen and noticed her left leg wasn't kicking.  Finding this odd, the consumer took his daughter to Greenville Memorial Hospital's Emergency Room to have her checked out. After his daughter was examined and x-rays were taken, he was informed she had a fractured left femur and that they had to contact the Police Department to rule out child endangerment. They asked the consumer if his child had suffered a fall or otherwise that could have caused the fractured femur. The child's mother stepped in and informed the Doctor's about the walker incident. They informed the consumer they would need to investigate the matter to see if the walker could, in fact, cause such injury. 

Child endangerment was ruled out since the consumer's daughter was sent to her home.

The child received a cast and was admitted to the hospital for two to three days. 10/28/2015 - The consumer's daughter's cast was removed by Orthopaedic Doctor [REDACTED]The Doctor informed the consumer his child's femur healed appropriately.

Forensic Doctor [REDACTED] informed the consumer that, for reasons unbeknownst to them and based on the tests they did, they believe the walker caused the injury. The Doctor is to send his report to the Investigator.

The injury occurred approximately after two months of the child sitting on the walker.

The consumer believes this product poses a safety hazard to consumers. The consumer plans on contacting the manufacturer.
justification: The child suffered a fractured femur due to the walker collapsing, which required hospitalization and a cast, indicating a significant injury.
