incident_description:
Caller purchased crib 2014, has moved and was using pack and play for a short while then assembled the crib again Friday, June 5th, 2015.

She put her baby to bed June 5th, 2015 and after he woke and was out of the crib Saturday, June 6th, 2015 she noticed that her 13 1/2 month old baby son was limping slightly.  She didn't know why but thought maybe he stepped on something then as the day wore on his limping improved. 

She placed her baby in the crib for a nap this morning Tuesday, June 9th, 2015 then after only 20 minutes he was screaming and crying, she went to his room and his right leg was caught in the slats up to his knee.
He was totally lodged between the slats.

The caller moved the baby's leg upwards to free him then noticed as he walked after being comforted that the limping had returned just as badly as it had been on Saturday.

The caller contacted the manufacturer today, June 9th, 2015, she spoke with a product manager named [REDACTED] who advised her that the gap between the slats is 2 1/8", that it is compliant and that she needs to get after market mesh to place on the crib to avoid these incidents.  The caller asked him if this was written in the product booklet and he responded that it is not.

The baby has not been seen by a doctor.

On 6/9/15 the caller purchased the after market mesh liner.  On 6/12/15 he apparently kicked over the mesh and down and had his foot and leg caught again.  On 6/15/15 his right leg was caught again.  The aftermarket mesh, also purchased at Target, does not help.
justification: The baby sustained a leg injury (limping) due to repeated incidents of getting caught in the crib slats, but there was no death or severe injury reported.

incident_description:
I purcheased a safety first  walker from walmart 
and everytime i put my baby in it she walks and it tilts sideways she fell with the whole walker sideways and she now has a bump on her head as a result of the walker tilting she has fallen whille in the walker 3 times i am very dissatisfyed with this product that is supposed to be safe for my child
justification: The baby sustained a head injury from the walker tilting, indicating a severity level of 3. The incident has occurred multiple times, suggesting a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: I purchased a fisher price rock and play sleeper before my daughter was born. She has used it for the past 4 months. It is a bassinet like sleeper that apparently has been recalled before. I did not know this, however after having seen the recall it is the same issue...MOLD. You would have thought they would have re-engineered the product considering this issue has happened in the past. There is a removable cover on it that I have taken off very frequently for washings. Having just moved and no longer having a washer or dryer in unit, it has been 2 weeks since it was last washed (which normally gets washed once a week.) Upon removal I discovered the mold. My daughter has recently been sick with cold like symptoms and I am hoping this is not the cause! I am extremely infuriated to say the least. Please do something! This can not be safe for any child!
justification: The presence of mold in the sleeper poses a health risk, and the child has shown cold-like symptoms, indicating potential injury.

incident_description: I received the Baby Einstein Sea & Explore Walker for my baby shower.  My child has been using the walker for about 2-3 months now (he is 9 months old).  There have been several incidents where he has hit his mouth on the steering wheel.  It is hard and located right in front of the child's face. He did not sustain any serious injuries from hitting his face on it. On one occasion he had a fat lip and two other times he just cried after hitting it.   I have since removed the steering wheel from the walker.
justification: The child sustained a fat lip and cried after hitting the hard steering wheel, indicating minor injuries.

incident_description:
When removing the fabric cover on my daughter's Rock and Play to launder it, mold was discovered just beginning to grow on the cover as well as a significant amount of growth on the plastic formed seat.  The cover has been routinely laundered since we began using the product after her birth in June.  I have not noticed mold or any discoloration until now, but she is currently being treated for an upper respiratory infection and a cough that will not resolve over the past 6 weeks.

I Googled my concern and found that other consumers had experienced this same issue with the Rock and Play product.  The statement that this issue is the result of uncleanliness, is not completely accurate.  Our daughter's cover has been washed every couple of weeks since birth and this still happened to us.
justification: The presence of mold and the child's ongoing respiratory issues indicate potential injury, and similar incidents have been reported by other consumers.

incident_description:
Caller stated that her 1 year old child's thigh (just above his knees) got stuck between the crib slats.  She contacted the manufacturer 6 weeks ago and on 10/15 she was advised that the crib was made in compliance to the standards.

Caller stated that the incident occurred twice which caused minor bruising just above the child knees.  No medical attention was received.

Caller feels that this crib poses a safety hazard and should be reported.
justification: The child experienced minor bruising from the incident, indicating an injury, and the incident occurred twice, suggesting a possible recurrence.

incident_description:
I own an Arm's Reach Cosleeper (model 8311) and wanted to report the following incident:

I placed my son (5.5months) in the cosleeper on his back last night and, at about 1am, heard him crying. We are sleep training him, so we let him cry himself back to sleep. When I went to get him this morning around 5:30am, he was no longer on the mattress. I lifted up the mattress and found him face down on the floor of the cosleeper.

As I tried to figure out what happened, I noticed that there is ample room on the sides of the cosleeper for an infant to slip down (the mesh walls are really compliant), particularly if the baby is heavier (my son is about 16lbs).

In addition to the fall risk, I am also concerned that the vinyl fabric on the bottom of the cosleeper may not be breathable and could pose a suffocation risk (my son is old enough to lift his head).

My son is totally fine, but this incident really scared me and I want to make sure that these products are safe. Pretty much everyone I know uses a cosleeper of some sort (often from this company) and I was totally unaware that this product had any safety risks until I visited your page. 

FYI, I have also sent a report to the company.
justification: The infant was found face down but unharmed, indicating an incident with no injury.

incident_description: I bought a fisher price sleep and play. After I take my baby out of it.  I notice there is water and moisture under the pad and on the hard plastic.   This is a safety issue, it could cause mold.  I have the  model number:  CHN29      I plan on returning this item.  Why is this happening.

incident_description:
This caller is reporting his 8 month old daughter's exersaucer/bouncer purchased in December 2014 from local retailer.
The caller's 8 month old daughter was sitting in her exersaucer while the caller/father was sitting next to her with his other daughter when the baby began crying.
He jumped up and ran to her and saw that the baby's finger was caught in lace type rope/string holding the cake toy together.

I am stunned that this is for sale and greatly concerned that this could harm a baby if someone purchases it that is not aware of these dangers. Can you please check into this product??
justification: The product has multiple safety hazards like detachable small parts that could pose a choking risk to babies, but no actual injury is reported.

incident_description:
To whom this may concern,

On the morning of Sunday, October 4th, I was feeding my eight month old daughter breakfast in her Safety1st Casablanca High Chair. She was fastened in and the tray was snug and immobile against her stomach. After my daughter was finished eating, I moved the tray foreward one click to gather the remaining puffs that had fallen in the side cracks and down her bib. I was standing less than one foot away from her. My daughter leaned forward to reach for me and the tray abruptly broke off and went crashing to the floor. My baby fell out of the chair restraints and landed on the floor next to the tray. My baby fell head first on our tile floor resulting in a very large contusion on her forehead that was at least half dollar in size. The breath got knocked out of her and she began frantically screaming in pain. We are lucky that she wasn't knocked unconscious. Her right side landed on the defective tray and the rest of her landed on top of my feet. She also bruised on her right arm, right thigh, and stomach region from landing on the tray. We called our pediatrician and she advised us to seek medical treatment in fear of a possible concussion or internal swelling or bleeding of the brain. We went to the emergency room at Baptist Health Hospital and received medical attention from a team of doctors and nurses. She was given an initial physical exam, a well check, and a CT scan. Thankfully, my daughter had no conclusive evidence of a concussion or swelling in the brain after the results of her CT scan. The physician at the hospital advised us to keep a very watchful eye for additional symptoms that are indicative of a concussion for the next 24 hours. My husband took the day off from work on Monday, October 5th to stay home with our baby and monitor her closely. Luckily, no additional symptoms showed up and her large contusion and bruising began to lighten in color. On Tuesday, October 7th, my local news reported the recall of thousands of safety 1st high chairs because of a tray malfunction that was resulting in chipped teeth and various injuries because children were falling out of this type of high chair. This is the exact model of high chair my baby fell out of, and the very reason she was injured. You must sympathize in the terror and fear that my family went through when our baby fell to the floor and the constant reminder of the incident from the nasty contusion she is wearing on her forehead. There is no possible way a 20 pound baby should be able to move or remove a properly manufactured and securely fastened high chair tray. But she did, and the defective tray injured my child and scared my family to death. I hope your company will consider sending us a new properly inspected and functioning high chair and compensating our medical bills and grievances. We have multiple photos of our daughters contusions and swelling that we are willing to share. My family and I are prepared to pursue legal action to make sure that our requests are met and that my child's safety is ensured. I pray that no other family or child has to experience this kind of trauma based on a dysfunctional high chair that we invested $120 in. 

Sincerely,

[REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in injury to the child, including a large contusion and bruising, requiring emergency medical attention, but no death or permanent damage was reported.

incident_description: We installed the Summer Infant Custom Fit Walk-thru Gate between our living room and kitchen to keep our son who is currently 20 months old out of the kitchen while we are cooking.  We installed the gate approximately 4 months ago.  After having the gate in use for about 2 months the welds holding the metal bars on the gate began to break loose.  The only pushing or pulling done on the gate was by a toddler.  The gate should be capable of taking pushing and pulling by a toddler.  After the welds came loose our son was able to remove the hinge from the bottom of the gate, since the metal bar turned into the pin on the hinge at the bottom.  This allowed our son to access the kitchen, thankfully we were able to see what had happened before our son got hurt on either 1.) the sharp metal edges now exposed or 2.) any number of items left in the kitchen which were supposed to be secured by the gate.
justification: The gate failed, allowing toddler access to a hazardous area, but no injury occurred as the parents intervened in time.

incident_description:
This caller is reporting a safety hazard with a clip on night light that holds a 25 watt bulb.  He purchased this product from a home supplies store in Pennsylvania sometime around June/July 2014.
He had no problems with this light until around the end of August 2015 when the light which also doubles as a spotlight and was being used by the caller's 8 year old granddaughter to enable reading and visual assistance when moving around the room.
There is no warning that states a child should not use this lamp.
The child got up to use the bathroom using this lamp clipped to her bed and was gone from the bed for approximately two or three minutes and saw that there was an approximately two inch hole burned in her pillow.
The child had not noticed that the pillow was touching her light.  The caller is reporting this as a fire hazard due to the small amount of time it took for the pillow to begin burning and because there is no warning not to use in a child's room.
There are no injuries being reported.
The caller contacted the manufacturer but was able to speak only with the retailer who then stated that the manufacturer stated that they had no problems with these light bulbs.
The caller is asking that this lamp become inspected, remade with an LED or CFL bulb as well as warnings against using in a child's room.
justification: No injuries were reported, but there was a fire hazard incident involving a child's pillow burning due to contact with the lamp.

One day, she removed the tray and her safety belt and fell face first on the ground. She started crying immediately and I noticed an abrasion to her arm where she hit the table. Later that day I also noticed bruising to the side of her face and leg.

incident_description:
Product: Inglesina Fast High Chair

Incident: 9mo Baby Fell while chair was attached to kitchen counter, resulting in ER visit (She is fortunately fine, despite the very bad fall).  Despite being bucked into the 3-point harness, our baby was able to tuck her feet from under herself and fall to the stone floor below.  I was with my baby but with my back turned momentarily, about 5 feet away.  Despite doing frequent visual checks, she was able to launch herself from the seat very quickly.

Concern: Midleading directions for use.  Inglesina markets its highchair for use from 6mo-37lbs/36 months on all of its upfront marketing materials on its own properties (websites, packaging), as well as on all partner websites.  However, there is a disclaimer that the chair should no longer be used once the child is able to stand (typically babies stand from 7-11 months old, and are within 15-25lbs when they are able to do so).  This disclaimer is not easily accessed, as it is in a product manual with a laundry list of a number of other precautions.  I believe this information should be better highlighted for parents, who commonly mistakenly believe this chair can be used until the 2YO mark.  Further, the manufacturer's product website has an instructional video that explicitly states the recommended usage of this chair is from 6mo-37lbs or 36 months, without the accompanying disclaimer about 'standing children'.  

On Amazon reviews, this does not seem to be a singular incident, as there are reports of other children who have fallen or nearly fallen from this product.  This concern is for this product, but also similar high chairs that do not have a 5-point harness like the [REDACTED] travel hook on high chair.  

I believe that Inglesina's product usage description does not adequately inform the consumer on safe use.  I know many other mothers who have bought or considered this product and have thought it can be used safely up to 2 years.
justification: The incident resulted in an ER visit, indicating an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) due to multiple reports of similar incidents and misleading product information.

He would be screaming in pain and also he cant move at all and when we use baby oil or something of that sort we can barely get him out. When we do get him out there is a deep red ring around his thigh of the impression of him being stuck. And just recently he got his arm stuck but we were able to free him but his shoulder was very tender.

He began to cry incessantly, when I went to see what was the matter I noticed the middle leg buckle stained with blood. Although the seat was buckled properly the edge of the velcro was rubbing his leg. Which caused the cut on the inside of his right thigh.

incident_description: We purchased the natural latex mattress from Ikea for my daughter less than a year ago. My husband and no known allergies to any of the materials that made up the mattress. Over time, just by putting her to bed, he developed allergic reactions to the mattress. The symptoms progressed over time, and he eventually had a serious asthma attack.As soon as we replaced the mattress, the symptoms disappeared. There is published research that indicates that latex allergies can develop over time, affecting 1% of the population. Our concern is that the minimal exposure over time caused a latex allergy, and this could happen to someone else. If a reporting trend occurs, could a label be provided on the mattresses to warn the consumer regarding the possibility? Ikea thought the materials provided on the label was sufficient. We would have never purchased the mattress had we known this was a possibility; these mattresses are being advertised as a safer alternative.
justification: The incident resulted in a serious asthma attack, which qualifies as an injury, and the likelihood is low (1% of the population) based on published research.

incident_description: My 4 month old son was sucking on the Ulubulu "Little Man" pacifier. He opened his mouth and the base became lodged in his mouth sideways causing scraping and bleeding to the roof of his mouth and lower guns where he has 2 teeth coming in. It was difficult to remove because his reaction was to clamp down which caused more pain. He cried and screamed for approximately 20 min after it was removed and had some difficulty with feeding. We will not buy any of these pacifiers or recommend them to others. It was heartbreaking to see our child in pain.
justification: The incident caused injury (scraping and bleeding) to the child's mouth and gums, and resulted in significant distress and feeding difficulties.

incident_description:
My child has been using the Ingenuity 3 in one highchair for a few months. When the tray mechanism is used to release the tray from the seat, it creates a small space underneath- Perfect for little fingers and toes. Today is the second time my daughter has had her foot resting in this space, and the second time her toe got caught. The first time was a minor injury. This time it cut her toe and it is now bruised and swollen.

I could easily see how a child could end up having a broken toe due to this issue
justification: The incident resulted in a cut, bruised, and swollen toe, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The issue has occurred twice, indicating it is likely to happen again (likelihood 4).

incident_description: I was given a high chair from Babies R US for my baby registry back in April. I just put the high chair together and I put my 4 month old in it and her finger got stuck in the clip. In the process I got my finger stuck as well. It has to do when you go to un clip it that it is almost impossible. Her finger didn't break or draw blood but she did scream for a good hour. I told them what happened and they said they could not do anything about it.

incident_description: We just found our 23 month old son trapped by his ankle  between the slats of his crib. The design of the first set of slats are wide at the top then narrow causing an entrapment hazard. We never noticed this before.
justification: The child was trapped by the ankle in the crib slats, indicating a potential injury risk, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: I purchased a Thule Infant Sling for my Chariot stroller http://www.thule.com/en-us/us/products/active-with-kids/multifunctional-child-carriers/accessories/thule-infant-sling-_-20101000.  The sling is an infant hammock style device and has 4 tie in supports and allows an infant with no head control to use a stroller unit designed for older more upright childen.  My sling was less than 2 weeks old on its third use, and the upper support's stitching gave way on one of the support straps causing it to turn my daughter sideways (she was strapped into it and did not fall out, was only badly scared) and her head to flop down.  The stitching had completely ripped out with my three month old using the product (it is marketed for 1-10 months), so guessing much larger and heavier kids than my daughter are using this thing.  Further, my family was over a mile from home on a walk, and because the sling is the only safe way for an infant to use the stroller, we had to hand carry her all the way home, causing her to get over-exposed to the sun, since she could not sit in the shade of the stroller as we had planned.  It seems dangerous that this product is designed to hold the full weight of infants in an active setting and is so poorly designed that the stitching will completely fail on the main components holding the child up.  It could easily result in a serious injury, not to mention since its a product designed for mobility could fail at very inconvenient times for parents who are far from home and have no other method for safely transporting their child.
justification: The incident involved a product failure that caused distress but no physical injury, and the description suggests potential for more severe outcomes in other cases.

incident_description: My son was in the ferrari walker and he has been using it for a couple months and he loves it. He was in his room which is all baby proof and my husband left him for 2 minutes came back and he saw tons of blood. blood all over his walker. it turned out he cut his hand on the walker in-between some edge that is sharp? both little fingers have cuts on each one. Here we go thinking we are putting him in something safe and he wouldn't stop bleeding from it?
justification: The child sustained cuts on both fingers, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
Graco Children's Products
Pack' N Play
Model 1813443
Manufacture date 05/23/2012

6 month old child placed on back in crib for nap mid-afternoon
Child was bare footed (summertime)
Child woke up, rolled on stomach, kicked both feet and rubbed feet on side mesh.
Mesh acted like a "cheese grater" and scrapped skin off both little toes leaving toes bloody and mesh side and crib sheet smeared in blood.

Upon discovery we removed baby, treated injury and cleaned blood off mesh and bottom of Pack' N Play

Reported incident to Graco on 9/11/15
justification: The child suffered bloody injuries to both toes, requiring treatment, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the specific circumstances described.

incident_description: This product is the evenflo Convertible High Chair model name is Marianna these high chairs were recalled in June of 2012, however under a different model number. My five month old [REDACTED] feel out of it yesterday September,3,2015 at approximately 1:30pm after I removed the tray to clean it. She was strapped in. A couple of seconds later she fell out onto the ceramic tiling in the kitchen with the inner black mesh the chair as as the cushion still on her arms. She was rushed to the hospital and has suffered from a contusion on her left eye. My safety concern is why we're recalled in 2012 just to be made again three years later ? It's a disgrace
justification: The incident resulted in a contusion on the child's left eye, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is rated as 4 (likely) due to the recall history and the described incident.

incident_description: My 7 week old son was using a pacifier from the Phillips Avent natural glass bottle gift set when he began hysterically crying. I pulled out the pacifier and his mouth was full of blood. He had a cut in the corner of his mouth. Upon inspecting the pacifier I saw that the silicone nipple was torn at the base and had caught his mouth while he was sucking on it. The other pacifier from the set was also discarded as the same kind of tear was discovered while washing it and seeing the nipple fill with water.
justification: The infant suffered a cut in the mouth from a torn pacifier, indicating an injury.

incident_description: My son nearly choked to death on a MAM Air Pacifier. The button fell off the base of the pacifier and he swallowed it. I knocked it out of him before it was too late.
justification: The child nearly choked to death, indicating a severe incident that could have resulted in death, but was prevented by intervention.

incident_description: My 17 month old has been using a crib for about a year now. He is still of age and size to be doing so. He has been stuck, leg to thigh, in between the railing 4 times now. Each time it is so hard to remove him due to panic and fear. I have looked into crib bumpers but he can stand and push them down. Each time he sustained very serve bruising and mild pain. I at one point attempted to take a hammer to a rail to get him out. I have since learned that applying a large amount of cooking oil to him and the bars can get him out a little easier. I'm at the point that if this happens again I will destroy the crib and purchase a new, different brand, to keep him and others safe. Here is a link to the exact crib we currently are using  http://www.walmart.com/ip/Child-of-Mine-by-Carter-s-Brookline-4-in-1-Fixed-Side-Crib-Chocolate/19414479#ProductDetail
justification: The child has sustained severe bruising and mild pain multiple times, indicating an injury.

incident_description: A baby bath tub had a defective part and should be recalled because it could lead to drowning. My infant son was taking a bath and the "baby stopper" simply detached--if i hadn't been holding his head he would have been underwater in a second.  The product is shown here (http://www.amazon.com/Fisher-Price-Tub-Penguin-Discontinued-Manufacturer/dp/B008DDPLM8), and the description includes the term "baby stopper," which is a yellow piece of plastic that stops nothing.
justification: The defective part could lead to drowning, but no injury occurred as the parent intervened.

incident_description: My 5 month old son's leg got stuck in between the bars of the ikea sundvik crib while he was asleep. He ended up with marks on his leg and foot.
justification: The incident resulted in marks on the child's leg and foot, indicating an injury.

incident_description: Our son, who is 6 pounds under the advertised weight limit of the jolly jumper with stand, was jumping. He was correctly in the harness with only his toes able to touch the floor, as the product directions states.  As he sprang off the floor, the bottom of the clip that connects the harness to the chain on the end of the spring snapped off. Our son fell flat on his face, had a bloody nose and then bad bruising on either side of his nose. While he did not suffer a concussion (or worse!), he was quite hurt and very scared.
justification: The child suffered a bloody nose and bruising, indicating an injury, but no concussion or worse. The incident occurred despite proper use, suggesting it's unlikely but possible.

incident_description:
I wanted to start off by saying that I have used Huggies diapers for my 2 year old son for over 1.5 years and have been pleased with the quality of the diapers up until last night. It was very disturbing and saddening to find maggot-like bugs in the diapers. I have used up almost the entire box before my husband found these bugs. Some were still alive! And I have taken pictures of them as proof as well as bagged one of them up.
After finding these bugs in the diapers, we went online to research. Apparently this has happened before to other families which is absolutely unacceptable! I am not sure what processes they have in place to ensure this wouldnÃÂt happen, but itÃÂs clearly not working. I purchased these boxes from either Target or Walmart. I do not believe that these stores are the issue. I believe the issue stems from the manufacturing plant as other people have had the same issues that lives across the world.
What is more heartbreaking is that my son has complained of his private area hurting/itching for weeks and every time I checked, my thought was to look for a rash. Never in a million years did I think he had maggot-like bugs biting him! 
I need answers.
justification: The incident involves maggot-like bugs in diapers causing discomfort and itching to a child, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
I purchased a BabiesRUs brand pacifier clip for my 10 month old granddaughter. Within 5 minute, I saw her with a small white plastic object in her mouth (approx 1/4 inch). Luckily she did not choke on it, but it IS a choking hazzard. It is part of the plastic snap that pulled out of the fabric connecting the pacifier to the clip. I have kept the packaging. 

I phoned the store (Folsom CA) and advised the assistant manager that was on duty Friday August 21 at 2pm to advise that this product should be removed from the shelf.
justification: The incident involved a choking hazard but no actual injury occurred, and the issue was reported to prevent future occurrences.

incident_description:
The product in question is a MAM brand pacifier clip. The clip is made of clear, hard, brittle plastic. I tried to attach the clip to my daughter's shirt and a piece of the fastener broke off. Had I not noticed it my daughter could have picked it up and swallowed it. The broken shard is somewhat small, jagged, and could cause considerable damage if ingested. I have contacted MAM about this and told them I would also contact CPSC as well. 

I believe that the MAM pacifier clips are unsafe and should be recalled immediately.
justification: The incident involved a broken piece that could have been ingested, posing a potential injury risk, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: I purchased two AFG Athena Nadia 3-in-1 Cribs from Walmart.com July 29, 2014.  My twins were born [REDACTED] and have been sleeping in them since birth.  Once the babies were able to flip over and roll and sleep in all positions, their legs frequently and painfully get stuck between the slats.  Thus far, we have had no serious injuries.  But bruising is a frequent occurrence.  I have an older crib purchased at [REDACTED] in 2007 that my two older children have used and this has never happened in that crib.  Both twins get a leg wedged between the slats at least 3-4 times per week and are unable to free themselves and end up with a good sized bruise on either side of their leg that where it was wedged.  I'm worried my twins or someone else's children will be hurt by this product.
justification: The incident describes frequent bruising from legs getting stuck between crib slats, indicating injury but no serious harm.

incident_description: My 6 month old was in her jumper with her pacifier in her mouth. My phone rang I checked the number and when I looked back at her she had the pacifier out of her mouth holding it and it was broken in half. I still haven't located the missing piece. I am taking her to the er if I cannot find it. I pray that she didn't swallow it.
justification: The pacifier broke but there is no indication of injury, though the missing piece poses a potential risk if swallowed.

incident_description: My son was using a newer Mam pacifier and the top part of the nipple tore off, causing a choking hazard. Luckly he was being watched closely and did not choke.
justification: The pacifier nipple tore off, creating a choking hazard, but no injury occurred due to close supervision.

incident_description: Several metal rods on crib mattress support have come unattached. Crib is Davinci Emily model #4691 serial number #HOO4713
justification: The incident involves a crib mattress support failure, which poses a potential hazard but no injury is reported.

incident_description: MAM pacifier came apart the nipple detached from the rest of the pacifier. it was caught in my child's mouth and blocking his airway. this is the second MAM pacifier we have had fail, we caught the first one before it came completely apart. the pacifier was about 2 weeks old.
justification: The pacifier detached and blocked the child's airway, posing a serious risk, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Yeah our 3 month old daughter was in the bassinet part of her pack n play and the mattress part slid out from underneath her and she slid down in between the 2 bars and it was lucky that the bar didn't go through or even crack her head on the bars. we contacted the evenflow company and they just didn't seem to care that the baby was hurt or anything and refused to give us our money back all the wanted to do was replace the mattress and why would I want the same mattress that she just fell through.
justification: The baby slid between bars but was not injured, indicating an incident without injury.

incident_description:
I purchased this for my grandson ( born [REDACTED]) He has been using this since he was two months old. My daughter, just recently, noticed when she was washing it - that there was black mold around the lining of this item. This was being used by my grandson periodically during the day and he slept in it all night. He started developing a cough and horrible congestion which was diagnosed by the Pediatrician as bronchitis/allergies. He was put on breathing treatments (Nebulizer) three times daily. He has watery eyes constantly and has hives that break out all over his body for no apparent reason. These red spots/hives appear all over his body at different times as we can find no rthym nor reason for them. 
I am appalled that this item is still being sold. My daughter called Fisher Price directly and they only wanted to hear that we would accept a replacement??? Are you kidding me?????? 
This product will affect/effect my grandson in the future as he is now on medications and do not know if this is a permanent illness or not. 
Why is this class action lawsuit only for those who have a problem?????? What about the people who do NOT know about this horrible defect????? 
I am very upset over this and do not know how this is going to play out. My grandsons' health is priceless to me and this product is certainly hindering his health.
justification: The grandson developed bronchitis/allergies, hives, and required medical treatment due to exposure to black mold, indicating an injury.

incident_description: Incident Description: The Safety 1st Decor Wood High Chair - Casablanca tray slides off the high chair when my 16 month old son leans forward or pushes the tray. Today, my son fell head first out of the high chair, luckily I was there to catch him. In addition, the seat belt unlatched as he fell forward.  Before this incident I had been very careful to attach the tray properly. The tray just does not stay attached. I checked the reviews on [REDACTED] and this has happened to other babies. This high chair is a safety concern and a fall hazard. A baby falling from this chair could face serious injury. This high chair needs to be recalled!
justification: The child fell but was caught by the parent, resulting in no injury, and the issue is reported by multiple users.

incident_description: 2 month infant was placed in the swing seat and the seat was placed sideways on the seat holder.  This prevented the seat from being locked into place.  It is presumed the family cat jumped down from a kitchen counter, causing the seat to topple from the holder.  The infant landed face down on the carpet with the seat on top of him, completely covering the infant.
justification: The infant landed face down with the seat on top, which could lead to suffocation or serious injury, indicating a high severity level.

incident_description: I have a blue dream on me bassinet believe it's product code is 440. I went to place my newborn son into bassinet andnit nearly collapsed with him in it. The metal frame will not keep their position to hold any weight including bassinet so it cannot sit in it properly.
justification: The bassinet nearly collapsed with the newborn in it, indicating a significant safety issue but no injury occurred.

incident_description:
Monday, July 13th, 2015 this caller handed her 21 month old son his pacifier which was on a  pacifier clip, however as he put the pacifier in his mouth with the clip still in the caller's hand the beads broke apart and came loose.

The beads on this pacifier clip are approximately 1/8" in diameter (just a bit larger than a blueberry) although she was able to pick all of these beads up before her baby could get to them, she is reporting that if a baby was handed the pacifier with clip and it broke after the child had it in his/her possession it could result in a choking hazard.
The consumer has pictures of this product but has disposed of the pacifier clip in the trash.

There are no injuries being reported

The caller contacted the manufacturer by email Tuesday, July 14th, 2015 but has not received a response yet.
justification: No injuries were reported, but the incident involved a potential choking hazard for a baby, which was prevented by the caller.

incident_description:
I purchased an avent pacifier pack of 2 for ages 0-6 months, my baby was 22 weeks.
The day after I purchased the product my son had managed to get the pacifier stuck in his mouth sideways which left him unable to breathe, luckily I was in the room when this happened and was able to act quickly. My son only used these when he sleeps which is rather worrying for any parent.
justification: The baby was unable to breathe due to the pacifier getting stuck, but no injury occurred as the parent intervened quickly.

incident_description: The bottom of my sons bed fell thru and he somehow got hisbleg stuck on that side when it happened and was screaming. We pulled him out with some minor bruising and he was startled and didn't wanna get into the crib for a while. I sensed up throwing it away after the incident and getting him a new bed. Didn't think to report it because I thought it was just out crib until I saw this recall.
justification: The child suffered minor bruising and was startled, indicating an injury (severity 3). The incident was isolated and resolved without further harm, making recurrence unlikely (likelihood 2).

incident_description: My two year old daughter was standing in her crib when one of the metal brackets that holds the mattress support broke. She was not injured.
justification: The crib bracket broke, which is an incident, but the child was not injured.

incident_description: DaVinci Baby crib, Reagan model. Two metal brackets snapped and broke. No injuries. Aware of the recall and ordered the replacement part. The recall said 10 reports; I thought you might want to make that 11. That company is impossible to contact. When it happened I could not find a number to call. Today I called the number provided and there was no answer.
justification: The incident involved broken metal brackets but no injuries, aligning with severity level 2. The recall and multiple reports suggest the occurrence likelihood is high.

incident_description: 6 month old baby placed a PhillipÃÂs AVENT Soothie Pacifier sideways in mouth and continued to cram the entire pacifier in her mouth. The nipple was facing the back of her throat, cutting off air flow. She was not coughing and her face started turning blue. The baby's grandmother had to stick her finger behind the back of the pacifier, which was in the throat, and pat on her back to get it unlogged from the baby's throat.
justification: The baby's airway was blocked, leading to a life-threatening situation, but no injury or death occurred due to timely intervention.

incident_description: Day 1 of using Pampers Easy Ups and my 2.5 year old started crying and grabbing at his diaper. When I took his diaper off it touched his shin. Within 2 minutes his leg from knee to ankle was red, hot and swollen. His bottom was red and blistered along the edges of where the diaper fits. The next day his leg was edematous with blisters.  It's been a week and it's about 50% better. On antibiotic.
justification: The child experienced significant skin irritation, swelling, and blisters requiring antibiotics, indicating an injury.

incident_description: I received the fisher Infant to toddler rocking chair from Amazon yesterday.  We put it together and were sitting on our back patio. My son was sitting in his new chair and it flipped over face first while he was strapped in. As I ran to him in panic while he was trapped under the seat I was worried about his face on the cement. Thankfully he only had a large goose egg. However he was so shaken up he cried for several hours last night. This item should be recalled. I am a long time fisher price customer and have never had any safety issues. The outcome could have been much worse.  This item appears to be a newer model and does not include a bar to keep it from tipping.
justification: The child suffered a large goose egg and was shaken up, indicating an injury (severity 3). The incident suggests a design flaw that could lead to similar occurrences, making it likely (4).

incident_description: I received my Graco Pack n play from my baby registry.  My husband and I followed the directions putting it together.  Everything is fine aside from the changing area.  Babies will roll to one side.  This is a huge safety concern!  We called Graco to report this, they sent us out new parts and the same problem occurred.  I looked online to see if we were doing something wrong, and found that we are one of many having this same issue.  Even in the directions where it shows how to put this part together, the problem is evident.  the clasps that are supposed to hold the changer up and stable are way too close to the one side that is already holding up the changer.  I'm not sure how this was overlooked, but this is a huge problem and major safety concern.
justification: The description indicates a design flaw causing babies to roll, posing a significant injury risk, and reports suggest this is a common issue.

incident_description: 6 month old sleeping in new Graco crib. Leg (thigh) has gotten stuck 3 times, requiring assistance from parent. On the 3rd incident took both parents to get unstuck, 1 holding baby/leg other pulling slates apart to make larger area for leg to get out of. Leg had a pinch mark with redness.
justification: The incident resulted in a pinch mark with redness, indicating an injury, and has occurred multiple times requiring parental intervention.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that she put on a diaper on her 7 months old son at night. The consumer woke up in the morning when she heard her son move around. The consumer went to look over and saw that the diaper had exploded (came apart from the seam) and all the clear, gel bead content came out everywhere.

The consumer stated that her son put the gel bead content in his mouth. The consumer was concerned about her son choking on the gel beads. She put her finger in his mouth and took out as many beads as possible.The consumer contacted the poison control and they informed her that the gel was made from plant extract and so it was non-toxic. 

The consumer cleaned up her son and put on another diaper from the same package. The consumer stated that the diaper was on for about 2 hours when the same thing happened again. The diaper came apart from the seam and all the gel beads came out. The consumer noticed it quickly and was able to avoid her son putting the beads in his mouth.

The consumer stated that the front seam came apart on both of exploded diapers. 

The consumer stated that her son received an allergic reaction from the gel content. On the day of the incident, the consumer noticed many red dots on his skin where the gel beads touched him. The consumer stated that the reaction progressed over time and by today the dots turned into puss filled blisters. The consumer stated that there are at least 200 blisters over his skin. She has an appointment with a pediatrician today (06/15/15). 

The consumer has the two diapers that came apart along with the other unused diapers from the package. 

The consumer has some additional information regarding the report she made on June 15 2015.  The report number is : 20150615-C6992-140781.  The consumer did take her son to his pediatrician on June 15 2015 @ 1:10pm due to the concerns regarding the gel content of the diaper explosion and the affects on his skin and other issues regarding the diaper explosion. His pediatrician did diagnose him as having an allergic reaction to the gel content, along with a possible ear infection due to gel content in his right ear. The pediatrician prescribed antibiotics for his ear and [REDACTED]  cream for the skin reaction and also suppositories for him for the inability to have a normal bowel movement also due to the swallowing of the diapers gel content. If there isn't improvement with her son by Wednesday June 17 2015 the consumer is to call and get him seen again by his pediatrician. 

The consumer also would like to inform you that she did call the diaper's manufacturer which is P&G to inform them of the incident. The consumer made the call at 8:17am on June 16 2015. They listened to her concern and asked that she hold onto 2 of the unused diapers from the pack in case their quality control department were to want them. They apologized for the incident and hoped her son would feel better soon. They are also going to send the consumer an $8.00 off coupon for my next package of LUVS diapers.  Which she will not be using the consumer has switched to a brand of diapers that does not have any gel content for the safety of her son. If you have any questions please feel free to contact me by e-mail or by phone at [REDACTED]. Thank you so much and have a great day.

[REDACTED]
justification: The infant suffered an allergic reaction and possible ear infection due to the diaper's gel content, requiring medical treatment.

incident_description: This evening when my daughter was using her pacifier, the pink plate part of the "colorful designer clip" came apart from the pacifier. Luckily, I found the clip on the floor next to her because god knows what could have happened. My baby could have easily have put that in her mouth and choked! I was in utter shock and disbelief that this piece came apart from her pacifier. I am still in shock as I'm writing you this email because I can only imagine what could have happened to my little girl! My life could have been over in a mere second because Munchkin LATCH made such a faulty product that parents like myself purchased and trusted to give to our child. I have no idea how Munchkin LATCH can even make it up to me for what happened! In no way do I even want a replacement. I am about to tell anyone and everyone that I know not to buy your product and to discontinue using it if they have it. I would never want anyone's baby to choke on this product! I suggest Munchkin LATCH discontinue selling this product and send out a recall! As of right now, I am fear to leave my daughter with any toys or pacifiers.  I am a nervous wreck and Munchkin LATCH company is to blame!
justification: The pacifier part came apart but was found before any harm occurred, indicating no injury but a potential choking hazard.

incident_description:
I bought the huggies little movers diapers for the
the first time and after using half a pack about 35, I notice bruising on my baby's waist where the front blue grip strip stays on the baby. One side of her waist at a time got bruised. I took pictures and stopped us in the diapers.
justification: The description reports bruising on the baby's waist from the diaper's grip strip, indicating an injury, but no mention of recurrence or widespread incidents.

incident_description: While using an evenflo doorway jumper at a little over four months old my daughters arm became entangled in the leg hole. This forced her neck directly onto the shoulder support bar and she began to choke. She did not have the coordination to get unstuck. After the incident I double checked the manual's requirements for use and she fit all of them. I immediately took the product back to the store and contacted the company. Apart from an automatic customer response email they never got back with me. The requirements for this device need to be updated for an older infant.
justification: The incident involved choking, which is a serious injury risk, but the child survived.

incident_description: My son keeps getting his fingers stuck in the high chair tray latch/releases. There is a large button on either side of the under side of the high chair tray that when pressed release the tray. But they happen to be right within a baby's reach. While my son is eating, he hooks his fingers over the edge of the tray sometimes and gets his fingers stuck between the buttons and the housing around the buttons. He's not able to actually press the buttons, just keeps getting his fingers stuck! He screams every time it happens mostly because he can't get his finger tips out by himself.  It takes an adult to gingerly pry his fingers out.
justification: The incident causes distress and requires adult intervention to free the child's fingers, indicating a minor injury (pain and potential bruising).

incident_description:
The infant swing has straps that are "secured" in the back of the seat with blue plastic discs. The discs will slide through the opening. It is designed that way so the straps are adjustable to a larger child, but it is also dangerous. The discs can work themselves loose when there isn't steady pressure on them and the baby can literally fall out of the swing.  Also, the discs can fall off and the strap will remain through the back opening until there is some pressure from baby leaning forward, then it pulls through the hole.  We lost one of the discs the first day of use. 

I bought the swing on Amazon. One of the other customer reviews said that the front plastic piece broke and the baby fell out. http://www.amazon.com/Little-Tikes-Snug-Secure-Swing-Pink/dp/B001P5GRF6/ref=cm_cr_pr_product_top?ie=UTF8

The latches that secure the front piece to hold the baby in are very hard to latch properly. If they aren't pushed all of the way in, they pop out. They are so cheaply made that only one of our latches worked properly. The other popped out when baby was in the swing.
justification: The incident describes a design flaw that can lead to the baby falling out of the swing, with reports of actual incidents and potential for injury.

incident_description:
Dear Sir or Madam: 

I purchased a Munchkin auto close metal gate at Toys R Us in South Philadelphia, PA in or around December, 2014 and it appears to be defective. 

The spring mechanism popped out of the gate while my infant was a few feet away from the gate. The spring is located in the bottom left of the gate, where the gate swivels to open and close (photos attached). A one inch screw and spacer also popped out of the gate, presumable from the upper swivel arm of the metal gate. 

It was quite unusual to say the least to be drinking a cup of coffee while watching a baby gate implode. If my infant ate this spring mechanism, he would have asphyxiated or worse. 

FYI: I do have photos that I can email if your would like to review them. 

Thank you.

 [REDACTED]
justification: The gate malfunctioned but no injury occurred, though there was potential for severe harm.

incident_description:
Caller stated that her 13 month old grand child left leg between his thigh and knee got entrapped between the crib slat.  Caller stated that she was unable to remove his leg, she had to call 911 for them to come out to rescue the child.  One of the police was able to pull back the slat and release the child's leg.  She administered ice to the swollen area.  The child did not receive medical attention.  Caller stated the bottom slats had become loose earlier that month causing the child to crawl out of it.

Caller stated that she tried to contact Lajobi but her call would not go through.

Caller feels that the crib is a safety hazard and should be reported.
justification: The child's leg was entrapped and swollen, requiring intervention but no medical attention, indicating an injury without long-term consequences.

incident_description: My 6 month old daughter pulled the Fisher Price 3-in-1 Projector Soother off of the side of her crib, and it fell on her head!  She had a red spot on her eyebrow and cried.
justification: The incident resulted in a visible injury (red spot) and caused the child to cry, indicating physical harm.

incident_description: I recently purchased a crib and mattress bundle for my seven month old son. The mattress included in the bundle was the kolcraft 800 pediatric mattress. First, the mattress is too small for cribs, leaving approximately 3 inches at the foot and side. Second, it is extremely soft. I have only put my son on this mattress a few times, and every time he has sat up the mattress has given no support, causing him to smash his head into the crib panels. His feet have also gotten caught in between the mattress and the crib while he's squirming.
justification: The description reports the child smashing his head into the crib panels and getting his feet caught, indicating physical injury.

incident_description: My daughter is 15 months old and she keeps getting her legs stuck in the rails in her crib and most of the time she is asleep when it happens this has happened 7 times now and thankfully she hasn't been injured and I have tried to contact the manufacturer and they say there is nothing they can do because it's regulations and I can buy an after market crib but I can't afford to buy another crib I just don't want to see my daughter have a broken leg in result of her getting her leg stuck in a crib that is suppose to be safe
justification: The description indicates repeated incidents of legs getting stuck without injury, but with high frequency (7 times).

incident_description:
No incident.
I am a pediatrician with research and prevention programming experience in the safe sleep field (fatality reviews, statewide education programs in NY) and someone sent me a link to this product - Lifenest infant mattress topper - intended for infant sleep.  It is unsafe - intended for sleep - curved, soft - essentially a pillow in a crib.  Must look into this product. Marketed to prevent plagiocephaly and as a "medical device"
http://www.ubimed.com/lifenest-help-prevent-flat-head.html
justification: The description states 'No incident' and focuses on a product safety concern without any reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description: This product only has a waist harness. It NEEDS a 5-point harness. This is great for a docile baby, but my baby at 9-months was able to wiggle out (very quickly) and stand up!!! I tried making the straps super tighter, but he just forces himself up and out. It is scary because he could have easily fell. We had it attached to our kitchen island counter/table.
justification: The baby was able to wiggle out of the harness, posing a fall risk, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: bulb burned out and melted the inside of the light
justification: The bulb burning out and melting the inside of the light is an incident with no injury reported.

incident_description:
Caller stated that the springs on the crib (mattress support) broke loose and her 16 month old child fell through partially to the floor, she was not hurt but could have been.

(6/2/15) Caller stated she contacted the company and they responded as if they were not concern, she feels that this crib is unsafe and should be reported.
justification: The child was not injured but could have been, indicating a potential hazard.

incident_description: We purchased a Delta Children's Brookside 4 in 1 crib from walmart in January 2015. Today makes at least 5 times my daughter has gotten her kneecap lodged between the slats on this crib. I have seen several reports claiming the same exact problem has occurred with their children. She screams at the top of her lungs and we have to push the slats inward to dislodge my child's kneecap. If she has knee problems when she gets older, I will hold your company FULLY responsible!
justification: The incident involves repeated occurrences of a child's kneecap getting lodged between crib slats, causing distress but no reported injury.

incident_description: I bought three Dream On Me Zodiac portable cribs two 5/18/14 and one 10/8/14 through Amazon.  I have been noticing that the foam in the mattress is not attached to the mattress and has over time bunched and made lumps in the mattresses.  If the foam is not lying flat against the board in the mattress but is bunched a baby could suffocate.  This is a very dangerous product.

In addition, we had to drive over 2 hours each way to this Ikea, which is the nearest one to us, & then wait over an hour to be helped. We found this an extraordinary demand considering that it was their mistake which caused this safety concern. Thank you for your consideration of this matter.

incident_description:
I bought my son a newborn rock n play sleeper and I noticed that he began to wheeze and he started to smell funny as I got to looking I noticed it had began growing mold underneath the sleeping [REDACTED] where it meets the plastic back. I bleached it thinking maybe something got on it. After about 2 days later it began growing mold again. My son has gotten a slight respiratory problem but nothing a little medicine can't fix. Upon inspection of the crib, the bottom screws on each side holding the entire back of the crib had come completely out. When he rolled over in the crib, the back of the crib opened like a trap door causing him to fall to the ground. We are thankful that he was not injured but we are aware of how much worse it could have gone.
justification: The child fell but was not injured, indicating a severity level of 2. The incident suggests a possible design or maintenance issue with the crib.

It is unclear whether he swallowed any; however, this is a serious potential choking hazard.  He is five months old, does not have any teeth, and was using the toy appropriately.
justification: The pacifier seam failed, exposing plastic beads, but there was no confirmed ingestion or injury.

On top of its head it had to round antenna/nubs.  While chewing, one of the nubs broke off into her mouth.  I happened to be sitting right next to her when it happened, and got it away from her. incident_description: I have always used pampers swaddlers on my son. He is now 2 years old and we are starting to have problems with the diapers. He had blisters all over his private area  and it was bright red. This is the second time this has happened in the past 2 months.
justification: The child suffered blisters and redness, indicating an injury, and this has happened twice in two months, suggesting a likely recurrence.

incident_description: When removing the cover to my Rock 'N Play Sleeper for washing, I discovered that there was mold growing underneath on the straps and the fabric that covers the hard plastic.  This fabric and the straps are not removable.  I always spot clean the cover, wipe off any spit up, and wash regularly.  I am disgusted to learn that my baby has been sleeping on top of mold.  Upon researching the internet, I have discovered that this is a common problem with this item.
justification: Mold exposure can pose health risks, especially to infants, but no injury was reported in this incident.

incident_description: We have a Fisher Price Rock'n'Play, apparently  mold can develop between the removable seat cushion and the hard plastic frame of the sleeper.  We received this sleeper as a gift at our baby shower, and our son has slept in in almost daily since we brought him home.  Recently (with in the last month or so) he has been very ill including a hospitalization and several doctors visits.  Including may expenses to us based on his daily exposure to mold.
justification: The child was hospitalized and had several doctor visits due to exposure to mold, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
While travelling in the US (I live in Canada) we had to stop and buy pacifiers for my baby. We bought 4 pacifiers from 2 locations (in 2 separate states). All of the pacifiers we bought were the NUK brand. They are all labeled as new & improved. Even though we followed the sterilization process correctly (this is our second child and we have had to sterilize many pacifiers over the years) every single one of the pacifiers developed tears in the rubber and disconnected posing a serious choking hazard. We were VERY lucky that my wife heard my son coughing in the early hours of the morning and found that the ripped pacifier was becoming lodged in his throat. If my wife hadn't woken up, or my son had sucked the entire rubber piece back before coughing I seriously feel he would have died that night. 

We of course threw away all of the pacifiers after this incident and bought new ones in Canada. We once again bought the NUK brand as this is the brand we have always bought and we felt it may be something isolated to the US. Within 1 week, we noticed that the pacifiers were tearing in the same spot, and you can notice a white line towards the bottom of the rubber piece that looks like it is either very weak at this point, or it is no longer manufactured as one piece and very susceptible to tearing. 

My wife and I both feel that we are extremely lucky, and if there is not an investigation and recall into this product it WILL result in a child's death. It is terrifying that they advertise this as "New & Improved" when it is clearly an inferior product that poses a series health risk to babies.
justification: The incident describes a serious choking hazard that could have resulted in death, but no actual injury occurred due to timely intervention.

incident_description: Rock N Play Sleeper bought September 2011 has mold on the piece that is unable to be removed.
justification: Mold presence indicates an incident but no injury is reported.

incident_description:
On May 22, 2015, I removed the cover from my daughter's Rock N Play Sleeper to wash as I had many times in the past.  I originally purchased this Sleeper from Amazon sometime in January 2012 (for my firstborn daughter).  I had heard about the recall due to mold when it came out in 2013, but I always kept an eye on the sleeper to make sure ours didn't develop any mold. incident_description: The high chair tray slides off the high chair when my son leans forward. The first time this happened, my 9 month old son fell head first on to the tile floor in my home. I thought this was a fluke and that  maybe it was user error, or that the tray was not attached properly. The tray came off again yesterday while my son was eating, this time the safety straps held him from falling, but he was quite scared hanging there upside down for the few seconds it took me to get him up. Before this incident I had been very careful to attach the tray properly. The tray just does not stay attached. incident_description: I am writing you to request status of the Fisher Price Ocean Wonders Cradle 'N' Swing (model number 79667). I am actively trying to prevent a similar injury from occurring to another new born baby.
justification: The description reports an injury to a 3-month-old, indicating a severity level of 3. The mention of the swing circulating in the used market suggests a possible recurrence.

incident_description: I put pampers baby dry size 5 on my son Thursday night. The next evening, Friday night, I noticed a terrible rash with welts and blisters on the back of his leg on his upper thigh. This is not a normal diaper rash area at all. After doing research on the diapers I realized the diapers were causing the rash and we switched to sensitive diapers.

incident_description:
This caller is reporting that she grabbed a disposable diaper from her 18 month old son's diaper organizer to change him April 6th, 2015 but when she laid it down she noticed that it had a pinkish brown stain that appeared to be in the shape of a mouse.

She had purchased the diapers April 2nd and had used a couple of the diapers from the box in the previous days but this was the first one she used from his room.

Tuesday, April 7th, 2015 the caller picked her little boy up from his nap after noting that he had slept longer than usual.

She saw that he was running a fever of 101.7 so she wrapped him up and took him to the emergency room because he had been chewing on his baby monitor the night before and she was afraid that he had swallowed a piece of metal.

The metal was ruled out and the diagnoses from Kapiolani Women and Children's Hospital Emergency room was that the child may have picked up a virus.

She had contacted the diaper company on April 6th, 2015 and described the pinkish brown stain then she received the explanation that  the shape & color on the diaper could be adhesive.

The representative [REDACTED] asked her to send the diaper to them but the caller has elected to hold onto it.
justification: The child developed a fever and required emergency room evaluation, indicating an injury, but the cause was likely a virus unrelated to the diaper stain.

incident_description: We purchased a Fisher Price Rock N Play sleeper around November 15, 2014 for our daughter that was due in Jan 2015. On May 12th 2015 I took the cover off to wash it as I do once a week. In doing so I noticed that the material was moist and that there was a black spot in the seem. I turned the material over and noticed multiple spots of discoloration as well as more black in the seem where it is stitched. I have washed the material with stain remover, baking soda, and vinegar multiple times and I am unable to get the black mold out of the material. Our daughter will be four months old on the 22nd of this month. She is still currently sleeping in this product, but I am not using this material until I receive a replacement from the manufacturer.
justification: The incident involves the discovery of mold in a baby sleeper, but no injury or harm has been reported.

incident_description: Got the rock and play sleeper as a baby shower gift.  My daughter had a accident that my husband didnt tell me about a couple days later i took it apart to wash and it was covered in mold. It sucks because its the only thing my daughter sleeps in.
justification: The incident involved a moldy baby sleeper, which poses a health risk but no immediate injury was reported.

incident_description:
Caller is reporting disposable diapers she purchased around March 10th or 11th, 2015.

She had used about 20 or 30 of them but then the evening of March 24th, 2015 when she was diapering her 6 month old daughter for bedtime she noticed a piece of metal that was coated with whatever the diaper is coated with to make it absorbant.
The metal is close to the leg of the diaper, wraps to the area by the posterior  and is four inches long, approximately the circumference that a paper clip would be but more flexible than a paper clip 
She removed the diaper from under her daughter and put it away instead of putting it on her
She has been checking the other diapers from the box and has found no additional abnormalities as of this date.

There are no injuries being reported.
The caller contacted the manufacturer March 25th, 2015 at 9:00AM and received an apology then an offer of coupons.
She does not believe that there was any sincere concern about the potential presence of a safety hazard.
justification: No injuries were reported, but a hazardous object was found in a diaper, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description:
I was giving my 2 month old baby a bath in the "Safety 1st - Space Saver Fold-Up Infant Tub" and his foot got stuck under the folding part of the bathtub. It was fully extended and clicked open. I was with him the entire time and he screamed out in pain. His little toe got stuck and it was cut open. I have broken it apart and disposed of it so it cannot be used again by anyone else.

There is no safe way to use this tub. Please help take it off the market or have the manufacture change the product.

Thank you. You provide a great service.
justification: The baby's toe was cut open, indicating an injury, which corresponds to severity level 3. The incident suggests a design flaw that could lead to similar injuries, making occurrence likely.

incident_description:
6 month old baby was able to stick his thumb through one of the two small holes on the Munchkin Latch Infant Orthodontic (3 months+)  pacifier (http://www.amazon.com/Munchkin-Lightweight-Infant-Orthodontic-Pacifier/dp/B00LCYTKOU/ref=sr_1_2?s=baby-products&ie=UTF8&qid=1430359323&sr=1-2&keywords=munchkin+latch+pacifier).  

The seal was tight enough that it cut off circulation to his thumb.  Thankfully he became fussy and I noticed the problem and was able to pull his thumb out of the hole and restore circulation.  This is a significant risk--especially since many babies sleep with pacifiers.  If he had fallen asleep after sticking his thumb into the hole this would have caused a severe issue.
justification: The baby's thumb was injured due to restricted circulation, but no long-term harm occurred.

Last weekend my husband removed the cover to the Rock and Play and found black mold under the cover. I'm concerned that the mold has been causing my sons respiratory problems. He was even sleeping in the Rock and Play at night because he was having trouble breathing and being more upright was suggested by the pediatrician.

incident_description: My less than 20 pound toddler was using her Minnie Mouse First Years Potty. She leaned backwards causing the lid to pop off. This resulted in her head hitting our tile floor. Thankfully she is okay. I contacted First Years where a representative was very unconserned. She would only comment that the lid was intended to pop off to prevent cracking and breaking producing sharp edges and that it was not intended to be leaned on. I do understand this, but I also feel like it should be stressed in the warnings that the unit be placed against a wall when in use. From her response it is obvious that the are aware that the lids easily pop off, that is the intention, she said this clearly.  Her solution was to not let my child lean back on the lid. Her solution did not make this unsafe potty safe in my opinion. There are pictures all over the Internet showing a little girl on the potty placed in the middle of the bathroom floor and the manufacturer even uses the term that it is a STURDY FREESTANDING POTTY.
justification: The toddler was not injured, but the incident involved a fall due to the potty's design, which the manufacturer acknowledges.

incident_description: My 18 month old daughter's fingers got stuck between the bottom bar and the "door" of the Munchkin Easy close Metal gate.

incident_description: The ingenuity 2 in 1 baby seat is very unsafe. It shows in the picture, a baby in the seat on the floor with the tray attached. We did this with my 6 month old daughter. She leaned forward and the whole seat tipped over. This is very unsafe baby product. I am very unhappy and would never recommend this seat to any parent due to it being dangerous.
justification: The incident describes the baby seat tipping over when the baby leaned forward, indicating a safety hazard but no reported injury.

incident_description:
The consumer's 2-1/2 year old (approx. 30 lbs., 32" tall)  daughter was sitting on the potty seat, when she pinched a finger on one of her hands.  The skin became discolored.

The daughter used the potty previously in the flat position.  The potty can be placed on top or a toilet seat or used by itself.  The incident occurred when the seat was being used by itself, on a flat surface on the floor.  

There are 2 (5" high) legs attached to the seat.  The legs have 3 positions (1 sitting on top of a toilet seat); the legs can be placed 90 degrees to the seat and it becomes a free standing toilet seat.  However, in the 90 degree position, the slightest amount of pressure applied to the product can cause it to collapse.  Then a child's fingers could be caught between the seat and the legs of the potty.

(4/8/2015)  The consumers called the brand name company and informed them about the problem.  They spoke with [REDACTED].  [REDACTED] said that the product had been tested and met all U.S. and European regulations.  [REDACTED} did not offer comment about the issue.  The consumers offered to send a video and [REDACTED] accepted that offer.  The consumer sent [REDACTED] a video of the incident. 

The product came fully assembled.  The product is for ages 16 and up and has a maximum weight limit of 96 lbs.

The consumer added the age limit is not accurate for toddlers.
justification: The child's finger was pinched, causing discoloration, which constitutes an injury.

incident_description: I placed my son in one of the Safety First highchairs model HC144BZF a few weeks ago, secured him inside and slid the tray back and turned to get his food. When I turned around the tray was almost completely pushed out. My son almost fell, head first, onto the floor. The chairs have a defect in the design of the tray locking mechanism. The side handles when pulled out repeatedly, wear out the hinge and prevent it from locking tightly in place. The plastic teeth on the tray that fit into the side slots are also not long enough, so when the handles don't secure down tightly, the teeth don't fit into the slots far enough so the tray can easily be pushed out of place. This is obviously a safety concern on my part and we no longer use the highchair because I am afraid that my babies may fall out of them due to this defect. Replacing the tray will not remedy the defect in the design of the tray. I am extremely disappointed that Safety First only offered to replace the tray for 25$ plus shipping. They did not seem concerned about the potential hazard the highchair poses to other unsuspecting children.
justification: The incident involved a near-fall due to a design defect, but no actual injury occurred.

Then, on March 15th, my 16 month old baby pushed the door of the gate (while it was closed and locked in place), it then flung open and my baby triple summersaulted down the stairs with serious momentum. Luckily he only sustained 2 rug burns on his face but this obviously could have been much worse and I want to prevent this from happening to any other baby!

I have never had a problem in the past with Nuk or there pacifier(4th kids), very dangerous. Company should issue a recall. Thank god my child wasnt hurt, but there are thousands of babies that are in danger right now.

incident_description: Rock and play for infants. My 3 month old sleeps in this and loves it. I went to clean it and discovered under the cushion mold. She has been sick for the past 11 days with a respiratory illness and nonstop coughing. Then I saw the recall for this product online and am very upset to know that this could be causing my daughter to be so sick.

incident_description: The infantino gaga gym is for babies newborn and up to play with the hanging toys. My son who was not completely at a sitting position, pulled one of the poles and it snapped, leaving a foam and wired exposed. He could have easily poked his eye if I was not paying attention and removed the toy immediately. I have a picture of the product and tried to contact "infantino," only to be blamed and patronized for not reading the instructions. There is not warning on the mat or anywhere visible.  I mentioned that the warning could be easily placed on the mat or pole, but the customer representative told me there was not space, and I had to read the box. I was treated poorly and I only wanted to bring the matter to their attention. I was offered a replacement at first, but when I confronted the rep with her lack of help and sensitivity to the issue, she withdrew the offer and said she will tell her manager. I know many moms who are buying this product, and I definitely not recommending it. I am also making sure by doing this that parents or whoever buys the product are aware of the possible harm that it could cause to their babies.

incident_description: I bought a Ferrari F1 baby walker from Buybuy Baby, NJ for my 6 months old. He used it couple months, and right around Thanksgiving he was using it in the house and the plastic underneath the wheels where the sizing occurs, collapsed while my son in it and the car deflated. There were no injuries, thank God. I contacted Team Tex America for a refund but got no response.
