incident_description:
I ordered the item "My Chewy Holder Sensory Tool" for my 3 year old child.  It is a flexible tube designed to be worn around the neck of the child to hold a sensory teething/chewing toy so that it does not get dropped/lost.  It is equipped with a "break away" clasp for safety.  
 
Upon receiving the item I attempted to pull apart the clasp and discovered that it took an astonishing amount of force to do so.  I closed it and pulled it apart several times and each time it was extremely difficult to get it to separate.  So I undertook some experiments.  I has able to support the weight of two full gallons of milk for 10 seconds with the closed tube before it broke away.  

I have worked as a paramedic for over 10 years and am very well acquainted with neck and airway anatomy of children.  I feel confident that this product poses a significant strangulation hazard to young children and should not be marketed for that age group.
justification: The product's clasp requires excessive force to release, posing a significant strangulation hazard to young children, which could lead to death.

incident_description: I was giving my 3 year old daughter and 7 month old son a bath tonight.  My son was using the Idea Baby Bath Seat that was actually purchased for my daughter 2 1/2 years ago, but we never used it that much then.  This is the 3rd time we have bathed my son in the seat, but I have noticed each time how unstable it is.  This evening I turned around to grab my son's towel to get him out of the tub and apparently he leaned over to grab a bath toy out of my daughters hand and the seat tipped over, completely submerging my 7 month old son in the bath water.  I of course heard the splash and turned back around to find him face up under the water, which scared me half to death.  He was probably under the water only seconds, but it felt like an eternity.  I of course quickly grabbed him out of the bath and he started gasping for air and coughing.  So, thank God I was there and this traumatic situation did not turn into a tragic situation, but I was happy to find out that this product was recalled.  However, through my research I did not find any reports online where something like this happened and so I wanted to share my story to stress how unsafe this product truly is.
justification: The child was submerged in water but was quickly rescued without lasting injury, indicating an incident with no injury.

incident_description: I have a daughter, [REDACTED] who just turned 1 years old. We received several bags of pampers swaddlers for her birthday. About 4 days ago, I first used these diapers on my daughter. We previously used [REDACTED] for her first year. We'll after the first day I noticed a rash down on her inner butt cheeks and labia. The next day it progressed. By the 4th day, she had about 15 blisters which had opened up, we're bleeding. She was in a lot of pain. I immediately took her to see her pediatrician which is [REDACTED] in melbourne, Florida. Phone number [REDACTED]. My daughter has had minor diaper rash before but it never turned into all these open blisters. Looks like she was burned several times. After day 4, I refused to put her in the pampers swaddlers with the dry max, and only use the [REDACTED] and her blisters have almost healed. I googled, pampers swaddlers rash and there were hundreds of parents giving testimony about how they're babies too have had these chemical burns from the baby dry inside these diapers. They are not safe for use!!! And should be pulled off shelves immediately. I've read that when the baby dry is combined with urine and heat it can cause the chemical used to make these diapers burn the skin. THAT IS SCARY!!!!

incident_description: On two-three different occasions, both of my twin boys have gotten their legs stuck in between the wooden bars of their cribs, the "jourdan" model from restoration hardware. The incident that that prompted this report, however, was the only one that resulted in noticable injuries afterward, causing one of my sons significant bruising and swelling as a result. Along with the pain during the time his leg was stuck, the removing the leg was obviously very painful. I had to maneuver his leg with some force to remove it. With the bed posts having square, wooden edges, when the legs do get stuck it makes it a lot more painful to remove the leg once it is wedged in there, resulting in further injury. On this particular isolated incident, my son was unquestionably in pain and had physical injuries, he was clearly in pain while it was stuck and also when I was trying to remove it as quickly and painlessly as possible, and he was quite noticeably injured afterwards (bruising around leg/ankle-pictures attached). Yes my son moves around a lot in his sleep and we do not use bumpers because we follow the safe sleep guidelines, but the injury that resulted from the leg being wedged between the bars was made much worse by the painful removing of the leg (that had already started to swell) from between the spindles, mostly because of its wooden, squared-off edges, and the significant maneuvering required by me, and my son was in noticeable pain before I even tried to start getting it out. He was shrieking in fear and pain (and he is typically a VERY tough kid, he's the type who only cries when something REALLY hurts badly). He was/is too young to clearly tell me about his pain but it was very obvious, not only from the bruises and swelling that developed shortly after, but his actions as well. He limped on the foot for about an hour that morning before he really felt comfortable walking on it. I took photos of his injuries the following day and still have those saved. I am happy to share them. This resulted in only a minor injury for my child, however had my son not alerted me as soon as he did or if for some reason I wasn't able to get to him, or god forbid he was younger and was stuck on his stomach and couldn't turn his head to clear an airway, I could see where this situation could have been a lot worse. Please excuse any repetition of details I wanted to include as much information as possible.
justification: The incident resulted in significant bruising and swelling, indicating an injury (severity 3). The description mentions this has happened multiple times, making occurrence likely (4).

incident_description: We purchased the Bonavita The Belmont Collection baby furniture in [REDACTED]. Our son is 14.5 months old and has used his crib for the last 8.5 months. On Tuesday, Jan 13, 2015 I put my son down for a nap in the safest place I thought. In a matter of 5 minutes from laying him down, I heard earth shattering screams from him. I raced to his room and discovered that my child had his entire leg stuck in between the rails on the backside of the crib. He was inconsolable and holding his breath. He tried to free his leg himself and by doing this panicked himself into a hysterical crying. I as a parent tried to free his leg, when the several attempts failed when it reached his knee cap. My only other option was to frantically call 911 and receive medical attention. the state troopers and EMTs arrived at my house and were able to free my scared and hurt 14.5 month old child. My child suffered from a knee cap severely bruised and the trauma of knowing that his crib is not the safest place for him. I am appalled that my baby was able to get his leg through the spaces between each rail, when it is clearly stated on the paper work that this crib is CPSC, ASTM & JPMA tested. Clearly that is not the case and the standards need to re looked at and reevaluated. My child should have NEVER been able to get his leg stuck. My husband had to zip tie plastic containers lids to the outside of his crib to protect him from getting his leg or arm stuck again. with the amount of money we played for this crib we should have had better results and higher safety standards for our son.
justification: The child suffered a severely bruised knee cap and emotional trauma, indicating an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is unlikely (2) as such incidents are not common with properly tested cribs.

incident_description: My son recently became big enough to use his Baby Einstein Neptune activity saucer. The very first time he used it the whale flipped around and got him right in the face. Why is the whale so close to them if it's going to flip around like that? My 6 month old doesn't know enough to lean away from a moving object. Poor design!! ):
justification: The whale flipping and hitting the baby in the face indicates an injury occurred, hence severity level 3.

incident_description: We are using an IKEA Sundvik crib-toddler bed for our son. Some months ago, I noticed that the bottom part of the crib is sagging in the middle. The base is only attached to the crib frame at the four corners with no support so ever at the middle of the crib. As my boy is getting older and heavier the base is bowing down more. I am afraid for his safety. The crib could break, allowing trapping him between the rail and the base.
justification: The crib's structural issue poses a risk of trapping the child, which could lead to injury if the base breaks.

incident_description: I have a fisher price rock n' play sleeper for my daughter and I seen a recall for them for having mold so I checked the plastic under the cover and there is mold on the plastic and the cover. My daughter has been using this product since she came home from the hospital and is now 2 months old. She has been sick the last 3 or 4 weeks and I've been wondering why it come and goes but won't stay away and now I realize it must be from the exposure to the mold. This is very upsetting to me. These product we buy for our children are supposed to be fun and good for them but instead hurt them or make them sick! Somethings needs to be done about this!
justification: The child has been sick for weeks due to mold exposure from the recalled product, indicating an injury.

incident_description: I found dark colored mold spots underneath the removable fabric
justification: Mold presence indicates an incident with potential health risks, but no immediate injury is reported.

incident_description:
I have the Emily 4-in-1 Convertible Crib with Toddler Rail. My son has been using it for a little under a year. He is 18 months but didn't start using this crib until he was about 7 months old.
 Last night at 2AM I heard a very loud bang come from his room followed by him screaming. I rushed in to find the front right corner of his mattress on the floor. Once I checked to make sure he wasn't hurt I lifted the mattress to find that the metal bracket that connects the mattress spring frame to the crib had snapped at the point where it is riveted to the metal spring frame. The piece that broke off was extremely sharp as well.My son could have been SERIOUSLY injured! Thankfully he wasn't! This should not have happen and I need answers. I am not sure who to contact and came across this site while searching for answers this afternoon.
justification: The crib's metal bracket snapped, creating a sharp hazard, but no injury occurred.

incident_description: SOOTHIE pacifier used when my 7 month old son sleeps.   The pacifier became stuck on his thumb while sleeping.   When getting picked up after his nap his thumb was found stuck on the opening located on the back of the soothie/ pacifier cutting off circulation.   His thumb was cold and discolored purple /grey.   Took 30 minutes after removing the pacifier  to improve.   Very dangerous to use with babies unsupervised.
justification: The incident caused injury to the baby's thumb, with discoloration and reduced circulation, but no long-term harm was reported.

incident_description:
To whom it may concern,
We received the Munchkin Teether Babies Lion (Item #70001) as a gift for our second child. He is now 10 months
old and was playing with this toy on a hardwood floor. While playing with it I saw him swinging it with his hand and
it hit the ground. I then heard something rolling across the floor. A closer look at the toy showed that the small
globe ball at the end of the ring had broke off from the impact our 10 month old caused with the toy hitting the
floor. I have attached pictures of the toy to the e-mall,
Our obvious concerns are the small size of the globe ball not attached to the toy anymore and the sharp plastic
edges on the ring and ball.
justification: The incident involved a toy breaking, creating a potential choking hazard and sharp edges, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Eleven year old [REDACTED] a handicapped boy died by his neck being stuck in the bed frame between the drop side rail and the foot board. This bed is on a recall list release #10-272. I am the Chief Deputy Coroner, [REDACTED] on the case, my cell is [REDACTED]. The Johnson County Sheriff Dept is investigating as well case# [REDACTED]. Their phone is [REDACTED][REDACTED] is investigating.
justification: The incident resulted in the death of a child, which is the highest severity level.

incident_description:
Bright Start monkey and rings musical teether toy, battery operated.

I am a grandparent of a ten month old baby and while the child was in my care at her home, I noticed her playing happily while leaning on an activity toy.  I immediately noticed an object in her mouth, went over to her, and pulled the object out of her mouth.  It was the battery cover with the one screw still intact, for three small, watch type batteries that make the toy have a musical sound when shaken.  The screwed on the cover had come loose, spilling the batteries across the room.  My granddaughter was not injured, but thinking of the what could have happened would have been potentially very dangerous.

I was in a state of shock this toy is available to small infants and if I had not been so quick to watch her or had turned my back for an instant, she could have swallowed and choked on the cover, as well as the small batteries that had spilled on the floor.

I cannot believe that a toy is on sold with these hazards, and as parents and caregivers we expect the toys we provide for our children are safe and free of dangers.

Thank you,
[REDACTED]
justification: The child was not injured, but the incident involved a potential choking hazard from the toy's battery cover and spilled batteries.

incident_description: My 8 month old daughter was sitting on the floor playing with her toys when I noticed her pacifier on the floor next to her.  When I picked it up to wash it, I noticed that the end of the nipple had a tear and was about to fall off.  I was horrified! Had I not stopped to pick it up, my daughter would have picked it up and possibly choked on the piece falling off.  I immediately went through the house and removed all pacifiers for fear of the same thing happening again.  I am extremely dissapointed in Philips Avent Soothie Pacifiers.  This could have ended tragically.
justification: The incident involved a potential choking hazard that was discovered and prevented before any harm occurred, indicating no injury but a clear risk.

incident_description:
5.5 month old baby was bouncing in the activity center, in the stage 2 position, when baby suddenly leaned forwarded and hit his face on one of the attached stationary toys. The incident resulted in bruising to the baby's face, in close proximity to the eye.

Baby meets all requirements including age and height for Stage 2 use and was using the product according to manufacturer's instructions. {Stage 2 is used for infants 4 months old (who can hold up head and neck unassisted) through walking age and under 30 inches tall.}
justification: The incident resulted in bruising to the baby's face, indicating an injury, and the description suggests such incidents are likely given the product's use.

incident_description: My son was in his crib for a nap and I heard him screaming at the top of his lungs in his room. I ran in to his bedroom and his arm was stuck in between the crib rails. He was crying hysterically from the pain and it was so stuck that I was unable to remove his arm. This crib has a major design flaw in which the front of the crib curves forward. This creates a wider gap between crib rails at the top of the side panel to accommodate the curve and a very narrow gap between rails at the bottom of the side panel. My son is able to stick his limbs in and out of the gaps between all the rails with no problem but since the gap on the side of the crib is wide at the top, he can side his arm in there and slide it down to where it gets stuck in the narrow gap at the bottom. His arm was so stuck that when I would try to slide his arm back up the whole crib would move with his arm and every time I would try to touch it he would scream and cry in pain! Graco needs to stop selling the cribs that have these side panels! A child should not be injured by their crib!!
justification: The child experienced significant pain and distress due to the arm being stuck in the crib, indicating an injury, and the design flaw suggests this is likely to happen again.

incident_description: Fisher price bouncer pink butterfly product was being used as it was  intended for when infant was playing with the swinging toys her finger became pinched and stuck between the gap of the grey piece and large flower
justification: The infant's finger was pinched and stuck, indicating an injury occurred during normal use of the product.

incident_description: While my son was sleeping in his crib, turned over to his side and stretched out his leg. When he extended his leg, it became lodged in between two wooden slats that come down vertically from the top rail to the bottom rails of the crib. His leg was wedged past the knee and he could not remove it himself and became stuck. My wife and I had to stabilize him and and pry the two wooden pieces apart to the point where they bent and eventually bent and cracked creating enough of a gap so that we could pull him back out. He was screaming in pain throughout the ordeal. Upon inspecting his leg, he had significant bruising and swelling around his left knee and required us to give him [REDACTED] and an ice pack to reduce the swelling. He was screaming amd writhing around so much that we had thought he broke his leg trying to get it out in the few seconds it took us to reach him.
justification: The child suffered significant bruising and swelling, indicating an injury, and required pain relief and ice treatment.

incident_description:
My husband and I along with our 18 month old son went to a restaurant in Irvine, CA. The restaurant had the RubberMaid high chairs. These chairs have wheels with no locks. It does have a harness. I put my child in the highchair with the harness. The restaurant floor was such that it was very easy to roll the chair and that caused an accident for my child. My son tried to reach out to his food and the chair rolled itself little too quick. As a result my son's instant reaction was to hold the tray. The tray on the farther corner had soup in it causing it to spill on him. He got burned and started to scream and cry. I followed all the first aid steps for a burn and hopefully will not cause his any blisters. 

I have enclosed the link to the product for easy reference. 
http://www.rubbermaidcommercialproducts.com/c395/c14/c71/7805-08-Sturdy-Chair-Youth-Seat-w-Wheels-p740.html

I would highly recommend either discontinuing this product or forcing locks on the wheels. If my son or any other child pushes themselves with any support around them (namely the table), they could roll themselves to a long or short distance. In restaurants there are servers walking with all kinds of food all the time. It can cause severe damage. Hope you agree. Thanks!

Sincerely,
[REDACTED]
justification: The child suffered burns from spilled soup due to the high chair rolling unexpectedly, requiring first aid but no mention of long-term injury.

incident_description: 7 month old infant was playing in Bright starts bounce bounce baby when a piece of plastic broke off.  Infant put piece in mouth  and began choking.   Mother turned baby upside down patting on babies back mother had to stick finger down infants throat to dislodge piece forcing it out of babies  throat.
justification: The infant choked on a broken piece of plastic, requiring intervention to dislodge it, indicating an injury occurred.

incident_description: I bought the fisher price rock and play my little lamb and i noticed recently the hole bottom is all mildew. This is obserd and sodangerous for my son! I was looking for new covers as i threw mine away. I dont think i should have to rebuy a cover for another 30$ 40$.  I think i should recieve a new one this is unexceptable
justification: The presence of mildew poses a potential health risk, but there is no mention of actual injury or harm.

incident_description: My 15 month old son's leg got caught in between the slats of the Princeton 4 in One crib. I almost thought I was going to have to saw the crib apart to get him free. If he had fallen back I believe his leg could have broken. His knee quite bruised and swollen and if the swelling doesn't go down I will be taking him to see a medical professional.  I am now scared to put him back in the crib. I wish I had a video of the incident it was terrifying.
justification: The child suffered a bruised and swollen knee, indicating an injury, and there was a risk of a broken leg.

incident_description: I have discovered my rock and play has mold on it....Im not sure how long it has been there....It is disturbing to me that she slept in it for 4 months assuming this mold has been there that long as that is the last time I cleaned it. I removed the material and washed it in the washer machine and then dried it in the dryer.
justification: The presence of mold is an incident, but there is no indication of injury or harm to the child.

incident_description: Black mold found growing under the pad of the Fisher Price Rock and Play sleeper.
justification: Black mold exposure can lead to respiratory issues or allergic reactions, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description:
I purchased the ChooMee Sip n' Soft top on Amazon about 3 months ago.  It's a soft silicone top for the top of a baby food pouch.  My son is 10 months old and has four front teeth.  He likes to bite and chew.  Well, this evening while having his dinner he bit off almost the entire side of the silicone spout.  After noticing him doing a bit too much chewing of his food, I checked his mouth and the baby food pouch and realized he had bitten off the top.  I tried retreiving the missing portion and patting his back, but he began gagging and had swallowed the silicone.
I'm very concerned that a product marketed and sold for babies 4 months and older is this unsafe.  Had I known this could be a problem and the material so easily torn, I would have never given this to my child.  I'm very surprised that something that can so easily be a choking hazard is sold specifically as something a child should put in their mouth.  This product is a danger and should be removed from the market.
justification: The baby swallowed a piece of the silicone top, which poses a choking hazard but did not result in injury or death.

incident_description: Mold found in fisher price rock n play. Mold was found on fabric between plastic backing and washable cover. I had registered my product back in 2011 and was not notified about the recall. Purchased in 2011. The cover had been washed multiple times. Daughter (7 months) put in hospital for a week with virus then found mold.
justification: The 7-month-old daughter was hospitalized for a week due to a virus linked to mold exposure, indicating an injury.

incident_description: Our baby was sleeping in the Fisher Price Rock 'N Play Baby Cradle as I was taking her out this morning I noticed black spots on the back so I immediately took the cover off to find it had mold on it. We've had the cradle for a couple months and our baby loved it, but we definitely won't be using it again.
justification: Mold was found on the cradle, but no injury or harm to the baby was reported.

incident_description:
The consumer would like to file a report against the company, indicating that the crib model described above poses a safety hazard.

09/26/2014 The consumer placed her son inside the crib at around 1900 hours to go to the kitchen to pick up a bottle to feed him. Approximately thirty seconds after exiting the room, the consumer heard loud screaming. She hurried to the bedroom where her son was and found him inside the crib lying diagonally on his stomach with his right leg all the way up to his hip stuck between the rails. Initially, his leg would not budge when she tried to take it out. The consumer was scared because she thought her sonÃÂs leg would break. He would not stop squirming, which in turn hurt him more and the screaming and crying continued. He remained doing this for the two minutes the consumer could not free him out of the cribÃÂs rails. Finally she was finally able to do so by turning him diagonally and squeezing his thigh while he cried even more.

The consumerÃÂs son cried for at least fifteen minutes after his leg was released. His thigh was red for the following thirty minutes and it was noticeable where the bars had his leg trapped. The baby was not bruised and the consumer states there were no further physical damages to him.
The consumer states that her son was only transitioning to the crib from his bassinet, having only been inside it maybe five times with stays of no longer than twenty minutes. Her son has not been placed inside the crib ever since the incident. The consumer recalls that her sonÃÂs leg was trapped between the bars once before but considering she was able to release it with ease; she found no need to report it.  

09/30/2014 The consumer contacted the manufacturer and spoke to [REDACTED]. She was not able to fully explain the incident before he told her that her crib model met the Consumer Product Safety CommissionÃÂs standards and that because of this there was nothing the company could do for her. He recommended that she buy products that prevent these types of incidents and that are specifically designed for hyperactive children. 

The consumer suggested to[REDACTED]that they refund her the money she spent on the crib ÃÂ an approximate 145.00 US$ ÃÂ and again he told her that they would do no such thing because CPSCÃÂs standards were met when manufacturing her crib model and it has not been involved in any recall. The consumer then asked to speak to another representative of the company and [REDACTED]informed her that this would not be possible. She asked him if he was the President or owner of the company and he responded that he was not. The call lasted between fifteen and twenty minutes. 

The consumer states that she has a hard time believing no one above [REDACTED]was available for her to speak to. She indicates that not once did he ask her about the welfare of her child. 
The consumer believes that she should receive a full refund for the product and thus plans on contacting the retailer to see if they would be more sensitive to the matter.
justification: The child suffered temporary pain and redness from being trapped in the crib rails, indicating an injury without lasting physical damage.

incident_description: We own a Lullaby LX Playard from Chicco. Our infant often sleeps for periods of time in it at night, and in the last two consecutive nights, one of the long sides has snapped and folded while she was sleeping in it. The first night, I woke to see the side sagging and removed my daughter. The second night, I had my husband verify that it was properly assembled, but I was later awoken by a cracking sound only to find that the same side had buckled again. This Playard is less than a year old.
justification: The playard's side snapped and folded twice, posing a risk to the infant, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: I was using a tommee tipper bottle warmer for my newborn I pulled the bottle out to feed him and didn't unplug it immediately but about 5 minutes later while I was feeding him my daughter reached up on the counter and knocked it over. It gave her second degree burns through her clothes on her chest. We had to go to the emergency room. The warmer was only on for about 10 minutes total and was up high on the counter. The water was so hot my husband watched her skin peel it was horrific. If the bottle warmer had an automatic shutoff like other products of its kind or had a max temperature that wasn't that hot this accident could have been prevented or not been as severe.
justification: The incident resulted in second-degree burns requiring emergency room treatment, indicating a significant injury.

incident_description: The bounder was turned to vibrate.  The mother fell asleep while the child was in the bouncer. The child moved until the child fell forward on the bouncer with it's face in the blankets and suffocated.
justification: The child suffocated, which resulted in death, the highest severity level.

incident_description: My 6 month old son was able to suck off the rubber tab or handle on the outside of the pacifier. Luckily we were watching him and he didn't choke. But this is a very hazardous pacifier it needs to be taken off the market and I'm planning to sue.
justification: The child did not choke due to parental supervision, but the pacifier's defect poses a hazard.

incident_description: I bought a Nook Pebble Lite crib mattress last year. I noticed then that it wasn't a snug fit like our cheaper mattress had been. Well last night my daughter got trapped between the mattress & crib side. There's at least a 2 inch gap now. Thankfully my husband heard her crying as I slept through it all having tended to our 5 month old throughout the night.
justification: The child got trapped but was unharmed, indicating an incident with no injury.

incident_description:
Child was using a Sassy Baby Rattle / Teether.  The outer rubber covering of part of the toy came completely off and could have resulted in the child choking perhaps even death.  However this was observed immediately and the toy was taken away. 

 I checked the manufactures website and could not find this product listed as recalled.  I am also concerned that other products of theirs may use that same teether ball design and would also be at risk of falling apart and lead to a child choking.

I have a copy of the email sent to the manufacturer and pictures of the product but I could not upload them in this form.  Please advise as how I can attach them to this incident case
justification: The rubber covering came off, posing a choking hazard, but the incident was observed and prevented.

incident_description: I purchased a big box of Luvs diapers( ultra leakguard) for my son who is 3 weeks old and I was hoping that it " helps lock wetness away" as mentioned on the box but actually it caused sever rash, pimples and burns to my infants' skin. I used an ointment for diaper rashes to calm him down but did not help at all and the diaper area gets worst everyday. I am going to see a doctor trying to find something to help my baby who screams a lot from pain.
justification: The infant suffered severe rash, pimples, and burns, indicating injury (severity 3). Diaper-related skin issues are possible (likelihood 3) based on the description.

incident_description: (10/05/2014) The consumer stated that she boiled the pacifier for five minutes as instructed. After the pacifier was boiled, the  tip of the nipple came off. The pacifier had not been used.
justification: The pacifier tip came off after boiling, but it was not used, so no injury occurred.

incident_description:
(08/29/2014) The consumer stated that he heard his daughter crying. He went into the room and found her left leg stuck in between the slats. Her leg was stuck near her ankle. The consumer stated that he had to move his daughter's leg around to get it out.

(09/29/2014) The consumer stated that the same happened with his daughter's right leg. It was stuck near her ankle


There were no injures.
justification: The incident involved a child's leg getting stuck twice with no reported injuries, fitting the criteria for severity level 2.

incident_description: There is mild build up in the inside of the rock n play sleeper. I do was it frequently. My son has a terrible cough and he developed bronchitis.
justification: The child developed bronchitis, indicating an injury, likely due to the buildup in the sleeper.

incident_description: My son was hit in the head on 2 different occasions by either the fish or tree on this jumper. I did not see it happen but I heard it happen, followed by his crying and a lump on the side of his head. The fish and tree was the recall replacement part for the original sun that injured other children.
justification: The child was hit in the head, resulting in crying and a lump, indicating an injury.

incident_description: My 6 month son was sitting on my lap holding his MAM pacifier as usually and putting it in and out of his mouth when suddenly he started screaming and crying hard. I look down and tried to pull out the pacifier but it was completely stuck sideways. Just like others stated, it was lodged between his gums and I struggled to pull it out without hurting him further. He was fine after I yanked it out but I no longer trust him alone with his pacifier :( always loved his brand for both my kids. Hopefully they revamp it ASAP. I called customer service as suggested, and no answer, only voice mail. I'm waiting for a response.
justification: The child was distressed but not injured, and the pacifier was removed without lasting harm.

incident_description:
(07/16/2014) The consumer stated there was tear at the plastic base of the pacifier . She contacted the company and explained that the product was damaged and was offered a replacement. 

The consumer stated that she inspected the product to make sure that there was no damage.

(08/08/2014) The consumer noticed after the second pacifier was used by the baby, there was a tear in the same space.  

(08/14/2014) The consumer noticed a tear on a third pacifier. 

No injuries occurred.
justification: The incident involved repeated product damage but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: Went to Sam's Club to get there Simply Right Diapers. There was none there.  When ask they said it was on recall.  2nd time visit stop at services and asked about why they were being recalled, and was told it was bacteria. Then asked what bacteria and they would not tell us.  Just bring back the diapers and wipes.  There is 3 children in my child daycare that has this brand and all three children have a rash
justification: Three children developed rashes from using the recalled diapers, indicating an injury.

incident_description: I took off the seat cover to my son's Rock n Play sleeper and there was mold all over the straps and the base of the cradle. I tried to scrub with a mildew and mold killer but nothing came off of the material. My son is a micro preemie and this is our primary source of a sleeper and we are no longer able to use this :(
justification: Mold presence poses a health risk, especially to a micro preemie, but no direct injury is reported.

incident_description: I bought this support pillow hoping that it would help my son. I used this product only for two months and the filling material is making its way out of the pillow very bad. It's coming from all over. The filling fibers are really tiny and the baby might swallow it and choke on.
justification: The pillow's filling is coming out, posing a potential choking hazard to the baby, but no injury has been reported yet.

incident_description:
I received an Evenflo ExerSaucerÃÂ® Double FunÃÂ Pink Bumbly Saucer as a gift for my daughter whom is just 6 months old now.  I am happy with the exersaucer but there is a problem with it that I find very dangerous.  On an earlier date I when pulling the baby/infant out of the seat I noticed that her foot was deeply scratched.  Not to the point of bleeding, but to the point of discomfort.  On the actual date listed, I took the baby/infant out of the exersaucer and her foot was badly scraped/scratched again.  I now realize that the ring that holds the fabric seat/sling part has sharp edges and cuts.

I took the seat apart and literally cut my finger on the roller ring due to sharp plastic sticking out and the edges being far too sharp for a baby toy.  If they had the seat/sling fabric attach to the ring portion on the inside as well it would eliminate much of the risk.  The problem is that the fabric seat/sling attaches on the outside of the ring and when pulling the baby/infant out of the toy it turns inside out exposing the inside of the ring to the baby's legs while pulling them out.  

I feel that this is just bad safety for a baby toy.  All plastic edges should be smoothed and made certain that they will not injure a child.  I wonder if all the units are made with such disregard for safety.  It is clear that this one was sent out knowing it was like this because no one is considering the fact it is a danger while pulling the child out of the toy.
justification: The incident describes repeated injuries (scratches and scrapes) to a baby's foot and a cut to an adult's finger, indicating a clear injury risk from sharp edges on the toy.

incident_description: To whom it may concern My FOUR YEAR OLD daughter suffered burns from a dream lite pillow pet (unicorn) on Sunday, Sept 14, 2014. She went to sleep around 8:30 pm and woke me at 4 AM screaming she was on FIRE!!!! I rushed to my daughters room, saw her shirt was burned and I immediately lifted her shirt off of her. She indeed was burned by this pillow and has 2nd degree burn measuring the same length of the plastic pink area as well as stars and moons and a unicorn that has now blistered up and started to burst on her abdomen!!!! She has been in pain since Sunday and is under doctor care!!! I am so outraged and disgusted by the fact that just I called your customer service number (9/18/14) and learned that these items are still being sold!!! What if she wouldn't have woken up-she could have burned to death in a house fire!! Would that have been a WAKE UP CALL for you to remove this PRODUCT FROM SHELVES!!!!! I have seen numerous reviews [REDACTED]now dated back as far as May of last year talking about the UNICORN and other dream lites causing the same thing to other families and the built in timers not even cutting off!...2nd and 3rd degree burns and house fires with the dream lites being declared cause of fire by Fire Marshall's but I guess that isn't enough for your company to remove these for purchase. My daughter is now a VICTIM!!!!! This product has bad reviews and is dangerous and SHOULD BE REMOVED FROM ALL SHELVES. I guess this toy will be a life time tag along being the scars will last forever!!!! ONE extremely upset MOTHER!!!"
justification: The incident resulted in second-degree burns to a child, indicating a severity level of 3 (Injury). The occurrence likelihood is high (4) due to multiple reported cases of similar incidents.

incident_description: We had been using the Dream On Me Karley Bassinet in Grey/Blue (bought from WalMart.com) which is rated for use for children up to 25lbs. My son was just 12lbs at time of incident. The tubing in the cover came lose and got stuck on his face! We are very lucky it wasn't IN HIS EYE! We promptly stopped using the product and bought a new bed for him to use.
justification: The tubing came loose and got stuck on the child's face, posing a risk of injury, though no actual injury was reported.

incident_description: The night light was plugged in and a hole burned through the bottom.  My son burned his finger on it and told me he saw fire.  This would have caused a fire if not discovered and immediately unplugged.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury to the child and had the potential to cause a fire, indicating significant risk.

incident_description:
Fisher Price Rock and Play Sleeper purchased at Walmart in June 2014.  

Removed washable seat cushion and found "spots" on the plastic frame underneath.  This appears to be mildew/mold.  Looked up the product and found there had been a recall in 2013 regarding the rock and play sleeper due to mold that can grow between the removable cushion and plastic frame.
justification: Mold was found on the product, which is a known issue due to a prior recall, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: The Babies R Us Play Yard (free standing gate) creates small, spiral-shaped fine plastic shavings as the gate is folded and unfolded.  The joints where the gate panels connect grind against each other as it is moved, and plastic shavings are produced which fall out.  These are very fine and appear in and around the gate, easily picked up by babies and children and are a major choking hazard.  My 6 month old daughter had picked one up and started to put it in her mouth before we luckily caught it and found several other shavings.  We cleaned them all up, thinking maybe they were just due to packaging, but saw that the gate continued to produce new shavings as we moved it around and folded/unfolded it.
justification: The incident involved a near-miss choking hazard with no actual injury, and the gate consistently produces hazardous shavings during use.

incident_description: Smell of Electrical Burning in Kitchen at 9pm at night. Traced to Amertac 71055 7W bulb NiteLite that was flickering & lightly smoking. The bottom of the plastic case was extremely hot to the touch but not melted. The AC connector prongs were hot enough to burn your fingers when removed from the wall socket.  The 120v AC wall socket was hot to the touch and no circuit breaker had tripped.  The wall socket took about an hour to cool down. There was no smoke detector operated as this was caught early as we were home. There was a good possibility of a house fire of we were gone for the week-end in my opinion. A second identical NiteLite was removed from our bedroom that evening and I replaced both NiteLites with an [REDACTED] NiteLight.
justification: The incident involved a smoking and overheating bulb with potential for a fire, but no actual injury or fire occurred.

incident_description:
Manufacturer: Tiny Love
Product: Gymini Sunny Day Activity Gym

incident_description: Subject is a 7 month old white male with no PMH.  Today subject was laid in crib on his back after second feeding by mother.  At around 1225 hrs mother went in to check on subject because he hadn't awoke and found him unresponsive in crib.  Subject's head was wedged in between crib mattress and bars of crib and his body and legs were hanging out the bottom of the crib below the mattress.  Mother started to scream because she was unable to free subject and father came into room and started to break crib apart.  Medics called.  Subject transported to Bayview.  Per police subject had bar marks on right side of face.  Father stated subject was cold too the touch when he was trying to remove him from crib.  Scene was townhouse where subject lived with mother, father, and four siblings.  Subject had bedroom in upper level of residence. Crib subject slept in was older style with drop down side.  Father broke side when trying to free subject.  Unable to get manufacturer information off crib - unable to locate it.  Mattress was Walmart brand - Model # KM109-AABP  serial # UM02.  Mattress was still covered in plastic and appeared to be in good condition.  Crib had sheet on mattress.  Two additional blankets, one pillow, and a stuffed animal were noted in crib on side by subject's feet.  Room is cluttered with baby stuff - food,toys, etc. Room is cooled with window unit air conditioner and is comfortable temperature.  Floors are carpeted.  Side bar that enables crib side to go down partially broken by father when he pulled subject out in resus effort. Crib is intact other than broken side bar. Subject passed away at Johns Hopkins Bayview Hospital.

Over time, the screws became loose and the when we tried to fasten the screws again, the screws would not make contact with the nuts and the screws could not be tightened. The holes where the screws entered  had become too large for the screws. 

We were concerned and tried to return the bed to Buy Buy Baby in 2012. We were told that we would have to contact Baby's Dream. Baby's Dream said they would send new larger connectors that may fit into worn holes. However, we felt that this solution would only be a temporary fix and would not prevent further deterioration of the holes. We felt the bed was no longer safe to use.

incident_description: I recently bought a Gum Drop 6-12 Month size pacifier for my infant.  I gave her the pacifier when she went to sleep.  In the night, it fell out and she tried to out it in herself.  When she stuck her thumb into the back of the product, her thumb got caught and she could not get it out.  After trying to sleep with her thumb in the pacifier, she woke screaming because it was cutting off the circulation to her thumb.  The 6 month pacifiers have a different kind of hole in the back which catches a child's finger and doesn't let go.  I am an adult, and it was extremely hard for me to get it off her thumb.  Who knows what would have happened if we had not found it when we did.  If her thumb had been in there all night, she may not have had use of it ever again. I am so angry this product is on the market.  This is supposed to be a safe, soothing mechanism, but instead it is quite the opposite.  This is a serious danger to children.

incident_description: I am a physician and recently cared for a toddler injured in a KidCo PeaPod Plus Travel Bed. He was put to sleep in it while his family was traveling. They were in a room without enough floor space to put the device on the floor and instead put it on a bed.  The child was found the next morning wedged between the wooden bed frame and the mattress, still inside the Travel Bed. He had bleeding into his scalp on both sides sufficiently severe that child abuse was considered and he was admitted overnight to a tertiary hospital intensive care unit. He is recovering without apparent long-term problems. The parents acknowledge that the Travel Bed is supposed to be used on the floor but felt they had little option because of the circumstances they were in. Obviously, there is the potential for more serious or fatal consequences for other children. I wrote the manufacturer and let them know what happened. I am not familiar with the warnings that come with this product but at a minimum there should be clear language that there is a risk of injury or death if the device is put on a bed. Given the risks and given what we know about the importance of providing a safe sleep environment for infants, toddlers and children, there is no need for this device and in my opinion it should be taken off the market.
justification: The child suffered severe injuries requiring ICU admission, indicating a severity level of 3. The incident highlights a clear risk when the product is misused, suggesting a likelihood of 4 (likely) given the described circumstances.

incident_description:
I did not have a specific incident or injury. This is a possible safety hazard that I've noticed.

I purchased an Ingenuity Moonlight Rocking Sleeper for my youngest daughter. The sleeper is advertised as being both an entertainer-seat and a safe bed, useable starting at birth.

My daughter was four days old when we first used the sleeper. When I placed her in the sleeper, I noticed that there was very little support for her back, head, and neck. The sleeper lacks any kind of firm support to keep the baby in a safe, semi-reclined position.

My daughter curled into herself, with her chin settled firmly into her chest. No matter how I adjusted her in the seat, I could not get her chin off of her chest- not even the finger's width that babies this age require to breathe easily. Infants this young can asphyxiate in this position (as has been seen in some baby carriers).

I have four children, and this child has been my largest baby. She was nine pounds at birth and was still nearly that weight when we tried to use the sleeper. I'm not sure if her weight has something to with me not being able to position her correctly.

I'm concerned that this product presents an asphyxiation hazard, and therefore, is not safe for newborns OR possibly not safe for "unusually large" newborns.

I submitted a review of the product on Ingenuity's website and expressed my concerns in it. In response, the company sent me an e-mail explaining that they will not publish the review unless I remove the safety concern from it and suggested that I contact their legal team.
justification: No incident or injury occurred, but the potential for asphyxiation due to poor support in the sleeper presents a safety hazard.
