incident_description:
Caller stated that her 9 month old child was rubbing her face against the netting on the play yard which caused her to receive lacerations on her nose.   She was placed in the play yard for only 5 mins when the incident occurred.  She took her to her pediatrician for examination, she was not given any medical treatment.  She was advised not to touch the child's nose to prevent an infection.

6/24/13 The manufacturer was contacted through email but no one responded.  (6/27/14) The  manufacturer informed her that she should return the product for a refund.  She requested to speak to a Supervisor who advised that the person she spoke was in charge of that department.  Caller feels that the manufacturer should change the design of the netting that caused this incident.  She is concerned that the company is not willing to prevent harm to children.

Caller feels that this product is a safety hazard for babies.
justification: The child received lacerations from the play yard netting, requiring a pediatrician visit but no medical treatment, indicating an injury without severe consequences.

incident_description: Kids II bright starts entertain and grow product is not very safe in my experience. The bottom of the product is a saucer with no legs. When my baby is in it playing and "bouncing" it looks like it is gonna tip over. The design makes it very unstable. My second concern with the product is a removable toy that is yellow and pink. It is a long stick that looks like a butterfly at the end. My baby chews on the rubber butterfly head that is like a baby chew toy. She often gags on this toy and twice got the butterfly head and wing stuck in her mouth. I had to jump up and remove it from her mouth for her. The stick was designed way to long.
justification: The product's instability and the removable toy causing gagging incidents indicate potential for injury, though no actual injury was reported.

incident_description: Mold is growing on my baby's rock and play sleeper
justification: Mold growth is an incident that could pose health risks, but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: Our pack n play/play yard has a floor mat that is made from some sort of hard material, surrounded on the outside by fabric. The hard material inside seems to be disintegrating in several places, and as a result our infant is able to fall in between the floor mat and the bottom of the pack n play and become trapped, which poses a suffocation risk.  It is a fairly new product, and has received normal use.
justification: The disintegrating floor mat poses a suffocation risk to the infant, which is a serious incident but no injury has been reported yet.

incident_description: My daughter's arm got stuck under the play mat. the boards keep moving leaving a gap.
justification: The incident involved a child's arm getting stuck under a play mat, indicating a potential hazard but no reported injury.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that hIS daughter's legs slip through the slat spacing of the crib. The consumer stated that the leg gets stuck at the thighs.

The consumer stated that he has to tug the leg out to free it from the spacing. The consumer stated that his daughter tries to twist and turn her leg to free it from the slats.

The consumer's daughter is 9 months old,  weighs 22.2 pounds, and  19 inches in height. 

The consumer stated that he contacted Graco regarding this issue. They informed him to contact LaJobi.

The consumer contacted LaJobi. They informed him that their crib meets the federal slat requirements.

The consumer stated that he measured the crib slat spacing to be 2 1/8 inches on back side and 2 1/4 inches on the front side. The consumer stated that the side slat spacing is roughly 2 inches.

The consumer stated that they have had this issue since they transferred his from the bassinet to the crib (Feb 2014).
justification: The incident involves the child's legs getting stuck in the crib slats, requiring intervention to free her, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
(5/12/14) Caller stated that her 13 month old child legs were entrapped between the crib slats and she had difficulty removing it, dishwashing detergent and water was used to release the child's legs.  The child weighs 23 pounds.  There had been 3 prior incidents where he was stuck but was able to release his own legs.  His legs were stuck all the way up to his thighs.  In removing the child's legs she noticed minor bruising (red marks).  No medical attention was received.

(5/13/14) The manufacturer was contacted and she was advised that if the child was placed in the crib again this incident could re-occur and that she should place the child in a toddler bed.

 Caller feels that this crib is a safety hazard and should be reported.
justification: The child sustained minor bruising (red marks) from the incident, indicating an injury, and the manufacturer confirmed the likelihood of recurrence if the crib continues to be used.

incident_description: We just switched from [REDACTED] to Pampers Cruisers size 4 this week because I used Pampers for some of my other children and we were having some leaking issues with our other diaper recently.  My 13 month old son had pooped in his diaper when I was cooking dinner and I didn't realize it so it may have had on the dirty diaper for up to 1/2 hour.  When I noticed and changed him, I was shocked.  His entire butt was not just red but swollen.  He is my 4th child and again, I have never seen anything like this.  It was not a rash.  He was screaming in pain when I tried to clean him.  I am very upset as I have no doubt what so ever that this was caused from his loose stool mixing wih chemicals in this diaper.  He has not had any issues with urine but he had a loose stool and I didn't realize he had a dirty diaper right away.  I am sure I am not the only parent that didn't immediately realize their child went to the bathroom.  Still, I felt awful because he was in terrible shape last night.  Today the swollen redness is gone other than 2 lines (one on each side) that looks like a burn.
justification: The child experienced significant pain and visible swelling, indicating an injury caused by the diaper.

incident_description: My 17 month old son's leg became stuck in the crib (BabyMod Olivia) at the thigh.  He had bruises and became very upset. In order to avoid further injury, we sawed him out of his crib.
justification: The child suffered bruises and distress, indicating an injury (severity 3). Crib entrapment incidents, while not daily, are documented occurrences.

incident_description:
Bought the Munchin High Speed Bottle Warmer 
http://www.munchkin.com/products/feeding/bottles-and-accessories/high-speed-bottle-warmer.html

The timer did not work properly, it would stop at random times but the burner would continue working..causing the milk to be too hot luckily i have enough common sense NOT to give it to my newborn but others may not and could burn the newborns mouth.
justification: The bottle warmer malfunctioned, potentially causing burns, but no injury was reported in this instance.

incident_description:
My 16-month-old infant was sitting in her Fisher-Price Home & Away 3-in-1 High Chair when it suddenly fell apart. She went crashing to the ground. Thankfully, she was strapped into her seat which did not break.  The high chair seems to have broken at the legs.  It was scary!

I have a photo of the broken high chair.
justification: The high chair fell apart, but the infant was not injured as she was strapped in.

incident_description: My 4 month old was in the swing strapped in and kicked the center part of the tray support and pushed him self up the end of the swing seat.  His head was almost lodged between the swing arm and frame support beam.  We were standing next to him when it happened and were able to catch him before he was injured.
justification: The infant was almost injured but was caught in time, resulting in no actual injury.

incident_description: I have been switching diaper brands on my baby since he was born, never had any serious issues with any of them. I tried pampers size 3 two night ago to see if they wouldn't leak overnight, he woke up with his first REAL diaper rash. Normally if he is a little red i put some [REDACTED] and by the next diaper change its gone, not this time. He got worst! By bed time his rash had spread to his front side and the back of his legs. I switched over to [REDACTED] before putting him to sleep and he woke up a little better today.
justification: The baby developed a severe diaper rash that spread, indicating an injury.

incident_description: I went to give my Fisher Price Rock N Play to a friend and found the lining was full of mold.  I read the online instructions from the company for cleaning the rocker.  We were going to use this for another baby so had been storing the rocker, folded up, and under my daughter's crib.  I had no idea there was a recall until I Googled the issue and found the recall.  So my now 2 year old daughter, has been sleeping with a moldy rocker under her crib for her entire life.  NOT happy.  The Fisher price should be accepting returns and offering full refunds, not just instructions to clean it.
justification: The incident involves exposure to mold but no reported injury or illness, fitting severity level 2. Mold issues in recalled products are a known but not universal occurrence, hence likelihood 3.

incident_description: From the floor, my daughter stepped up on the bottom back bar of the high chair, leaned forward on the top back bar and placed her head/chin above it. She got hung up on the bar with it pushing against her neck. I heard her make a sound and removed her.
justification: The child got hung up on the high chair bar but was quickly removed without injury, indicating an incident with no harm.

incident_description: My baby has a bloody toe! I could not figure out what she could have cut her toe on. When I went to get her out of the Fisher-Price Superstar Step 'N Play Piano I looked underneath her and there was blood all over the piano keys on the base of toe.
justification: The baby suffered a cut leading to visible blood, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
We purchased the Baby Einstein Rhythm of the Reef Activity Saucer from Target on 06/25/14. Our seven-month old baby was playing with the octopus and the two ribbons attached to it begun to unravel into long threads, which he managed to get all tangled up in. The threads were wrapped around his body, neck and little fingers. As this is a 360-degree Activity Saucer, he kept getting wrapped up more tightly in the threads, cutting off his circulation.

Since we did not leave him unsupervised, we noticed the issue in time to safely remove all the thread from around the baby. Our baby was NOT injured. However, this is a potentially fatal defect. If someone were to leave their baby out of sight in this for even a few minutes, the octopus is a major strangulation hazard.

I emailed all this information to Kids II, the manufacturer of Baby Einstein toys tonight. The model number is 60246. The Date Code is: AJ1014

Please feel free to call me at [REDACTED]. I have pictures. We cut off the ribbons, and hopefully they can ship us an octopus without any threads in it.

Sincerely,

[REDACTED]
justification: The baby was not injured, but the incident involved a potentially fatal defect with the toy's threads.

incident_description: Last week, we purchased a "Wall Warmer" tart warmer by Patriot Candles which is designed to plug into an electrical outlet much light a night light, has a ceramic cover that latches into the base, and a tray for the wax of a candle tart to melt into.  It was used for two days, roughly 8 hours total operation, on the second day after 3 hours of usage, I noticed that the tray was not level on top.  When I went to check if it was fully plugged into the outlet, the ceramic cover came off with no effort as if it was just balancing on it.  I turned off the device, removed it from the wall, and allowed the components to cool separately as they operate around 160-180 degrees.  The plastic on the portion that plugs into the wall was melting around the base collapsing inward to where the portion that should latch onto the ceramic cover were directed upwards and no longer offering support.  Further use would have fully lost the "balance" that was holding it upright projecting hot ceramics and melted wax to anyone near it.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning device that could have caused injury but was discovered and addressed before harm occurred.

incident_description: I ordered the Safety 1st Heavenly Dreams mattress before my daughter was born. It seemed to fit well in the crib. She didn't sleep in it, she slept in a [REDACTED] in our bedroom. When she was approximately 3 months old I'd thought about transitioning her into her crib in her room. This is when I realized the mattress has shrunk. She could easily become wedged between the mattress and crib. This is very unsafe and a SIDS haard.
justification: The mattress shrinkage poses a SIDS hazard, but no incident or injury has occurred yet.

incident_description: A piece of the toy fall out and my daughter almost swallow it. we have to put out hand in her month to take it back. My daughter cannot breathe for a second
justification: The child could not breathe for a second, indicating a potential choking hazard, but no lasting injury was reported.

incident_description: Reporting a near miss with baby product.  The harness buckle on Bright Starts Plug-in Sway & Swing broke while child was in it.  Child was well within weight restrictions of swing (13-14 lb child, swing weight restriction is 25 lbs).  Also, small piece of plastic buckle that attached the harness strap to buckle came free when harness buckle broke; this plastic piece was the perfect size for a choking hazard.
justification: The harness buckle broke but no injury occurred, though the small plastic piece poses a potential choking hazard.

incident_description: Evenflo exersaucer baby active fall hazard. My 6 month old daught was in her bouncer and the tabs the lock the 3 pillars in place had given way. The pillars popped out of the base of the exersaucer and the lower portions fell inward while the weight of the upper portion of the exersaucer and my daughteds weight fell down nearly crushing her lower body. Shes not incredibly active so she doesnt stree the locking tabs as my son had done with the one we bought for him. Im a mechanic and insist on double checking my work when assembling everything. Approximately 3 months have passed with this object was being used. I ensured the tabs and other locking mechanisms where properly in place befor use, and as I had put it back together when it broke, the tabs would not lock, then it fell apart without the babys weight. This product is unsafe as the structural design is only made to last a short time period. Please figure this situation out befor any children get hurt.
justification: The incident involved a structural failure of the exersaucer that nearly crushed the child, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: I was using [REDACTED] as soon as my daughter hit size 2 she got the mosy terrible rash I have ever seen! (I've worked at 2 daycare centers so I know what normal rashes are) this was horrible Her skin was blistered and red. It took me a while to realize it was the diapers. After switching diapers Ive had no problem. Until recently Im now trying to potty train I put her in huggies pull ups and the same rash came back. Its frustrating because Im potty training the longest she's left in a diaper is when she's sleeping otherwise Im constantly having Het sit on her potty and changing her
justification: The description indicates a severe rash with blisters, which constitutes an injury.

incident_description:
First we had emailed to [REDACTED] Recall Specialist at Dream on Me (baby cribs) 11.15.2011 about the recall we had seen online.  After corresponding on email several times, she informed us that the date on our crib was not part of the recall.  (I have record of those emails if needed.)  We were told that the crib recall was due to the drop side, and the materials used. 

After that, when my son was approximately 16 months old (ish) we had a major issue with the crib.  We NEVER received a crib replacement, and had an issue where our son fell between the crib side and the bottom (it gave way, the screws didn't stay in place even thought tightened with [REDACTED] wrench.)    We ended up re-tightening and securing the area to itself with [REDACTED] heavy duty restraints to keep from separating.  We then transferred him into a toddler bed with extra side rails, because we felt the crib wasn't safe.  I haven't had the time to follow up with this, and always wanted to contact the company.  I however was contacted recently (06.23.14) from U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission.  I would LOVE to send you the crib (of course being reimbursed for shipping, or have someone come pick it up to see what safety issue I'm referring to.) We would also like receive an updated replacement if possible.  We really would like you to see see what happened with this crib so it doesn't happen to anyone else.  Luckily we were there, and heard him crying it could have been a lot worse, which is every parents nightmare.
justification: The incident involved a crib failure leading to a child falling, but no injury was reported, only potential risk.

incident_description: Hi, our son, [REDACTED], is 2.5y old. we just started using pull ups, but had to stop them almost immediately. He developed a severe rash (we have lots of pictures). first it started around the inner part of the upper legs, then it spread out down to his toes and some on his arms/hands. we went to doctors care the first night, they had no idea what to do with him. the following morning we went to his pediatrician, he was shocked with the severity of the rash. The doctor advised us to start soothing baths with and stop all other baby products. the soothing baths and soothing lotion/cream did help him with itch and the blisters started to dry out after the 4-th day. now, its been 2 weeks and all blisters are gone and his legs and arms are covered in spots of new skin. we wanted to try one more time with the pull ups, it took maybe 20 minutes and he developed redness and his skin around the inner part part the legs started to bump up and started to itch and cry. we immediately shower him and used the soothing lotion. this did help a bit, but it took very long time to calm him down. he did fall asleep after a good hour of crying and scratching his sides and he did hurt him self because of the severe rash/itch. we went back to using [REDACTED]. so far, we have no problem with using them.
justification: The child developed a severe rash and blisters, causing pain and self-injury from scratching, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description: i have 2 sons ones 1 year and the other is 1 month i use pampers dippers on both my kids but recently both my boys have major rashes the skin is cracked and its redder the a normal rash.. at first i thought it was a normal rash but then when i realized than my youngest had started to get the rash i was concerned ive changed the brand of diaper i use and my oldest rash is going away very slowly but the dipper rash creams are not working on my kids so they are in pain my one month old little balls are so red and and have open little blisters ...
justification: Both children have severe rashes with cracked skin and blisters, indicating injury and pain.

incident_description: Pampers Cruisers, size 6. I am a HUGE pampers fan. they are the best when it comes to leaks and absorbancy, but yesterday my local store as out of the pampers baby dry size 6, so i bought instead the pampers cruisers size 6. My son broke out with the worst rash between his legs where his thighs hit the diaper, a chemical burn.  I immediately called his dr and had him seen and she too agreed it was from the diaper. She gave me a prescription for [REDACTED] and a cortisone cream for him. I switched his diaper back to the baby dry and withing the day it had completely disappeared. I was extremely dissappointed when all pampers wanted to do was send me a coupon or refund my money. This is my child, a less then 2 year old that had a bad chemical reaction to there product. I am completely against pampers now!
justification: The child suffered a chemical burn requiring medical treatment, which constitutes an injury.

incident_description: I was messaged by my sister in law today about the recall on the Fisher Price rock 'n' play sleeper. The report stated mold issues and could cause respiratory issues. My son has had breathing problems for the past few months he sounds congested and even has periods in his sleep that he stops breathing.   We have consulted out doctor and found it not to be sleep apnea and even treated for possible reflux but that didn't work. Seemed that we couldn't find the cause. As soon as I got the message about the recall I called my husband and had him pull the top piece off and check. What he found mortified and disgusts me. His sleeper is full of mold! I've taken pictures and will be making an appointment first thing tomorrow to make sure there's no serious issues of this extensive mold exposure.  As a parent it is a sickening feeling knowing I was subjecting my infant son to such a disgusting thing.
justification: The infant experienced respiratory issues likely caused by mold exposure, which constitutes an injury.

incident_description: I noticed that the slats on my daughter's crib were splitting vertically. If rubbed, you can get splinters. Thankfully I noticed before the slat split all the way and no injuries have been sustained. The crib has been used for approximately 11 months and has had only normal use. The crib is a Graco Mason convertible crib and was manufactured by Lajobi. The model number is 6825532. PO# 8703 with a production date of February 7, 2013.
justification: Splitting slats pose a potential hazard but no injuries occurred, indicating a severity level of 2. The likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the crib's age and normal use.

incident_description: I was using pampers swaddlers as soon as my daughter hit size 2 she got the mosy terrible rash I have ever seen! (I've worked at 2 daycare centers so I know what normal rashes are) this was horrible Her skin was blistered and red. It took me a while to realize it was the diapers. After switching diapers Ive had no problem. Until recently Im now trying to potty train I put her in [REDACTED] and the same rash came back. Its frustrating because Im potty training the longest she's left in a diaper is when she's sleeping otherwise Im constantly having Het sit on her potty and changing her.
justification: The description indicates a severe rash with blisters and redness, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description:
MY SON WAS JUMPING IN THE ACTIVITY JUMPER AND TWO OF THE 4 STRAPS RIPPED. lUCKILY I WAS STANDING WITH HIM SO i WAS ABLE TO CATCH HIM, BUT IF I WAS NOT HE COULD HAVE BEEN SERIOSULY 

This item was very LIGHTLY used prior to the incident.
justification: The straps ripped but the child was caught, resulting in no injury. The incident could have led to serious injury if not for immediate intervention.

incident_description: black mold was growing on my product
justification: Black mold on a product is an incident that could lead to health issues if not addressed, but no injury is reported here.

incident_description:
Caller stated that her 11 month old child was able to chew on the crib and bite off a chunk of wood. The child choked on the object and eventually regurgitated.  No medical attention was received.  (6/2/14) The retailer was contacted and they advised her that the crib was unsafe for her child and they are willing to replace it.  (6/4/14) She contacted the manufacturer and was informed that they are not responsible for the child chewing on the crib and that it was not under warranty, she was also advised that she could purchase another rail.  Approximately 5 months ago she had notice teeth marks on the rail but was unaware that the child was able to penetrate the wood with teeth, knowing that he had just started teething.

Caller is concerned that this crib is a choking hazard to children and that the manufacturer should be held responsible to recall the product.


This is in reference to report No. 20140604-D54D8-1406592 that we received on 6/14/14. Attached is a signed copy of the report and multiple photos of the damage an eleven month old child did to his crib. Since this report was created, the Target store that we were dealing with said to return it to them and they would replace the crib. On June 7th, we disassemble the crib and took it back to the store where we were then told by another "manager" that they could not accept it because "we do not carry it at Target. I've never heard of a stork craft. It's up to the manufacturer", she said. During the initial contact, it was explained several times that it was bought online at TARGET.COM. This means we still
possess the crib that we cannot use safely. 

There are several photos showing the splinters that our child vomited when he choked.  We had to shrink the size of these photos to email them. If you need a higher quality photo just reply with the Image number and we will
send the original file.

[REDACTED]
justification: The child choked on a piece of wood but regurgitated it without requiring medical attention, indicating an injury without severe consequences.

incident_description: My 14 month old daughter was injured in the front crib slat of the Dream on Me Inc. 3 in 1 convertible crib, style no. 626 mfg. October 2012 on 6/13/14.  Looking at the front of the crib, she got her knee wedged in the front of the crib, 2nd or 3rd front slat from the right side of the front, and had twisted her body so she was stuck.  She was screaming her head off and this left bruising on her knee and thigh.  If I had been in the shower or something, she would have broken her leg.
justification: The child sustained bruising from being stuck in the crib slats, indicating an injury occurred.

incident_description:
Caller stated that her 18 month old grandchild legs were both entrapped between the crib slat all the way to the knees. Her legs were removed after much difficulty of twisting and turning. She received minor injuries such as redness and bruising.  Child's weight is 25 lbs.  No medical attention was received.

5/19/14  The manufacturer was contacted and she was informed that she should purchase a mesh to place around the bottom of the slats.

Caller feels that the crib slats are unsafe and should be reported.
justification: The child suffered minor injuries (redness and bruising) from being entrapped in the crib slats, warranting a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) as the incident was significant enough to prompt manufacturer contact and a safety recommendation.

incident_description:
My son was in the COSCO Beep Beep Beep walker and it needed to be lowered.  I should have removed him from the walker before lowering it, but I didn't.  I have seen my husband (who is much stronger than me) move it up or down with our son it it, so I didn't think anything about it.  When pushed the red button to lower the walker so my son's feet could touch the ground, both of my thumbs were pulled into the section that lowers the part the baby sits in.  There was no one home, and with BOTH of my thumbs stuck, and the weight of my son bearing down on my stuck thumbs, there was absolutely nothing that I could do.  Each time the seat part would lower more my thumbs would pull further into the part.  I was completely stuck, I was crying and my son was crying, so finally after being stuck for about 2 whole minutes I turned the walker sideways so my son fell out and I got my thumbs free.  It was a terrifying experience and my left thumb is still completely numb.  I have no feeling at all in it.

I understand that this is my fault since I left my son in the walker while I was trying to lower it, but I thought the manufacturer should know that this could happen.  Thank you!
justification: The incident resulted in injury (numbness in the thumb) and a terrifying experience, but no death or severe harm occurred.

incident_description: My husband was riding a bike with an Aosom Elite 2in1 Double Child Bike Trailer / Jogger attached to it. He was trying to cross a street when the trailer suddenly flipped over, just as he went over the curb. The curb was accessible for strollers, wheelchairs, and bikes, so this was very unexpected. My son, who is 2 years old, was wearing his seat belt and helmet, but he still sustained serious scrapes on his arms and hands. Some of the trailer mesh was damaged in the process.
justification: The child sustained serious scrapes, indicating injury (severity 3), but the incident was unexpected and involved proper safety measures, making recurrence unlikely (likelihood 2).

incident_description: My five month old was sitting in front of me holding her  Mam pacifier when she started crying. Next she started screaming terribly and I thought something was pinching her. When I picked her up she let go of her pacifier and I saw that it was lodged sideways deeply in her mouth. I could not remove it from her mouth, it was stuck. I called my husband and he eventually was able to remove it from her mouth, but it scraped up the roof of her mouth. She was bleeding from the roof of her mouth. The pacifier was a Mam air pacifier for 0-6 mo. She had just turned 5 months that day so I didn't think that I needed to buy her a bigger size.
justification: The infant suffered bleeding and injury to the roof of her mouth, indicating a severity level of 3 (Injury). The incident involved a common baby product, suggesting a possible likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description:
For Christmas, our son received a Fisher-Price Cruise and Groove Ballapalooza.  It is a great toy in which a ball is dropped from a device onto a trampoline, which sends it onto a spiral slide, to a ramp, then down to the bottom.  The ramp has on it a pinwheel/fan through which the ball passes.  There are sensors all over the device to trigger lights and music when a ball passes.

On Saturday, our son, who is now 16 months old (toy is advertised for children aged 6 to 36 months) was exploring the ramp area and discovered the sensor behind the pinwheel/fan.  He attempted to grab it, and got his fingers stuck between the pinwheel/fan and the sensor/ramp.  Pulling back made the matter much worse, as it pulled the pinwheel/fan up, tightening the space.  My wife and I were able to push it down to remove his hand, but it caused him a great deal of pain and distress.  We have since removed the pinwheel/fan altogether, and the toy works just as well without it.

A review of online reviews indicates we are not the first to experience this problem.

It is our opinion that Fisher-Price should be required to remove the pinwheel/fan from this toy, increase the space between the pinwheel/fan and sensor/ramp, or warn parents to remove the pinwheel/fan once children are old/tall enough to reach it.
justification: The incident caused pain and distress to the child, indicating an injury, and online reviews suggest it's a recurring issue.

incident_description: My life was forever changed two weeks ago, in a split second, when my three month old son and I were headed to the playground with my husband and three year old daughter. I was walking with my son, [REDACTED] , in an ergo front pack carrier when suddenly I tripped and fell.  [REDACTED] was facing inwards sound asleep when we fell.  I fell so hard and fast that I couldn't get my hands down in time to break my fall. My son [REDACTED] head hit the concrete while still in the pack and he sustained a serious head injury on the right side of his head.  We called 911 and paramedics rushed to the scene.  [REDACTED] was taken to [REDACTED] where we were told he would need to have emergency brain surgery.  He had a skull fracture, epidural bleed and swelling. The next two plus hours where a complete blur to me as we sat waiting for our precious newborn to come out of surgery.  Once the operation was finished we were told that his dura was also torn and repaired during the surgery and he required a blood transfusion.  The next 72 hours, [REDACTED] , would be in critical condition, his brain pressure was monitored, while blood was draining from his brain.  We were told if the pressure increased his condition could be fatal.  Luckily, my son survived but after 11 days in the hospital he is now still recovering at home.  We begin physical therapy this week as his left side was weakened due to the accident.  Also, no one can say what other long term affects might be.  Until the accident, I never realized how dangerous baby carriers can be. Surely, designs could be changed to make babies safer in the event a caregiver falls down while baby wearing.
justification: The infant sustained a serious head injury requiring emergency brain surgery and long-term recovery, indicating a high severity level.

incident_description:
Purchased a Meridian LED "Flower Power" auto on when dark-night light Item #10267  
UPC 8 7563800192 3 on June 7, 2014.  Took home plugged it in to see how it looked before putting it in the children's room.  As soon as we plugged it into the electric outlet the base exploded shooting electricity out and popping the base off and plug part was still in the wall.  It burned up the night light and the wall plug.  The circuit breaker thank goodness worked and killed the power to the outlet.  I will have to replace the outlet as well now.  The outlet was in perfect working order and has been used on a daily basis.  We tried another night light also purchased same day and it was fine.  I have photos of the night light after it exploded.
justification: The incident involved an explosion and electrical hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: My daughter whom is 16 months, got her leg stuck between the bars twice!

incident_description: I JUST WANT TO BRING ATTENTION TO THE CHOKING HAZARDS OF THE SOOTHIE PACIFIERS.  ABOUT 10 MINUTES AGO I HAD TO PULL ONE OUT THAT WAS ALMOST COMPLETELY LODGED IN MY SON'S MOUTH. THANK GOD I HEARD HIM CHOKING SO I COULD PULL IT OUT. HE WAS CRYING WHILE SUCKING HIS PACIFIER AND HAD ROLLED ONTO HIS STOMACH WHICH LED TO HIM SOMEHOW GETTING THE BINKY STUCK IN HIS MOUTH. incident_description: I purchased the Bright starts big kid rocker for my baby. It is a bouncer seat which claims you can use until they are 40 lbs. It has two straps which hook into a central hook. My child was strapped into the seat and when I went to remove her the small round piece which fits into the hook area was gone. Luckily I located it underneath of her but she or any baby could have easily eaten the small round piece. It came off the product completely and we have not even had the product for a month. It is a major choking hazard and any infant or toddler would put it in their mouth.
justification: The incident involved a choking hazard but no actual injury occurred, and the likelihood is high given the product's defect and typical child behavior.

incident_description: My five month old son was at day care with his newer Philips Avent pacifier for 6 to 18 months, the night one with the glow in the dark handle. he had been using the pacifier earlier in the afternoon. when he was sitting at the high chair table and the pacifier was on the table they noticed the nipple was partially detached from the holder. Both the day care staff and myself are alarmed that this is even possible. My son has no teeth and there is no way that this should have happen. the pacifier is obviously defective and could have become lodged in his throat  and god forbid he was unable to get care in time he could have died. I  have bought several of these pacifier and have since this incident collected them all and placed them out of reach from my son until I can find out from the company the problem with this product.
justification: The pacifier was defective but no injury occurred, though there was potential for serious harm.

incident_description: Today I was coming up my stairs and went to open the baby gate that I had installed two weeks ago. I had installed it exactly as the instructions said to and at the top of my basement stairs. It is clearly stated that this gate can be installed at the top of stairs. There are four plastic cups that bolt to the door frame and on each side of the gate there are two long bolts with threaded plastic pieces that twist the length of the bolt so you can tighten the round threaded pieces creating tension, this puts the threaded piece into the cup and secures it to the wall...or so I thought. You must lift the gate up and pull in the little lever with your thumb at the same time. The gate swings both ways and you have no control over who leaves it which way. As I came up the stairs I had to pull the gate towards me as I pushed in the thumb lever and pulled up. My hand slipped a bit and I ended up pulling on the gate more than I intended to as I did this the gate pulled out of the bolted cup and towards me, I fell backwards and hit the hand rail, fortunately I caught myself and only incurred minor bruises. When I looked at the gate I could clearly see that the bolt was not long enough to support the gate, there was only 1/4 of an inch going into the gate. My doorway is 30" and within the specifications listed for this gate. The cup that attaches to the wall/door frame is not deep enough to keep the plastic round piece that inserts into it from coming out if the gate is pulled on, intentionally or accidentally as in my case. It is not metal nor are the disks that are threaded to go up and down the bolt, it would appear the manufacturer tried to save some money here, which makes no sense as the the rest of this gate is metal. I paid a goodly price for a gate that is a SAFETY product, it clearly is NOT a safe product and should never be used at the top of stairs as it is made right now. Those cups should be steel and the bolt should be much longer, the threaded washers should also be steel. There is a two inch high bar on the bottom that runs the length of the gate, it too is a safety hazard because if you are unaware of it being there, don't look down, it is very possible to trip on. And when it is at the top of the stairs you are tripping forward. At the top of stairs this gate should not open both ways but only outward into a hallway or other space, never into the stairwell. This product should be recalled and replaced or parts sent to those who purchased it that will ensure its safe use. I am now officially terrified of this gate. I do not have the packaging as it has been in my house for two weeks, so I have no way to return it to Amazon.com where I purchased it. I am concerned with public safety.
justification: The incident resulted in minor bruises from a fall, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The design flaws in the baby gate make such incidents likely to occur (occurrence likelihood 4).

incident_description:
Fisher-Price Rainforest Melodies and Lights Deluxe Gym

Infant (7 months old, 7.0 kg) was laying on her back, playing with the dangling toys. The "butterfly arch" (which the toys hang from) separated from the "hub" of the "giraffe tube" and both the "butterfly arch" and "giraffe tube" collapsed around her. I replaced the arch and the tube to their proper positions, but they would not lock together. This was when I noticed my child gnawing on a small piece of plastic. Thankfully that was extent of her interaction with the toy. Upon further examination I found that the plastic piece was a broken piece of the inside of the "hub".

Not only did this event prove the toy to be unstable and unsafe for a child to play under, but that when it does break, it poses a choking hazard.

Fisher Price was contacted immediately. A replacement toy is being shipped to me and they have asked to send the broken piece of the toy to them.
justification: The infant was not injured but the toy broke, posing a potential choking hazard.

incident_description: My mother in law bought us the rock and play sleeper for my son who would not sleep flat in his crib anymore, it was working great. Yesterday, I took it apart to wash the outer piece and there was mold on the back of it. Last week my son had an upper respiratory infection and scared me to death. Obviously this product made him sick. I wash it frequently because he spills milk and drools in it a lot, sometimes he overflows his diapers, so it gets washed at least once a week. I see no good reason for this product to mold with that frequent of washing.
justification: The presence of mold led to a respiratory infection, indicating an injury.

incident_description: I received a Sophie the Giraffe as a gift for my baby.  I noticed that my son who is just beginning to teethe bit off a rubber piece of the giraffe's ear and I saw it in his mouth. I took the rubber piece out of his mouth before he swallowed it. There is now a hole on the tip of the giraffe's ear.  This is a horrible choking hazard.
justification: The baby did not swallow the rubber piece, so there was no injury, but the incident highlights a choking hazard.

incident_description: Mold formed on my childs Fisher Price Rock and Play sleeper.  I have had to take her to the dr for respiratory issues also.  I have scrubbed and scrubbed the sleeper but haven't been able to get it clean.
justification: Mold formation led to respiratory issues requiring medical attention, indicating an injury.

incident_description: I put my baby in his crib where the Bright Starts mobile was being used. I was watching it because I was a little weary of the product, because of how bulky it is and its placement above the baby's head. I walked to the other side of the room when I heard a loud popping noise. The clip holding the mobile to the crib had detached and the mobile fell onto my baby's head. This product does not attach well and is poorly designed. It could really hurt a child and I've read other reviews on the product saying the same thing happened to them. This item is not safe and should be recalled.
justification: The mobile fell onto the baby's head, indicating potential injury, and similar incidents have been reported by others, suggesting a design flaw.

incident_description: My daughter is 5 months old. The doctor recommended purchasing the fisher price "rock and play sleeper" when she was first born due to having severe reflux. Until last Friday May 9th, 2014 the product worked great. She slept in it every night and took her naps in it due to still having reflux and needed to be inclined. At her 6 month doctors appointment we were to discuss moving her to a crib or [REDACTED] now that she is bigger and starting to out grow the rock and play but not yet able to sit up and is only 14lbs. Friday we put her down for her nap like we normally do. Buckled her in to the rock and play, turned on the monitor, and went downstairs. About 5 minutes later we hear this awful screaming coming from our daughter upstairs. I run upstairs to find her on the floor and the rock and play still standing. I grabbed her, checked her for injures and rushed her to the nearest emergency room (Carroll County Hospital). Once there we tried to explain how it was possible that she was on the floor after being buckled in to the rock and play. The doctor checked her and found the strap marks on her legs and came to the conclusion that she must of pushed herself up (which she has never done before and can not sit up yet) and it rocked forward and when it rocked forward it flipped her out and she ended up on the floor. She was checked over had tests done and just ended up with a giant knot on her head, some nasty bruises but luckily nothing life threading or sever and was discharged. Before leaving the doctor asked me what kind of buckle it had and I explained only a waist buckle which was how she was able to fall out of this product. There is a warning clearing labeled on the product but it states don't use once child can sit or push up or after they reach 25 lbs so until this we were no concerned because she wasn't able to do any of the things listed and only weighs 14lbs. I later checked the website for any recalls or other incidents of this and only saw the one about possible mold. I know that normally infants are not still using this product at 5 months old but I'm sure we are not the only one and it scares me to think this could happen to someone else's child and could be much more serious. The product should be made with a shoulder strap since it does rock and this is a possible issue. We will never put her back in the rock and play and I hope something is done before someone else's child isn't hurt as well.
justification: The infant suffered a head injury and bruises from falling out of the rock and play sleeper, but no life-threatening or severe injuries were reported.

incident_description: After placing my ten month old in Phil and Ted's travel crib, he stood up by leaning against the mesh sides. He was able to physically flip the crib to the side. By jumping holding on the sides he lifted it off the ground. No child who can stand should be allowed to be in this crib
justification: The child was able to flip the crib but no injury was reported, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that she placed her 8 month old,21 pound granddaughter in the activity walker. Immediately after the locking mechanism failed and the seat collapsed downwards while the child was sitting. The child's legs were trapped between the walker's seat and the floor for approximately 5 seconds when the consumer was able to release and remove the child from the walker. The consumer noticed a blue bruise the size of a dime on the left side of her ribs. The consumer discontinued the use of this product.

4/8/14-The consumer reviewed the product on the retailer's web site.

4/8/11- The consumer plans to visit the retailer to return the product.
justification: The child sustained a minor injury (bruise) due to the walker's failure, warranting a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as such incidents are not uncommon with faulty products.

incident_description: I purchased a crib before my daughter was born on January 21, 2012 from Cymax.com it is a 	DaVinci Kalani 4-in-1 Convertible Wood Baby Crib w/ Toddler Rail. Since then she was born on [REDACTED] her legs and arms have been able to go through the slots of the crib. This has occurred several times when she was younger i just moved her arms and legs but now that she is older her knees get caught and it very hard to get them out. Today, in fact I put her down for a nap and it happened three times.  If I wasn't a diligent mother she could have been severely injured. I am concerned for other children who may have this crib as well.
justification: The child's limbs getting caught in the crib slots poses a risk of injury, though no injury was reported in this instance.

incident_description: I have the Fisher price nature touch cradle swing. It requires batteries. I put a fresh batch of batteries in it and turned it on. It immediately started smoking and under the dial/button spot started glowing. This swing has no lights on it. The glow was the swing sparking. We took the batteries out and it still smoked a little. After this I searched online for more reports of this and found many. This swing is unsafe. I was about to put my Son in it. Things for babies should not do that.
justification: The incident involved immediate smoking and sparking, posing a significant hazard, but no injury occurred as the child was not in the swing at the time.

incident_description: My daughter was in her crib napping and woke up screaming (something she never does). Upon going into her room to get her, I found her leg caught in the rail of the crib up to the top of thigh. This has happened on more than one occasion. I have never used bumpers as they are not recommended due to the potential of suffocation. It was extremely difficult to get her out and I noticed she had significant markings and bruising on her leg prior to getting it out from in between the rails.  I am beyond upset that this happened to my child and fear what could have happened. Companies need to be held responsible for these types of incidents.
justification: The child suffered significant markings and bruising, indicating an injury, and the incident has occurred multiple times.

incident_description: I have an Eddie Bauer high chair (dark wood but now the newest one that tilts) that I bought less than a year ago and only have been usig 2-3 months. We put it together after we purchased it. When we started using it a few months ago, we noticed that it was really wobbly. We tightened the screws, and that helped but now they are loose again. The product feels like it is going to fall apart. In addition, the lap belt does not stay locked at all. Everytime I put my little guy in and use the belt his (fairly moderate) wiggling make it come undone. Thirdly there is not enough padding behind his head, and when he wiggles, he often smacks his head in to the wood. He has gotten a bruise from it once. Although my little guy has not gotten hurt, I'm going to discontinue use as it is only a matter of time before something happens.
justification: The high chair's instability and faulty lap belt pose a risk of injury, as evidenced by the child already getting a bruise from hitting his head on the wood.

incident_description:
We bought Little Sprouts Self-feeders.   http://www.amazon.com/Baby-Food-Silicone-Feeder-Set/dp/B00I3OUPIC/ref=sr_1_1?ie=UTF8&qid=1399382304&sr=8-1&keywords=silicone+feeder

incident_description: The incident of mold occurred on the rock and play after using it for 8 months and now my goddaughter has had pneumonia and has been hospitalized 3 times with no known cause to why she was getting sick.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that her daughter started using the crib in July/August 2013. 

The consumer stated that when her daughter took out the mattress from the crib, she saw that the metal support frames have come off of the crib frame. The consumer stated that there was a gap between the frame and the support frame.

incident_description: Dangerous! The sling where you lay baby down will detach causing baby's head to go underwater and also cause head injury! The battery cover leaks the acid overall it's an accident waiting to happen my daughter only weights 16 pounds and it slipped she hit her head and swallowed a small amount of water! This need to be recalled ASAP I called the company and they said oh well we will send you the clips it really bothered me and I told the gentleman helping me well why don't you just put them in the box before people purchase them why do you guys wait for something to happened!

incident_description:
Regarding the Phil&Teds Peanut Bassinet for Smart Stroller:

We have used this product only a handful of times. It is advertised also as a sort of carrycot, it has handles to transport a newborn (up to 20 pounds) in the bassinet. Rarely do I use this feature, usually I just carry my 9 pound six-week old son in my arms and exclusively use the bassinet attached to the stroller. This evening we took it into a restaurant, just the bassinet part, carried it from the car to the restaurant by its handles and set it down near me so I could lay my son down if he fell asleep. Ideally, baby is safely and soundly transported by carrying him in the bassinet by its handles and back to the car. Thankfully, he woke up and I removed him from the bassinet. I then grabbed both handles of the bassinet to pick it up (with nothing in it!) and one of the handles broke! I cannot bring myself to imagine what could have happened to my son, or anyone else's baby, if he had been in it! This item must be recalled before anyone gets hurt.
justification: The handle broke during use, but no injury occurred as the bassinet was empty at the time.

incident_description: My baby has recently started rolling over onto her belly and some part of her leg has been getting stuck in between the slats of her Pali Lucca crib. This past week however was the worst and is prompting us to contact your organization because of the nature of the incident. Both of her legs were stuck in the slats (up in the air), titling her torso so that her belly was on the mattress and her face was planted in the mattress. Had I not been in the room or had my husband and I been sleeping, I fear she could have suffocated. It was clear she could not get herself out of the position. I am reporting this incident because of what could have happened to my baby and what could happen to someone else's baby. We purchased the crib from buybuybaby and have asked them to take it back. We have not received a reply.
justification: The baby's legs were stuck in the crib slats, posing a suffocation risk, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I purchased a crib from Target 6 months ago. It was a Delta 4 in 1 convertible crib in Black Cherry. We planned to have this crib and eventually turn it into a toddler bed when he was ready. However last month, my son was able to break the underneath wiring that the mattress lays on. It was very dangerous because the metal was sticking up and he could have easily impaled himself on it. He had done it after his nap and I wasn't able to run out and buy another bed until the next day so I had to rig the wires together with a wiring and it held for the night however I didn't sleep at all because I was terrified that he would fall through or impale himself from it coming undone. A child who is less than 30lbs (crib says up to 50 lbs), should NOT be able to break METAL. It shouldn't matter if a child jumps on it, pulls at it with his hands, or whatever. A 2 year old should not be able to snap metal. It's very dangerous!
justification: The incident involved a dangerous situation with potential for injury, but no actual injury occurred, and the likelihood is possible given the description of the event.

incident_description:
My son was playing in the Baby Einstein activity center, the one that just had a recall for the sun on a spring. We were shipped the replacement section for the sun part.  The replacement section has a yellow bee with blue wings on it, my son was playing with it and it had sprung back and hit him on the nose right by his right eye. Left a raised bruise about 1/2" long.  Luckily it wasn't a serious injury but this could happen to any child and had he been a little stronger, it could have done more damage.
I just wanted to make you aware in case it becomes a more widespread problem with other kids.
justification: The incident resulted in a raised bruise, indicating an injury, but no serious harm occurred.

incident_description:
I purchased a ring sling from ECHO resales in Madison Indiana, these slings are made and sold by the owner of the shop.

As I was wearing this sling it ripped apart and caused my son to fall to the ground, luckily we were over mulch so he only has some scratches but it could have been much much worse.

When I purchased this sling I was not aware of the safety issues involved in babywearing, I have now discovered that not only was the stitching not done safely but the fabric used was unsafe, not lead tested and the rings where not safe at all or lead tested either.

The owner of the store has threatened to sue me if I do not leave her alone, all I have done was ask that she gets her items up to safety standards, I never even asked for a refund but she refuses to take any accountability and actually has claimed she does not have to do anything legally.

So I am coming here to you.
justification: The incident resulted in a fall causing scratches, indicating an injury, and the unsafe product design suggests a likely recurrence if not addressed.

incident_description:
I received the Under the Nile Organic Veggie Corn teether as part of an AGE APPROPRIATE monthly shipment from the company Citrus Lane for my 6 month old daughter.

At first, my daughter loved teething on the top part of the "husk;" however, after only a few times playing with the toy I heard her COUGHING and turned to find her spitting out a CHOKING SIZE PIECE of the yellow fabric. The teether had fallen apart at the top where it was poorly constructed. I was HORRIFIED when I saw what happened.

I recommend not selling this product to anyone else unless it is marked as an "over the age of 3" product where the children are not going to be teething, putting everything in their mouths, and creating a potential choking hazard. I am not sure how the other Veggies are constructed, but this one certainly appears to be cheaply made. THIS TOY SHOULD NOT BE MARKETED TO INFANTS. End of story.
justification: The incident involved a choking hazard with a piece of the teether, posing a risk of injury to the infant.

incident_description: Caller reported that the amber teething necklace poses a risk of choking hazard.  She stated that it has beads and that infants pull on things and this is not safe.  Caller [stated] that she saw the product online and feels that the agency should investigate.
justification: The caller reported a potential choking hazard but no actual incident or injury occurred.

incident_description: My baby is 8 months old. When he was about 5 months old I noticed cuts on the back of his legs near his ankles. He moves his legs around a lot so I thought he just cutting himself on his toenails. This lasted a couple months. They then went went away for about a month and I figured that was because he was not kicking his legs as much. I noticed the cuts started to appear again. He always had it on the back of both legs, not just one leg. A couple weeks ago I picked him up out of his high chair, he was happy I was picking him up, then he kicked his legs back, and started screaming. That's when I realized the high chair was actually cutting his legs! It a plastic part that is so sharp on the bottom. Before the next feeding I had my husband cushion that piece so it could no longer cut him. It appears not only is he cutting himself when I pick him up, but also when he is just sitting in it and kicking his legs around. After thinking about it, I realized the only reason it went away for about a month was because it was really cold and I always had socks on him. I called the company - Ingenuity - a couple weeks ago to report the problem. They sent me a replacement high chair. I just received that chair in the mail today, and it has the same sharp plastic edge on it. I do not feel safe using this high chair.
justification: The baby sustained cuts from the high chair, indicating injury (severity 3). The issue recurred multiple times and was only temporarily mitigated by socks, making it likely (likelihood 4).

incident_description: This is a product attached to the Report No. 20140429-C302E-2147445003 I filed. My baby's legs were cut on a high chair. I called the manufacturer and they sent me a replacement. Unfortunately the replacement also had the same sharp edge like the chair I already owned. The replacement they sent me was a different model, which is why I'm filing this report. This report is for the replacement.
justification: The baby's legs were cut by the high chair, indicating an injury occurred.

incident_description: Purchased the crib brand new from Target last year. Chronically since then, the long rails come loose and wiggle. Even after constant tightening the rails still come loose. Contacted Delta to request assistance and was met by a rude representative who shipped out replacement rails. When I got the replacement rails, they were the incorrect rails. After repeated Facebook and phone attempts to contact the company to rectify this issue, I'm filing a report.
justification: The incident involves a product defect and poor customer service, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: My infant son's dream lite was on top of a toy box and was melting on its own.  It was not by a heater or turned on.  My husband could smell the burning.  Our house burnt down in January due to furnace issues.  My now 8 month old son received this as a gift, after the fire.  I could not imagine what may have happened.  This is a very unsafe product and needs to be recalled.  I wasn't able to get in contact with anybody despite trying several different numbers.  Most numbers were for delivery purposes.
justification: The incident involved a product malfunction (melting) that could have led to injury or death, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description:
On Saturday April 12, 2014, I was in the bathroom putting on makeup, when my two year old son came in to use the potty.  I put the Luvable Friends Potty Trainer Seat on the toilet and he got on and went potty.  When he got off, he started crying and I asked what was wrong, and that's when I saw blood.  The Potty Trainer Seat had cut my sons penis at the base and it was bleeding heavily.  I immediately grabbed a washcloth to put pressure on his penis while I dialed the pediatricians office.  As I was on the phone with them I got some gauze and put it on my son's cut and held it to help stop the bleeding.  The Pediatrician recommended that we come immediately to their office since it was closer than the hospital.  Once the Pediatrician saw his injury, she then sent us on to the [REDACTED] Emergency room where my son was treated with a butterfly stitch. I have contacted the manufacturer ([REDACTED] at Baby Vision) who denied that their product was defective and refused to turn in a claim to their insurance carrier. 
Our Luvable Friends Potty Trainer Seat that I purchased about 4 years ago from Amazon.com has a defect in the front of the seat that you can see and if you feel it, it is very sharp.
I am very concerned about this.  This was a very traumatic injury and I would hate for this to happen to another child.
justification: The incident resulted in a significant injury requiring medical treatment, but no long-term harm or death was reported. The likelihood is unlikely as it appears to be a rare defect in the product.

incident_description: After I bathed my son i noticed I had no more diapers left in his drawer so I went and opened a brand new pack out of a unopened box of pampers swaddlers size 2. I put the diaper on my son and gave him his bottle and put him down for his nap. When his dad arrived home from work he went in to our sons bedroom and picked him up and started to change him. When he took the diaper off he screamed for me to come in and when I walked in my son had the WORST rash/burn on his butt from the back all the way to the front. My son has nerve had diaper rash before and rarely ever cries so I knew that something was wrong as he was screaming worse then I've ever heard him scream! I immediately called his pediatrician and she advised me to come in. When we went In the doctor proceeded to tell me that it was a chemical burn from something in the diaper most likely the chlorine. She told me to put [REDACTED] ointment on so his urine or a bm wouldn't be able to burn him even more. My son had this burn on him for over a week! When I contacted pampers the 1st time the supervisor basically brushed me off and said "we will reimburse you for your diapers hope he feels better." I was concerned about the refund I was more concerned about these diapers being taken off of the shelfs so other children didn't get burned by this batch! Unsaturated with the way this supervisor responded to my call I called back and asked for a manager. Well let's just say she was just as rude if not worse then the supervisor! I told her I wanted contacted when their team did some investigation and she said they don't do that. She also advised me to keep the diapers incase they want them for research. It's now been 1 month and the only thing that has happened is I received a letter saying sorry and a 30 dollar prepaid [REDACTED] *which I don't care about AT all! I'm beyond disgusted with pampers and refuse to use them ever again! I used them and only them for the first 6 months of my sons life and I switched to [REDACTED] as soon as this happened! Someone needs to do some investigating with this because I know a few moms that have been threw this!
justification: The incident resulted in a chemical burn injury to the child, warranting a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 2 (unlikely) since such incidents are not common but have been reported by a few other parents.

incident_description: Child tugged on pacifier clip string and the plastic area where it bends broke and left a few pieces to be cleaned up
justification: The incident involved a broken pacifier clip with no reported injury, only requiring cleanup.

incident_description:

The consumer stated that if her daughter would have bitten any more into the ring, the grooves of the teething ring would have [come] off. The consumer stated that her daughter could have ingested the material.

incident_description: Baby was being rocked to sleep while sucking on a Monkey Wubbanub pacifier toy. It is a pacifier attached to a stuffed monkey. Baby started sucking on the monkey's leg. The baby started flailing around. He was not making any sounds through his mouth. Looked down to see that the baby had shoved the leg completely in his mouth and could not breathe through his mouth. Toy was removed and baby was ok.
justification: The baby could not breathe due to the toy blocking the airway, but no injury occurred as the toy was removed in time.

incident_description:
I sent this email to the company describing the product faulty. 

Hi, I bought 2 Munchkin Pacifier Clips today for my 4 months old after having used one with my first child and I found it to be the best pacifier clip around. I have seen many people selling on markets and eBay and other brands try to imitate Munchkin clip but I thought their the metal clip where the ribbon attaches to isn't of a good quality which could pose choking hazard. I liked the fact that with Munchkin clip the inner white plastic parts which are attached to the metal clip are secured with metal bits so I don't have to worry about them coming off and posing choking hazard. So I was shocked when I got home and had a closer look at the metal clips and I saw that the round plastic part which attaches to the metal clip has a split that will allow it to fully come off and pose a choking hazard just like other Pacifier clip that I have been intentionally avoiding to use! I am distressed with the thought of if I hadn't seen it what might have happened.

And their response to this was that "all of our munchkin products do meet and exceed all federal safety requirements" "If you are not pleased with your purchase, please let me know so we can replace it with other items that is comparable in price."

They are shockingly not concerned at all about the product faulty, the danger that it presents let alone improving the product quality.
justification: The incident describes a potential choking hazard in a product, but no actual injury or death has occurred.

incident_description: Mold found on product
justification: Mold on product is an incident with no immediate injury, but poses potential health risks.

incident_description: I recently changed from pampers baby dry to pampers cruisers diapers.  We haven't tried new foods, haven't had any significant changes in our life, but in the past week my daughter has developed a very uncomfortable rash in her groin and anal area.  It is extremely painful to touch.  I am very diligent about diaper changes as I have never wanted her to get a rash and use coconut oil as well as [REDACTED] cream on her to prevent the rashes from occurring.  The [REDACTED] cream and coconut oil have not helped and my daughter screams in pain every time I have to change her diaper.  Today, the rash is spreading to her legs and I have given her [REDACTED] to ease the pain.  It is heart breaking.
justification: The child has developed a painful and spreading rash, indicating an injury caused by the diaper change, despite preventive measures.

incident_description: On Tuesday evening April 8, 2014 I was in my daughters room putting away laundry and my  three year old daughter was sitting on the bed and my six year old son was sitting on the floor playing at the foot of the bed. There were two other adults with me in the room looking at some clothing. As we were talking I heard a very loud noise, and turned around to see that the bed had collapses pinning my son between the footboard and another piece of furniture and my daughter had fallen off of the bed and hurt her arm. Upon closer inspection, the screws from the rails had completely stripped from the fooboard and caused it to fall forward. Thankfully the fooboard hit the other piece of furniture instead of landing on my son causing him to be seriously injured. My daughters arm was very red and she complained about her elbow, but thankfully it was just a bruise. The furniture was from the Munire Bristol Collection that I purchased in the spring of 2011.
justification: The daughter suffered a bruised arm, which constitutes an injury, and the son was at risk of serious injury but was unharmed.

incident_description: I was potty train my almost 3 year old son. He was sitting on the potty trying to do his thing. He started leaning back and the lid popped off causing him to fall backwards and in doing so he severely scratched up his bum on the corners of the seat where the lid clicks in and out. If you are going to make a lid that pops on and off why not round off the corners. I never knew the lid would do this an leave such sharp edges exposed.
justification: The child suffered severe scratches from falling on the potty seat's sharp edges, indicating an injury.

incident_description: Delta Crib N Changer Style 7500-100 Lot: SC12046 Date: 201209.  The changing pad has a space where baby's hand fits and if a parent does not realize the baby's hand is there when picking up baby, this can result in a broken hand.  It almost happened to my baby so I now roll and fit a blanket in that area.  My son is now four months to pushes the blanket with his hands sometimes, so I still have to look and be very careful
justification: The description indicates a near-miss incident with potential for injury (broken hand) but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: my child pulled the SUN and it snapped open and he continued to chew on the plastic which is sharp under neath the actual sun and it sliced inside his mouth he was bleeding then as the plastic sliced inside his mouth her jerked his head back and the plastic cut his lip on the outside.
justification: The child suffered cuts inside the mouth and on the lip, resulting in bleeding, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description: We have an InStep Quick N EZ Double Bicycle Trailer (colors are blue and grey) which is a few years old (possibly 2008).  The safety harnesses/child seat-belt restraints are disintegrating (dry rot) and have come unattached.   I've written a letter to the manufacturer, but I do not see any recall information for this and it seems like a safety issue, though we noticed this before use and no one has been injured. It is the item pictured in this photo on their website:  https://www.instep.net/biketemplates/instep/images/pz.jpg    https://www.instep.net
