incident_description: We have two fisher price rock and play sleepers that have mold on them. There are recalls on these items what should we do? Return them? We've had them since May of 2013. Our son has had a few respitory problems as well.  This is ridiculous
justification: Mold on the sleepers and respiratory problems in the child indicate a potential health impact, warranting a severity level of 3.

incident_description:
Caller purchased a porta-crib October 27th, 2013 and had no problems until February 17th, 2014 when she heard her baby daughter crying.
She reached to pick her 13 month old daughter up but saw that the baby's right leg was caught between the bars up to above her knee and could not get loose.
The caller was afraid the baby mights break her leg due to panic and thrashing around trying to remove her leg from between the slats.
The caller was at her mothers and fathers house and yelled for help thinking that there was a possibility that the slats were cutting the circulation off in her daughters leg.
When they could not loosen the baby's leg from between the slats within a few moments the caller's father got a saw and sawed the slats to release the baby's leg.
When they removed the baby from the porta-crib her right leg was very red but not injured.
The caller treated her baby's leg with ice packs.

No physician was involved
She contacted the manufacturer on March 19th, 2014 and spoke with [REDACTED] who took a report but did not provide a report number.
He did ask if this caller would like for the manufacturer to send her replacement slats to which she replied that she did not because she had no intention of using the product again.
She put the porta-crib outside for refuse pick up when the incident happened.
justification: The baby's leg was caught and reddened but not injured, indicating an incident without injury.

incident_description:
The baby was bouncing in the activity center (set in the rocking mode) when suddenly the baby leaned forward and the tray tilted over. The baby came out flying out of the activity center.  
He fell on the floor face down, hitting his forehead and losing his breath. The babyÃÂs grandmother picked him up and started blowing air into his face. ÃÂThe consumer specifically indicated that she blew breaths of air over the babyÃÂs face.ÃÂ   After a few moments the baby stated to breathe again. 
The baby had a big bump on the left side of the forehead. The consumer proceeded to take the baby to Saint ChristopherÃÂs ChildrenÃÂs Hospital, Philadelphia, PA, right after the incident.
The doctor diagnosed the baby with a mild concussion. 

The consumer will provide more medical information when she receives the report for her review.
 
Notes:  This product has been recalled (CAP# 09-131) according to the model number and when it was manufactured. The incident type is different from the ones described in the recall notice, since the activity center tilted over.
justification: The baby suffered a mild concussion and a bump on the forehead, indicating an injury (severity 3). The occurrence likelihood is possible (3) as the incident type differs from the recall notice.

incident_description: This excersaucer has three stages. The third stage is for an older baby that can stand and play with toys. The toy turns into an a S shaped platform on 4 legs.  When my daughter played with it it has tipped over on two occasions. I have looked online and found many other people that had the same problem and was to make home fixes.  When I called evenflow they told me " the child should not put their weight on it", in theory that makes sense but explain that to a 14 month old baby, not very realistic to expect a baby to not lean on a toy while playing.  This should not be on the market
justification: The excersaucer tipping over poses a risk of injury to the child, as evidenced by multiple reports of the issue and the impractical expectation for a baby not to lean on it.

incident_description:
I came in to get my 15 month old twins once I heard them up and stirring from their afternoon naps all to find one of my boys surrounded by vomit that included a giant screw mixed in it. Turns out the screw came loose from his crib, and he must have nearly choked on it. After further investigating, we later found two other loose screws in another corner of the crib and a third had fell off. His brother has the same crib and for some reason, all of the screws on his were tightly secure. 

Even though the manual says to check the screws manually, there shouldn't be any screws in any location where my baby could access them in the first place. The idea of screws on the interior of the crib where a parent might not notice them getting loose but a baby can get their hands on them is very scary.


FYI: These are the model cribs we have, which were purchased from Cribs to College in Naperville.

http://www.simplybabyfurniture.com/52v127.html?CS_003=23651609&CS_010=52v127&gclid=CJDBz6Cbn70CFbFaMgodznkAOQ
justification: The baby nearly choked on a loose screw from the crib, indicating a potential for serious harm, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: I have been using the recalled rock and play from fisher price since my child was born. She has had constant screaming pains and thrush and infections. So now i will be taking her back to the doctor to be fully checked out due to the mold to see if there is any extended health issues.
justification: The child has experienced health issues (screaming pains, thrush, infections) potentially linked to the recalled product, indicating injury.

incident_description: I removed the cover of our Fisher Price rock n play sleeper for the first time today to wash it and discovered mold between the cover and the hard under shell.
justification: Mold was discovered, which is an incident but no injury or harm was reported.

incident_description: I purchased 2 different Summer Infant Right Height Bathtubs and with the first one, the stitching came undone on one of the clips for the newborn sling and dropped my infant sharply into the tub full of water. The second one hasn't even been removed from the plastic and I can clearly see that only HALF of the stitching is intact on the sling clip.
justification: The incident involved a product defect causing an infant to drop into water, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
My son woke up screaming (instead of crying) from his nap. When I entered his room I found him face down on the mattress with both legs stuck in the crib slats. His left leg was stuck up above his knee, almost to his thigh. It was very difficult to free him because every slight move I made caused him to scream in pain. I was able to remove his right leg quickly but his left leg was stuck so tightly that I thought I would have to cut the wood slats. It took over a minute to free him - I had to lift his whole body up with one arm and work his pants up to allow for some slight give. He was distraught and now has several bruises on his left leg (which I documented). 

THIS IS THE SECOND TIME THIS HAS HAPPENED. The first incident occurred roughly 6 months ago. Again, one leg was trapped and it led to extensive bruising. I did not report because I figured it was an isolated incident.

Attn: Babyletto/MDB Rep - do not reply with a canned "we follow industry standards" response. We can read your previous responses! I am trying to alert other consumers and the industry to consider different standards in the future! I hate the thought of converting to a toddler bed because honestly he is not ready for that. He is <35", and has never attempted to climb his crib! He just rolls around a lot in his sleep!
justification: The child suffered bruises and significant distress, indicating an injury, and this has happened twice in six months.

incident_description: Bassinet was being used in my home for my newborn pre-mature infant when I first came come from the NICU.  Despite LOCKING the rocking mechanism, the rocker still tilted and as a result my newborn was rolled onto the side of the railings and became trapped against the side rail bedding.  I assumed it was my fault for not locking the rocker properly the first time but this happened a second and third time before I finally realized it is a faulty locking mechanism and a serious suffocation danger.   After each incident my infant spent several minutes gasping after being removed from the corner of the bassinet.
justification: The infant was trapped and gasping for air, indicating physical distress and potential injury, but no death occurred.

incident_description: I found black mold spots on my babies rock and play. We have only been using it for a couple of months. We have the Fisher-Price My Little Lamb Platinum Edition Deluxe Newborn Rock 'n Play Sleeper with Vibration. There was mold on the cushion and between the insert and the hard plastic.
justification: Black mold exposure can lead to respiratory issues or allergic reactions, posing a health risk to the baby.

incident_description: My daughter was using the "London Frog Bounce and Sway" seat and the entire seat flipped over onto its side.  It appears as though the base is not sturdy enough to prevent the seat from turning over.  My husband and I were shocked because she was buckled into the seat and we were closely watching her.  It seems very unsafe and the base needs to be adjusted to support the weight of infants.
justification: The seat flipped over but no injury was reported, indicating an incident without injury; the description suggests this is likely to happen again due to the base's instability.

incident_description: My 9mo. old son was in the Cosco Funsport Playard (Giraffe Print) for about 15 minutes and started screaming.When i ran to see what happened I didn't see his head just his body.The board that folds up and is used for the base unlocked from inside and made it so my son thought he could go under,but he tried head first and the weight of his body pushed down at that moment and I don't think he could scream but some how his body was able to move enough so he could and thats when I saw him and tipped the playard over holding the board up with one hand and with the other I pulled my son out.His face was red and neck had a redish/blue line a cross it.
justification: The child sustained visible injuries (red face and neck marks) but no long-term harm or death occurred, indicating a severity level of 3. The incident was unlikely as it required specific conditions (board unlocking and child attempting to go under).

incident_description:
(02/22/2014) The consumer stated that he had just put the baby in the highchair. The baby was sitting in the chair about 10 minutes when the chair collapsed straight down. The consumer stated that he is the grandparent and doesnÃÂt know how much the child weighs. The child is 18 months old.  

The child did not get injured.

The consumer stated that there are plastic pieces that are located on the back of the legs that support the chair. These pieces broke off and the entire chair came down.
justification: The highchair collapsed but the child was not injured, indicating an incident without injury. The likelihood is possible given the description of broken plastic pieces causing the collapse.

incident_description:
This is the message I sent Fisher Price on their Facebook page: 
I am extremely upset, irritated, and angered over the BEST product you put out: the Rock 'N Play infant sleeper. We purchased our first one for our little girl and it was the smartest purchase we made. After your recall was made in Jan 2013 due to mold growth, we inspected ours and tried our best to clean it according to your instructions; it did not work. Understandably these things happen. We had to throw that one away and purchased a new one a short time later since we were expecting our second child. We began using it and wash the outer fabric frequently. Upon removing the liner yesterday I noticed mold growth on this product purchased AFTER the recall.
 UNACCEPTABLE, Fisher-Price. 
I trusted the products you put out after the recall would be deemed safe. Our 6 month old son was in the ER on Sunday with respiratory illness. It makes me sick to think this could have been from the Rock 'N Play sleeper. 
Does the recall that was made in Jan 2013 affect all future products?!? If so, that should have been made clear because I can assure you I would not have put my son at risk.
justification: The incident involves a respiratory illness in a 6-month-old child potentially linked to mold exposure, indicating an injury.

incident_description: My 11 month-old daughter was playing with her Infantino Go GaGa Stack, Sort & Ball Drop Elephant when I noticed she was holding the speaker in her hand, about to bite onto it. The wires had dislodged from the inside of the product, but was still attached to both the speakers and the toy.
justification: The child was about to bite exposed wires, which could have led to injury, but no actual harm occurred.

incident_description: We have a Fisher Price sleep n play. My son uses it to sleep in due to his reflux. We have used it for 8 months and wash and clean regularly. Today I went to clean it and it was covered in mold. My son has been treated for pneumonia, ear infections, cough, and other respiratory issues in the last month. I don't know if this is why, but He quit sleeping in this on 2/26/14 and everything cleared up. I didn't  know about the recall until today when discovering the mold because we got this from a friend. We now have a large medical bill due to his pneumonia and other office visits. I have also tried to clean this by soaking it in a tub with bleach 2 and scrubbing with a hard scrubber and it has not come clean.
justification: The child suffered from respiratory issues and pneumonia, likely linked to mold exposure, indicating injury.

incident_description:
To Whom It May Concern:
Last Monday (2/24/14) I put my son to bed expecting what every mother expects. That is a good night sleep for their children & to wake up the same way they went to bed & thatÃÂs safe & healthy. The next morning (2/25/14) I woke up to a terrifying sight. My sons head was scraped & scratched from one side to the other. He moves around when he sleeps. I took him to the doctor to make sure that it was nothing more serious. The doctor literally walked into the exam room & looked at my sons head & said that it was lacerations to keep his head clean with warm & soapy water & to keep antibiotic ointment on it so it doesnÃÂt get infected. I got home from the doctor around 2 oÃÂclock in the afternoon & at 2:30 after I was done giving my son a bottle & changing his diaper I started my phone calls with the manufacturing company so that I could make them aware of what had happened. I got through the first customer service representative that helped me to set up my complaint file so I could get transferred to the appropriate department so I could get help. Thank You For Your Time,

justification: The child suffered lacerations requiring medical attention, indicating an injury.

incident_description: Baby was playing with Sophie teether while on her tummy. Baby was chewing on the teether's leg and laid her head on the ground. As her head went to the ground, the leg became lodged in her throat and she began gagging and choking. I had to run over to her to dislodge the leg. It was so far down her throat that I don't believe she would have been able to dislodge the leg on her own.
justification: The baby choked on the teether and required intervention, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: My son was playing with the baby teething toy Sophie the giraffe.  I looked over at him, and the leg of the toy was lodged down his throat and he was choking.  This is a very unsafe toy.
justification: The child was choking on the toy, which is a serious incident but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description:
The gate portion of the room divider has fractured in two(2) seperate locations resulting in instability as well as the ability for a child to exit/enter with limited restriction. The fractured locations also present with jagged edges that could result in injury. The fractures appear to have occured at a NON-seam location but they do seem to be the same type and size of fracture in the plastic.

I have digital pictures available for review and the gate is still in my possession.
justification: The fractured gate presents jagged edges that could cause injury, and allows unrestricted child access, indicating a potential hazard.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that her kids were playing with the product. The consumer's daughter is 1.5 years old and her son is 3.5 years old. 

The consumer stated that the product ripped from the bottom (about 12in long rip). The consumer stated that the rip occurred on the the bottom side that is used to fold up the product. 

The consumer's daughter was playing with the product and got her neck caught in the rip. The consumer stated that the product started folding while her daughter's neck was caught up. The consumer stated that the product twisted around her daughter's neck. 


The consumer's husband was able to untwist the product and get their daughter out of the product.

The consumer contacted the manf this morning and left a message. The consumer is waiting to hear back from them.
justification: The incident involved a child getting her neck caught in a rip, which could have led to injury or worse, but no actual injury was reported.

incident_description: I was bathing my daughter in the Summer Infant tub.  She is 5 months old and does not yet sit up on her own. I was using the bathing insert for support for her. As the material of the head support got wet it seemed to stretch out. It stretched so much that it was no longer right around the frame. It collapsed inward, causing her head to drop down into the tub. There is so warning of the possibility of the material stretching and causing this kind of accident. This could've easily been a very serious injury. I tried to contact the Summer Infant brand by phone, email and Facebook, none of which were successfully. I haven't received a response from the email or Facebook message and I was never even able to get through by phone.
justification: The incident involved a potential hazard with the bathing insert, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: Baby Einstein Sea Dream Soother was mounted securely to infant crib. With the slightest bump it fell , hitting my infant 3 month old son in the head. After calming him and seeing he was okay I proceeded to examine the cause of the incident. I found that the latch system isn't secure. With the slightest tug it easily came unlatched. Not only did it come unlatched the the inner piece of the latch broke off. Not only is this a dangerous cause for injury, but this could also become a choke hazard. I feel that I wasted my money on this toy and also feel that it is very cheaply put together for a high buying price. This product needs to be taken off the market and recalled immediately before a baby is severely injured. I will continue to try to get my money back.
justification: The incident caused the toy to fall and hit the infant, but no injury was reported, indicating a severity level of 2. The latch system's failure suggests the occurrence likelihood is high.

incident_description:
My baby was playing with his pacifier (Mam Trends) -- he often pulls it out, and in the process of trying to put it back into his mouth will turn it around and end up sucking on the little knob on the back. Suddenly he started shrieking. I looked down, and saw that he had managed to wedge the paci into his mouth sideways, with the lip of the knob stuck behind his lower gum, and the edge of the side of the paci wedged behind his upper gum. 

I reached down to remove it, but I couldn't get it out. It was wedged really well. I finally had to yank it out, causing the gums and the roof of his mouth to be scraped.
justification: The baby's gums and the roof of his mouth were scraped, indicating an injury.

incident_description: I purchased the Creations Summer Evening 4 in 1 convertible sleigh crib in antique black in November 2012.  My son has been sleeping in it since he was 3 months old (born [REDACTED]) and he just turned 1 last week, so in the 9 months he's been using it we never had a problem until a couple days ago.  My son starting screaming like I've never heard before only a few minutes after putting him in his crib for a nap.  I went in to find his leg trapped above his knee and twisted in the slats on the back side up against the wall.  I pulled the crib out from the wall and tried to remove his leg, but it wouldn't budge at all.  My husband and I tried to wiggle it free for about 5-10 minutes to no avail, fearing that his little leg would break or cut off circulation, my husband was about to break the wood slats with his hands but I decided to finally lather the leg and crib slats in globs of soft butter instead and was able to free him up.  This was very traumatizing for all of us and I don't know what the solution is, but I pray it doesn't happen to us or anyone else ever again.
justification: The child's leg was trapped and at risk of injury, but no actual injury occurred, warranting a severity level of 3. The incident is unlikely to happen frequently, hence an occurrence likelihood of 2.

incident_description:
Sophie the Giraffe

When I purchased this there was a piece of the rubber on the head of the giraffe that had been torn/pulled away from the horn on the top of the head.  I had to pull this off because it was coming lose and could have been a choking hazard for my daughter.  Now there is a hole in the back of the head that I could only assume is going to get bigger as she chews on it and in turn the whole horn could fall off.  On the stuffed animal giraffe the ear is only sewn on half way.  Therefore, it is very easy to pull off and will also be a choking hazard.

I googled a customer service phone number for the company and got a telephone number on the same web page as a form I could email.  I called this number and a guy named [REDACTED] answered.  He sounded surprised and bothered to get my phone call.  He started asking me where I got his phone number from.  I then told him I was trying to file a complaint about this product and asked who I could talk to.  He told me that I could talk to him but he did not sound happy about it all.  When I advised him of the problems he told me that it must be something that I did to the product because they have sold over 50 million of this products.  I advised him that all I have done was run the rubber giraffe under water to rinse it off and that was it.  I have not even washed the stuffed animal giraffe.  When I told [REDACTED] this he told me that it must be from a dog chewing on it.  I advised him that my dogs are not allowed near my daughter's toys so it was not from them.  When I advised him that I understood that he might have sold 50,000 of these products but mine was defective, [REDACTED] corrected me in the middle of my sentence by telling me that he actually sold 50 million not 50,000. [REDACTED] then told me that he has received several frivolous complaints about the product (which to me meant he did not believe anything I was saying).  Then he asked me to send him pictures of the defects, which I complied.  However, [REDACTED] should have just asked for the pictures in the first place so he could investigate the problem instead of treating me like a liar to begin with.
justification: The incident describes a defective product with potential choking hazards but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: I was changing my 7 weeks old baby's diaper when I noticed something tiny and dark in the diaper around the waist band. it was a sharp metal shard. I looked at the other diapers and found that they also had small metal shards .
justification: The presence of sharp metal shards in diapers poses a potential injury risk, but no actual injury was reported in the description.

incident_description:
Caller purchased her baby's jumper from Babies R Us in June 2011 and wasn't aware of any problems until the Sun toy attached to it was recalled July 23rd, 2013 with release# 13-244.
She contacted the firm's recall hotline and obtained the bumble bee toy that replaced the sun.

February 17th, 2014 her 6 month old son was playing with the replacement bumble bee toy while sitting in his jumper and the stick for it easily broke.
Caller is reporting due to the potential of harm to her baby and any others this could happen with.
There are no injuries to report
She contacted the manufacturer February 17th, 2014 and is being shipped a second replacement toy at manufacturer expense.
justification: The incident involved a broken toy with potential for harm, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description:

incident_description:
We have a fixed-side Oeuf Sparrow crib that we purchased in September 2010.  During my son's nap, he was able to pull off the top panel of the side panel of the crib, causing all the side spindles to come loose, and he then fell out of the crib. At that point he was screaming that he had hit his head.  I should add that my son is VERY small at 5th percentile for his age and not strong.  The nature of this defect meant that he also could have been strangled by the loose spindles, which splayed.

On closer inspection and comparison to my daughter's crib by a different manufacturer, I see that this is a very defective design.  The only thing securing the entire side panels of the crib to the headboard and footboard are small beads of WOOD GLUE.  No screws.  This wood glue obviously had dried to the point that the whole side panel was not secured to the headboard except by a vertical dowel.  My son, three years old, therefore was simply able to lift the top rail of the side panel, which made all the spindles come loose, and fall out.  I have a succession of pictures showing the exact nature of this defective design, which is all the more surprising given the high price tag of this high end designer.  I cannot believe that there are no screws holding the side panels and end panels together to ensure the structural integrity of the crib.

My daughter's crib, by a less expensive manufacturer, has screws that secure the side panels of the crib to the headboard and footboard.
justification: The child fell out of the crib and hit his head, indicating an injury, and the design defect could have led to strangulation, a severe risk.

When I looked more closely, I realized that the nipple was large enough for her to suck on, then the base part covers her nose, up almost to her eyes. We had a few more incidents like this, until if finally clicked in my sleep deprived brain, to watch it every single time.  
She is 6 months old now, and we still find ourselves having to be extra careful especially when feeding her in her carseat.  The angle she sits at, you can't see her face while feeding her, and it does the same thing.  She is old enough now though, that when it happens you can hear her  trying to "suck in" and get her breath around it, and know to move it.   I'm just worried that someone else may not notice until it's too late.

incident_description: We received the Munchkin Precision Digital Bottle Warmer as a baby shower gift for our now 2 month old son. After approximately two weeks of use the unit began to beep, buzz, and power off randomly during the course of a heating cycle. Upon powering off the unit would stay seemingly in an unpowered state for a few seconds to a few minutes before powering back on automatically without user input. The unit inconsistently would "reset" to an empty timer (0:00), a timer of 1:33, or show 0:00 and begin a heating cycle (again without user input) that would continue until the unit was unplugged. We immediately discontinued use of this product upon these observations out of fear of a fire hazard should the unit begin an unlimited/unsupervised heating cycle. incident_description:
My four-year-old son was jumping in a friend's Little Tikes Shady Jump 'n Slide Bouncer (item 620089, product website here: http://www.littletikes.com/dry-bouncers/shady-jump-n-slide-bouncer/invt/620089 ).  It was set up on an enclosed porch with a cement floor.  The [fastener] vertical yellow opening on the back of the bouncer had been fastened with the [fastener] pieces that are sewn along the edge, and there were adults, including myself, supervising right in front of the open side of the bouncer (which has a slide and no net wall).

My son landed in a sitting position and immediately tipped backwards, against the vertical yellow [fastener] line in the net.  The [fastener] instantly opened up, offering no apparent resistance, and he continued falling backwards rotationally, out of the bouncer, landing on the back of his head on the concrete floor, with his feet in the air and part of his upper body against the lower sidewall of the bouncer.  There was a loud "smack" noise as I rushed around the bouncer from the slide side to the opposite [fastener] side.  My son was in quite a bit of pain and got a large raised bruise on his head.  We put an ice pack on the area and had him rest (no more jumping).  We are watching for symptoms of concussion, as my son doesn't recall falling out of the bouncer.

The similar non-shaded version of this bouncer ("Jump 'n Slide Bouncer," item 620072 ) does not have an opening in the back net.  I don't know why the shaded version (620089) has this opening at all.  Because it's on the opposite side from the open slide, which also has to be monitored, and because the [fastener] completely failed to hold the opening shut, despite its appearance of secure closure, I consider this rear opening a safety issue, and hope that Little Tikes will take steps to address this hazard.
justification: The child suffered a head injury with a large bruise and potential concussion symptoms, indicating a severity level of 3. The incident occurred despite supervision, suggesting a possible design flaw.

incident_description:
My daughter was injured rocking normally with parental supervision.

 There are a ton of reviews of this product on Amazon that mention the same concern.  The implication that a parent is not watching their child when using the product, implies that the child could safely operate it on their own without concern for injury.  This product is not sturdy at all.  "Designed for 10 months and up" is inaccurate. We never felt it was safe for a child of any age or weight.  The front of the rocker slides forward with the slightest movement and it sways side to side so easily that when we tested it with a doll, the doll went flying off.   The ladybug is not properly attached to the base nor are the proportions of material safe for use.  There is no belt and the handles are too far away for the average toddler's arms to adequately reach them. 

To ensure it wasn't operator error, we've attempted to use the rocker numerous times and each time, if we were to let go of her or not hold onto to our child, the rocker would flip her forward, landing her on her head and then the rocker would flip on top of her.

It is my belief that this product is a consumer hazard and should be taken off the market. It SHOULD NOT be sold or handed down, but destroyed.

For another report about this product, please see:
http://www.saferproducts.gov/Search/Result.aspx?cid=18057&dm=0&q=Ladybug&srt=0

I am extremely shocked at the poor quality and finish of this product.I shudder to think that it could have been a very different outcome had I not noticed the splinter.  I would have expected a safe  product from babies r us. This crib is unusable because the mesh won't protect the baby for long, as soon as he starts moving more this will happen again. I discussed the issue with babies r us, they have refunded the crib amount  after a long discussion and time. I am discarding this crib, after all the time , money and effort put into it. incident_description:
On October 13, 2013 I purchased a Munchkin bobble bee suction toy for my infant from the Fort Campbell Blvd Walmart in Clarksville, TN. My husband and I tried to figure out what was wrong and realized that his middle finger on his left hand was stuck in the neck of the bee toy. After the toy was removed his finger sustained swelling and his fingernail started to bruise. I have photos of the toy and injury it caused. I request that this toy be removed from the shelves so that no other child has to have their finger stuck in the toy. 

Thank you.

incident_description: I purchased the petite paradise room in a box from burlington coat factory. My son has not received any injuries, but I'm worried he might or someone else's child might. The wood nor the finish is good. While teething my son has bit all the finish off an on October 2nd I realized he is now biting little strips of wood off.. im sure that can not be good. incident_description: I called Storkcraft manufacturing to report an issue I was having with my crib. I bought this crib in 2006 for my step-son and this was used approximately 1 year. This is a convertible crib, so usage for 1 year should not warrant the crib encountering problems. I recently put this crib back together for my 1-year-old and noticed immediately the base of the crib was bowing. This crib is also a drop side and I figured I could call for both issues at the same time. When I spoke to the woman, she said the crib should have a piece to go across the bottom and support the base. There is neither this piece she is speaking of or a place for this piece to screw in. She said I would have to purchase this part and pay for shipping because I had not done this within the warranty period which is one year. How could this be a warranty issue, if this never came with the crib in the first place? Also, she refused to send the parts for the drop side because the crib was not in "safe working order". I tried to speak to a supervisor regarding this issue and was told it was company policy to not allow customers to speak to supervisors over the phone. This crib is obviously unsafe and the problem of the manufacturer, but they refuse to fix it because it was manufactured in 2005. I understand this is several years, but if it is a convertible crib and could be used for many years, two is not a lot and should be the responsibility of the manufacturer to fix or at least care about the safety.

incident_description:
Storkcraft Tuscany 4-in-1 crib

The bottom of my daughter's crib collapsed. She had just woken from a nap and was standing in the corner when it collapsed. She did not sustain any injuries.

The support screw (front right) ripped out of it's socket - damaging the socket and the screw.  Almost immediately the three remaining screws also popped out.  We are unable to re-secure the bottom mattress support frame & board due to the damaged socket. I contacted Storkcraft and was told simply that they would sell me a replacement part.

Tuscany Stages Crib (Cherry)
Model: 04588-494
Date: APR.2011 
CARB: P2
Made in China

incident_description:
5 month old previously healthy infant had Phillips Avent Soothie Pacifier lodged in back of throat causing airway obstruction. The pacifier could not be manually removed. Child was brought by ambulance to a local Emergency Department and emergent circoidotomy was done. The child was then brought to the operating remove and the pacifier was removed from the airway by otolaryngology; force was needed to remove the pacifier. There was airway swelling, laceration to the epiglottis, and evidence of airway trauma.
The baby remained intubated for 2 days and remained in the hospital for approximately one week secondary to poor oral intake secondary to discomfort.
Baby discharged home doing well.

It is unclear how infant manipulated pacifier into his mouth. There are some case reports in the literature of this happening:

[REDACTED]. Airway Obstruction by a child's pacifier could flange design be safer? Eur J Pdiar(1988) 157: 252-254

Blogs reporting similar incidents: http://www.lifamilies.com/chat/topic-521096-1.html

incident_description:
We received a Baby Cache Chantal White Linen crib and matching dresser as baby shower gifts, and picked up the items from Babies R Us in December 2012 and January 2013, respectively.  On assembly, both items had an overpowering chemical odor.  Thinking this was normal for new furniture, we left them in a garage to air out until March 2013, when we moved them into our house.  The odor was still present, and was strong enough to make our eyes water and cause us to cough.  We moved them back into the garage.

A friend mentioned than some furniture is made with particleboard that contains formaldehyde, so we ordered a formaldehyde vapor test kit.  We assembled the products again, and set up the test kit in the crib, with the door to the room closed, as it would be if our daughter were sleeping.  The formaldhyde concentration in the air above the crib was 0.051 ppm, half of the EPA maximum recommended exposure level of 0.1 ppm.  We received the test results around 6/21/2013.

We had previously contacted the company about a warranty return (4/25/2013), but since we did not purchase the item, and the person who did had lost the receipt, we were told the warranty would not apply.  We are attempting to return the product through Babies R Us.  The products are still in our garage; we retested them 8/26 (to be sure the first test was valid) after being in the garage since the last test; the latest result was 0.049 ppm. 

This product is marketed as having a "non-toxic" finish, but the underlying material is obviously not.  It is outrageous to us that a product intended for infants, who would spend at least 6-8 hours a day in it, would have such a high level of formaldehyde!  Given the known toxicity of formaldhyde, any exposure to an infant is unacceptable.
justification: The incident involves exposure to formaldehyde at levels below EPA limits, causing discomfort but no reported injury or death.

mouth and pulled out a large piece of the black trim on the teether. This teether is an

The set was brand new and this was the first time she was given the teething ring.

incident_description:
In December 2011 I ordered the Pottery Barn Kids Sleigh Crib in White for my yet-to-be-born son. The following December, when he was 9 months old, I picked him out of the crib after a nap to find that paint was chipping off the rails (in big pieces) and the exposed wood was splintering. My son had paint flecks on his face and gums, and he most certainly ate some of the splintered wood as I found it in his diaper the next day. My son is/was not rough with the crib and only spends "sleeping time" in it. I am very vigilant on the monitor and take him out within 2 minutes of him waking up.

At that time I contacted Pottery Barn Kids, sent them pictures and described the incident. They were quick to tell me that this must have been a defective crib and so they would be replacing it. I explicitly asked the representative [REDACTED] if this would happen again with the replacement crib and he assured me that it would not - he said that our first crib was a "fluke" and defective, and that the new crib would not break and splinter as the first did. 

After having the replacement for just one month (same exact Sleigh Fixed Gate Crib), my 11 month old son woke up from his afternoon nap I noticed he again had white paint chips stuck around his mouth. Of course I then checked out the crib and saw that there were two areas where the paint and "wood" were entirely eaten away. There was sawdust on the crib sheets. Until he went to bed that night he was coughing aggressively, presumably because some of the splinters of wood he ate were stuck in his throat. There were three separate splintering holes in the side of the crib. One was as large as a quarter. The quantity of wood that he was able to consume in just a few minutes was ridiculous. My poor son had wood coming out in his diapers for days. Not to mention who knows what was in the paint that he ate - PBK would not disclose any of the ingredients.

As I said before, my son was not even a year old. He is only in his crib for naps and sleeping at night. We do everything we can to purchase products we think are well made and, most importantly, safe. I am outraged that Pottery Barn Kids knowingly put my child in such a dangerous position, not once but TWICE.  I hate to think what would have happened if he had more than just a few minutes to chew on the rail. My child's pediatrician agreed that this was an unacceptable instance and clearly had the potential to be a tragic event.

These Pottery Barn cribs are dangerous and should be recalled and PBK knows it. A friend of mine had a nearly identical experience with Pottery Barn Kids Kendall Crib in Espresso, and the in-store representative confirmed that they've had a number of instances like this. PLEASE, someone look into this and have these cribs recalled.
justification: The child ingested paint chips and wood splinters, leading to coughing and potential harm, indicating an injury.

If this mold is the culprit of it all I can hope is that it will go away after I throw it out. I had washed it a week prior to today and there was no mold then. incident_description:
On the evening of 9-4-13 I was watching tv in the bedroom when the smoke/carbon dioxide alarm sounded in my kitchen. Upon entering the kitchen I found my night light was engulfed in flames. The night light is an EL ADI aaron designs #99984.I secured the power and removed the night light before the fire spread to the wall. No one was hurt in the incident but if I hadn't been home I wouldn't have a home this morning. 
     I live off the grid and at the time of the incident the night light was plugged into a GFCI receptacle in the kitchen. I was powered at the time off a battery pack through a 1500 watt inverter. I am a master electrician licensed in the state of Maine, Lic# [REDACTED] so I can verify the correctness of my installation.
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard but was contained without injury, indicating a severity level of 2. The likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the specific conditions described.

incident_description:
I purchased the Graco Ashland crib in white in early August 2013 at a local Walmart. Upon opening the box I noticed a smell and assumed it was just a new item smell. After setting up the crib I had to leave for a couple hours. I returned home to our whole upstairs smell strong of chemicals. My husband and me received an instant headache and I felt nauseous. 

Due to the fumes I had to disassemble the crib and move it to another room near an opened window. I thought some fresh air for a few days would remove the smell. I checked on it daily with the welcoming of an instant headache upon opening the door. I then placed baking soda and vinegar in bowls to help reduce the odor. I could still smell the fumes over them the next day. The crib has been in front of a window for 2 weeks and still smells just as strong as the first day.

I tried to contact the manufacturer by phone but kept getting looped around. I then sent them an email about the problem and they contacted me back about 5 days later. I was told it was paint fumes and to spray [REDACTED] onto the crib. Then I was told the fumes weren't harmful to my child. I know enough that [REDACTED] just covers odors and that paint fumes aren't good to be breathing. 

Upon further inspection of the crib I did notice that the wood was extremely soft. I could indent it with my fingernail and the paint easily chips off. I would not trust a baby old enough to chew on the crib to not get splinters or paint chips into their mouths. Even if you put mouth guards onto the top railings a baby could still scratch the paint off and place the chips into their mouths.

The slats are sized to code but they do look big enough for a baby to get a limb entangled between them. I would recommend at least having a mesh bumper for a smaller infant but I don't know what would be safe for when the baby is old enough to stand. 

I have contacted Walmart about the problem and they are willing to let me return the crib which I will be doing. I do find that this crib is a safety hazard is why I'm filing a report. Even if the crib did off gas after a few more weeks I still would not trust an older baby in it due to the possibility of the wood splintering into their mouths.
justification: The incident caused headaches and nausea, indicating injury (severity 3). The likelihood is high (4) due to the persistent fumes and poor crib quality.

incident_description: The baby Einstein jumper that we have the sun snapped back & hit my son on the hand.
justification: The jumper snapped back and hit the child's hand, indicating an injury occurred.

incident_description:
I used this chair daily to feed my eleven month old son, when one day it suddenly collapsed.

The legs buckled and he fell to the tile floor, hitting his head.  Luckily, he didn't sustain serious injury, but had he been younger he very well may have.

The chair didn't collapse because of weight, because my child is average size, but seemed to fail suddenly.  The chair no longer stands upright on its own.  

This chair needs to be recalled immediately before someone is seriously injured or worse.
justification: The child fell and hit his head, but did not sustain serious injury, indicating a severity level of 3. The chair's sudden failure suggests a possible occurrence likelihood.

incident_description: My infant sleeps in a fisher price rock n play sleeper. I had already called the company & made a report with them & they directed me how to clean the product since I had found mold growing between the lining (which I remove & wash daily) & the rocker itself. I cleaned as instructed & the mold ended up growing back. My son had a skin irritation that turned into an infection and was placed on antibiotics for this.

incident_description: Early yesterday morning my daughter got her leg stuck through the crib and between the crib and the wall. I went to get her unstuck but since the crib is lowered all the way (she can stand up) and I am short I had to lean on the crib a bit to reach her. As I was trying to get her leg out I heard a loud pop and noticed the top rail of the crib cracked, and is close to breaking in half. Since my daughter can stand there's a risk of her pinching her hand or her mouth (since she's teething and always putting chewing on things) or worse, putting enough pressure on it while she stands to break it in half completely. I have contacted the manufacturer several times as my daughter now has no bed of her own and they don't seem to understand the severity of this case as they have not yet responded and told me to wait. I'm not fat, I only weight about 115 pounds so it shouldn't have broken so easily. I have friends who said they sit on the rails of their kids' cribs and have had no issue. Me slightly leaning on it causing it to break is ridiculous!

There are two metal attachments between the plastic holder and the metal bar. One of the attachments had broken, allowing the seat to completely tip sideways.

incident_description:
In April, two days after my son was born, I placed him in a Fisher Price My Little Lamb Platinum Edition Rock n Play Sleeper because it was labelled/marketed as a safe environment for an infant to sleep.  (The Fisher Price website touts this product as "a perfect solution for sleep and play.")  He slept in this product day and night.

In late June, at his two-month checkup, he was diagnosed with torticollis and referred to physical therapy.  Since early July, I've had to do a series of physical exercises designed to stretch taut neck and torso muscles with my son six times each day.

In August, my son was diagnosed with plagiocephaly/brachycephaly and referred to a cranial orthotist.  Today -- his four-month birthday -- I learned that his cranial asymmetry is five (5) standard deviations above the mean, which means he'll have to wear a helmet for 4-8 months, for which I'll have to pay a minimum of $3000 out-of-pocket.

I am outraged at this product is labelled/marketed as a safe environment for an infant to sleep since I now know that my son's injuries are the same as countless other infants whose parents unwittingly believed Fisher Price's claims of safety.  They should be ashamed, and this product should be recalled.
justification: The infant suffered from torticollis and plagiocephaly/brachycephaly, requiring physical therapy and a helmet, which constitutes an injury.

incident_description: My 8 month old (was 7 1/2 months when incident occured) was just trying to put the sun in his mouth, and when he let go suddenly, it snapped back and hit him on his upper lip just below his nose. He has no teeth. No bruise was formed but my child did cry from the impact.

Then a week later (approx) the whole strap came un attached from the mobile and fell into the crib with my son. incident_description:
My 16 month old son was using the Pottery Barn Larkin crib. On 8/5/13, my wife awoke to our son crying and screaming. When she went into his room, she discovered that my son's left leg had become stuck between the slats of the crib. His leg was stuck at the thigh. My wife was unable to free his leg and was forced to contact the fire department. The slats of the crib had to be forced apart by crow bars to free the leg. 
That night, a mesh bumper was placed in the crib to prevent my son from putting his leg through the slats again. The next day, I was driving to work when my wife called to tell me that our son's right leg had become stuck in the crib again despite the use of the mesh bumper. I came home and had to use a hammer to break one of the slats to free his trapped leg. 
He has not been in the crib since. Our concern is that this crib could seriously injure a child by trapping legs. This problem could be solved by allowing for quick and/or easy removal of the slats.
justification: The child's leg was trapped multiple times, requiring emergency intervention, indicating potential for injury.

incident_description: We purchased a high end Franklin and Ben crib for my infant some about a year ago.  Last week my 8 month old was taking a nap.  After being laid down for approx 20 min I noticed on the video monitor that he was playing with something.  I went in to check on him and his face was covered in white paint and little piece of wood.  A plastic crib rail protector had been placed on the front rail.  When I went to look at where the wood could have come from I found that he had chewed off a chunk of wood from the underside of the crib!  This seems like a giant safety and choking hazard.  When I contacted the company they stated that the wood they used is soft enough that this is known to happen.  HOW IS THIS ALLOWED!!!!!
justification: The infant chewed off a chunk of wood from the crib, posing a choking hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: While jumping the hanging fish toy unhooked and fell on daughters head.

incident_description: My 7 month old son choked on his Gerber Nuk pacifier.  He is able to pick up the pacifier and put it back in his mouth now, and since he is teething, he sometimes turns it backwards and chews on the round handle.  While I was making dinner, he was sitting in his highchair and was playing with the pacifier.  I turned my back for maybe 30 seconds, and when I turned back to him, the pacifier handle was stuck way down into his mouth, blocking his throat.  His eyes were all red and he didn't make any noise.  He was just staring at me, looking shocked.  He had thrown up in his mouth and some had trickled down onto his shirt.  Thankfully, I was there to pull the pacifier out.  It would have been very serious had this not occurred in the room.  We have already disposed of all of those pacifiers that we have in the house.

The consumer says her daughter who is 13 months was on the floor playing.  She sat a blanket over top of ceramic tile floors.  She set  4 toys by her.  One of the toys was a teether purse.  Her daughter stood up and put her hand on the couch.  She leaned to take a step and fell forward right onto the teether purse. 

On the purse was an indented flower that caught the left side of her nose.  An imprint of a rose pedal was on her daughter's nose ended up puncturing and slicing through the middle of her nose.  A plastic surgeon had to put her nose back together.

The caller wanted to add also that the key ring also made by the company has the same type of piece except instead of a flower, it is a key ring.
justification: The incident resulted in a significant injury requiring plastic surgery, which falls under severity level 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 2 (unlikely) because such severe injuries from toys are not common but have been documented.

incident_description:
My son has used Pampers diapers since birth. 
The last diaper he wore caused a severe skin reaction within minutes of a diaper change.
There was a stronger chemical in the diaper he was changed into and he immediately began itching. By the time we got home (15 minutes later) his skin under and around the diaper was bright red and he was swollen and breaking out into hives.
We were deeply concerned for his safety so we rushed him to the ER where the doctor confirmed that it was a reaction to the diaper.
He is still in the healing phase and cannot wear a diaper at all until it goes away.
We are now being forced to rush potty training since he is only safe to wear cloth underpants.
justification: The child suffered a severe skin reaction requiring ER visit, indicating an injury.

She has had a low fever due to teething so we have been making sure she stayed hydrated so she was peeing alot. The next day it looked like there had been a poped blister on that area. I then went to my dad who is an RN the next day and asked what he thought, its the size of my thumb now, and he said it looked like a chemical burn. I have seen many more storys like this. Why has there not been a recall.
justification: The description indicates a chemical burn injury from diaper use, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The occurrence likelihood is set to 3 (possible) based on the mention of similar stories but no widespread recall.

incident_description:
We purchased a Baby Cache crib-uptown style, natural color in the winter of 2012.  
In May 2013, my almost 16 month old daughter broke her tibia bone in her left leg as a result of it getting stuck between the side rails.  The rails go from wide to very narrow as you get to the bottom.  We assume she got her leg in the top of the rail where it could fit in and she pushed her leg down the railing and it got stuck in the narrow part. She was found face down on her stomach but her leg was still positioned in the railing as if she was on her back.  She must of panicked and twisted and turned.  As soon as she started screaming bloody murder, my husband knew it wasn't just an ordinary wake up cry. He rushed up there and had trouble getting her leg out of the crib.  He thought he was going to have to break the railing. He finally released it and we took her to the ER where an xray was done . She was in a cast for two weeks and has healed now. I'm making this report because through my research on line I have come across other complaints with this same issue. The crib is not safe and shouldn't be sold. What if a younger baby got their leg stuck in the crib the way my daughter did and ended up on their stomach and suffocated because they couldn't turn their head. This crib should be revised. thank you
justification: The incident resulted in a broken bone (tibia) requiring medical treatment, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description:
My four year old son was sitting on a Bemis NextStep round toilet seat purchased from Home Depot.  He was leaning forward, and fell off of the toilet seat.  As a result, he ended up with a significant cut at the base of his penis that required a visit to the emergency room.  Initially they thought he would require stitches, but they were able to use surgical glue instead.

I believe my son's injury was caused by the skin being pulled as it was caught between the front edge of the seat and his body as he fell. 

(A similar complaint about this seat from someone else on here blamed a sharp edge, but I think my son's injury was from the skin being caught and pulled, rather than cut on an edge)

The incident date here is estimated, but I can get the exact date if necessary.
justification: The child suffered a significant cut requiring emergency room treatment, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
GMG Yepp Maxi child carrier Bike Seat

I recently purchased the GMG Yepp Maxi from Amazon.com. I purchased this seat because the Maximum weight advertised for the child is listed as 22kg/48lb.  This Maximum weight limit is listed on the GMG Yepp website, Amazon product information,  all other websites selling this product, including the cardboard box the seat is packaged in. This is not the case though, after opening the Yepp Maxi box, the installation pamphlet attached to the chair itself and the black/orange safety sticker adhered to the side of the leg protectors clearly states the Yepp Maxi seat is only rated for a maximum load of 18kg/40lb. That is an eight pound difference. For a child to gain eight pounds in early childhood can take some a year or more. If this seat is used regularly that highly increases the possibly rate of failure due to the child becoming heavier and the consumer under the impression the child still fits properly. I have reported this to Amazon.com and a second and third replacement Yepp seat was sent out to me. All of these seats have the same weights listed on them 22kg/48lb Max on the product's box and 18kg/40lb Max on the actual chair. I have since returned these seats and Amazon has their listing under review. I have also done extensive research on the web to find a possible 40lb Yepp Maxi seat for the case the packaging was mislabeled and they do not make/list a product as such. Additionally, I emailed the GMG Yepp contact us option on the Yepp website inquiring about this issue and have not received any response from them. I took pictures of this issue (screen-shot of Amazon's listing and MGM Yepp Maxi website listing, product's cardboard box, installation pamphlet, and safety sticker) with the contradicting information.
justification: The discrepancy in weight limits could lead to potential failure, but no actual incident or injury has been reported yet.

incident_description:
While camping at Otsego Lake State Park, in Gaylord, Michigan, on 7/24/2013, an EL-ADI (R) Aaron Designs Inc. LED
Night Light was plugged into a GFCI electrical outlet in our travel trailer for ambient lighting. The trailer was
plugged into the Campground's 30 amp service. At approximately 10:00 a.m., while we were outside the trailer, we
heard smoke alarms and opened the door to find the trailer filled with black smoke and a small fire at the outlet
with flames going up the wall. We grabbed the fire extinguisher and were able to quickly extinguished the fire.
Apparently, the LED Night Light melted and subsequently caught fire, since melted plastic was all over the
upholstery and dinette, but the fire was small. It also melted the GFCI outlet. After extinguishing the fire, we
immediately unplugged everything and turned off all power. We assume we caught the fire just as it burst into
flames, or when we opened the door it might have ignited more with oxygen entering the trailer. Everything was
covered with black soot and we were coughing hard from smoke inhalation. Our nostrils and mouths were lined
with carbon/black soot. Since the fire was quickly extinguished, the local fire company was not called and a report
was not made. However, we reported the incident to the insurance company (Progressive) and they will be
investigating the fire soon for further determination of the extent of damage and cause. We are just glad the fire
happened while it was daytime and we were able to hear the smoke alarm. Minor smoke inhalation and irritation is
minimal considering what would have happened if we were in the trailer sleeping.
justification: The incident involved a small fire and smoke inhalation, causing minor injuries but no death.

incident_description: Daughter fell forward in bath seat landing face down in bath water. being within arms reach she is fine besides being scared and hitting the tub bottom and bath seat front bar hitting her in the chest/stomach. after the incident, we cleaned tub floor and made sure suction cups were working and it happened again so we had to stop using the seat.

incident_description:
We purchased a Graco brand crib at Wal-Mart on 8/8/2011.  My toddler keeps getting his legs stuck in between the slats up above the knee which causes him extreme pain and bruising which continues to be sore for days.  The slats are very flexible even though the company claims the crib meets all federal guidelines.  I was told by the company today (6/21/2013) there is nothing they can recommend and to contact the CPSC if I was still concerned because the CPSC passed the crib as safe.
This happened to my child once when he was about 14 months old and several times since.  He is now 19 months old and average weight and height for his age and definitely not ready to be moved out of his crib.  He is my third child and we used a different crib with the other two children and this is the only crib that has such flexible slats.  I never had issues with the older two getting their legs stuck and bruising badly.
I do not feel a bumper pad would do much benefit and would potentially be something for him to climb on top of to climb or fall out of the crib.  The slats are flexible enough that you can push on them and they bend or warp.  

I have pictures of his leg being stuck and then the bruising from two different days.

Graco brand
Stanton covertible crib in classic white
Model # 68916029
PO# 5911
Vendor 53
Production Date 8/20/10
purchased online at Walmart.com 8/8/2011

Sincerely,
[REDACTED]
justification: The description reports repeated incidents of a toddler getting legs stuck in crib slats, causing extreme pain and bruising, which constitutes injury.

incident_description: I use the Fisher Price space saver high chair to feet my son.  He kicks his legs and rests his feet on the underside of the tray.  He started having mysterious injuries to his toes.  Skin was missing.  We eventually figured out that his toes were getting skinned from the underside of the high chair tray.  There are sharp edges of plastic and exposed heads of screws.  I had to try and cover the sharp edges with duct tape to prevent further injury, but this makes the front latch unusable to use for removal of the tray.

incident_description: I began using the Fisher Price Rock and Play Sleeper approximately 2 months ago.  My newborn son had severe acid reflux and we needed to keep him sleeping at an angle to help prevent the spit up and reflux.  Over the course of the past two months he has developed torticollis and brachycephaly.  I decided to do an online search and found many other parents reporting the same results of them using the Rock and Play sleeper at night to help babies with reflux.  I do not believe that limited use causes the same issues, but the product is listed as a sleeper and I feel that this is dangerous and a costly mistake!  We now have to have my son go to physical therapy and be fitted for a [REDACTED] helmet to correct the two issues that arose.
justification: The newborn developed torticollis and brachycephaly requiring physical therapy and a corrective helmet, indicating an injury.

incident_description: On April 14, 2013, we put our 8 week old baby into the Baby Bjorn Original.  She was in the carrier for approximately 1 hour.  After arriving home we changed her diaper and noticed that her left leg was purple from her knee to her toes.  After speaking to the doctor and being examined, it was believed that her circulation was cut off.  Thankfully, she is fine and tests showed no issues with blood flow.  We believe it was due to the carrier based upon the following timeline:  12:30 pm: dressed and changed diaper at home, no issue; 1:00-1:45 pm in carrier (she was wearing footed pants so couldn't see legs); at 4:00 we were home and changed her diaper and noticed her leg.  We believe it was caused by the carrier.  We practiced putting her in the night before and made all the adjustments according to the instructions.  It IS possible and maybe even probable that this was our error and that WE didn't have her in correctly.  However, I wanted to advise of the issue anyway.
justification: The baby's leg turned purple due to circulation being cut off, but no lasting injury occurred.

incident_description: My son was given a Garanimals Textured Bead Teether sometime around September 2011. The toy is a ring with chewy balls for babies to gnaw on. Unfortunately, the balls come off with persistent chewing (which is what teething is all about). The balls are the perfect size to be swallowed and thus present a huge choking risk. My son doesn't use the teething ring very often, but he managed to chew off two balls in relatively short order. The seams of glue that hold the balls together around the ring come right apart with enough pressure. I've taken the teether away from my son, obviously, but I'm concerned about other babies who have this ring. A brief search online revealed that others have had the exact same problem and have contacted the company, but no recall has been initiated.

incident_description:
I used three Similac bottles and this is what occurred:  When I sterilized the bottles, the plastic became very cloudy and pitted, and one of them actually broke.  They were no longer useable.  My concerns are not only about their appearance (aesthetics) but about their safety for my baby.  I had them evaluated by the testing laboratory where I am employed, and it was determined that the plastic is polyethylene terephthalate (PET), and they are not BPA-free.  The Similac lab came back with difrent results. 

Neither the packaging nor the instructions include any warnings against sterilization of these products or against their use in a bottle warming device.  It is customary for baby bottles to require sterilization and for baby formula to be served warm.  It is quite apparent that these bottles are not designed for contact with hot water, as the material broke down so readily when sterilized and warmed. 

I have always considered Similac to be a strong brand in the infant care products market, but the performance of these bottles is not in line with your companyÃÂs reputation.  I am very upset about the quality of this product.  I am also very concerned about their safety for my baby as well as for the many babies out there whose mothers have chosen to use these bottles for feeding them.  I wonder what chemicals may be leaching into the formula as the plastic breaks down, and I am even more concerned about the breakage as this could have resulted in a dangerous choking hazard.

  I also photographed the bottles so that I have a record of their condition.  

Please advise
justification: The incident describes product failure and potential safety concerns but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: 4 mo old infant in a summer infant 3 stage booster seat.  The infant's 9 yo sister spun the surrounding tray to entertain.    Infants' left arm was pushed backward because if was wedged against one of the vertical toys on the surrounding tray.  This was witnessed by father in room.   As sister spun the tray, the toy pushed infants' arm behind her resulting in pain and decreased movement of the left arm.  Pain improved with acetomimophen but progressive discomfort and decrease use of left arm prompted Ped ED visit.   Radiographs were negative for fracture.   A nursemaid's elbow reduction procedure was performed with a palpable pop noted.  Observation in ED revealed complete resolution of symptoms thus verifying nursemaid's elbow.

At her 9 month examination, when she began to sit up, it was discovered that she had curvature of the spine.  She was evaluated, and suspicions led parents to change her sleeping place to a flat crib with a mattress.  The scoliosis improved quickly but did not go away. Two watch sized batteries came pre-installed in the turtle which is supposed to play music when you pull the ribbon. Thankfully the batteries were not inside the turtle, which hangs from a toy bar inches from baby's face. I have kept both batteries and removed them to a safe place for now.

incident_description:
I purchased an EllaRoo brand baby Ring Sling style carrier from a local store. I do not remember which store. I used it once in my home to try it out, then put it away in the cabinet. I proceeded to use my other carriers more regularly. During the first week of may 2013, I wanted to use the sling again so I took it out and used it two more times to carry my 8month old baby boy while running errands. I used it for about 15-20 minutes each time. The 2nd time I noticed it was starting to get loose, and the material was slipping through the rings. I knew this was not supposed to happen but I couldn't figure out why it was starting to slip. So again I put the sling away and decided to try again later. On May 10th, 2013, my husband and I decided to go for a walkaround the neighborhood. I let my husband try the EllaRoo ring sling this time....we were walking for approx. 10 minutes when I asked if he liked the sling. he told me it was slipping through the rings and was not feeling very safe. It felt like the baby could slip out at anytime. By now, I was thoroughly frustrated because it was NOT supposed to be doing that. It should feel tight and secure. I inspected the sling and saw that one of the rings was bending..It was supposed to be a circular shape, but instead it was an oval shape. This oval shape was preventing the rings from fitting together properly and keeping the baby safely in the sling. When i first got the sling it was circular, but somehow it was now bending into an oval. I believe the ring is somehow faulty and the weight of the baby was pulling the ring into this oval shape,  This should not happen. The rings should be strong enough to hold a baby safely, and not loose shape. I intend on contacting the manufacturer as well. I am very unhappy with this sling because it poses a definite safety hazard. had I not noticed the slipping of the material, my baby boyt could have fallen to the ground and gotten seriously injured.

CPSC Note: This product has been recalled. Please refer to CPSC Recall 08-215 -- http://www.cpsc.gov/en/Recalls/2008/Ellaroo-Recalls-Infant-Sling-Carriers-Due-to-Fall-Hazard/
justification: The incident involved a faulty product that could have led to injury, but no actual harm occurred as the issue was noticed in time.

incident_description: My 10 month old baby boy has been having horrible rashes on his scrotum, penis, and general diaper region.  He has been in Pampers Sensitive Swaddlers since birth so I did not think this was the problem, although he is now wearing size 4s.  We tried all different types of diaper ointments, and even going to the pediatrician to get prescription ointments to see if it is possibly a yeast reaction.   Nothing has helped.   I recently found out that Pampers puts Dry Max in their size 3 and 4 boxes without labeling them as such.   My poor baby has been suffering what looks like a chemical burn for two months now because these diapers are not labeled properly.  I never would have put him in diapers with Dry Max because I knew about the the problems and lawsuits with it in 2010, and 2011.  In addition to the physical pain my baby has been in, we now have opened cases of diapers that we will not use, doctors appointments to pay for, not to mention all of the money spent in trying to find ointments to help.   I can't believe Pampers has caused my baby to suffer, it's absolutely disgraceful!
justification: The baby has suffered from rashes and what looks like a chemical burn, indicating injury, but the occurrence is unlikely as it is linked to a specific unlabeled product issue.

incident_description: At approximately 9:30 pm I checked on my 14-month-old son, who had been in his Sorelle Verona crib for two-and-a-half hours. He was sleeping on his back at an odd angle with his left leg dangling through the slats. His leg was pushed through past his knee and bent at a 90 degree angle. Not wanting him to injure himself by attempting to re-situate himself, I tried to lift his leg out for him. My son would not budge (please note that I did not pull very hard - didn't want to wake him). He woke up at this point and began screaming. After carefully trying to manipulate his knee and leg back through the slats for a few minutes, I cut off his pajama pants. At this point I found his knee was incredibly swollen from the pressure of the slats. I briefly tried icing it to bring down some swelling, but that did not help. He was still screaming in pain and frustration. While inspecting his knee, it appeared its bones and structure were a bit wider than the slats themselves. I'm not sure how he managed to get it through in the first place. At this point, there was no choice left other than to dismantle the crib. I used a hand saw to remove one of the offending slats to free my son. He limped at first, but after a few minutes that was gone. The swelling was almost gone the next morning and completely gone by the afternoon. Aside from bruising on both sides of his knee, there does not appear to be any permanent damage. Fortunately I discovered his leg was stuck before he woke up the next morning, energetic and ready to go, and decided to extricate himself. There is no telling what kind of damage he could have done to his knee, leg, and even his back if he had been left to his own devices.
justification: The child suffered a swollen knee and bruising, indicating an injury, but no permanent damage or death occurred.

My son leaned too far forward in his Fisher Price Newborn-to-Toddler Portable Rocker and fell out, pulling the chair down on top of him because he was buckled in. We are now putting the chair away until our son is old enough to use without the belt.

incident_description:
My 15 month old child was placed in his crib at 7:30 pm for bedtime on 3/7/13. He slept uneventfully until 9 pm when I overheard him via the baby monitor to be softly fussing. This lasted intermittently for 4-5 minutes, however, our concerns quickly subsided as he returned to sleep. Then, my child awoke at 12:15 am on 3/8/13 screaming in pain.  My wife and I went into bedroom and found our child to have his right leg stuck in the vertical slats of crib at the level of this thigh just above his knee. I repositioned his leg and was able to dislodge it. My child continued screaming in pain. I quickly removed his pajamas to reveal his right leg below the knee to be cold and pallorous with weak palpable distal pulses (checked dorsalis pedis pulse). This is all evidence the leg was not being perfused appropriately. The right leg on the lateral aspects of his thigh just above the knee was edematous with erythematous areas, evidence of where his leg was stuck.  Additionally, there were forming black and blue contusions in the same area of the right knee as a result of the soft tissue trauma caused by the crib.  I have obtained photo documentation of this.

Somehow this crib is rated as safe. I am a physician and will be following up with local health officials about this. Per this website I see this is not the first time this has happened to a child.  My child appeared to make a full recovery with no ill effects and is doing well currently. He does still have bruises on both sides of his knee 1 week later.  I will be following up with the CPSC and the maker of this crib via phone.

My child had a sustained soft tissue injury resulting from this crib design. Additionally, it is safe to say that had my child not had the ability to communicate (for example, if he had a tracheostomy, vocal cord paralysis, CP, etc) he likely would have had permanent vascular damage as a result of his leg getting trapped, possibly losing the function of his leg permanently. Clearly, this product is not safe for children once they become mobile in the crib.  Of note, I constructed this crib according to specifications and followed the instructions precisely and did not use any out of the box materials.

The concerning part is that after a quick look on the internet, many cribs appear to have the same design with vertical slats that allow children's legs and arms through at certain angles.
justification: The child sustained a soft tissue injury with potential for permanent vascular damage, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is 3 as similar incidents have been reported but are not extremely common.

incident_description:
4 month old infant with recurrent tongue bruising while using Dr. Brown's #2 nipple. Infant thoroughly evaluated
for abuse and any bleeding disorder (including multiple radiographs and blood/urine tests). Abuse and bleeding
disorders have been ruled out as causes. As a consultant on the case, I do not know at this point if the recurrent
tongue bruising is due to something unique about the infant (sucking dynamics or overly vigorous sucking) or is
due to something wrong with the nipple. The nipple does not appear to be defective or worn out (no sign of wear).
I cannot find any cases in the medical literature noting tongue bruising from innocent means such as taking a
bottle, however there are multiple reports in the lay media on-line. The family has now switched nipple brands and
size, and so far, the bruising has not recurred. While bruising ofthe tip ofthe tongue might seem to be a trivial
injury, it is not; an isolated, unexplained bruise in an infant who is not yet able to pull to a stand and take some steps
is worrisome for abuse. It often will prompt a full work-up and investigation for abuse including head a, multiple
X-rays of the bones (skeletal survey and repeat skeletal survey 2 weeks later) as well as blood and urine tests. In
addition, the family is put through a child abuse investigation that can involve child protective services and police. I
plan to submit this case for publication in a medical journal as doing so might save other children and their families
from this experience.
justification: The incident involves recurrent tongue bruising in an infant, which is classified as an injury. The occurrence likelihood is considered rare as there are no known medical literature cases, only lay media reports.
