incident_description:
I purchased a Lana crib in 2007 before the birth of my son in 2008. This crib was recalled in 2010 by CPSC (Release #10-222). The company, C&T International, provided an immobilization kit for the drop side crib in order to comply with the recall. On January 28, 2013, I tried to install the immobilizer kit on the fully assembled crib in my home. 

The problem is that the kit, as provided, would not assemble on the Lana crib I had purchased using C&T's directions. C&T, provided 2 immobilizer brackets and 2 locking washers to be added, via a set of instructions, to the drop side part of the crib. After much difficulty, I actually got one of the assemblies together in the manner prescribed by the instructions. The difficulty came from the fact that the bolt the new locking washer and immobilizer bracket were supposed to fit on was TOO SHORT to hold both the locking washer and the bracket with the native wingnut. Once the locking washer was removed, the wingnut went back onto the bolt just fine. At one point, I took a pair of pliers and squeezed one of the locking washers until it was flatter. After some trying, this seemed to work and the assembly was holding. However, I gave it one more turn to make sure it was on tight and the whole thing popped off the bolt again.

In my opinion, this immobilizer kit is more dangerous that the original failure. People are expecting a rational, well thought-out fix to a relatively simple problem. In fact, with an immobilizer kit that contains only 4 parts, 2 brackets and 2 locking washers, I find it almost impossible to comprehend how this comapny, C&T, STILL could not figure out how provide consumers with a safe, easy fix to their original design flaw.

I have currently removed both locking washers and have tightened the assembly with the wingnut and the immobilizer bracket in place. I'm not sure what I expect here but to me it is incomprehensible that a company that manufactures a child's crib that is subsequently recalled by the CPSC can provide a solution that, in itself, doesn't work. Ignorance or incompetence?
justification: The incident describes a faulty immobilizer kit that did not function as intended, but no injury or death occurred as a result.

incident_description: My son has slept in his Newborn Rock N Play since he was born in September 2012. In December my infant started to get what i thought was a normal cold. Wrong. He went to the doctors and they prescribed him Albuteral cough syrup. A week later the cough was not getting any better it was getting worse so I took him back into the doctors. That is when they prescribed him the Nebulizer which is a breathing treatment machine which he is required to do every 4 hours. That still wasn't breaking up the congestion or making him any better. That is when the doctor diagnosed him with possible asthma. I heard about this issue with mold and the Rock N Plays so I removed the cover on mine and noticed a bunch of black spots which is mold! Now I am concerned that this may be the reason for my sons respiratory problems. I work for an Environmental firm and we test for Mold so I am aware of how toxic mold can be, especially to a newborn infant who's lungs are still developing.
justification: The infant developed respiratory problems likely due to mold exposure, which constitutes an injury (severity 3). Mold in baby products is a known issue, making occurrence likely (4).

incident_description:
The consumer says her son has gotten his leg stuck in between the railing of the crib about a half a dozen times.  In one incident that child had bruising around the left knee.  He says that his child will stand up, lose his footing, and his leg will get stuck above the knee thru the railing.  Her son just turned one on the 22nd of December and weighs 22lbs and 29 inches long. 

The issue is become more frequent now that he is able to stand.  She had to free his leg twice on the same day recently.  

The consumer says that she spoke to the branded company who said that they don't make the crib.  The manufacturer told her that the crib complies with all federal laws.   

The consumer says that she is upset that the manufacturer and brand company are willing to just pass the buck and not take any responsibility.
justification: The child has sustained bruising from getting his leg stuck in the crib, indicating an injury, and the incident has occurred multiple times, including twice in one day.

incident_description:
We have had about ten different instances of our baby getting his thigh stuck between the slats of his crib.  The most recent instance occurred today, and he was stuck so bad that I was afraid I wasn't going to be able to get him loose without having to call the fire department or by possibly breaking the slats with a hammer.  I was finally able to get him dislodged after several minutes.  He has not sustained any permanent injuries or required hospitalization from these occurrences, but it leaves deep red marks on his delicate skin and causes him significant pain and fear.  

My baby is about 14 months old (DOB [REDACTED]), and this started becoming an issue around October 2012.  He weighs about 25 pounds.  All of these instances have occurred when he was awake in the crib.

It seems that a baby's crib should be the one place where one can leave a baby safely unattended in one's home, but this is absolutely not the case for us.  He is at considerable risk in his crib due to this issue.

The slats on this crib are 2" apart, which is in compliance with the CPSC's regulations for distance between crib slats.  This concerns me greatly because there is simply no other crib option on the market besides other wooden cribs which will also have similarly distanced (less than the 2 & 3/8" regulation) wooden slats.  Although most [play pens] have mesh sides which are much safer in regards to this issue, I am not comfortable with him sleeping in one of these every night, because the mattresses for these products are very flimsy compared to a supportive crib mattress.  Because of the lack of a better product, we feel we are forced to continue to allow him to sleep and play in this unsafe environment.

We contacted the manufacturer about this issue and were told to try "safety bumpers."  However, our pediatrician has instructed us to avoid crib bumpers entirely due to other safety concerns.  Additionally, we purchased a [REDACTED], which is taller than a traditional bumper.  Our baby was able to pull it down, step on it, and potentially pull himself up over the side of the crib, which obviously puts him in significant danger of falling.

My concern is that wooden slats on cribs can be very unsafe, but there are no other options available for consumers who want to avoid this.  Does a crib without wooden slats exist?  Or are there other ways besides unsafe bumpers or crib shields to make my crib a safe place for my growing baby?  Any further help would be greatly appreciated.
justification: The baby experiences significant pain and fear with deep red marks, indicating injury, and the issue occurs frequently.

incident_description: My young child was holding and playing in the living room with his DreamLite by Pillow Pets.  As he was playing, he tripped forward and landed with his face on the pillow where there is a plastic housing cover for the light to shine through.  The plastic housing cover cracked exposing sharp edges as the crack went from one star pattern to another.  These cracks in the plastic was very sharp and exposed enough that it cause laceration to the facial area.  Two areas, on the forehead and on the cheek, the laceration was deep enough that pressure had to applied several minutes to stop the bleeding.  I am very concerned that toys made for small children would be made with such a cheap plastic such that it would break so easily with simple fall.
justification: The child suffered lacerations requiring prolonged pressure to stop bleeding, indicating a significant injury.

incident_description: While standing and playing with the mailbox on the Little Tikes Activity Garden my child began to cry loudly with pain. As I went to my child her right hand was caught and pinching her fingers from the bottom of the mail box door. I couldn't pull her hand out so I pushed the lid to the mailbox to close it and she screamed louder in pain. I then went the other way opening it all the way down so that the top of the lid is pointing to the ground and her fingers came out. Her first three fingers, the pointer, middle and ring finger were very red just at the tips and it took a while to calm her down. I never seen her in pain like that before so I was concerned that the mailbox was dangerous. After trying to re-inact how she could have got her fingers pinched I realized that if you open the mail box door all the way so that it is pointing to the ground there is a gap in the hinges area where little fingers could get trapped and then pinched.
justification: The child experienced significant pain and visible redness on multiple fingers, indicating an injury, and the incident description suggests the hazard is likely to occur again due to the design flaw.

incident_description: The bassinet lock/unlock mechanism was in the lock position but the bassinet rocked to the side and my 6 week old baby could not breath. I was afraid and did not use the bassinet and spoke with my aunt. My aunt checked the safeproducts.gov site and found the recall information. My aunt called Dorel Juvenile Group  (877) 416-0165 and spoke with [redacted]  who said "The repair kit will ship to you in 5-10 days." My aunt requested overnight shipping. [redacted] said they do not use overnight shipping. My aunt requested to speak with a supervisor. [redacted] came back to the phone and since you are in Michigan and we are Indiana it should get to you sooner.Again my aunt requested to speak with a supervisor, again [redacted] came back to the phone and said that they will 2 day air ship the repair kit. My baby could have died and the Dorel Juvenile Group is only concerned about putting shipping money issues before the lives of children that parents have entrusted to use this bassinet. The American Pediatrics Association recommends that babys up to 1year of age sleep in the same room as the parent because it lowers the risk of SIDS.
justification: The bassinet malfunction posed a serious risk to the baby's life, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: The Nuby Bug-A-Loop Teething ring has caused injury to my child. One of the blue plastic beads developed a sharp point that resulted in several scratches on my daughter's face. There is also deterioration and peeling on the green oval bead that is definitely a cause for concern.
justification: The teething ring caused several scratches on the child's face, indicating an injury.

incident_description: I purchased the "MAM Cooler Teether 4+ months" on August 19, 2012. The water filled cooling part broke and upon further inspection I noticed that there was black mold growing in between the cooling part and the round plastic design piece. Luckily the product broke so that I could inspect it more in-depth; with the water out of the water filled portion it became more pliable and I was able to separate the pieces. I am very concerned that this could have made my child sick, as the product states it is a teether and therefore ALWAYS in the mouth, directly in contact with the black mold that was growing. I can provide pictures with proof of purchase, if necessary.
justification: The product had mold, which could have posed a health risk, but no actual injury was reported.

incident_description: We recently bought a Today's kids play yard. My 1yr old can push the play yard across the room when we put her inside of it to play. While she was inside the play yard playing with the toys on the one panel she pushed on the one toy and the whole play yard will slide across the floor and the panels then folded together and she fell and hit her face on the panels when they folded together and also bent her little wrist when she fell forward with it as it slid across the floor her. Arm went into one of the slots in the gate. Luckily nothing was broke and she only had a little bruise on her face but I do not feel that is it safe to place a toddler inside of this to play if their little bodies are able to push this across the room simply by playing with the toys on the panel. We had bought this thinking it would help keep her away from the tv and things she shouldn't touch but instead made it to where she can just push it to them and hurt herself while trying to play
justification: The child suffered injuries including a bruised face and a bent wrist, but no broken bones or serious harm occurred.

incident_description: Screws constantly were becoming loose. The inside of the screws worked with an allen wrench which easily striped the screws. From the screws coming loose the bassinet would tend to start to rock. The plastic around the top of the screws that holds the metal frame in place, that the actually bed sits in, breaks giving one side or corner away causing a risk of fall injury. This happen while my little one was sleeping thank goodness I went to check on him before he fell out.
justification: The incident describes a risk of fall injury due to structural failure, which could have resulted in harm to the child.

incident_description: The crib end that attaches to the crib spring broke and the crib spring fell down towards the floor during my son's nap time.
justification: The crib spring fell during nap time, but there was no mention of injury.

incident_description: My 22 month old nephew has bruised his knee by getting it stuck in the slats on the crib. I have tried a bumper that is above his knee and he has still injured his knee. I am in the process of attaching protection that goes from the top of the rail to under the mattress. I am going to try another bumper attached to this one or something. I see no evidence of a recall since the space between the slats is within limits. If they were slightly wider the child would not get their leg into the gap. Slightly narrower slats the child could remove their leg but it might not meet requirements for slat width. Please check this out. A child could injure their kneecap seriously. He has a bruise the size of a half-dollar or larger.
justification: The child sustained a bruise, which qualifies as an injury, and the description suggests this could happen again with the current crib setup.

incident_description: Fisher Price Newborn Rock 'n Play Sleeper recalled mold on their product and when I checked it, it did indeed have black mold under the cloth cushion on the plastic. My daughter has had a cough for the past 2 weeks. She has had rashes on and off since she was born and the doctor thought it was a milk allergy. She has not used dairy products since 1 1/2 months of age and has still had rashes on and off. This is probably why. We have been using this product since August 24, 2012.
justification: The presence of black mold and the child's persistent cough and rashes suggest a probable injury caused by the product.

incident_description: My daughter slept in this sleeper for 5 months. We started noticing that her head was bowing out on the side and the back was getting flat. our NP didn't want to listen and we went to a different NP and got referred to a specialist now my 5 month old is getting fitted for a cranial helmet that she will have to wear for 23 hours a day for 5 months. Please beware of this product because this could happen to your child too. No she wasn't born this way her head was perfectly round. The sleeper says for playing and sleeping comfortably in. She has acid re-flux and that is why we let her sleep in it at night so she could be at the perfect incline.
justification: The child developed a flat head and required a cranial helmet, indicating an injury due to prolonged use of the sleeper.

incident_description: The fisher price deluxe infant to toddler comfort rocker has metal parts that hold the toy bar in place. These two metal parts stick out on the side of the seat, despite pictures showing otherwise. My infant son who likes to try to sit up has hit his head several times on these metal parts often hurting himself. As infants learn to sit they often tend to lean to one side or another and then try to regain their balance. Again, in doing so, my infant son has hit his head several times against the metal parts on the sides of this seat, and pretty hard in some cases that it left a mark on his head.  They should have designed the seat similar to the original infant to toddler seat which poses no such danger to infants.
justification: The infant has hit his head several times on the metal parts, leaving marks, indicating injury.

incident_description: We removed the fabric cover, and found mold on the underside of the fabric cover. There was also mold on the base of the frame.
justification: Mold presence indicates an incident with potential health risks, but no immediate injury is reported.

incident_description: My 3 year old son was going to take a nap and took his Penguin DreamLite to bed. He was trying to turn the light on by pressing the button. He pressed another area which is round and his finger went throught the plastic wear there is an emblim of a face on the top. His finger got stuck and it cut him as he struggled to get it out. The emblim does not appear to be secure.
justification: The child's finger was cut while trying to free it from the toy, indicating an injury occurred.

incident_description:
(01/16/2013) The consumer stated that her grandmother saw something on television about the recall. She called her and told her to check her product. The consumer lifted up the cushion of the sleeper to check. She found a lot of mold on the sheer covering. It was starting to form on the back of the cushion. She took the product to her basement. She stated that she wanted it out of the room. The consumer stated that her son has been sleeping in the sleeper since July, 2012. She stated that he sleeps in it because of acid reflux. He cannot sleep on his back.

The consumer does not know at this particular time if her child is affected by the mold. She did call her pediatrician to advise his of the mold. She has a appointment to take her child in on 1/28 for a six months checkup.. 

(1/17/2013)The consumer stated that she called the manufacturer. She spoke with a gentleman and told him that she had the Rock N Play with mold, She was advised that the mold was due to not cleaning it properly. He advised her to use bleach to clean the product. She was also advised that this was not a recall but an inspection for a recall. After voicing her concerns about using bleach as a cleaner, the consumer was transferred to [REDACTED].  The consumer explained everything to her. [REDACTED] scheduled a pickup for the Rock N Play. The consumer was advised that the refund would be issued when the product was received by the manufacturer. The consumer's case number with Fisher-Price is [REDACTED]
justification: The incident involves mold exposure but no confirmed injury at this time, and the product is being recalled.

incident_description: We currently own 2 of the fisher price rock and play sleepers for our twins who sleep in them every night due to severe acid reflux.  After hearing about the recall today we checked both items and both contained mold.  Our twins have been treated for respitory and sinus problems for the past 2 months.
justification: The twins have been treated for respiratory and sinus problems, indicating injury due to mold exposure.

incident_description: We have multiple young children and therefore have several highchairs of the same model and have had multiple safety incidents with this model among the various chairs. They are Safety First high chairs model HC051 (Manufacture date 9/2009). The waist clasp on this model can result in significant pinching of hands or fingers resulting in pain, redness, bruising, or even removal of skin. It has happened to myself, my husband, and a grandparent on multiple occasions, and now that our children are no longer infants but toddlers, on two occasions (including today), one of our toddlers was playing with the clasp and got his skin severely pinched and caught in the clasp until I could dislodge the unit and release his skin. We'll be throwing these chairs in the garbage as they are anything but "Safety First". It is also critical to note that these chairs are designed to have shoulder straps (in the hard back of the chair) and say they are appropriate for infants, however, no shoulder straps are ever included in these models and there are no slots to allow shoulder straps in the chair covers for this model. Therefore, younger children/infants could fall out the side of the chair as there is only a minimal adjustment of the waist straps. Because we knew from the beginning how unsafe these "Safety First" high chairs were, were always used [REDACTED] highchairs for feeding our infants and used these for supervised specific purposes for medical reasons with our one son (who has a feeding tube) because of its size and reclining ability. However, this is a very dangerous product for the general market. Please make the manufacturer address these safety issues to protect young children! Thank you!
justification: The incident describes multiple instances of injury including pain, redness, bruising, and skin removal, qualifying as Injury (severity 3). The likelihood is high (4) as it has occurred multiple times to different individuals.

incident_description: My son's crib is constructed using barrel nuts, several of which face the sleeping area. We have reassembled this crib twice after moving. Each time, we have discovered badly corroded and broken-in-half barrel nuts. When broken, entire screws can slide out of place, leaving entire sides of the crib to disconnect. In out case, two broken nuts became stuck as we tried to use them, unaware that they had split. We were unable to remove half of one. This made the screw connection significantly less secure when the crib was fully assembled. Further, as the crib moves in daily use (baby's and the family members' who bump into/touch it), the front half of a broken barrel nut can fall out of its pre-drilled hole onto the baby's mattress, creating an ingestion hazard. Because the barrel nuts are only replaceable with other barrel nuts, presumably subject to the same corrosion/breakage, I believe they were an unsafe choice for crib construction.
justification: The incident describes a potential ingestion hazard and structural instability in the crib, which could lead to injury but no actual injury is reported.

incident_description: We've used all sorts of brands of diapers with my infant son and have never had a problem like the one we had when we used Pampers Baby Dry. We bought a big box of them and halfway through the box I changed my son and he had [red marks] on the sides of both of his legs. They were so bad they hurt him to the touch and were a deep blood red color. I was horrified. The marks on his legs coincided with the elastic bands of the diapers on his thighs. This was not a diaper rash. I took a picture of it right then and there. This incident happened a couple of months ago and you can still see faint marks on my sons legs, like he will have a scar on his legs from the diapers. I want to complain to Pampers but I do not want them to send me more of their product. This is completely unacceptable, especially if my child is scarred for the rest of his life.
justification: The infant suffered red marks and potential scarring from the diaper's elastic bands, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
I purchased a Bam Argington Crib/Bassinet Set in Ebony from online retailer Amazon.com on November 12, 2010 for my daughter.  She has used it for approximately 2 years (we put her in the crib at about three months and she is 2 years and 1 month old currently).  She is of normal height/weight for her age (28 pounds).  She was in the crib and the base of the crib splintered without warning.  It is duct-taped together now but I feel it is unsafe and that we need either a replacement part or, preferably, a new crib.  I have tried to contact the company via email (as its website instructed) and by phone (I left a VM on a random employee's voice mail because the mailbox for general complaints was full and was not taking more messages).  I believe that the crib is unsafe and that you should look into this matter further to make sure other children aren't in danger.  Luckily my daughter is older and can talk and move around so we were able to get her out of the crib quickly but this could be deadly to a younger child who doesn't have those capabilities yet.

I believe that a crib, especially one that was $585.00, should last for at least two years (or at least through one child).  The manufacturer claimed that the wood was all hardwood and was not pressed particle board, which was one of the main reasons we purchased it.

If you do get them to respond to you, please tell them to give me a call to rectify my situation.  I can be reached at [REDACTED] and my name is [REDACTED].  I will also be contacting my local and state representatives in this matter.

Best regards,
[REDACTED]
justification: The crib splintered but no injury occurred, and the child was safely removed. The likelihood of recurrence is possible given the product's failure.

incident_description: My infant once at age 5 months and once at at 6 months has fallen out of his high chair due to the locking pegs not engaging properly. The high chair was given to me as a gift in May of 2010. It is a Chicco. My now 2 year old son used it without incident. We started placing my younger son in it 2 months ago. The pegs began to fail because they would not properly engage into the hole when slide forward. We would try and be extra careful and just make sure they engaged properly but on two seperate incidents my older daughter placed my son in the high chair and did not make sure the tray was secure and he fell out. I realize we should be buckling him in but that also was overlooked.
justification: The infant fell out of the high chair twice due to improper locking pegs, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Was using and infant bathing tub in our double sink and the middle section that hold the baby bottom up suddenly came loose and the baby dropped into the water, She got rub burns from the non slip mat down her back and want underwater. I believe the middle section came loose due to the water it doesnt latch well. This happened a few more time so i quite using this product.
justification: The baby suffered rub burns from the non-slip mat and was underwater, indicating an injury occurred. The incident happened multiple times, suggesting a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: My 6-month old was just beginning to chew on his teething ring when the liquid inside started squirting out into his mouth and dripping down his chin.  I cleaned out his month and then examined the teether.  The ring had ripped open, all of the liquid was oozing out and the star that floats inside was hanging out.  I frequently inspect the teether to make sure there are no tears or cracks and have not boiled it or frozen it.
justification: The teether ruptured but no injury was reported, only the potential for harm.

incident_description:
Good evening,

I'm heart broken over a recent recall notice I received for my Fisher Price sleep and play rocker (recall below).  My baby girl has had the rocker since birth.  She has struggled with respiratory issues off and on, most recently serious enough for her to need a breathing machine.  I believe the mold issue the sleeper is being recalled for contributed to her illness if not directly was the cause. 

My other big concern is that even after cleaning the unit, mold still a few short weeks later.  I think they need to get this product off the market or at a minumum warn consumers to wash and inspect the unit every day.

http://www.cpsc.gov/cpscpub/prerel/prhtml13/13087.html

Thank you,

[REDACTED]
justification: The baby suffered serious respiratory issues requiring a breathing machine, indicating an injury (severity 3). The mold issue is recurring despite cleaning, making occurrence likely (4).

incident_description: I have a 3 month old that we bought a Fisher Price My Little Snugabunny Cradle 'on Swing for. I noticed it getting wet and the plastic being like someone had spilled water into it. So I dried it and washed the cover. Well it has created mold on the seat cover and washing and using stain removal has not helped. I thought maybe our daughter was spiting up on it. But that wasn't the case. Ever if she has a wet diaper at night it creates moisture and the plastic becomes wet. I recently saw a  product recall of the same problems by fisher price call the Rock n play.
justification: The incident involves mold growth due to moisture, posing a potential health risk, but no injury or death has been reported.

incident_description: My wife purchased a childrens "LAVA" nite lite for our 7 year old daughter's room  She plugged it in and left the room.  About an hour later, I was checking on the lite, and noticed the aluminum base was scolding hot.  This would have burned my daughter had she tried to remove her nite lite.  The entire metal/aluminum base gets so hot in a short time, one cannot hold it at all.  I thnk this is very dangerous for kid's rooms or households.  There is a definite fire threat and injury threat,  I unplugged the lite and have not used it again.
justification: The night light's base gets scolding hot, posing a burn injury risk if touched, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description:
I have a crib that is unsafe it is a 
Generation 2 Worldwide 
20-8101 May-02 
Made in Dothan, Al USA36301 
RPF-020155
justification: The crib is identified as unsafe, which poses a risk but no injury or incident is reported.

incident_description:
My daughter is 5 months old and was playing with a "Sophie the giraffe" by Vulli. When I next looked over a leg was lodged in her throat and her airway was completely blocked. She could not have pulled it out. It took a good pull to get it out of her throat. Had I been in the shower he would have died. I have contacted the company and have had no reply. It is my hope there is a recal or, at minimum, a very strong warning of the choking hazard. Please help before a baby dies. 

http://sophiethegiraffe.com/
justification: The incident involved a complete airway blockage that could have resulted in death if not for immediate intervention, indicating a high severity. The likelihood is possible given the described scenario.

incident_description: Crib purchased t Kmart corp modl 071539 and collapsed on my granddaughter almost suffocating her...local Kmart store will not do anything so I'm making a complaint
justification: The crib collapsed and almost suffocated the granddaughter, indicating a serious injury risk.

incident_description: I've been having to take my 8 month old baby to the emergency room 3 times already. The doctor said it was a respiratory infection and ear infection. My baby is still sick. The medicine hasn't helped. Now it all makes sence.I was watching the news earlier and it shows my baby's rock n play sleep bed is on recall for mold under the bedding. I would like to report my situation and also need help on what I can do.
justification: The baby has been repeatedly sick with respiratory and ear infections likely caused by mold in the recalled sleep bed, indicating injury.

incident_description: Our child has a very raspy breathing with a bad sinus infectin from sleeping in the Fischer Price Rock and Play Sleeper
justification: The child has a bad sinus infection and raspy breathing, indicating an injury (severity 3). Sinus infections from sleepers are possible but not extremely common (likelihood 3).

incident_description: We had recieved a rock and play by fisher price for my infant daughter. It has developed mold within the past month. After carefully following the instrucitons to clean the mold the stains will not remove from the sleeper.
justification: The presence of mold in the infant sleeper poses a potential health risk, but there is no mention of injury or death.

incident_description: We frequently would wipe the rock n play down but the straps still wound up getting moldy. They weren't part of the fabric, they were part of the plastic so we couldn't wash them properly and to get all of the fabric off we would have to cut it off of the plastic seat. It was a shame, our baby loved the rock n play.
justification: Moldy straps pose a hygiene issue but no injury was reported; the problem occurred frequently.

incident_description:
We have the Eddie Bauer wood high chair as a hand me down from my brother, it was purchased in approximately 2006.  The buckle is very unsafe.  The way it goes around the childs waist and through the legs makes it so that the child can still stand up while buckled and it slips down around their legs.  It cannot be tightened to allow it to fit snugger to the seat and therefore is very unsafe since it all ows the child enough slack to stand up.  Our 11 month old daughter was buckled in and when we turned around to finish cleaning her up on Sunday she was standing on the seat.  It worries me so much that she could have fallen and hit her head.  

I feel that the design of the straps is very inadequate and unsafe.
justification: The incident describes a near-miss where the child could have fallen but did not, indicating no injury occurred, and the likelihood is high given the design flaw.

incident_description: My child was placed in her crib for bed. A minute later, we heard her screaming. When we went into her room, her arm was trapped between the front bar of her crib and the side bar, which had come apart and is only held together by a wooded dowel. Thankfully, it was only her arm/shoulder and not her neck!! She is 18 months old, and weighs 24 pounds. This crib was supposed to last her another year!
justification: The child's arm was trapped, indicating an injury occurred, but there was no death or life-threatening situation.

incident_description:
SUBJECT: Evenflo exersaucer 3 in 1 (A 3 stage toy - meant to grow with baby)

I have had numerous issues with this product.

I did not use stage 1, as the arch over the child moves very easily. i dont know that it can be dangerous as i simply preferred not to use it.

The exersaucer stage is great - except for 2 things: 1) The sound/music level of the toys is very high - even on the lowest setting. I cannot imagine that it does not damage a baby's hearing. 2) There is a dragonfly toy that the baby can pull at. This poses a risk of injury to baby's face, as baby movements are 'jerky' & they can easily hurt themselves with the edges of the dragonfly wings. Its especially scary when it comes close to the eyes)

The stage 3 walking stage is HORRIBLE & VERY DANGEROUS!!!! Besides for the same issues above (as it uses the exact same toys): 1) It is EXTREMELY SHAKY and FALLS ON TOP OF CHILD when tries to stand up against it [this happened to my child TWICE in just the first couple days of changing to this stage] 2) the 'locks' (that are meant to keep the legs from turning or collapsing) have tabs that stick out. If a child even lightly presses these tabs (can EASILY be done accidentally, just while paying with the toy), the tab will fall ALONG WITH A SMALL SPRING that is 100% - a CHOKING HAZARD!!!!!!! This toy MUST be recalled BEFORE it claims the lives of innocent children!!!!!!!!!! [this happened a couple times too - altho Thank G-d a million times over - I saw it happen immediately & was able to take away from my child]

Needless to say, after only a couple days, we already dis-assembled this product!
justification: The product poses multiple risks including potential hearing damage, facial injuries, and choking hazards, with actual incidents of the toy falling on the child and choking hazards being encountered.

incident_description: I am writing to let you know of a problem. My daughter called me crying that her 18month old daughter had gotten her foot stuck in the highchair she has which is a cosco dorel juvenile group jasmine style model number 03354. The baby got her foot stuck between the front bar and the tray. My daughter and her husband had to break the high chair to get the baby out without causing her harm to her foot. I am calling the company today to see if there is anything they can do. The high chair was bought brand new for the child that was in it and now she has gotten hurt. Her foot will heal however she will never go in that high chair again.  Her foot is ok however there is some bruising and it is tender to the touch. I do not want to see another child get hurt the same way. She is tiny and was strapped in using the safety belts on the chair. She just put her foot in the space between the bar and the tray and was stuck, crying, and now her foot hurts her.
justification: The baby suffered bruising and tenderness, indicating an injury, and the incident required breaking the highchair to free her, suggesting a likely recurrence risk.

incident_description: We have owned the Safety 1st Easy Care Swing Tray booster seat (pink) for approximately six months, but it was rarely used until recently.  My child has used this seat a total of about 4-5 times.  On January 16, 2013, we put our 2 1/2 year old child into the seat for dinner.  One of the front adjustable legs came out of place, causing the booster seat to tip forward which caused the chair it was attached to to also fall forward.  My child was strapped into the seat, so she fell with the entire structure, landing face first on our wooden kitchen floor.  She had a cut and very large bruise and knot on the left side of her forehead.  We immediately took her to the emergency room for evaluation.
justification: The child suffered a cut and large bruise requiring emergency room evaluation, indicating an injury (severity 3). The incident occurred after minimal use, suggesting it is unlikely but possible with similar products (likelihood 2).

incident_description:
June 2012 my newborn son slept in the product. A product that was recommended by several other parents to help my son's Acid Reflux. 

January 2013 he developed a cough, congestion, runny nose, watery eyes, restless sleeping, so I took him to the Dr. At the Dr. appointment he was diagnosed with an ear infection. My son is no longer in the sleeper because I saw dark brown mold, after learning about this recall.

They were NOT helpful and took my information and said someone would call me since I took him to a Dr. Still waiting on a return call. VERY DISAPPOINTED with this outcome. My child got sick from their product and there wasn't any remorse from the person I spoke with. I will forever be worried that this product has caused long term harm to my child (and other children). 

I truly hope that something will be done about the produce (what about the families that will not know about this recall or clean the product and try to sell it - I don't think that cleaning the product is enough) and the children that have called to report this product. We need someone to protect the children!

Mold marks are present, and have been, even with cleaning. 2 weeks ago I was in the emergency room all day with my daughter for a severe respiratory virus. I'm sure it's not a coincidence. She no longer sleeps in her rocker, but telling us how to clean it isn't helping, as I've cleaned it thoroughly since day 1. A mold stained rocker is no good to myself or anyone else.

incident_description: I noticed today the Fisher Price Rock N Play Sleeper was recalled due to mold. This is not the only reason this product should be recalled. My daughter and my sister's son both used the product from the day they were taken home from the hospital (my daughter was born on [REDACTED] and my nephew was born on [REDACTED]). incident_description: I removed the removable cover from my Fisher Price Rock and Play sleeper to clean it because my infant had soaked through his diaper overnight and it felt damp. I found black mold growing on the hard plastic base. This was the first time I had done this, but this was the first incident where I thought the cover felt damp, so I am not sure what could have caused the mold to grow. It was a significant amount of mold and so I disposed of the entire thing immediately because I did not think it would be wise to clean it. Sure enough I removed the pad and found mold on the support material attached to the frame near and around the belts, however the mold was not on the removable pad. I wash the removable pad regularly and I always put a blanket under my baby every night when she goes to sleep. I disagree that the mold is due to infrequent washing because I wash the pad regularly. I assume the mold is created from the sweat/body my baby gives off in her sleep.

incident_description: My mother was watching the baby so I could get ready before she left for work. We put her in the bassinet which doubles almost as a bouncy seat because you can strap her in and she can sit on an incline. We gave her a teether/rattle to play with which is in the shape of a dragonfly. The bottom part of the dragonfly is a loop so the baby can hold onto it and she had that part in her mouth and the next thing my mother knew was that she had the whole loop part in her mouth and could not get it out. She started gagging and thank God my mother was there with her because she was able to help her. I just can't believe they would make a toy where a small baby could get part of it in her mouth all the way and then not be able to get the toy back out again. I couldn't imagine what could have happened if I had given it to her while I was in the shower and she was in her crib. I just think everyone needs to know about the toy and that they shouldn't just leave there baby with it un supervised.

I didn't immediately associate this as being caused by the diapers, however I did go ahead and stop using the Cruisers just in case and changed to [REDACTED]. Within a week of using creams on the rash and her wearing a different brand of diaper, the blisters and rash were completely gone. It has been a couple of months since this happened, I have had no problems. I purchased another box of Pampers Cruisers to try a few days ago, as I hadn't been completely certain that they were the cause of the rash and blisters previously, and within 24 hours of my daughter wearing them she once again began scratching and has bumps and red rash all over her bottom, front, and sides basically every place that the diaper touched her body. This time I went back to the store to exchange the diapers for [REDACTED] and the woman whom assisted me actually was not surprised at all and told me that they get returns and complaints somewhat often about the Pampers Cruisers causing blisters and rashes on babies.

My 7 month old infant son plays in his Fisher Price infant and toddler rocker almost everyday. Two days back (01/01/2013) he was sitting as he usually does wearing his seat belt. 
He found something interesting that he wanted to catch and started sitting up and leaned forward to grab and eventually fell face down on hard wood flooring bumping his still to mature skull to the ground . Needless to say that this incident was painful for him and more so for us as parents. 

It seems Fisher Price did not invest enough time and resources in the design of this baby gear as it is certainly not suitable for babies who are learning to sit up and get attracted to every thing around them.

I have tried contacting the manufacturer with the details of this incident but have not seen a response as yet from their side.

I would strongly recommend a recall of this product and compensation for all affected parents / families as there have been complains from other parents as well of babies falling down. One of the customers has even commented this on Target's webpage where this product is listed.

Here is a link for reference : http://www.target.com/p/fisher-price-infant-to-toddler-rocker/-/A-13868676#prodSlot=medium_1_1&term=infant and toddler rocker

incident_description: My husband and I bought a bouncy seat for our five month old almost six month old daughter sometime at the end of September or beginning of October. We had a bouncy seat for our other kids but after nine years it broke with all the use. We ended up getting a Bright Starts Pretty in Pink Meadow Blossoms Bouncer. My daughter from the time we got the seat ends up hanging out of the seat by her legs. The seat sits up too high. It needs to sit back and down a little so the child isn't able to sit forward. Also the restraints loosen up. I really think if the seat is going to sit up higher it should have a better restraint maybe one that comes up higher on the child or where you can put the arms in, like some strollers have. The company sent me an email saying to discontinue using the seat if my daughter can sit on her own. She can sit on her own now but she wasn't able to when we started using the seat. A bouncy seat should be able to be used when then are more than a couple of months old. The bouncy seat is for them to bounce in. They can not bounce themselves at just a couple of months old. Our other bouncy was great. We had no problem like this at all and we able to use it for each child up to their first birth day. I really depend on this seat to get house work done. But when I turn around there she is hanging by her legs crying. I hope something is done before a little one is hurt.

I have removed all potential allergens from my diet and she is still exhibiting the same symptoms.  I am almost positive now that it is from the mold. I asked if the product was safe to use after cleaning, and they assured me it was, but I never want to touch the thing again!  And I want my money back!

incident_description:
Our five month old child was laying on his back in the living room using his WubbaNub Infant Pacifier - Yellow Duck By: Gracie (sold at Baby's R Us listed as  ÃÂRÃÂWeb#: 551629  SKU:3735C658  UPC/EAN/ISBN:719771211958  Manufacturer #: WN21196).

My wife went into the kitchen to prepare his bottle and heard him stop crying for his food and start gagging.  Upon returning to the living room, our son's face was red, tears were coming from his eyes, and he had a panicked look.  One of the red legs of the duck was in his mouth and partially down his throat obstructing his airway.  It was sufficiently far enough down his throat to require some force to remove it.

Upon reflection, it appears rather obvious now that a baby will chew on the product's extremities and try to swallow them.  The legs of this particular product have beads in them and flairs at the bottom.  It's just a guess, but it seems to me that when placing the leg in their mouth the beads may be pushed upwards, then upon swallowing the beads could be forced back down causing the item to swell and further lodge in the child's throat.

We had just purchased a frog of the same product and it has legs with substantially the same design.  In the past, we would allow our son to sleep with this product.

incident_description:
We recently used a Phil & Teds Metoo Highchair that includes all the safety modifications that are delineated on their official recall notice.  We have used this chair for our granddaughter once or twice before without a problem.  As in previous uses we had the chair clamped to our granite counter top that is not curved.  I had the clamps tightened fairly tight.  She was in the chair at least 30 minutes during which time she was being feed from the left side of the chair so had her upper body turned to the left while feeding.  After that we we in the same room but were distracted with cooking.  We heard her scream and noticed that the right clamp had slipped off the counter and she was dangling in the chair.  Luckily she was strapped in and the other clamp did not come loose or she would have fallen on our tile floor.  She did not suffer any harm other than a short emotional one so we were thankful.  After checking on line I noticed the recall but nothing that addresses the "improved" model that we have.  
To me the issue is the clamp design itself.  It is too short and does not engage enough of the counter even when pushed in as far as it will go.  The center of the screw clamp is only 1.125" from the throat of the bracket so at best only engages about an inch of any counter.  This does not leave much room for any movement of the chair and leads to one or both of the clamps disengaging from the counter.
Bottom line we will NOT use this chair again and will pursue getting our money back for this product.
justification: The incident involved a safety issue with the highchair clamp, but no physical injury occurred, only emotional distress.

incident_description:
I believe the seat-belt included with the Cosco Flat-fold Highchair needs to be modified to allow quick release of the child in case of emergency, such as choking. My child began to choke while properly secured in her highchair. I was unable to free her from the seatbelt, and had to lift her and her highchair to administer first aid.

My eleven-month old child was seated in her high chair eating dinner. The seatbelt was fastened securely and properly around her and the tray was in place. She began to display signs of choking - her face grew deep red and her mouth moved in a silent gagging motion as she struggled to breathe. Her eyes were bulging and she was not taking in air; she just kept struggling to thrust her tongue forward but was unable to push the food out of her throat or draw air. Her eyes looked terrified, but she could not cry out. It was clear she needed help. I reached for the seatbelt clasp to free her, but the buckle was jammed and would not release. I struggled with the belt but could not open the clasp. She was not breathing. I then tried lifting her out of the seat with the belt still attached, hoping it would break or that she would slide out, but the highchair lifted with her. It was clear that I would not be able to remove her from the seat.

I lifted both her and the highchair into the air and brought her as close to my body as I could. I could not sit and place her over my knee to administer proper first aid as she had an entire highchair, including the tray, attached to her body. All I could do was try to lean her forward on one arm, highchair and all, and hit her on the back with the other hand. It was difficult to find an effective angle with which to dislodge to obstruction, as the seat back blocked access to her back. I had to try many times, in the end quite hard, to dislodge the food enough that she could gasp. She gasped and struggled to breathe for several breaths before she was able to draw enough air to sob.

I have never been so happy to hear a child cry as when she finally drew air and was able to make a sound.

I still needed to sweep her mouth for the obstructing article of food, which was difficult to do as I had to reposition her with a highchair attached to her thighs. When she seemed stable, I was able to set her highchair back down and work on freeing her from the belt so that I could remove her, examine her further, and comfort her. We are fortunate that our incident was resolved with a child that was able to be comforted (after some time.) This could have ended tragically. Helping her while she was stuck in her high chair was difficult and terrifying, and it must have been painful for her to have a large highchair hang from her body. 

The high chair restraint interfered with emergency care and did not easily release the child. Safer design of the restraint could prevent injuries in similar instances by addressing the following flaws. The seatbelt on the Cosco Flat-fold Highchair is difficult to disengage with one hand. The operator needs to be sure the buckle is lined up and that there is not too much tension on the buckle before pressing the tab or the buckle sometimes sticks closed. Also, the seatbelt design demands that each side of the belt be disengaged separately in a two-step process. The process of disengaging the buckle must be successfully performed twice to release the child. In a choking emergency, when the focus is on unblocking the airway so that a child can breathe, the operator may be unable to take his or her focus off of the child in order to successfully open the seatbelt. Additionally, it is difficult to free a child from this seatbelt with one hand, especially if the child is struggling. One hand is needed to steady the center piece while the other hand depresses the buckle-tongue and slides the pieces apart.

These changes to the seatbelt design would allow access to the child in an emergency:

1. The seatbelt on this, or any, highchair needs to be able to be disengaged quickly and easily with ONE HAND to allow access to the child in an emergency.

2. Releasing a child should take only one step.

3. The release button should be clearly marked - a red button, such as used on carseats, would facilitate expedient release of the child in an emergency where seconds matter, such as when the child is choking.
justification: The child experienced a choking incident and was injured due to the inability to quickly release the seatbelt, but there was no death.

incident_description:
I received as a baby shower gift the Fisher Price Rock and Play Sleeper.  Per the packaging, the product is approved for night time sleep.  We used this product for our daughter (now 6.5 months old) for approximately 4.5 months. She slept in a bassinet at night and would be transferred to the Rock and Play after her first feeding of the day.  We liked how it was at an incline (much like a car seat) so it kept her somewhat upright after her feeding.  We also used it for her daytime naps.  

We bagan to notice a flat spot had developed on the back of our daughter's head.  Looking at the angle of the sleeper and where her flat spot is located, it is most definitely the result of this product.  After making this discovery, I've seen MANY online reviews stating the same consequence on other infants and warnings from pediatricians regarding this product.

I contacted Fisher Price and was told we can return the product for a refund. I was read a "script" by an associate informing me of the increase of flat heads in infants since the "Back to Sleep" campaign. This product keeps the infant snug, in one spot, with limited ability to move their head from side to side, thus constant pressure on one part of the skull.  Fisher Price needs to warn parents that this product should NOT be used for nighttime sleep!  Just as a car seat should not be used for long periods of time, neither should this product!

Our daughter now must wear a remolding helmet for 3-4 months to correct her skull deformation.  It will be an out of pocket expense of $1500 to our family and a 5 hour drive twice a month to have it fit. The financial aspect is a small part of my sadness, having to see my baby in a helmet every day for up to 16 weeks breaks my heart.

I hope Fisher Price is required to provide a warning on the packaging or redesign the product so other parents and babies never have to go through this unnecessary heartbreak.
justification: The incident resulted in a skull deformation requiring a corrective helmet, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is high (4) given the numerous similar reports and the product's design.

incident_description:
On January 15, 2010 my mother had me purchase a Baby Mod(manufactured under Million Dollar Baby) Candice 4 in 1 convertible crib for my son who was due in May 2010. Got the crib and love it a lot. My son didn't actually start using the crib until November/December 2010. We loved the crib so much we purchased a second one in September 2011 for our daughter born October 2011, which we later realized the matrices frame support and the parts to hold it on the wooden frame are different. 

On October 12, 2012 I went to put my son in his crib at nap time, to my horror I noticed that the thin metal that attaches to the frame of the support had broken free for almost half of the support. Upon farther inspection it looks like they were cheaply and minimally welded on, like a tack weld.  My son is 2 years old but is delayed and we are in the process of getting him tested for Autism. We had tried to switch to a toddler bed around his second birthday, but he couldn't understand what was happening and seemed to feel more secure with the crib rail back on. 

I called Million Dollar Baby after setting up my son's playpen in his room to take a nap. I spoke with [REDACTED]. After sending many pictures [REDACTED] got his supervises approval to replace the support at their cost but I would have to pay $37.15 for "shipping and handling." I was told they had to get special approval because the crib was out of the "one year warranty." Which the kept going by date of manufacture(October 2009) that was on the crib, not the day that I bought the crib. I agreed to that since I had really no choice. I needed a place bed for him to sleep in. [REDACTED] kept insisting that "for his safety it MUST be turned into the toddler bed due to his age and weight." Even after I explained that my son has delays, I've also looked over the manual for anything about weight/age. All it talked about was if the child was climbing out which my son wasn't. I reluctantly agreed to give it a try. The support wasn't shipped till Monday(Oct 15, 2012) since I called on a Friday(Oct 19, 2012) afternoon. We didn't get it till the following Friday afternoon which it was put on my son's crib right away with the toddler bed rail. In the mean time my son had to sleep in his pack and play.

On December 6, 2012 I put my son to bed like normal. Around 1130pm I went to check on him. Again to my horror the support is broken AGAIN. This time one of the 4 metal "hangers" has snapped off the support. The support has been used less than 2 months and should NOT have broken that quickly. We did try to use it as a toddler bed for a week, but after lots of tantrums, little to no sleep for him(which in delayed children makes the tantrums worse and more frequently), and after talking with my son's therapist it was agreed that he wasn't ready for the toddler bed. So we put the crib rail back up. We have had no issues till tonight when I went in to see it broken.
justification: The crib's support broke twice, but no injury was reported, only potential risk.

Thank you

We distribute a NUKÃÂ® Pacifier primarily to hospitals that use our infant formulas. The plastic portion of the NUKÃÂ® Newborn Orthodontic Pacifier-Exerciser is made of polypropylene and the bulb/nipple part is made of latex rubber. There is no BPA used in our NUKÃÂ® Newborn Orthodontic Pacifier-Exerciser. There is a tear-off pad included within the pacifier packaging box which provides the following Warning information:

incident_description:
We purchased our Fischer Price Rock and Play Sleeper in February 2011 for my newborn son this product was recommended to us by several other parents to help our son with GERD/Acid Reflux. He slept in the sleeper since we purchased it. Starting in September he developed a cough, congestion, runny nose, so we took him to the doctor. At the appointment we were informed that he had two ear infections and that the other symptoms were probably due to allergies since there was no fever. They prescribed him antibiotics and sent us home. Ten days after finishing the antibiotic he was still not better so we took him back to the doctor for the same symptoms. Again he still had the double ear infection at this time they prescribed a different antibiotic. We finished this one and went back because he wasn't better. They prescribed another antibiotic and told us that if this does not clear it up then they would have to do the [REDACTED] shots and then at that point if it was not clear he would need tubes. That night when we went home when my husband was putting our son in the sleeper when he noticed an odor coming from the sleeper. We took it apart to wash it and found black mold from the top (where his head would go) all the way to the bottom part of the sleeper. We immediately removed it from our home and our son is no longer sleeping in it. Since removing him from the sleeper his respiratory problems have cleared up, but we are still battling the ear infections. The Pediatrician said that the mold would definitely cause the symptoms that he was having.Our son had to do the [REDACTED] shots (1 shot for 3 days) and is on another antibiotic and getting ready to have tubes. So my son has been sick now for almost three months now on something that could have been prevented. 

 We Googled Rock and Play Sleeper and were astonished to find pages of complaints from other parents regarding this product. I wish I had read the comments sooner because I would not have purchased this product. 

We called Fischer Price and complained to them and they just want us to send them the sleeper.They didn't offer an apology that their product caused our son to get sick or anything. We trusted that Fischer Price made quality products and have found that to not be true. 

 I am very upset that this product has not been recalled mold is not something to play with and with so many complaints I am having a hard time understanding why. The mold could have caused my 9 month old son to develop pneumonia or could have died from it. I have alerted everyone I know of to not purchase this product. I hope you will take my comments seriously and pull all of these products from the shelf immediately as I do not want anymore infants getting sick from this product.
justification: The infant suffered from respiratory problems and ear infections due to mold exposure, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description:
This morning I went into my baby's bedroom to get her up (I responded to her as soon as I heard her make noise), and when I went to pick her up out of her crib I noticed a strange substance in her crib. There were a bunch of little membrane-like pieces of something, and as I collected them (it filled a small [REDACTED]!) I could tell it was some sort of plastic but I could not figure out where it had come from. I wondered at first if somehow her diaper had disintegrated! After collecting all the pieces (they were embedded in her crib sheet, her jammies, her hair), I began searching for the source. After pulling her crib away from the wall, I found that under her crib sheet, the crib mattress had split and this membrane-like plastic lining stuff was all pulled out, like a big pouch! We are vigilant parents and there had been no situation where we had come in and found her with her crib sheet removed previously, and we do not leave her in her crib to play or cry or fuss unattended. We respond to her every time she cries, so it's not as if she had hours of unattended time to take this thing apart!

I am so concerned about the safety issues present here! Again, the mattress had no holes, there was no indication of any problem, and it just apparently split open allowing her to pull out all of these little bite-sized pieces of very fine plastic, as well as this larger pouch-like plastic piece that posed a terrible danger to her. Of course I have no idea (yet!) if she swallowed any of the small pieces.

My baby is 12 months old; the crib mattress is a Simmons, and we did not purchase it. It was given to us (again, in perfect condition!) from a friend who had used it previously.
justification: The incident involved a potential choking hazard but there was no indication of injury or ingestion.

His leg both times has become bruised. First time bruising went away within a few days, and the second time took almost a week. I would greatly appreciate a new regulation on these crib slats. incident_description:
I recently purchased a total of 6 AmerTac Nite Lites, model 71281. (Two 3 packs) They are a small flat plastic panel that glows when plugged into an outlet. I bought them to replace similar night lights, so I plugged them into the same outlets I had used for a many years. After having the new ones plugged in for a couple weeks, I started to notice a burning smell in my kitchen on various occasions. However, I couldn't locate the source. Several days later I saw an outlet smoldering and quickly unplugged the light. The back of the Nite Lite was burnt and blackened where it plugs into the wall. Subsequent checking of the other lights turned up one other light that was partially melted but less severely, on a separate circuit in a different part of my home. I am convinced if I had not noticed the smoldering light in time, the house would have caught fire.

I feel this could be a safety hazard and I thought it best to report it in case others have found the same problem.
justification: The incident involved a smoldering outlet and potential fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: The Dream Baby Extra Tall Pressure Mount Hallway Gate does not work properly with the pressure mount. I purchased this gate to stop my toddler from going from the living room into the kitchen.  I followed the installation instructions to install the gate without screwing it into my walls. When you attempt to move it back and forth it seems secure.  However, today I went to open the gate, the bottom of it got caught, although the top was open. When I tried to pull the opening part of the gate up to open it the gate fell forward with the weight of it pulling me forward. I fell on top of it hurting my knees, my elbow and my back. I just thank God I did not have my daughter walking in front of me or she could have been seriously injured.  This gate should not be marketed with just the mounting system because it does not work and can be dangerous.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries to the user (knees, elbow, back) and potential for serious injury to a child, indicating a severity level of 3. The likelihood is possible (3) as the issue seems to stem from a design flaw that could affect other users under similar conditions.

incident_description:
The crib has a wedge-shaped (tapered) opening on both sides near the back of the crib. My 9-month-old son's leg was trapped in this opening between the rear side slat and the back corner post when he put his foot through the wider opening near the top and then kicked downwards into the narrower part of the opening.

The back openings on the side panels, where my son's leg was trapped by the way the opening narrows, is 2 inches wide at the top and tapers down to 1 1/8 inch wide before widening out again at the bottom.

My son's ankle was bruised, and circulation was being cut off while his leg was trapped. It was impossible for my son to remove his leg from this tapered opening, and I had difficulty removing it from this tapered opening.

I contacted the manufacturer on 9/24/2012 and was told that the CPSC requires a wedge-shaped opening rather than a consistent opening, which is complete nonsense. The manufacturer then refused to take an injury report.

This is an unsafe design flaw which makes limb entrapments more likely and more serious. The CPSC should investigate, and the manufacturer should provide a free repair kit.
justification: The incident resulted in a bruised ankle and restricted circulation, indicating an injury.

My 17 month old came up to him and rotated the tray and my 4 month old son's left arm was caught behind the ladybug toy located on the rotating tray and it was hyper extended back. incident_description: I am writing because I have a safety issue with the front rail of my sons crib. The crib is a Stork craft model 04588-32N+ and I have owned it for 4 years which I understand is past it's parts warranty, but there is no expiration date on the crib so there is no reason why I shouldn't expect it to be safe for my baby to use. My son usually wakes up in a very happy mood and will immediately stand up holding onto the front rail and make happy sounds while bouncing up and down (he doesn't use his crib like a trampoline). I have a video/audio system installed in his room and as soon as I see him wake up I go and get him, I never leave him alone in his crib when he is awake and we do not misuse the crib in any way. When my son woke up the other day and started bouncing the crib rail cracked leaving a sharp piece of wood protruding from it. Thankfully I was just arriving into his room when it happened and was able to get him before he got hurt.  My son is only 30 inches tall and does not come close to exceeding the height requirement for this crib and there is no weight limit. Mothers trust that when they place their babies in their crib that it is supposed to be a safe place for them to be and I and very upset that this happened. Also since the top railing cracked it is a potential suffocation hazard because if my son was laying against the railing on his mattress the rail bends away from the crib and would allow for him to slide down and get stuck between the crib rail and mattress. I don't know if it was a defect in this particular rail but it is alarming that my baby was able to break his crib and if I didn't immediately get my son when he woke up it could have been a different story. Thank God I never listened to the doctor and let him cry it out in a his crib since it is supposed to be a "safe place" to leave your baby.

When her knee gets caught and she falls onto her mattress, her leg could snap.  Many parent forums online are reporting the same exact incident, with the new crib slat spacing regulations. incident_description: Today my 11 month year old daughter got her leg stuck in between the slots in the crib. Her leg was stuck up past her knee to her upper thigh. She was screaming and crying , at first I tried to just pull her out but it only made her more upset. I applied [REDACTED] on her leg and had to slowly pry her out a little at a time. In the past week on 2 occasions she has gotten her leg stuck through the crib slats (2" apart) and has hurt her leg both times. justification: The incident resulted in injury to the child on two occasions, indicating a severity level of 3.

incident_description: I bought the CoCo & Company Musical Mobile Bailey and attached it to our crib by following the instructions. About a month after it was installed I found a small piece laying next to our 4 month old baby in her crib.  It was a small cap that was attached to a piece labeled as a threaded tube.  The instruction manual does not show this cap piece as being separate from the threaded tube or indicate that it can become detached.  I do not know if it arrived loosely attached or became loose over time.
justification: A small part detached but no injury occurred, and the likelihood is possible given the description of the incident.

incident_description: We've been using Pampers since our daughter was born. We stocked up on the Swaddlers diapers while I was pregnant (2+ years ago). Due to stocking up on them during my pregnancy, we haven't needed to purchase any diapers since our daughter was born. We have had no issues with any of the diapers we purchased at that time. I prefer Pampers over other brands due to the fact that they were more gentle on our daughter's skin than some of the other brands. Currently we are out of state and had to buy some diapers to get her through the rest of the week. We bought the Pampers Cruiser diapers in size 3. Upon opening the package, I could smell there was a difference between this package and our other Pampers. A very strong "baby powder" type of smell. I figured it was just the difference in stages and ignored it. Immediately after changing her first diaper, she had a rash. I thought maybe it was from something she ate. I put a ton of cream on (like we always do if she gets a little rash) and figured it'd be taken care of in the next few hours. Nope. From that point on, her "rash" has become more and more severe. She is miserable and in obvious pain. This is definitely not a diaper rash and is not a reaction to something she has consumed, it is a reaction from the diapers. I'm trying to let her air dry as much as possible and caking on the diaper creams. She's in so much discomfort, that I've been having to give her pain medicine. Something else that makes it obvious that it's the diapers: At night we have her wear [REDACTED] Overnight diapers. After changing her out of those diapers in the morning, her "rash" looks so much better and is almost healed. But as soon as we start putting the Pampers Cruisers back on her, she is suffering. This is not right. Some ingredient in their diapers is causing this and it needs to be removed immediately!!
justification: The incident describes a severe skin reaction in a child caused by Pampers Cruisers diapers, leading to discomfort and the need for pain medication, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description: Was using high chair to feed my 14 month old. He was strapped in. He was rocking back and forth and fell on his head, while still completley attatched to high chair. Landed on his head and suffered swollen eyes and big bump on his cheek
justification: The child suffered physical injuries (swollen eyes and a bump on the cheek), warranting a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is 3 (possible) as such incidents can happen with active toddlers in high chairs.

The consumer could not move the slats apart. She called her brother and a friend who used a saw to cut the slats. There was metal all over the bed and the child.

incident_description: We have a VTech - Sit to Stand Dancing Tower for my 10 month old twins. And the following incident has happened more than once with this product. The first time I thought it may have just been a fluke accident. But each of them have hurt themselves. While standing and holding on to the handles the babys hand slipped and went into the handle. As he fell his arm remained stuck in the handle and he hung by his arm until I freed him. Each of them have been left with bruises from getting their arms stuck in the handles. The top of the toy freely rotates a few inches and thats when their hands slip. All of this happened while be supervised.
