incident_description: I have five children.  My oldest is 7 and youngest is 13 months.  I have been a loyal user of Pampers diapers since my oldest was born.  The only times that my non-potty trained children have not been in Pampers diapers are when they have been at church and there wasn't a diaper in their bags.  This has happened very infrequently (at most 2 times per child).  My two youngest children are the only ones that have experienced extreme diaper rashes and I only recently heard something about Pampers possibly causing the type of diaper rashes my children have had.  It makes sense to me that the diaper might be the culprit.  The older of my two youngest was born in October of 2010.  The diaper rashes typically occur when the kids have had colds or been on antibiotics and have had loose stools.  Having loose stools is not uncommon nor something that none of my other children have had, of course!  But the type of diaper rash that my youngest two have had multiple times is not something that my older children experienced.  This rash consists of very red, raw, blister-like lesions on the skin and it is difficult to get rid of and has left scars on the bottom where the blisters have been.  I have not changed diapers but am planning to switch brands to see if the extreme diaper rashes stop.  I have used Pampers Swaddlers, Pampers Cruisers and Pampers Baby Dry.  The Baby Dry diapers are what I am currently using and the ones I believe to be giving the rash with the raw blisters.
justification: The description reports severe diaper rashes with blister-like lesions and scarring, indicating injury (severity 3). The rashes have occurred multiple times under specific conditions, suggesting a possible (3) likelihood.

incident_description: My daughter has been suffering with a awful rash blister bleeding pain for 8 months we have had her to the doctors several times with numerous diagnosis creams prescription and months of suffering for my little baby to just find out that she is allergic to papers  diaper I was vary angry when I found out that is was not that my baby had sensitive skin that there is thousands off  babes suffering from the same thing something needs done my baby girl screams and cries holding her diaper area because of these horrible diapers thanks [redacted]
justification: The description indicates prolonged injury (rash, blistering, bleeding, pain) due to an allergic reaction, warranting a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is high (4) given the mention of 'thousands of babies' affected.

incident_description: My son got a hold of the lid and was playing with it when he put it up to his mouth and inhaled, the lid got sucked onto his face, covering his mouth and nose. HE COULD NOT BREATH!!!!! I literally had to rip the lid off his face! would have never expected this to happen to a baby's bottle lid! This lid is complete hazard to babies and should be recalled!! Thank god I was sitting right next to him, because he couldn't  even cry or make a sound!!! Parents must be made aware of this item!
justification: The baby could not breathe and required immediate intervention, indicating a serious risk of injury or death.

incident_description:
I noticed on Munchkin Safety Gate that is installed in my home that the bottom stop to hold the gate was loose. I took a close look at it and it seemed as the the screws were loose, That's when I noticed the screw head had popped off. I also examined the gate further and noticed the bottom hinge that was screwed to the wall was loose, that too had the screw head pop off.

Not only could a child have swallowed the screw heads but these screws leave this gate totally unsafe and leave the potential for a child to fall down stairs.
justification: The loose screws and potential for a child to swallow them or fall down stairs indicate an incident with no injury reported yet.

incident_description:
I work at a Babies R Us.  It is NOT a side-by-side store coupled to a Toys R Us.  This Item is sold at BOTH stores: Imaginarium Alphabet & Numbers Foam Puzzle Mat - 36-Piece  http://www.toysrus.com/product/index.jsp?productId=11773791&prodFindSrc=search#showReviews
It states on the packaging that it is recommended for ages 2+ but nowhere on the packaging does it warn about young babies (6 mo. and older) who are teething, having the opportunity of chewing off little chunks (a choke hazard).  The letters separate out of the pad, and the centers of characters, like B, A, D, R & 4, 6, 9 also come out.  They are small enough for a teether to hold in their hand and chew on.  
I have mentioned this to a few of the Babies R Us managers and their answer is to let parents make their own decisions about it and that I am not to warn parents of the possible danger.

I feel that this item should NOT be offered in the Babies R Us (stand alone) stores or they need to be RE-PACKAGED with a very visible warning about choking hazards.
justification: The description indicates a potential choking hazard for babies, which could lead to injury or death, but no actual incidents are reported.

incident_description: No injuries were sustained, but the Nuk Design OrthoStar pacifier poses a huge choking hazard. TWO  of my child's OrthoStar pacifiers have snapped in half leaving the circular end (the size of a quarter) detached from the pacifier. The first time I thought it was a fluke, after two times we will be getting rid of these pacifiers. Luckily both times we caught it before my infant could grab the piece and put it in his mouth. We have had these pacifiers for about five months. The pacifier is made of hard plastic and when it hits a hard floor (ie ceramic tile, wood) it breaks the connection between the circular piece and the pacifier, allowing the circular piece to dislodge. We have only washed these pacifiers in warm water, no dishwasher. So the plastic shouldn't have been weakened.
justification: The pacifiers broke twice, posing a choking hazard, but no injury occurred as the pieces were caught in time.

incident_description:
Around the end of July 2012, caller began noticing that her then 12 month old son's who is 19" tall and weighs 24 lbs legs were becoming entrapped between his fixed side cribs slats.

She hasn't written dates down but said in July she put her baby down for his nap but after only twenty minutes she heard him screaming, went into his room and saw that his right ankle was stuck between the slats of his crib, she removed it within approximately five minutes but his ankle was bruised and there were indentations in his leg above the ankle.

The second time was approximately one week later, she had put bumper back on crib to avoid his becoming stuck but again after putting him to bed she returned to screaming and his left leg was stuck up to his calf and again it didn't take very long to get his leg unstuck but this time there was no injury other than indentations on his leg.

This has happened the same way a couple more times and then approximately September 6th or 7th, 2012 she put him to bed and then around 3:00AM she heard him screaming, ran to his room his right leg was stuck just above the ankle again, she loosened his leg in approximately ten minutes but his ankle was badly bruised and it took her most of the day to get the indentations out of his leg by rubbing with lotion.
She did consult with pediatrician but he did not visit pediatrician.

She did contact manufacturer September 9th, 2012 and was advised to contact CPSC

She is reporting the slats as dangerous and considers them to be unsafe for her baby boy.
justification: The incident resulted in bruises and indentations on the child's legs, indicating injury.

incident_description: I strapped my 7 month old son into the Carter's Infant Bouncer Seat and set it at waist height on the dining room table to make it easier to feed him solids. After I was done feeding him, I picked him up in the infant seat (still strapped in), and went to move him to the floor. As I was moving him, and the seat was just below waist height, the infant seat collapsed. I lost my handling of the seat, and my son , along with the seat, fell to the floor. His upper body was not secured (there are no shoulder straps on the seat), and he hit the left side of his head on the hardwood floor. I picked him up immediately and after assessing his condition, I called the Seattle Children's Hospital Nurse Line. The nurse instructed me to get him to the emergency room immediately. My son suffered a skull fracture and internal bleed. He was in the ICU for two nights, and released on the third day.

He bit into it and had a piece lodged in his throat.  The child coughed up the plastic piece. incident_description: When we sat down to build this crib, both my husband and I were surprised with how flimsy the entire crib felt. Of course, seeing the JPMA Certified sticker, we were hoping to be able to rely on that.   My son has used this crib for about 9 months now (13 month old boy). When we leaned up against the crib always made us nervous, because it didn't feel safe. Well, the other day my husband leaned against the crib to carefully put a sleeping toddler down and the rail snapped.  My husband weighs 190 lbs, but that should not be an issue. A crib only used for 9 months shouldn't snap like that. Also, the paint has been chipped along both rails where my son will stand and wait to be picked up.  According to the process that the JPMA goes through before certifying this crib. This crib should be sustainable. However, it clear is not.  My son is pretty calm in his crib, but I couldn't imagine when he gets older being in this "3 in 1" crib. The  crib is not sustainable, certainly not able to fulfill it's promise of "3 in 1", and the finish on the crib is not safe either.

Therefore, there is a high liklihood that some toddlers would also cause the head piece to snap.  Fyi- my son is approximately 15 lbs.

justification: The child's foot got stuck in the toy, but there was no reported injury, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: I put my son in the bedroom to sleep for the night in the bassinet he has used since birth. It is a simplicity 3-in-1. The bar which collapses to convert to a co-sleeper has given us problems the entire time. It doesn't seem long enough to be secure when used as a regular bassinet. I heard my son crying several minutes later, went into the room and felt into the bassinet to pick him up and he wasn't there! I screamed, turned on the light and there he was, on the floor and the bar I spoke of was hanging down!
justification: The child fell from the bassinet but there is no mention of injury, only the incident itself.

incident_description: Pampers swaddlers sensitive in size 3 caused marks that looked like burns on my daughter in the diaper area even with frequent changing. We used from newborn without issue and my daughter has never had a rash of ANY kind until now so couldn't imagine diapers were the problem. We visited the pediatrician and upon changing diaper brands burn marks were gone withing a few days. We later learned DRY MAX added in swaddlers beginning with size 3.
justification: The incident caused injury (marks resembling burns) to the child, warranting a severity level of 3. The likelihood is unlikely (2) as it appears to be a specific reaction to a particular diaper brand/ingredient.

incident_description: I have a 2007 Pottery Barn Kids Sleigh Drop-Side Crib with the repair kit (2010) to make it a fixed-side crib.  Our children have been very gentle on the crib, and we purchased it brand new from Pottery Barn Kids.  Within the first year of ownership, we had trouble with the crib staying together, and the company completely replaced the crib.  In 2010, we added the fix-side kit to make it stationary, per current US regulations and the recall of all drop-side cribs.  Last night, Sept. 19, 2012, I went to move the crib a few inches (it came with casters), and as I gently pulled it toward me, the back side (NOT the drop rail side, which is now stationary anyway, but the original fixed side) bolt completely popped out causing the back side of the crib to come apart, which in turn caused the diagonally opposite front side rail to pop upward off the fixed track.  The crib literally fell apart where it stood.  It was rendered unusable.  This does not seem to be an issue caused by the drop-side, although the drop-side tracks completely failed when the back failed.  The only positive here is that my child was not in the crib at the time.  We had to completely disassemble the crib and store it in another room, and my child had to sleep on a mattress on the floor.
justification: The crib fell apart but no child was injured, indicating an incident without injury.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that she laid her 14 month old daughter and after approximately 5-10 minutes her daughter stated scream. The consumer stated that she went to look at what was going on and she found her daughter with her leg stuck between the slats. The consumer stated that only her foot was stuck between the slats. 

The consumer stated that the measurement between the slats was approximately 2 3/8ÃÂ. 

The consumer stated that she held her daughter still and took her a couple of minutes to twist her foot enough to get it unstuck. 

The consumer stated that her daughter had a red mark and an indentation on her skin. The consumer stated that today her foot bruised. 
The consumer stated that she did not have to take her daughter to the doctor and she only put ice on her foot. 

The consumer stated that she contacted the manufacturer and they informed her that the crib in compliance with the spacing between the slats. She stated that they referred to CPSC. 

The consumer believes this product should be investigated due to the entrapment hazard that it poses to her child.
justification: The child sustained a bruise and red mark from getting her foot stuck, indicating an injury, but no medical treatment was required.

incident_description:
28 month old daughter started using Night time glow in the dark pull ups. 2 nights, on the second night. After bath time. she was 2hours unable to sleep and pulling on her diaper. When I noticed it was full of urine, I removed it and found both butt cheeks very swollen and hot to the touch. I was confined to the area that was wet with urine and in contact with the diaper. Gave children [REDACTED] and [REDACTED] and over the next 2 hours allergic reaction subsided. We used a different brand for the rest of the night. She has no history of allergies, no new food was introduced, no new product was used during bath time, no product was used on buttocks after bath. Believe it to be a reaction to product in diaper.
The next day she reacted on her legs only. her buttocks were fine as we had a different diaper on. Turns out we forgot to change the bed sheet and there must have been residue on the sheets. again we treated her. The next night with new bedsheets and diapers, no reactions occurred.
justification: The child experienced swelling and an allergic reaction requiring treatment, indicating an injury (severity 3). The reaction occurred twice under specific conditions, suggesting it is possible (likelihood 3) with the product's use.

incident_description: I have been buying these nite lights at Walmart for a couple years.  They come in packs of 4.  They are automatic (turn on when the room is dark), and they have LED "bulbs".  One of them, during daylight,  when plugged into a bathroom GFCI outlet, burst into flames and caused a small fire.  This was in broad daylight, and no one was home.  Fortunately, it did not spread, and went out on its own, but it was obvious that it had actually burst into flames.  I have the melted light remnants, and took pictures.  Much black soot, and the wood below the light was burned by falling melted plastic.  I checked the circuit, and the GFCI circuit breaker had NOT popped, and it tested fine afterward.  Luckily, no one was hurt.  Looked like a manufacturing defect.  First trouble (and the LAST!) I had with these types of lights.
justification: The incident involved a fire caused by a defective night light, but no one was injured.

incident_description: I bought my son a babytrend playard, in january 2012. And everything was fine up untill a few days ago. I woke up to my son laying on the floor with his head where the mesh was connected to the playard. Somehow it came loose during the night and my son scooted out of it.. I am EXTREMELY Dissatisfied with this product!!! I also have no idea how this happend as my son is only 7 months old. I would also never recommend this product to ANYONE! Its an extreme HAZZARD to young children.
justification: The child fell out of the playard but there is no mention of injury, only dissatisfaction with the product.

incident_description: I have a Delta Winter Park 3-in-1 Convertible Crib in  Spiced Cinnamon that I purchased from Target. I put my baby down for a nap and a few minutes later heard a scream. When I went to check on her  she was hysterical and her arm was stuck between the slats of the crib. She was flailing it from side to side and it would not release. I had to help her squeeze her arm out of the bars and her arms was red and had indentation marks from the slats.
justification: The baby's arm was stuck and had red marks and indentations, indicating an injury.

incident_description: Pampers baby dry diapers caused chemical burn on my son Monday 9/10/12 . I called in complained. This is confirmed chemical burn from our doctor.  Pampers is all we have used on my 1 yr old. I'm shocked no recall has been done due to the number of babies this is happening with daily. I was offered coupons as a fix all. That's insane. My son is so much in pain from his skin melting off and oozing blood and pampers want to send me coupons to fix it. Well sorry not ok.  My son hurts and so do tons of other babies. My email has gotten no response, this along with other moms too . I'm offended that a baby supplier is not willing to put our children's safety first. The lawsuit that was against pampers in 2010 was settled for 30 million because of chemical burns. You would think that warrents mandate changes. Obviously not becquse this week my child has suffered daily because of pampers negligent quality assurance. I refuse to stop until a recall is in store. This is absolutely absurd that any child is suffering because of a diaper. There are plenty of things that we has parents have to worry about with our children.  We don't need a company we trust and pay outrageous amounts to hurt them.  By the way, I purchased the big box of 156 Pampers Baby Dry for $35.99 . We opened it and he wore three of them before I noticed the burn. 153 diapers that need to be tested for overload a chemical toxins to make a permanent resolution to this horrid issue. I want a recall!!! I want your company to step up and take responsibility for your wrong doing and fix the problem while preventing any other children pain. Therefore, until contact is made with the person that actually has a heart and cares to help. The journey will continue. He has been unable to wear diapers five days now. The burns are healing up but this is unfornate I'm not getting help.
justification: The description confirms a chemical burn injury from the diapers, supported by a doctor's diagnosis, indicating a severity level of 3.

incident_description:
Hello, 

I purchased this product,
http://www.toysrus.com/product/index.jsp?productId=10954822&cp=2255957.2273443.2255986.2256246.3252379.3250730&green&ab=MyBuys:product 
a few months ago. I walked into my sons room the other day and he had a piece of the mobile in his mouth. It had fallen out of the mobile. It was the size of about a half dollar and could have easily lodged in his throat. I am so thankful I went in when I did and he was okay. The piece that dislodged was supposed to be glued on it seems. I have a picture of the piece of mobile that it was. I am very upset about this and want to make sure that it does not happen to anyone else who has purchased this mobile. Please let me know if you would like any additional information. 

Thank you for your time, 

[REDACTED]
justification: The child was unharmed but could have choked on the dislodged piece, indicating a potential hazard.

incident_description:
Caller's 8 month baby's crib mattress is supported by metal wire spring and is attached to the crib by four bolts.

When caller was lowering the mattress support sometime around August 1st, 2012 one of the four bolts snapped in half causing the mattress to fall.

Caller's husband purchased a bolt at a nearby hardware store and put it in the crib but has now realized that he should not repair the crib himself and has as of today, August 24th, 2012 taken his daughter out of the crib in agreement with his wife.

Caller contacted the manufacturer August 24th, 2012 by faxing a letter to thir warranty/parts department.

There were no injuries

Caller is reporting this incident to allow consumers to be aware.

On or about 8/25/12 called noticed that a second support bolt had snapped in half.
.
justification: The incident involved a crib malfunction with no injuries reported, fitting severity level 2. The recurrence of bolt snapping suggests a possible likelihood of occurrence.

incident_description: We had a severe reaction to Pampers Baby Dry diapers.  My two-year-old grandson was visiting and we bought Pampers diapers.  He had always used [REDACTED] or [REDACTED].  We used the diapers on August 30 & 31.  We went to the emergency room the evening of Aug. 31 with severe swelling of the skin on his penis and the beginning of a rash. He was diagnosed with infection and given an antibiotic. The next morning (Sept. 1) when the diaper was taken off, the swelling was much worse.  We have pictures to document this.  To say it was alarming is an understatement.  It is hard to describe the shocking nature of the condition. We saw a pediatrician, who called the Primary Children's Hospital. After examining the photos and discussing the situation, the urologist there agreed with the local pediatrician that it was an allergic reaction to the diaper and not an infection.  In addition to going back to [REDACTED] diapers, our grandson was treated with Hydrocortisone and Mupirocin cremes.  The doctor saw him several times.  Over the period of days, the swelling eventually went down and the solid rash that covered his entire diaper area began to leave.
justification: The child suffered a severe allergic reaction requiring medical treatment, including emergency room visit and multiple doctor consultations, indicating an injury.

incident_description: toddler able to open stairway approved gate with no issues.
justification: The toddler opening the gate is an incident with no reported injury, but poses a potential risk.

incident_description: My son was sitting in his Cosco Fold Flat high chair he was strapped in with the restraint and I was standing with him the back leg folded up and my son was trapped in the seat he also hurt his arm.
justification: The child was trapped and hurt his arm, indicating an injury occurred.

incident_description: I bought a teething toy for my 4 1/2 month old baby, the Bright Starts Pretty in Pink Carry & Teeth Purse. She was chewing on it, then she just started crying. I took the toy and then realized she was bleeding in her mouth! This happened on July 10th, 2012, and I contacted the company through their Twitter page. They never responded.
justification: The baby suffered a mouth injury from the teething toy, warranting a severity level of 3. The likelihood is unlikely (2) as such incidents are not common but do occur.

incident_description: My child got her knee stuck in between the rails of the crib while standing inside the crib. She was screaming and her knee was very red and her foot was turning blue.  It took my husband a few minutes to get her knee out.
justification: The child's knee was stuck, causing redness and her foot turning blue, indicating injury.

incident_description: We purchased the Dream On Me, Lullaby Cradle Glider from Sears.  This item was shipped to us and we put it together exactly to the directions included with it.  The first night my grandson slept in it, the bottom of the cradle slid out of the slots that were suppose to hold it in place and our grandson fell out onto the floor!  We had tested the strength of the bottom of the cradle after it was put together and it seemed to be good.  During the night, when our grandson became fussy, his mom began to "rock" the cradle, that is when we believe the bottom slid loose.  We could have had a very horrible outcome, but we were blessed, our grandson was only scared, not harmed - but we would like to inform other parents and grandparents of this problem with the product.
justification: The incident involved the cradle failing, causing the child to fall, but no injury occurred.

incident_description:
I put my daughter down for a nap about two months ago, she usually fusses a bit so if she cries, I don't think very much of it because she always falls asleep. She kept crying and started screaming very loud, so I went in her bedroom to find her swollen knee stuck between the bars of the crib. I could not push it back through because she had bent her leg while it was stuck in there. It had swelled up so bad to where I had to hurt her to push it back through. He leg had marks on each side of her knee (four marks because she had bent it). Her knee was extremely purple and swollen. If this would have gone on longer, my daughter would have lost blood flow to the rest of her leg. The bottom half of her leg was completely discolored and her foot was cold, I would assume from lack of blood flow. We have mesh bumpers all around her crib also. 

We continued to use the crib as I figured this wouldn't happen again. Just yesterday we put her down for a nap and her leg was stuck again! She was in pain as she was screaming and crying very loud. We had to use a lot of force to push her leg back through.

Again last night when we put her down for bed, she was screaming again. My fiance went in to try and soothe her to sleep and yelled for me a moment later. This time she was sitting up with one of her legs stuck past her knee in between the bars and he could not get her free. He leg was once again turning red. I immediately ran into the bathroom to get soapy water to try and free her. Even then, we had to use extreme force to push her leg back through. She was very upset and has a blue bruise on each side of her knee where the crib marks were. We have made an appt with her doctor to make sure her knee is okay because it is very swollen with blue bruises.

This crib needs to be recalled. We will be having her sleep in the pack n play until we can afford to buy a different brand crib. A crib is supposed to be safe. This is not safe.
justification: The child suffered injuries including swelling, bruising, and potential blood flow restriction, indicating a severity level of 3. The incident has occurred multiple times, making the occurrence likelihood high.

incident_description:
My wife and I have a 13 month old son (only child) and we purchased the Munchkin brand auto-close gate in February of 2012 and installed it at the bottom of the stairs in our house between two solid walls. In early September of 2012 the top hinge of the gate failed; a spring and screw fell out of the hinge and onto the floor and the gate was no longer secured. Upon inspection the plastic sleeve that holds the screw in place split for no apparent reason. If my wife had not been near by when it happened our son could have either eaten the screw or spring or pulled the gate down on himself. While reading other consumer reviews on Amazon I found that 3 out of 28 reviews described the exact same failure.

I have contacted Munchkin customer service who initially offered to replace the gate with the same model. When I argued that the design was flawed and that I did not trust the design of the auto close model they offered a similar model (easy close) which did not have a spring loaded hinge and was less likely to fail. I agreed to accept the easy close gate as a replacement and Munchkin said they would send it to me along with an extension since the easy close is slightly shorter than the auto close. After almost two weeks I received a package from Munchkin and it contains an auto close gate with no extension. I do not want the auto close gate and will be returning it and asking for a simple refund on the original purchase which I know is against Munchkin company policy.
justification: The gate failure could have led to injury or ingestion of small parts, but no actual harm occurred.

incident_description:
The consumer says the diapers caused big red rashes at the latch site on her child.  She says that the plastic diaper caused big rashes on both of his hips.  She says the straps are on loose so it is not that the straps are too tight.  

The consumer feels that it is due to a chemical in the diaper.  The consumer has been using the product for two day but stopped once she noticed the rashes.  

She noticed the rashes within 1-2 days of having them on her son  The rashes have gone away after using a different brand.  Her son is 21 months old.  She says he is 8lbs under the top weight for this diaper.
justification: The incident describes a child developing rashes from diaper use, indicating an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is rated as 4 (likely) given the detailed account and the resolution after switching brands.

incident_description: On Saturday, I opened a pack of Pampers Baby Dry and put a diaper on my 10 month old daughter. She wore the diaper for a couple hours until she wet herself. My daughter hates to be wet I went to change her because she was screaming and upon removal of the diaper I noticed extreme redness around her vagina and there were several fluid filled bumps. Normally I use cloth diapers or an occational [REDACTED] on her and she has only had a few small rashs that went away as quickly as they appeared. This looked nothing like the rashes she or either of her two older brothers have ever had. I always used Pampers on the brothers when they were small and they had many rashes (they are 7 & 3 now). I put a cloth diaper back on her and smothered the effected area with [REDACTED] (the miracle of all diaper creams). Normally this will make the rash disappear by next change, but it is now three days later and it has only just begun to clear. My concern is the fluid filled bumps and the amount of time it took her to heal from whatever this was. Between friends, family, and myself,  I have been looking at diaper rash and changing baby bums over 15 years. I have never seen anything like this. The only difference from our normal routine was the Pampers brand diaper.
justification: The incident describes a severe diaper rash with fluid-filled bumps, indicating an injury to the child, though not life-threatening.

incident_description: My daughter was securely strapped into her 2012 Inglesina Fast Table High Chair and eating beside me at the table.  She pushed up on the bottom bars with her feet, twisted her body sideways, and went head first over the side of the high chair.  I caught her by her legs, so she suffered no injuries because she did not fall all the way to the floor.  This chair needs a 5 point harness system, not just a waist belt in my opinion.  It is unsafe for babies who are particularly active and thin, as mine is.
justification: The child did not sustain any injuries as she was caught before hitting the floor, but the incident did occur due to the high chair's design.

incident_description: My name is [REDACTED] I am a new mom to a 2 month old baby. I am writing you to let you know about a pacifier I have purchased for my new born baby in June 2012. I was using the orthodontic pacifiers by Born Free for 0-3month old babies. They were part of the Disney collection designed for Babies R Us. My son was using the pacifier for about a month when I noticed that it had mold around the base of it and on the inside of it. I threw it out immediately and opened the other one for him to use thinking it wouldn't do the same. A few weeks later I noticed the same on the second pacifier, there was mold inside and around the base of it as well. I think the mold may have been caused by milk getting into the base, it looked like the rubber nipple was not sealed well to the base. When I went to rinse it off, water got into the nipple and that's when I noticed the mold.  Being a new mom I was concerned with my child's safty and wanted to let you know about this issue so that other parents can be advised. I am hoping that this issue gets fixed by the company because my son liked this product and I haven't found another pacifier that works as well for him. I am afraid to buy him another set of the Born Free brand in case they get moldy again.
justification: The incident involved mold in pacifiers but no reported injury or death, only concern for safety.

incident_description:
My six (6) week old son, approximately eleven (11) pounds, was sitting in the Baby Bjorn Babysitter Balance, in the "A" or "play" position, when it suddenly collapsed down into the "C" or sleep position.  The product was on a hardwood floor and I used it according to the manufactures specifications.  I was not actively bouncing my son in the product; however, my son's movements did make the product bounce moderately up and down.  This activity was within normal use of the product and did not cause abnormal loads on any structure of the product.  My son was thrust violently backwards; no physical injury resulted.

I believe the hard plastic "positioner" on this product is poorly designed and can easily and spontaneously come out of its position causing the product to violently collapse down into another position potentially causing serious injury or trauma.  Also, any upward force and/or pressure applied at the bottom of the positioner will cause the positioner to eject out of the position notch.  There is no way, such as with a simple locking mechanism, to effectively and securely lock the "positioner" into one of the three (3) active positions.
justification: The incident involved a sudden collapse of the product but no physical injury resulted, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is possible (3) as the issue could recur under similar conditions.

incident_description: I was bathing my infant son of 4 months in this bath tub,, when he tilted his head back as I was washing his hair this tub tipped backwards this also happened when he was about 3 months old also,,, you can release the ends of the tub so that a toddler can sit in it but this is not an option for my son as he is still a supported sitter and cannot yet sit independently.
justification: The infant's head tilting back and the tub tipping could lead to injury, though none was reported this time.

incident_description: Rail support/holding mattress to crib came apart at the welded portion of the rail. Mattress no longer fits securely into the crib.
justification: The rail support failure is an incident with no reported injury, but it poses a potential hazard if not addressed.

incident_description: I was using plug-in LED night lights throughout my home.  I discovered that one of them, made by AmerTac, model #71352, had caught on fire, burned, and melted while still being connected to the socket.  Lucky the entire house didn't burn down.  I read on the internet that other models of AmerTac plug-in LED lights have been recalled for possible fire and shock dangers.  Please advise.  Thanks.  [REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved a fire hazard with no reported injuries, and there is evidence of similar incidents with other models.

incident_description: Every morning my 5 month old daughter wakes up crying after sleeping all through the night. She is a reflux baby so she naps and sleeps in her Rock N Play (made by Fisher-Price). She is always buckled in when in the Rock N Play for safety purposes. When I heard her crying this morning, I went into her bedroom and was shocked and terrified at what I saw. I frantically rushed to the Rock N Play to untangle my 5 month old daughter who had fallen out of the sleeper but had her leg tangled in the safety restraint. The restraint had cut off the circulation to her left leg from her knee down. She was hanging upside down and her head was barely touching the ground so the restraint really had a tight grip on her calf. Based off of the coloring in her cheeks, she had not been hanging upside down very long, but for this to happen at all is a nightmare! I am saddened that I trusted this product yet it led me to find the horrific sight of my infant daughter hanging upside down. I am just beside myself and so is she. She has clung to me all day and wakes up from her naps frightened. Recall this product now before something worse happens than a strawberry and a burn on her leg from her trying to get loose. This was the scariest day of my life thanks to Fisher-Price's Rock N Play sleeper.
justification: The infant suffered a burn and restricted circulation, indicating physical injury.

incident_description:
I bought a night light for my 89 year old aunt's apartment. She said when she went past it in her wheelchair, it was smoking. She pulled it out. It had burned the top of the unit, probably from inside, since it was a good inch from the electrical prongs. Her building maintenance department checked and said there is nothing wrong with the outlet. 

This particular night light could easily have been bought for a baby/child's room..it contains a toy turtle and shell, and is filled with some liquid.

I am so thankful that my aunt was awake and noticed this. It is troublesome to have to do this paperwork, etc., but I can't ignore the potential for a fire and worse.
justification: The night light was smoking and could have caused a fire, but no injury occurred.

incident_description: I pulled on the nipple of a MAM pacifier to check it before I gave it to my daughter and a small hole appeared where the nipple and hard plastic shield meet.  I continued to pull and was able to easily rip the nipple off about 3/4 of the way.
justification: The pacifier nipple was damaged but no injury occurred, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description:
I have already notified IKEA about an accident I had with one of its Antilop high chairs with tray.  

When feeding my son yesterday, I rested my elbows on the tray attached to my IKEA Antilop high chair, and the tray popped off hitting me violently in the face and slicing my nose by the small pointed (and very sharp) piece that hooks the tray into the high chair itself.  I do know that there was already a recall on these high chairs for an unrelated issue, and I am appalled to learn the hard way of this newest safety concern.  I am so very thankful that my child was not injured -- it could have been a grave injury to someone so little, including a very serious eye injury that could have blinded him based on where it hit me.
This is a serious matter, that I sincerely hope will get the attention it deserves before a child is maimed, or worse.
Sincerely,
 
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in a facial injury to the parent, and there was a potential for serious injury to a child, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is set to 4 as the incident happened and there is evidence of a design flaw.

incident_description: My son was playing with this potty seat and put it on his head.  The seat was able to slip over his head and got stuck around his neck.  We had a very hard time getting the seat off of his neck and were about to head to the hospital to cut it off when we finally did manage to pull it off.
justification: The potty seat got stuck around the child's neck, causing distress but no injury, and was eventually removed without medical intervention.

incident_description:
I have an ibert safe T bike seat designed for children.  The seat is attached to a metal t base by a ring and clip, the clip being a cotter pin.  While riding with my son the clip broke causing the pin to disengage and thus causing the seat to tumble off the bike.  The whole seat is dependent upon the cotter pin for safety.  This product is potentially very dangerous, as breaks like this will continue, again this is a bike carrier for a child, traffic is a concern if the child should fall off.  
I was using the product within all guidelines provided by the company.
justification: The incident involved a bike seat failure that could have led to injury, but no actual injury was reported.

incident_description: Sealy crib mattress pad shrinks with washings.  When put on crib mattress, it compacts the mattress length, leaving a 3 to 4 inch space between the mattress and crib.  There were no injuries, I cut the side fabric so it would not pull.
justification: The mattress pad shrinking caused a gap in the crib, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: My 17 month old son was sitting in the Eddie Bauer Pop-Up Travel Chair at the table. With his feet, he pushed back against the table and knocked his chair over backwards. The seat cushion of the travel chair came out of the base (it is only attached to the base in the back), so that when my son fell backwards, he was also flung up about 6 inches. Because of this, he hit his head hard on the hard tile floor and needed a trip to the ER. If the travel chair had a buckle attaching the seat cushion to the front of the base, this would not have happened.
justification: The child suffered a head injury requiring an ER visit, indicating a severity level of 3. The incident is possible but not highly frequent, hence a likelihood of 3.

incident_description: The product is called Fisher Price Rock n Play Sleeper. My son has been using since he was born on [REDACTED]. After 3 1/2 months of use i noticed that his head has become extremely flat of the back. I am positive that it is a result of sleeping in his rocker. After researching the product more online i noticed that there are other parents that have the same problem, flat heads. His doctor is treating it with pillows trying to reshape his head but he could possibly need to wear a helmet to correct the problem. This product should be recalled.
justification: The incident describes a physical injury (flat head syndrome) requiring medical treatment, and online reports suggest it is a common issue with the product.

incident_description:
This is in regards to the Graco Lauren crib. 

8/29: We had to cut one of the slats on the crib because our 15 month old son's leg got got in between two of the side rails! He was screaming and crying because he couldn't get his leg out. I did not expect this to happen with this product since we purchased this crib based on its high reviews (online and in baby books). I now have a crib with a sawed-through slat! 

I was informed by the manufacturers of this crib (Lajobi) that the crib is made to the specs of the CPSC.  I also read that this is a general issue with all cribs (and kids getting their legs caught between the rails) and the suggested solution is to place a breathable bumper in the crib.  It is my understanding that bumpers shouldn't be placed in cribs (to prevent SIDS).  So, my question is, isn't there a better solution?
justification: The child's leg got stuck between the crib rails, causing distress and potential injury, indicating a severity level of 3. The issue is described as a general problem with cribs, suggesting a likelihood of 4.

incident_description:
I purchased a Baby Cache Kensington crib and dresser (http://www.babycache.com/site/products_kensington.html) from Babies R Us.  

Crib Issue:
* Holes not drilled on right rail (company promised to ship replacement part and did not ship)
***Potential Safety Issue: Improper quality control can lead crib to collapse if holes aren't drilled properly
* Inferior staining and glue stains

incident_description:

When I contacted Munire about this, they responded with the following:

You can get assistance from the store you purchased from if needed.  Sorry for the problem and thank you for purchasing Munire Furniture."

We purchased a baby gate manufactured by Summer Infant, Inc.

Summer Infant, Inc.
1275 Park East Dr
Woonsocket, RI 02895-9905
1-800-268-6237

Model number 07710.   The manufacture date has eight numbers. The first number is difficult to read.; it may be a "1" or it may be a "7". The remaining numbers are _1052504.   The product is described as a "6 foot extra tall metal expansion gate".

The gait was properly installed and in use for a few days. Our 3-year old niece opened the gait door and lacerated her pinky finger in the hinge area.  The gate door nearly amputated her finger. She was rushed to the ER and an orthopedist sutured her finger back together. X-rays revealed that her finger was not only lacerated but also broken. Her entire fingernail was found on the floor next to the gait. 

The part of the door/gate that caused this injury was pre-assembled before shipping. Therefore, there is nothing I did wrong during assembly to create this pinch-point.

It is interesting to note that the picture of the gate on the box has a different door mechanism than the one we received in the box.  

I feel this gait needs to be recalled because it has an obvious pinch-point that will amputate fingers. 

We have other gates in our house from Summer Infant but they are different model numbers and slightly different gates.  The other gates don't have this same dangerous door mechanism.

I hope this saves other children from having to endure the pain of this injury.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe injury (laceration, broken finger, and near amputation) requiring emergency medical treatment.

incident_description:
My son has the Million Dollar Baby crib "kalani" with the full size bed conversion kit.  The bed rails are designed such that there is a 1 inch deep lip for the mattress and box springs to rest down into.  The problem is that a full sized bed requires three 1x4 bed slats, and once the slats are in the boxspring no longer rests within the bedrails.  It slides all around.  One morning recently when my 4 year old was getting out of bed, because the boxspring had slid about a foot off the frame, he got caught completely between the bedrails and the boxspring.  Prior to this on numerous occasions he has gotten his foot stuck the same way.  Also, on one occasion, the mattress had slid so far off the bedframe, unbeknownst to us, that when my husband went to sit on the corner of the bed to read a bedtime story, that the mattress pivoted up in the air like a seesaw, nearly launching my son off the bed!  I have contacted Million Dollar Baby on numerous occasions to try to report/resove this and they initially told me that the rails didn't require slats and weren't designed to used them, and when I told them that the mattress warranty required them, they changed their story to "you must have the bed assembled incorrectly."  So I sent them pictures that the bed was assembled the only way that it will go.  They then said that the slats must be sitting ontop of the rails rather than resting within them, which is not true.  They have since closed the complaint without resolving it.  I have been very lucky that my son has not been injured worse than the few cuts, scrapes, and bruises.  I feel that I shouldn't have to check his bed every morning and evening to make sure he isn't going to get hurt, and neither should other parents.

If desired, I can copy you on all of the emails that have been sent regarding this issue.

Sincerely,
[REDACTED]
justification: The child has suffered cuts, scrapes, and bruises from the bed issue, and the problem occurs frequently, as described.

incident_description:
This is part of a letter that I sent to Pottery Barn Kids and Williams-Sonoma, Inc.
company on July 9th via e-mail and hard copy letter. I tried to follow-up almost a week later and and was told that someone would contact me. I followed up again on July 20th and received no response.

The day after Thanksgiving in 2011 I went to your store in Kenwood Town Center in Cincinnati, Ohio. I was expecting my second child and was interested in buying the Ella Crib which I had seen on-line. This crib was reasonably priced and I believed that since it was a product from one of your stores that it would be a high quality product that would last. The associates in the store were very helpful. The crib was being discontinued and they were able to find the color crib that I wanted at a different store along with the conversion kit. I was so excited. It took a few weeks and some following up on my end, but the crib came in. We left it in the box until a few weeks before my due date (Feb. 21, 2012). When we opened it the crib looked lovely but had a somewhat strong paint smell. After it aired out a bit the smell went away. We checked the conversion kit at this time and it appeared to have all of the parts. We then assembled the crib and we put a mobile on the crib as well. 

The mobile was a nice mobile that we had used on my first sonÃÂs Bellini drop side crib. The mobile did not leave any mark. In fact that crib is a bit older has been used by a few kids before my son and does not have a scratch on it. 

The mobile was on the PBK crib for a few months and recently I noticed that my son was able to kick it with his feet so I took it off and noticed that the paint on the side of the crib was chipping off in chunks. I picked away the loose pieces but little hands that pick like my first son could probably easily pick additional paint off in chunks. I was shocked to see this. I would fully expect that a Pottery Barn Kids Crib would be designed with the expectation that the customer would put a mobile on it. I assumed that there was something wrong with the paint and that if I called your customer service someone would help me.

On July 3rd I contacted the customer service number on your website. I explained what happened and I was transferred to someone else. I then explained what happened again and again I was transferred. I explained my situation for a third time and was told that there was a special group who dealt just with cribs, but that they were not in on July 3rd because of the holiday. I was given a different number [REDACTED]) and told to call back on Thursday. 

On Thursday I called back. I explained what happened and was told that since I purchased the product in the store they could not help me. I was told to contact the store. I hung up the phone and called the store. The same very nice associate who helped me to order the crib answered the phone. I explained my situation to her and she said that she would contact someone and see what they could do. I said that I thought it was the Ella crib but that I was at work and was not 100% sure. She said to e-mail her a photo of the crib. That afternoon I sent her a picture of the crib so she could see the model and a close up of the paint chips. I heard nothing back. 

On Saturday I happened to be at the mall so I stopped by your store. I explained what had happened and the associate who I had sent the e-mail to was in the back. They called her and she came to the front. She was holding a piece of paper and chatted with some other people before coming to talk to me. She said that she had received the e-mail. She then gave me a piece of paper with a number for the furniture doctor. She said that if she were me she would contact them and have them fix the crib because PBK does not make the crib anymore and because PBK has a policy of not providing replacement crib parts. I asked if PBK would cover the cost. She said that BPK would cover it if we had purchased the mobile from PBK but since we did not the cost would not be covered. She then said that BPK mobiles would not hook on the same way that ours did. I asked how they work and she explained one that hooked on differently and one that worked exactly as ours had. I said that I would have expected that your cribs would work with a mobile and that most customers who shop at your stores would use a mobile. She said that she could not help me, but that she would pass my e-mail on to her regional director (I believe that is the title, but I am not positive). Since I had not heard back from her originally I do not anticipate hearing back from anyone. 

I went home and read the materials that came with the crib. It does not say not to use a mobile that hooks onto the crib and it does not say to only use PBK mobiles. It does say to contact customer service if there is a problem with the crib and that PBK will help to find replacement parts if needed. 

I have used this mobile on a different crib with no problems and would not anticipate a problem with a quality product from PBK. If the crib had started to chip and I had received any service from anyone I would not be bothered. I know that quality issues can occur with any product. For all I know the paint was not completely dry before the parts were packaged (maybe that is why it had a strong paint smell when we opened the box) or something strange happened that the paint was not set in properly. I understand with mass production that problems can happen, but I am slightly disturbed with the service that I received when I had a problem. No one has been interested in helping me at all. 

Please understand I do not mind the way that the crib looks I am primarily concerned that when my son gets older he may be able to pick the paint off and eat it. Even if the location in question is repaired what if this is a problem with the paint overall and other areas that we are unaware of are weak and he can pick the paint when we are not watching him. The crib should be a safe area in the house where you can leave your child and know that they are safe without watching them 100% of the time. 

At this point I am looking for someone that is interested in helping me. I would be interested in either getting a replacement railing, returning the crib and conversion kit and getting a replacement crib and conversion kit or just getting a store credit for the crib and conversion kit.
justification: The incident involves a crib with chipping paint posing a potential safety hazard, but no injury or death has occurred.

This has several pieces, including the top, the legs, and the base. The legs contain springs which make it potentially very bouncy if you have an enthusiastic baby (which I do). The bottom of the legs attach to the base pretty securely. They pop in and sort of click in place. The top part of the leg attaches by matching it up with a notched section on the top, pushing against the spring, and turning it so it doesn't line up with the notched part. There is not anything that fastens it, or prevents it from turning back the way it went in.

I think this is what happened--after some use with an occasionally enthusiastically bouncing baby, the piece at the top turned slowly and worked its way back toward the notched opening. Luckily I was 2 feet away when it happened and he wasn't hurt, but one leg popped off entirely, one detached from the top and one detached from the base. It would have been pretty ridiculous if it wasn't so alarming--the thing just quite literally fell apart with him in it. He could easily have had a leg pinned in the wrong direction and had it hurt by the weight of his body pulling down on the top. What a disaster. He was terrified but unhurt, thankfully.

If you buy this for your child, please periodically check under the top to make sure the legs have not twisted back toward the notch in the top to prevent this from happening again!

justification: The child fell head over heels, which suggests a potential for injury, though the description does not confirm one.

incident_description:
The caller works in a hospital, the product is used in a newborn ICU.  She says the baby was in the bouncy chair on the floor.  The seat became detached, causing the baby to fall in hit his head.  the baby received a bruise on his forehead.  

The baby did not require medical care but did require observation to make sure he did not need medical treatment.
justification: The baby fell and sustained a bruise, which qualifies as an injury, but did not require medical care.

incident_description:
The cradle is under CAP# 99-020A. The consumer has one of the products mentioned in the recall, but wanted to point out that there are other problems that are not mentioned in the recall.

(1998)  When the consumer's son rolled over against the side slats, the full top assembly and the side slats, all came out of the holes that they were secured into.  The consumer caught her son in time and he did not fall out of the cradle.  There were no injuries.  The consumer discontinued use of the cradle, but she still has it.

(4/26/2012)  The consumer was looking at the CPSC website, when she discovered that the cradle she has was included in recall CAP# 99-020A.  The legs on the cradle that she owns have become loose, but there have not been any incidents, because the consumer stopped using it back in 1998.
justification: The incident involved the cradle's side slats coming loose, but the child was caught in time with no injuries.

incident_description: We had an AmerTec LED night light in my son's bedroom at night. This morning he came running and screaming out of his bedroom saying that his light was broken (he is 3 years old). When I went to look, all I saw was smoke and smelled burning plastic. I took a picture of the light, also. It looks like it exploded on the inside. This particular light was not listed on the recall. The model number is 71352.  It is a white, rounded light with SY on the back. Very scary incident for my little boy. We live in a brand new house, so I knew it couldn't be a wiring issue.
justification: The incident involved a night light exploding and emitting smoke, causing fear but no physical injury to the child.

incident_description: I purchased the Fisher Price Discover n Grow Baby Booster. The product is a baby high chair with feeding tray, and the feeding tray contains a toy insert that fits in the tray. My 4 month old was able to lift the toy insert easily and hit himself in the face with it. Luckily he missed his eye, but if I hadn't been watching, this could have happened again. I then put the toy insert back in the tray carefully, thinking it hadn't been correctly placed before, but my baby lifted the tray out and tossed it on the floor. I tried again, and he lifted it slightly, then pushed it back in. It was a good thing his tiny fingers didn't get stuck under the edge. I contacted Fisher Price, and they told me they'd never heard of such a thing before, but I should send it to them and they'll issue a refund. I am filling out this report because I believe this could be a safety  hazard. Many teething babies attempt to bring toys to their mouths - my son cannot be the only one. If a 4 month old can lift the tray, older children certainly could as well.
justification: The incident involved a baby lifting and potentially injuring himself with a toy insert, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: I purchase the Cotton Tale Bouncer made by Bright Star from Target. I went to place by two month old into the bouncer and when her weight was put onto it the back clip popped off which caused the back bar to come apart and the bouncer collapsed to the ground. I caught her just in time for her not to slam her head to the floor but she did pump it causing a red mark on the right side of her forehead. I contacted the company about this matter, they offered to replace the bouncer with a different kind but I believe this product is unsafe and needs to be redesign so the clips in the back can not come off without removing some sort of securing device .
justification: The infant sustained a red mark on the forehead due to the bouncer collapsing, indicating an injury. The incident suggests a design flaw that could recur under similar conditions.

incident_description: My baby got trapped on more than one occasion between the mattress and the bottom of the playpen. At first I thought it was because the bottom is not heavy enough to put a normal playpen sheet on it. It seems to pull it up at the sides and it doesn't fit right. I stopped using sheets and relied solely on the playpen's design of [REDACTED] to keep the mattress down. To my dismay, this happened again today with a child that I was babysitting!! Thank GOD that I went in to check on the quiet little one to make sure she was asleep. Half of her face and body were underneath the mattress. She could have suffocated and I am so upset about this!!!!  The mattress doesn't sit tight against the sides like all other playpens that I have seen. There is quite a gap on all 4 sides, posing a suffocation hazard.
justification: The incident describes a near-miss suffocation hazard with no actual injury or death, but a clear potential for severe harm.

incident_description: Simmons Crib Model # 225070. My 3 year old son tried to climb in crib while 'drop down side" of crib was in down position.  "Drop down side" broke away from crib when plastic attaching it to crib broke causing my son to fall on floor with "drop down side" of crib landing on top of him.
justification: The child fell and was hit by the crib side, indicating potential injury but no mention of serious harm or death.

incident_description: After one night of use, a red Retro Rocket Night Light we bought at the gift shop at the Space Needle in Seattle in late April, became so hot, it began to melt.  The base of the rocket began to collapse.
justification: The incident involved a night light overheating and melting, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: My 8 month old son was sleeping in his crib with a Nuk OrthoStar Pacifier. He woke up and while I was walking up the stairs I heard him choking. I ran into his room and saw he had the whole pacifier in his mouth and was choking and gaging. He vomited a little bit while I pried it loose. He is fine now.
justification: The child choked on the pacifier but was fine after intervention, indicating no lasting injury.

incident_description:
I was assembling a Target Circo Musical Mobile 030 -02-1159 that plays brahm's lullaby when I found that there was an error in the dies used for manufacturing and the mobile will only assemble backwards (I.E. different that the instructions display).  The mobile we have can only be assembled so that the clamping nut orients to the inside of the crib.  The nut is of large diameter and could be loosened by a child once they gain their faculties.  In the upright an arm there is an alignment groove/tang and locking tit that orients the unit, and they are diametrically opposed to how the instructions show them.   Unsure if every unit was mis-manufactured or just this lot, but some unknowing person will assemble it and not realize the nut is on the wrong side of the crib.
I haven't returned to the store yet, and would be happy to send photos of the unit and a PDF of the assy. instructions
justification: The mobile can be assembled incorrectly, posing a potential hazard if the nut is loosened by a child, but no injury has occurred yet.

incident_description: My daughter was having her morning bottle when she started to gag and choke.  I rushed to her.  Milk was flooding her face and she was struggling to get something out of her mouth.  The nipple tip broke off in her mouth!  I am an RN and was able to safely remove the broken tip from her throat.  I have a picture of this, and have saved the item.
justification: The child choked on a broken bottle nipple but was unharmed due to timely intervention by an RN.

incident_description: After using bottles given to us by our adopted daughter's foster mom, we found out that the ounces marked on the bottles are not accurate. In other words, when you measure 4 ounces in a measuring cup and pour it in the bottle, it shows the water at 4.5 ounces. This means that when mixing formula straight in the bottle, as is common, you have formula that is more concentrated than intended which can be very dangerous for the baby.
justification: Inaccurate bottle markings can lead to over-concentration of formula, posing a serious health risk to the baby, which qualifies as an injury risk.

incident_description: My daughter, who is fourteen months, was playing with the VTech - Learn & Dance Interactive Zoo which she has had for about six months. While she was playing with it, she went to press one of the four buttons on the top that sing about different animals, and her thumb got lodged under the button. I did not know what was wrong at the time, and when I saw the problem, I gently tried to pull her thumb out, but it would not come out. I had to pry the button up with my hand, with force, to finally free her thumb. She had a large indention from where it caught her thumb. I then looked underneath it, and saw that there was a very large gap in between the buttons and the toy itself.
justification: The child sustained a large indentation on her thumb from being caught under the button, indicating an injury, but such incidents are unlikely to occur frequently.

incident_description: I correctly assembled the travel bed, and placed my 4.5 month old infant down for a nap in the travel bed. Thankfully I actually remained in the same room, and quickly heard him screaming and crying. He was entrapped between the mattress and the side of the tent, but fortunately, I was able to quickly retreive him. Although I immediately determined that this product would go back to the store, I placed him in the tent again (while I stood next to it to watch), and observed him quickly roll onto his stomach, and the momentum of the roll caused him to roll again and wedge himself partially on his back and partially on his stomach between the side of the mattress and the tent. Again I retrieved him, and watch this happen an additional time. This product represents a substantial entrapment risk to infants.
justification: The infant was entrapped multiple times but was quickly retrieved without injury, indicating a high likelihood of recurrence with no harm.

incident_description:
The consumer says that a child can easily roll over  she says that there is padding underneath wood sides.  She says that a child drops off into the next slat, rolls over and have their faces buried face down.  CONSUMER ADDED:  when laying on mat in bassinet or in bottom.  Baby rolls over, three times found with face buried.  The mat dips down and is not level.  This can be seen in photos. Did it with one baby in play yard.  The company tried to use two babies as an excuse.  When husband put plywood under mat it was fine.  In photos you can see gap between wood pieces.  

The consumer says she would never place the children on there stomachs who are about now 8 months.  She contacted the manufacturer who offered to send replacement padding.  She says at time of the incident the babies were 2 1/2 weeks to 1 month old twins inside the play yard.
justification: The incident describes a hazardous situation where babies could suffocate due to the design flaw, but no actual injury or death was reported.

incident_description:
The consumer says the rockers are too short and is very easy for the child to rock to hard and have the rocker flip over.  The consumer has seen this occur twice with two different children.  

The consumer contacted the manufacturer today who told her that it is due to operator error and that the child should remain centered while on the rocker.
justification: The rocker flipping over is an incident that has occurred twice without reported injury, indicating a severity level of 2. The likelihood is rated as 4 (likely) due to the consumer observing it happen multiple times.

incident_description: Our 2 year old daughter had never suffered a serious diaper rash. We have always used a zinc oxide based diaper rash cream along with either pampers dry max or [REDACTED] diapers. Recently we put her into day care in the mornings. One time she was changed there into a Pampers crusier diaper, when I took her home that afternoon she had developed a horrible case of diaper rash complete with what appeared to be blistering. She had never had anything even remotely like it before. There was no sign of any problem that morning. I had heard something about some babies having a reaction to the crusiers and told the day care not to use them on her again. She had never worn one before. The rash (burn?) is slowly healing but is still quite noticeable after nearly 2 weeks.
justification: The child developed a severe diaper rash with blistering, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
This is the second occurrence of a child entrapment injury with this same GRACO crib.  I filed a prior CPSC report on 2/17/12, including photos, when the first incident occurred and I never received a response from CPSC investigators or the manufacturer.  See CPSC report 20120217-BC4A4-2147470080.

On or about 4/23/12 (similar to the 2/17/12 injury) my wife placed our 17 month-old daughter in the GRACO crib for a nap.  We generally stopped using the crib after the first injury, but my wife was washing the sheets of the another portable crib that we were using for our daughter, so this crib was the only option.  About 5 to 10 minutes later, my wife heard a loud and distinctive scream from our daughter.  Our daughter almost never cries or screams, even when she injures herself.  This scream was distinctive and left no doubt that our daughter was in extreme pain.  My wife ran into our daughter's bedroom and found our daughter trapped in the front rails of the crib.  Our daughter's leg was pinned between the wooden rails and her body was twisted, trapping her in such a position that her neck was twisted.  The screams became muffled as our daughter's airway closed off, beginning to suffocate her.  My wife worked frantically to dislodge our daughter from the rails, but she described the process as "very difficult" to dislodge our daughter.

Again, our daughter suffered deep bruising on the area of her leg that was trapped, along with swelling and pain.  Fortunately, my wife was nearby and was able to dislodge our daughter before she became unconscious from her neck being trapped in a twisted position.

I do not believe the CPSC, GRACO, or LAJOBI (the manufacturer) have taken appropriate steps to prevent these serious entrapment injuries.

On 6/26/12, I phoned GRACO and notified them of the two injuries associated with this model crib, knowing that many other children must be suffering similar or more serious injuries.  I have now disassembled the crib completely and will no longer use it.  THIS CRIB DESIGN IS UNSAFE AND HAS INJURED MY ONE YEAR-OLD DAUGHTER TWICE.  GRACO was entirely uninterested in investigating or correcting the hazard, and they refused to offer replacement or refund money for the crib during my phone conversation.  GRACO directed me to contact the manufacturer, LAJOBI.

LAJOBI showed even less interest in doing anything, while admitting that they receive a high volume  of calls regarding children being injured by these cribs.  The LAJOBI representative I phoned blamed the CPSC, explaining that LAJOBI crib rails are designed from CPSC standards and until the CPSC changes those standards they will continue to market and sell these cribs.  LAJOBI said they will not replace any cribs or refund any money, citing the CPSC standards.

I told the LAJOBI representative that it seemed odd that a manufacturer would knowingly continue to sell a product that is injuring a high number of children, and again she explained that it was the CPSC's fault, not theirs.  She said the CPSC was aware of the injures and has failed to changed the standards, so there is nothing the manufacturers will do.

Based on my initial investigation, there is plenty of liability to spread around (between GRACO, LAJOBI, and CPSC) and finger-pointing, but everyone is missing this goal of protecting our children - - very odd, since all the parties involved have children as their primary responsibility.
justification: The child suffered deep bruising, swelling, and pain from being trapped in the crib, indicating an injury (severity 3). The recurrence of similar incidents and the manufacturer's admission of high volume of injury reports suggest this is likely to happen again (likelihood 4).

incident_description: My child almost fell out of her IKEA Antilop chair.  I caught her as she was falling. The restraint buckle opened and that is how she stood up and fell out.  We noticed the strap opening several times after that and we stopped using the chair.
justification: The child was caught before falling, so no injury occurred, but the incident involved a restraint failure.

incident_description: I am one very upset mother as I type this letter about my baby crib!  I have the "Renew Standard Crib(#RN343-9504B)" from JcPenny's I have huge complaint about this crib, today I woke up to my 1yr almost 2 screaming bloody murder because his leg got stuck in between the slates on the crib.  I tried everything in order to get his leg out and last resort was to rip the slat off which I was afraid of hurting him more if I didn't do this!  So, now here I sit with a unusable crib.  Just let me say this is not the first time this has happened.  I am so surprised this has not between recalled or maybe it is and I just unaware.  Please let me know.  I am so afraid that next time it will end in broken leg or who knows what else.  I just want you to take this very "Seriously"

incident_description: The Jasco LED Nightlight (GE Branded) was plugged into an outlet in the master bedroom of our 2nd home.  Twenty minutes later, I awoke to a loud popping noise and looked up to see a six inch flaming shooting out of the front of the nightlight.  I leapt out of bed and was able to blow it out before finding gloves to allow me to take it out of the wall, which was badly scorched around the outlet.
justification: The incident involved a flaming nightlight and scorched outlet, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: I have a Lenny Lamb mei tai baby carrier.  It was brought to my attention that there had been some structural failures of others mei tais made by them, so I checked mine as instructed by my local babywearing group leader.  The body panel of the carrier easily separated from the waist strap.  There was only a tiny amount of overlap for the seam.  Very poor construction!

The consumer stated that she had the tent on the crib and one night her 2 years old son pulled the tent down inside out. The consumer stated that her son was resting with the bars of the tent on top of him. The consumer stated that she placed the tent on the crib because her son had figured out how to jump off the crib.

The consumer stated that her son started screaming and he was once again resting on the crib with the bars on top of him. The consumer stated that her son was not insured. 

The consumer stated that she stopped using the tent. 

The consumer stated that she had not contacted the manufacturer, but she will be contacting them to file a complaint.
justification: The incident involved a child being trapped under the tent bars but no injury was reported, indicating a severity level of 2. The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) as the child's behavior suggests a recurring risk.

incident_description: My son is 10 Weeks n 6 days old today, he sleeps in his crib every night n when he takes his naps during the day. When he first wakes up in the morning, he looks around at his animals n kicks his legs. This morning his right foot n shin went between the bars n when he kicked with his left leg it pushed his body to the right, bending his right leg between the bars.
