incident_description:
Caller has an 11 month old daughter who was given a Jumper with a sunshine spring toy.

Baby has been crying at times when playing in jumper but parents had no idea why until they observed her pulling back on the sunshine toy attached to the jumper and saw it bounce back and hit her in the forehead then then above the eye by her temple.

The parents pulled back on the thick plastic sunshine toy and say that it is very tightly spring loaded and comes back with considerable force.

Callers believe this to be a safety issue due to the thought that if hit hard enough by this toy in the eye it could damage a baby's eyesight.

He and his wife found bruises on their baby's face where the sunshine toy hit her

Caller is reporting because this toy has caused harm to his child and could cause harm to other children.

He contacted the manufacturer 06/01/2012 and submitted report to them but he would like more action for the safety of other children.
justification: The baby sustained bruises from the toy hitting her face, indicating an injury, and the parents report it could potentially cause eye damage.

incident_description: My 6 month old son has gotten his forearm stuck between the red, white, and green birds. He was screaming in pain. This has happened two times.
justification: The child was screaming in pain, indicating an injury, and this has happened twice, suggesting it is likely to occur again.

incident_description: My nine month old pushed a panel out of an Oeuf crib side.  Robin model.
justification: The panel was pushed out but no injury was reported, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: My 5 month old son was sitting in his bumpo seat, I looked away for just a second and he somehow knocked it over.  He fell and hit his head causing a skull fracture.
justification: The incident resulted in a skull fracture, which is an injury, and such incidents are possible given the context of a young child in a Bumbo seat.

incident_description: I received as a gift a pair of Cozy Crib Tent II made by Tots In Mind for my twins.  My toddlers were able to invert the tents down into their cribs.  They were on the outside climbing over when this happened so were not trapped under their tents.  However, one tent pole shattered when the inversion occurred and the sharp shards poking through the fabric created a very dangerous situation.  I sustained minor injuries while removing the broken tent.  I emailed the company to let them know about the incident and subsequently declined their offer for replacement of the product.  I then disposed of both tents.
justification: The incident resulted in minor injuries to the parent while removing the broken tent, and the shattered pole created a dangerous situation.

incident_description:
The consumer says that the seam started to come out.  A string was hanging on his mattress.  She changed the sheets one day.  Later that morning her child was screaming.  She tried to pick him up but noticed that a string was wrapped around his neck.  

The consumer says the string is from the thread of the mattress.  She says her husband had to cut the string with a pair of scissors.  The baby was not injured but has a red mark on his neck.  The consumer tried to contact the manufacturer yesterday and left a message.
justification: The baby had a red mark on his neck from the string, indicating an injury, but no serious harm occurred.

incident_description:
Summer Infant 3-Stage Super Seat Model 13094

I just wanted to share a word of caution from what we experienced with our child. She was playing with the ladybug/mirror part and when you spin it around because it's not a globe it leaves a gap underneath it when it's vertical. Well she spun it and had her fingers on the holder. As she spun it down her fingers became wedged between the ladybug and the holder. She didn't appear to be in any pain but we had to very carefully rock the ladybug back and forth until we could slide her fingers out. We quickly realized that if you tried to rock it too quickly you could easily squish, maybe break her fingers. All was okay in the end but we will not let her play with that one toy anymore.
justification: The child's fingers were wedged but no injury occurred, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: I have a Graco Playard model # 9B08CAT manufactured in 2/2010 and in use since 1/2011 (~16 months).  When using the bassinet portion of the playard for my 4 month old son, he began crying like he was hurt.  A different cry than usual.  I went into the bedroom to check on him and pick him up and he was stuck.  I couldn't physically pick him up.  I then realized his head was stuck under the oval wall part of the bassinet and the 4 panel mattress has bunched up (the 4 panels overlapped each by about 1/2 inch - 1 inch) to create a space at the end of the mattress.  He was stuck face down into the nylon bottom of the bassinet with the mattress pinning his head against the wall and the oval wall part above his head pinning it down into the nylon floor beside (not on top of) the mattress.  I pulled the mattress further away from the wall and was able to maneuver his head out to free him.  I am an emergency physician and saw that he was unhurt but also see the potential for this to fatally injure an infant.  I wanted to report this so that if there other similar reports, a safety recall could be issued to prevent future injuries.  I believe the problem is that the fabric of the mattress has stretched a bit over the 16 months of usage and now allows the 4 boards inside the mattress to overlap a bit which creates space at the edges of the bassinet.  Because the bassinet has walls that shape the space into an oval, the oval wall can trap a baby's head.  My mattress also with 16 months of use has bowed a bit also shortening the panels.  I have only used my playard in line with Graco's recommendations.
justification: The infant was stuck but unharmed, indicating an incident without injury. The potential for fatal injury is noted, but not realized in this case.

incident_description: My 7 month old son has received a rash from wearing the ALVA Baby diapers. These diapers are produced in China and brought into the US threw CO-Ops. As soon as I saw the rash I began treating it with an all natural cloth diaper cream. And also because of a previous incident with another child in a group I participate in I took him out of the Alva Baby Diaper he was using and used other cloth diapers. THe rash cleared up within two days. I waited a week and put him back in the ALVA baby Diapers and the rash reappeared within a week.
justification: The description indicates a recurring rash (injury) linked to the use of ALVA Baby diapers, suggesting a likely reoccurrence when the product is used again.

incident_description: We had just bought his high chair, brand new in box, online, and used it 1 time. The 2nd time I went to put my baby in the chair, and the straps were way too short for my child, who was only about 14 months at the time, so I decided to put the tray on in the meantime, so I could go around to the back to see about adjusting the straps. To my HORROR, my son barely pushed on the tray and it popped off, and he tumbles to the floor. He cried, and was shaken up.  I immediatly contacted the online retailer, and I have proof of the date of the message sent, so this is not to "jump on the wagon" with all the other re-calls..I was one of the 1st ones to report this.  It was really a trying time, having to sit right next to my baby, taking the high chair down from the higher height, down to the lower level, close to the floor, and I had to sit right next to him, so if the tray did pop off, I was right there. My son still is learning to walk, so I figured that once he can walk himself, then I wouldnt need the tray anyways. I am very happy that its been re-called, and that my claims are valid!
justification: The child fell from the high chair and was shaken up, indicating an injury, and the incident was reported among the first, suggesting it's possible but not extremely rare.

incident_description: I read online about a friend's Lenny Lamb Mei tai ripping when she was using it so I inspected mine and pulled on the straps. The straps ripped out of the carrier. No injuries were sustained as the baby was not in it at the time.
justification: The carrier straps ripped, but no injuries occurred as the baby was not in it at the time.

incident_description: I purchased a Lenny Lamb Mei Tai in April.  I had only used it a handful of times when someone posted in a Facebook group that they had the same one and it ripped at the seat while their child was in it!  Luckily the child wasn't hurt, but it scared me enough to go give mine a tug.  With barely any effort, the seat ripped away from the waist portion of the carrier.  It was easy to see that it was an obvious design flaw, because the seat only extended into the padded waist by approximately 1/4 inch.  Several other mothers discovered the same thing when they tested their own.
justification: The incident involved a carrier ripping but no injury occurred, and the issue was identified by multiple users indicating a design flaw.

incident_description: This baby Asian Mei Tai carrier ripped at the seams. They only had an 1/8 of an inch seam allowance and barley sewed it. Sadly a wider seam allowance and better sewing would have fixed this issue. Babies can fall out of the carrier and hit the floor. This is designed to wear front OR back.
justification: The carrier's failure could lead to a baby falling, which poses a risk of injury, but the description does not confirm any actual injury occurred.

incident_description:
The consumer says the night light apparently shorted.  It is blackened on the inside and it blew the circuit breaker.  The consumer says it was discovered by the odor of the hot plastic.

The consumer says he doesn't recall how long the light was on for but it was not very long.  It had been in the same location for quite a while.

incident_description: I purchased an Evenflo convertible highchair a couple months ago for my 2 1/2 year old daughter from Wal-mart.  One day she was trying to climb into the highchair by herself.  She put her foot on the table part and pulled herself up on to the table completely.  Once she had both feet on the table she was using the tray to hoist herself into her seat and even though the tray was in correctly it completely came out of place and my daughter tumbled off and broke her right clavicle.
justification: The child suffered a broken clavicle, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The incident occurred due to a product failure, suggesting a possible likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description:
The consumer wanted to express his concerns about his crib tent as his 2 year old child was trapped in the tent. The consumer stated that he placed his child in the tent and attempted to remove the child from the tent, but had an extremely hard time removing the zipper to remove the child from the tent. This difficulty went on for 30-45 minutes and recorded the incident on video. The consumer had to go as far as cutting the netting of the tent to remove his child.

 The consumer stated that his child was not harmed or injured. The consumer placed  call to the firm in late April. The consumer stated that the mailbox was full and could not leave a message. The consumer called the company a few days later and was able to leave a message. He called the firm at [REDACTED] and never received a call back. 

The consumer also sent an email to the firm on May 1, 2012 and an email on May 8, 2012, with also no response. The consumer came to realize that the company was out of business after learning that the product was cited in release 12-179. The consumer cannot recall the retailer but does know it was from an online retailer.
justification: The child was trapped but not harmed, and the incident was resolved without injury. The occurrence likelihood is possible given the described scenario.

incident_description: I had my son in a Fisher Price jumperoo model number M8930 Manufacture date 1052Q2. It has three puzzle pieces shaped like vegetables that are attached by a green piece of material. At the end of the green material there is a fold that is sewn in that is attached to a slot on the main saucer. I turned around and looked at my son and he had pulled the whole carrot piece off with the attached piece of material and was trying to put it in his mouth. It is enough material that if he began to swallow it, it could cause an airway obstruction. I can provide pictures of the item if needed. I believe this is a serious potential choking hazard and this item needs to be attached more securely.
justification: The child could choke on the detached piece, posing a serious injury risk, and the likelihood is high given the described scenario.

incident_description: In December 2011 I bought my daughter the Bright Starts, Bounce Bounce Baby Activity Zone. The first incidents were between five to eight months old I noticed cuts in the folds of her legs - I assumed she had scratched herself during a diaper change and I had just failed to notice when diapering her. However recently after direct removal from her Bright Starts, Bounce Bounce Baby Activity Zone at 10 months old after being in it less than 20 minutes my daughter suffered multiple cuts (some deep) to her vagina & inner legs from the seats leg holes. My daughter rarely used this item but the few times she did resulted in cuts from the fabric. My daughter has used other brand products with a similar seat and holes and had no problems. Bright Starts, Bounce Bounce Baby Activity Zone needs to recall this item and redo their design so this does not happen to other infants.
justification: The incident resulted in multiple cuts, some deep, indicating an injury.

incident_description: We had just switched my son to a size 3 diaper. He has been in Pamper Diapers (swaddlers) since birth after two days of use my son had a horrible rash that looked like a burn on his lower back and bottom. It just continued to get worse regardless of our efforts. It caused me sons bottom and lower back to get extremely red and blistered and started to bleed with in a matter of hours from when the rash started.Once we realized it was a chemical burn we immediatle switched him to a different brand an the burn hasn't healed but it has stopped getting worse.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe chemical burn with blistering and bleeding, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
I am having a really big issue with the crib that my 1 year old son sleeps in. When he is playing in it after or before sleeping his legs get stuck in the rails! It is not like they get stuck once or twice here or there, but many many times a day. They are getting stuck in the sides so bad that his legs turn blue. In order for me to get his legs out I have to put a lot of lotion on his legs and the rails and slowly work them out. I am so scared that he might end up breaking his leg! I have e-mailed the crib company about my concerns and the reply I got was the following; "We recognize and appreciate your concerns regarding your sonÃÂs leg getting stuck between the railing on the crib sides. As children grow and start to become active they begin to explore their environment which includes their crib.
Please be assured that all Stork Craft cribs, including your Sheffield Stages Crib, meets or exceeds safety standards for both Canadian and  United States.  Government and Industry standards regulate the design and construction of cribs in Canada and the U.S., these regulatory requirements stipulate, among other things, the dimensions and spacing.  The spacing between the spindles in the rails or panels must not be more than 6 cm or 2 3/8 inches.  The intent behind the specifications regulated by the standards is to protect infants from life threatening or debilitating injuries such as head entrapment."
I understand that they have to make it to where young ones don't get hurt. But my son is getting hurt! He has bruises on his legs from them getting stuck. I have gone to look at other cribs but I can not afford a new one. What am I suppose to do?
justification: The child is experiencing repeated injuries (bruises and legs turning blue) due to getting stuck in the crib rails, indicating a clear injury risk.

incident_description:
My 5 month old daughter was swinging in a fisher price open top rainforest cradle swing when the seat of the swing broke off without warning and fell sideways onto the floor.  Since my baby was securely fastened into the seat she did not fall out but her head did bump against the hard tile floor.  She did not require emergency care but her head was red and very sore where it hit the floor.  After examining the swing I found that the plastic at the base of the seat looked like it just snapped off.  When the seat fell sideways it actually bent at least one of the screws that had been screwed into the base as well.  At only 5 months of age my child was no where near the maximum weight recommendation for the swing so it should not have broke if it had been designed safely.  
I was very fortunate that my daughter did not sustain more severe injuries.  If the plastic on this swing can "snap" that easily this is a VERY unsafe product!  I know this is a very popular swing model and I was surprised that I could not find any recall information on it as I am sure my child is not the only one this has happened to.
justification: The baby sustained a head injury from the swing breaking, but did not require emergency care, indicating a severity level of 3. The incident suggests a possible design flaw, making recurrence likely for other users.

incident_description:
The consumer wanted to express his concerns about the moonlight he purchased as the product began to "snap electrically". The consumer purchased the product in package of two. The consumer placed the product near the keyboard of his computer. The product is operated by 4 AA batteries. The consumer stated that after using the product for nearly 3 weeks, the consumer noticed that the model was working strangely.
The consumer could hear a loud "arching" noise from where his computer was. The consumer figured that it may be his computer and after further inspection he realized the moonlight was making a loud sizzle noise. The consumer figured that the product had batteries burned out. The consumer picked up the product to dispose of the batteries and realized that his right hand was "burning" on the back of his index finger. The consumer then noticed that this sensation was battery acid leaking.
The consumer washed his hands with water and baking soda paste. The consumer checked and was absolutely sure the batteries were inserted properly. The consumer has not sought any medical attention. The consumer did not have any problems with the product before the incident. The consumer is a former fire fighter and is not sure what in the product could possibly cause the battery to react in that manner.

 

The consumer has not called the retailer or the firm. The light has not caused any damage to the consumer's home no evidence of burning inside of the product. The consumer's wife heard the same noise a few days prior to the incident.
justification: The consumer suffered a burn from battery acid leakage, which constitutes an injury, but the incident appears isolated with no prior issues reported.

incident_description: My daughter is almost 5 months old, i was feeding her on Monday and sitting at the table next to her, she got mad and started throwing a fit.  She pushed her head back and the locking device that holds the chair down, came unlocked and she flipped backwards, thank god i was next to her or she would of hit the floor.
justification: The child did not hit the floor due to immediate intervention, so no injury occurred, but the incident involved a near-miss with potential for harm.

incident_description: After being alerted to another consumer's Lenny Lamb Mei Tai baby carrier ripping at a load bearing seam while wearing her daughter, I decided to test my own.  I was not wearing my baby at the time.  I simply grabbed on to the padded waist strap and the body panel with both hands and applied gentle force.  Within 5 seconds the body had completely separated from the waist strap.  It was clear upon inspection that the seam allowance was 1/2 of an inch at best and lacking in any kind of proper reinforcement.  This is a huge design flaw and major safety concern for a baby carrier!  Usually the body panel should be sewn deep inside any of the straps and then reinforced with proper materials and/or stitching techniques to prevent the carrier from falling apart.  I took a photo and contacted Lenny Lamb, who emailed me back promptly stating that they believed it was a batch of "bad thread" and offered to send me a replacement.  I have deep concerns that they do not understand how to properly construct a safe, secure baby carrier if they believe this was simply due to faulty thread.  Even the strongest of threads would not keep this carrier from falling apart.  The woven fabric used to construct the carrier has an open weave and will fray with time.  The shallow seam allowance at the joins is NOT ACCEPTABLE!
justification: The incident describes a significant design flaw in a baby carrier that could lead to injury, but no actual injury occurred in this case.

incident_description:
I found my  2 yr old son almost strangled today in his bed. He had a string from the mattress wrapped extremely tight around his neck, he couldn't move. He just screamed and cried. Luckily I came to get him right away, but the horrible thing is I don't always come get him right away hoping he will put himself back to sleep. He would have lost air and died and I would have thought it was just him going back to sleep.
 Anyways, the top of the mattress is filled with pockets of string that can easily be accessed.  It's an organic mattress so that was their idea for keeping airflow. They need to redo the product and made the pockets full of PIECES of string, not yards long of string. I have two mattresses (twins) that are less than two years old. The kids never have sharp objects in bed, it's merely just their hands taking this apart. The pockets are only covered with and fine layer of cheese cloth like material, very very thin!
 Both beds are falling apart. When I reported this to the company today they told me they would send me a replacement cover. They are not considering the fact that this can happen to other babies!,! Sickening
 This needs to be stopped ASAP! I can't believe tons of babies are exposed to this string and parents don't realize it's in their beds... Unsupervised!!
justification: The child was almost strangled by a string from the mattress, which could have led to death if not discovered in time.

incident_description: Kolcraft Tender Vibes:  One of the metal arms that lock into place to hold bassinet had come undone.  Noticed it when taking down bassinet to store away.
justification: The metal arm coming undone is an incident, but there was no injury reported.

incident_description:
RE:  Giant Progeny BS-2 Child Carrier (for bike)

This product does not hold my child in place.  It is a 3 point harness and the base of the harness is inches from the trunk/groin area, causing my child to slide forward and down while riding, the shoulder straps to dig into his neck, and his helmet to catch on the back of the seat as he slides down.  Now that he is a little bigger/older I have observed that he still slides forward, the shoulder straps (still) cannot be made snug enough for him to not be able to wiggle his way out of them -I guess because the base of the harness is inches out from his groin.

I purchased the carrier on June 9, 2011.  I called the manufacturer, Giant, on September 27, 2011 (my child was 13 months at that time) to explain my concerns about the safety of this product and was told they would not replace or refund the item, and if I wanted to try to take it back to the store where I purchased it I could try that.  The store I purchased it at said they would not take it back and the owner said he had the same carrier for his son and had the same issues I do and that "I should just put pillows all around my child to try and keep him in place"... 

Because it is unsafe, we generally do not ride.  Because I was 'stuck with it', we try to ride periodically -hopeful he may grow into it.  This did not result in any more secure fitting or safety, just an older baby who is better at getting out of the ill-fitting shoulder straps WHILE WE RIDE, or simply communicating his discomfort of sliding forward/ having straps dig into his neck, and saying, "Home Mommy".
justification: The child carrier is described as unsafe, causing discomfort and potential for the child to wiggle out, but no actual injury is reported.

incident_description: We have been using Pampers Swaddlers newborn diapers for the first 3 weeks with our newborn son.  Soon, approximately 2-3 days into using the diapers, he developed a rash which we thought was just a result from being damp and not enough changings, but after a couple more days it appeared to be more than just a "diaper rash".  The said "rash" consisted of peeling skin, boils, raw spots, and appeared to look more like a chemical burn. So we began to use [REDACTED] Baby Powder, daily baths, time without a diaper, and [REDACTED] the rash was only getting worse.  I noticed at times there were crystals on his skin and raw tiny boils were left on his skin near the crystals.  Almost 75% of his diaper area was covered with raw rash and in an attempt to try anything to help him we switched to [REDACTED].  It has been one day since we switched him and his rash is almost gone.  We are now stuck with about 120 Pampers Swaddlers that I will not put back on my son.
justification: The newborn developed severe skin reactions including peeling skin, boils, and raw spots, indicating an injury caused by the diapers.

He had some bumps and bruises, but nothing super serious (although I think we were just lucky) since then I have been using them on the floor without the table. The trays still come off occasionally but since they are only about 8-10 inches off the floor it isn't a long way to fall.

incident_description:
My son was given a Sugarbooger by ORE Buzzy Bee wooden teething toy.  It can be found here:  https://www.oreoriginals.com/estore/loadProduct.do?productId=1449

Unfortunately, what you can't see in the picture, is a wooden ring, about 1 1/8 inches in diameter that acts as a handle.  It is slightly larger than a quarter, but smaller than a toilet paper tube.  It is a ring, not a solid circle.  My son is six months old and has no teeth.  He liked to chew on this toy by putting the entire ring in his mouth.  The ring is attached by what appears to be a cotton or other natural fiber rope.  Today I found the wooden ring completely detached from the toy.  I don't think he chewed on it, the toy is configured such that I think it would be very hard from him to get his gums on the rope.  I think that simply from him continually drooling on it and banging it around the rope simply degraded and tore.  My son is six months old and received this as a gift just before he was born, less than a year ago.

While I know that a ring is much less likely to cause a choking hazard than something that is solid, the size of this ring is significantly smaller that what we have been told is adequate to prevent choking (we were told if something can fit through a toilet paper tube, it is too small).
justification: The wooden ring detached but no injury occurred, indicating an incident without harm. The likelihood is possible given the described degradation from drooling and use.

incident_description:
Summer's Infant Sure and Secure 6 foot Metal Expansion Gate

My 12 mos old daughter reached her arm through one of the skinnier areas in the bars on the section that has the door that swings open.  She was able to squeeze her arm through, but when she got past her elbow and bent her arm, she was unable to pull it out.  (When you bend your arm, you'll notice that near the elbow the width of your arm increases.)  When she realized she couldn't pull it out, she pulled harder with her arm still bent and then got her arm wedged tight in between the bars.  She started to scream, which got my attention.  Seeing she was stuck and not immediately recognizing what had happened, I tried to pull her arm out as well, hurting her even more.  After a few minutes of tugging with her in pain and crying, I finally realized that straightening her arm would help.  I was then able to free her from the gate.  She cried for a long time after and her arm is quite red where it was stuck.  I imagine it will bruise but do not know because this incident just occurred.  The other bars on the gate are a reasonable space apart, but these narrow areas are clearly a danger to children, which is ironic considering this is a safety product.  I shudder to think what would have happened if I were in the shower or restroom at the time and could not hear her cries.
justification: The child sustained visible injury (redness and potential bruising) from being stuck in the gate, but there was no death or severe harm. The likelihood is possible (3) as the incident occurred once but could happen again under similar conditions.

incident_description: I have installed this baby gate at the bottom of my stairs as well as one in the hallway at the top. http://www.amazon.com/Summer-Infant-Secure-Extra-Walk-Thru/dp/B0000DEW91  The one at the top, I used the provided wall cups to make it more secure--not just pressure mounted.  Yesterday, I left my 9 month old upstairs with her sister and ran down to get some laundry.  I heard a kind of whining sound, so I went back up to see if soemthing was wrong.  The baby had crawled out of the gate and had one hand on the stair to go down!  These gates are supposed to "close and lock automatically".  I am assuming this one had not closed and locked as it would have been nearly impossible for a crawling baby to open it--I can't even open it sometimes.  Her sister was in the bathroom and claims not to have touched the gate, so I do not think it was her either.  I had noticed the gate at the bottom of the stairs will not close unless it is done manually, but I figured it was because we had to add a piece of wood next to the banister to hold it in place properly.  The one at the top was not similiarly rigged and was installed per directions and had worked, as far as I know, up until this point.  I am so blessed that my baby caught herself and was able to vocalize her fear, but this is a very dangerous product and would like others to be aware of the problem.
justification: The baby nearly fell down the stairs due to a malfunctioning gate, but no injury occurred.

Sincerely

incident_description: I received a Phil and Ted Me Too portable high chair as a hand me down from a friend.  We loved the chair, used it on a daily basis, and had no problems with it.  When it was recalled, I discontinued use until we received the retrofit kit, which I installed according to the directions.  After the installation, the new black caps that covered the two clamps would slip off and the chair would move backwards away from the counter.  This problem was worse when my friend's son used the chair and kicked the cabinets.  I slid the clamps back on on a daily basis and continued to use the chair.  One day my husband put our son in the chair without knowing about the problem.  One of the clamps slid out of the cap.  The other clamp remained attached to the counter.  The chair turned sideways.  Fortunately, my son was able to hang on and swung back and forth clinging on.  We no longer use the chair as we don't consider it safe.
justification: The incident involved the chair malfunctioning but no injury occurred, as the child was able to hang on safely.

The consumer stated that she placed her daughter down for a nap and approximately 5 minutes after she placed her in the crib she heard her cried. The consumer stated that when she walked to the crib she noticed that both of her daughterÃÂs legs were stuck between the slats. I am very dissatisfied with this product. I will never buy baby trend again!  My son suffered injuries from baby trend for being liable for this product they put on the shelves of the retail store I purchased this from.

incident_description:
9-month old baby falls out of Evenflo Exersaucer Mega, manufactured on Feb. 1, 2007. Baby was on tippy toes and leaned herself over and fell out. Baby hit head on the floor, luckily diagnosed at the ER with minor acute closed head injury. Baby is 28" tall.

This product unit does not have any indication printed on it as to when baby must discontinue use of product based on baby's height. The only information printed is to discontinue when baby is walking.

Product manual says to discontinue when baby is over 30" tall or can stand flat-footed in the unit.

I want to alert the manufacturer to change their guidelines for when baby must discontinue using product based on height. This product is already dangerous to a baby 28" tall!

Also, manufacturer MUST PRINT ON THE PRODUCT ITSELF VERY CLEARLY WHEN TO DISCONTINUE PRODUCT BASED ON HEIGHT. (revised guidelines to 28" tall.)
justification: Baby suffered a minor acute closed head injury from falling out of the product, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) due to the product's design flaw and lack of clear height guidelines.

incident_description:
One Step Ahead sells the PeaPod Plus Baby Travel Bed. It is marketed for babies to sleep in. It has a "cushy, inflatable mattress" and, per at least one customer comment, unbreathable sides.

incident_description:
Jardine Baby - Berkley Single Crib BC-110C 
My 3 year old son was able to kick two spindles right out of the drop gate and break them.  My opinion is that an inferior material was chosen for the spindle bars.  A post-event analysis indicates that the spindles are made of a low density particle board.  The particle board spindles appear to have been attached to the drop gate frame with small wooden dowels, which were seated in (presumably) pre-drilled holes on both the frame and the spindle.  

The dowel/frame transition creates a sudden step-wise reduction in the cross-sectional area of the spindle.  This reduction in area creates an opportunity for a stress concentration. Given that particle board is about 8 times weaker in shear than in tension, these factors combined create a higher likelihood of failure of the spindle member, even under modest adverse loading conditions.

The following design alternatives are suggested:
1) Change the spindle material to a fibrous, higher strength wood product, such as birch or pine.
2) Taper the ends of spindles, so that each end terminates in a round cross-section that transitions to a square cross-section at some point along the axis of the spindle.  This will serve to ease the  transition between cross-sections, reducing the severity of the associated stress concentration.
justification: The incident involved a crib failure but no injury was reported, indicating a severity level of 2. The analysis suggests a design flaw that could lead to frequent failures under modest loading, making occurrence likely.

incident_description: This is a beautiful, sturdy bed, but from day one I had a problem with the little bar at the end of the changing table, our little one (we foster and got her at 11 months) kept getting her little foot under the bar (why in the world would you allow such a large gap at the end of a table where a child's feet is), I placed a rolled up blanket there for awhile, but she kept pulling it out ~ well, it finally happened, I didn't realize her LEG had gotten under the bar when I lifted her out, it immediately was bruised and required a trip to Urgent Care - fortunately everything is ok, but we have removed that bar, the gap between the bar and the changing pad was large enough for my husband to stick his arm in.  I can send pictures if you would like.  This bed should be recalled due to the large space on the changing table.  After this happened, I read other reviews from people stating the same thing, that their child's', leg, foot and/or ankle had gotten caught under that bar.
justification: The incident resulted in a bruised leg requiring urgent care, indicating an injury (severity 3). Multiple reviews report similar incidents, suggesting the issue is likely (occurrence 4).

incident_description: I put my 4 month old daughter in the swing to play, she fell asleep in the swing.  I figured it was safe to leave her there like I have done many times before and was in the kitchen grabbing something and heard a thud noise followed by my daughter screaming.  Ran into the living room where she was to find her head tilted over to the side and a red mark where the leg of the swing hit her.  It is the first time this has ever happened and now planning on throwing the swing away.  Please look into this so other children don't hurt themselves.
justification: The child sustained a visible injury (red mark) from the swing, indicating a severity level of 3.

incident_description: My daughter was playing with the Bright Starts Starry Teether yesterday and it came apart and two of the pieces were stuck in her mouth/throat.  Luckily I noticed it right away and was able to get the pieces out by putting my finger in her mouth/throat and pulling out the pieces.
justification: The teether came apart and pieces were stuck in the child's mouth/throat, posing a choking hazard, but no injury occurred as the parent intervened quickly.

incident_description:
Our almost 5 1/2 month old was in the Bright Starts Comfort and Harmony Bouncer, which was placed on the bathroom floor near the shower, while I was in the shower. While I was in the shower I peeked out at him, as I always do, and found him still belted into the seat but flipped forward, twisted a bit, and hanging off the side of the bouncer. This happened a day or two earlier as well, same situation. We will not be putting him back in the bouncer. 

Our son is not sitting up unassisted, nor is he 25 lbs as the seat warnings state. I feel this is a flaw with the safety belt design (belt sits too low to keep an older, bigger baby secure) or overall design of the seat (inclines too far forward to be safe for an older, wiggly baby, therefore being propelled forward by their movements).
justification: The baby was not injured but was found in a potentially dangerous position, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: I had brought a child craft baby bed not knowing it was a drop down side. I went to put the side back up and it just fell down, it won't stay up. I looked online and saw a recall for it. I would love this bed fixed or have a new replacement. I am a first time mom and I do not want my baby or anyone else's baby hurt because of this particular bed. Please help me either fix this product or junk it and give me a better bed for my child!
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning baby bed with a recalled drop-down side, but no injury occurred.

incident_description:
My son wore a Pampers Easy Ups size 3t-4t one time for 1 hours and 30 minutes. He began screaming and pointing to his diaper area that it hurt. He was hysterical. When we took off the pull up his diaper area was hot and red - it looked like a burn. Previous to putting on the Easy Up he had no rash and he did not have a bowel movement while wearing it. He has not had a change in diet or any other reason that would cause a "rash" like this. He wore it for less than 2 hours which I do not feel is a long time to be wet - I am also assuming he was not wet the minute he put it on. This appeared to be a chemical burn. 

He screamed throughout the night whenever he urinated. He was in so much pain that he was shaking. I called our pediatrician and we are treating him at home for now. It has been 3 days and the burn is improving slightly. When I spoke with the nurse at the pediatrician she stated that I should find out what is in their diapers that would cause this. 

When I called Pampers to report this incident I asked what chemicals are in their products so that I could figure out what had caused this reaction on my son. There response was that their diapers are chemical free. Huh? It is blue and scented and I know that cotton or cellulose, whatever substrate they use, does not grow in nature this way. I think they should provide a MSDS for the product on request. Also, they should be honest about the processing. While there may not be any chemicals sprayed on the diaper at the last step, there ARE chemicals used in processing. Symantics.

I understand that kids get diaper rash. My son is 3 and I also have a 7 year old daughter. I have been a parent using diapers for many years - using Pampers products for most of those years. I know what a normal diaper rash looks like. This was not normal.
justification: The child suffered a painful chemical burn requiring medical attention, indicating an injury (severity 3). Such severe reactions are uncommon but not unheard of (likelihood 2).

incident_description: My child developed a severe leg rash from Pamper's Cruisers Diapers.  He developed the rash within the day of switching him to the Cruisers from Baby Dry.  The rash is severe and not going away with typical diaper cream.  These diapers should not be allowed on the market with the incidents and the severity of my child's rash and others I have since heard about.
justification: The child developed a severe rash, indicating an injury, but there is no mention of death or life-threatening conditions.

incident_description: I received a replacement crib from Jardine JA2614RC for my lifetime crib 0303G00 and upon taking it out of the box, found a huge crack at the top on one of the sides that is coming from a screw. I didn't even start to put the crib together, I'm sure the wood would break off or splinter even more if I tried to put it together and this makes it very unsafe. I want a safe crib for my child and not from this company.
justification: The crib has a significant defect that makes it unsafe, but no injury or death has occurred yet.

incident_description: i purchased a 3 in 1 delta i believe  crib  from KMART  about 2 months ago my 1 year old son  has for the second time gotten his knee cap stuck and lodged in between  the spaces of not only the crib wall but the head area too  His knee was stuck to a point were i couldnt brake the wood  without injuring him  this has happened twice now  please respond immediately  i would appreciate it  i have a picture of the redness and when it bruises this time i will take another  thank you   ..sincerely  [REDACTED]
justification: The child's knee was stuck to the point of causing redness and potential bruising, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
The consumer noticed that after removing  the crib from the plastic packaging (crib came unassembled) there was a strong chemical odor  coming from the crib.

The obnoxious odor caused her and her family severe headaches, dizziness and nauseous. The consumer placed the crib in the childÃÂs room with a fan to attempt to air it out.

Within three hours the odor spread throughout the entire home so the windows in the home  were opened. The smell did not dissipate so the crib was later placed in the garage. 

The consumer indicated that when she went into the garage a few hours later the odor was not as strong .

The firm was contacted on 3/5/2012 and the consumer was advised that the finish is non toxic and lead free and there was nothing to worry about. 

The consumer indicated that she has decided to not use the crib and will leave the crib in the garage for a while. She has not contacted the retailer and she also indicated that she might return the crib.
justification: The incident caused severe headaches, dizziness, and nausea, which are clear signs of injury due to chemical exposure.

incident_description:
The consumer noticed while removing the diapers out of their original packaging she saw a metal shard and continued on throughout the day.  While applying one of the diapers the consumer noticed one metal shard on the back waist band of the diaper.  

The size of the metal shard is less an inch in width and size, similar to the middle section of a staple. She noticed one other piece of metal within the other diapers.

She contacted the firm the week of 2/13/2012 and was advised that they would mail out a package for the diaper to be sent back and evaluated. 

The consumer did not use the diaper that had the metal shard and there were no injuries reported.
justification: The consumer noticed metal shards in diapers but did not use the affected diaper and no injuries were reported.

incident_description: I was searching for baby cribs online and was stunned by a product I came across..a plastic inflatable baby crib with inflatable plastic walls no less. Who in their rite mind would place an infant in this? Mom is standing in the kitchen around the corner while little Timmy is asleep in his crib, along comes Tabby the cat... I think I will stretch and sink my claws into this velour covered plastic pad..no sound just the plastic walls collapsing on little Timmy in a few minutes..and this is just one scenario I can think of hundreds. You might want to review this product before you are swamped with infant obituaries.  Product Information: www.GrowingRoomInc.com   Growing Room, Inc. P.O. Box 9690 Tavernier,Fl. 33070
justification: The description highlights a potential hazard with the inflatable baby crib, suggesting a risk of injury or death to infants, which warrants a high severity level.

incident_description:
I've been using a Graco silhouette pack n play in their Crawford print for about a year now. Once my baby was big enough to put him in the bottom portion of the playpen I started having problems. The mattress does not lay properly in the bottom of the playpen and that causes the quilted mattress cover to bunch in the middle. (It seems like that's an area where the mattress folds for storage.) The bulge in the middle of the mattress is pretty big and could become a suffocation hazard. 

I have contacted Graco in November 2011 and they sent me a temporary mattress (mine was on back order) and the temporary mattress did the same thing. I also just received the final replacement last week and it bunches as well.
justification: The mattress bunching poses a potential suffocation hazard, but no actual injury or death has been reported.

incident_description:
I a  bought a Baby Relax - Deluxe Glider Rocker and Ottoman, Walnut from Walmart. Walmart number
260094110

Several times the hardware under the base of the main chair falls off all on it's own. The gliding motion causes the bolt and washer to slide loose and come off the chair. This has happened several times without me knowing it. I have found the small parts on the floor in my baby's room. Due to this chair being in a baby/child's room this posses a choking hazard/ risk.  Since purchasing this rocker I have read other reviews of other customers having the same problem, making this not an isolated event. Instead it must be a design problem. Thus I feel this warrants a recall of this product so the manufacturer  can correct the problem.
justification: The incident describes a hardware failure posing a choking hazard in a baby's room, with no reported injury but potential for harm.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that his night light is potential fire hazard. The product goes into a standard outlet and the consumer suspects that the bulb of the product is not replaceable and the product is discarded after it begins to malfunction. The consumer stated that the tip of the bulb apparently burst in the middle of the night and inner contents flew up to the ceiling and dried overnight. 

The consumer estimates that the product was on for roughly  hours and is unsure at what point the bulb erupted as the consumer was asleep. The product has one small toggle switch to power the bulb on and off and there is no range of temperature for the bulb. The stain on his ceiling is roughly six inches across. The bulb appears to be okay but the tip of the bulb seemingly erupted. The bulb still seems to work.

 The lamp was in a bathroom and no one was injured. The consumer stated that the product is in the shape of a snowman hanging on to a candle. The design is similar to that of a lava lamp and when the lamp gets hot the inner fluid contents will bubble. The UL number is E212526. The consumer has yet to call the manufacturer or the retailer since he received the product as a gift. 

The consumer has not called the fire department or his home insurance after the incident. The consumer has seen many similar products online with many designs that would appeal to children. The consumer has been using the product with regularity, not necessarily every single night, however.
justification: The incident involved a bulb eruption causing a stain but no injuries, and similar products are commonly available, indicating a possible likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: The swing was great until my child became more active, he moves his little legs like most 3 month olds do. Well I didnt notice it at first, my sitter did, but the cloth on the swing where you buckle him in is rubbing against his leg and rubbing it raw. He is by no means hefty, or have chunky legs. he is actually kind of small for his age.I put him in it again thinking maybe the strap was just placed wrong or somthing, and even though i made sure it wasnt touching his legs at first it still ended up rubbing it raw! 'Ive never had this kind of problem with any other swing itve used and i have 4 children so i have used a few brands!
justification: The child's leg was rubbed raw by the swing's strap, indicating an injury, and the issue recurred despite adjustments, suggesting it's likely to happen again.

incident_description:
In mid December 2011, I gave my grandson the "My Busy World" cube by ALEX Toys for his first birthday.  On 1/31/12, he was playing with this toy, rotating the rectangular blocks on one side of this cube. This particular side of the the cube is designed to encourage children to match the pictures of animal parts on the the sides of the blocks to form a complete picture of the animal.  As he was pushing one of the blocks to rotate it, his hand slipped down into the space between the block and the frame of the cube. His hand went down into the space up to his wrist, and he was unable to pull it out as it became trapped in the space.  His mother immediately tried to ease it out, but was unable to do so.  She then coated his hand and the block first with soap and then with vaseline, and was finally able to slide his hand out.  By this time, my grandson was crying and was extremely upset. His hand was very red.  My grandson was 13 months old at the time and was of average size for a toddler his age.  There is nothing unusual about his build that would contribute to his hand being caught in the space.
  I returned the "My Busy World" cube to Buy Buy Baby, the store where it was purchased and received a refund.  On 2/2/12, I  contacted ALEX Toys by email and reported the incident in detail and expressed my concern that this toy was dangerous. I suggested that it be recalled. I was promptly contacted by [REDACTED] Accounts & Customer Relations for ALEX Toys.  
She stated that she had forwarded my report to their Safe and Compliance team for review. She also assured me that their products endure rigorous testing and meet all applicable regulatory standards around the world.  She advised me to visit their web site and select another item free of charge. 
  On 2/3/12, I received an email from [REDACTED] Safety & Compliance  at ALEX Toys.  She informed me that they had reviewed the design of the cube and safety testing reports from their third party testing laboratories, and the cube passed all safety testing.  However, they would review for possible modification of the side of the cube in question. She also advised that I should select another small toy from their web site.
  I never accepted the offer of another toy since this was not my goal in contacting ALEX Toys. My only concern is the safety of children
  On 2/8/12, [REDACTED] reported that the product was being re-examined at a third party laboratory for evaluation.
   On 3/7/12, I again contacted [REDACTED] since I had not heard any update in a month's time.  She replied that the laboratory did not make any adjustment recommendations during their evaluation, and she "confirmed" that the product was safe.
   I find this to be totally unacceptable, and cannot understand how they can CONFIRM that the product is safe if a small child's hand can become trapped in it.  I think that it should be recalled and removed from shelves.
justification: The child's hand was trapped and became red, indicating physical injury, but no long-term harm or death occurred.

incident_description: My son, [REDACTED] head was damaged from the Fisher Price Newborn Rock'n Play Sleeper. I bought this product from Target when I pregnant rather than getting a bassinet. [REDACTED] slept in this sleeper every night starting the day I brought him home from the hospital on August 10, 2011 until he was diagnosed with Occipital Plagiocephaly on January 10th 2012. The plastic surgeon prescribed my baby a $3,000 Orthotics helmet to reshape his head. He has to wear the helmet for 23 hours per day for 4-6 months. When I returned home from the doctor appointment on Jan. 10th I inspected the Fisher Price Sleeper more closely. I discovered it had a hard shell as well as no room for head movement to avoid flat spots. I was greatly saddened that I had not realized this earlier. I then became outraged when I started to search the internet to see if there were similar cases out there. I discovered multiple posts of babies with the same medical issues of Occipital Plagiocephaly as well as Torticollis from using the Fisher Price Newborn Rock'n Play Sleeper on the 1star reviews posted on Amazon.com. I then brought the sleeper to [REDACTED] 6 month well baby check up for his doctors opinion. [REDACTED] pediatrician agreed the product was not safe. As well as being hard and no room for head movement the design/angle of the sleeper is a sling, adding extra pressure on the head due to the weight of the baby pushing down on the hard support area. I regret buying and ever putting my son in this sleeper.
justification: The incident resulted in a medical condition (Occipital Plagiocephaly) requiring treatment, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description: i bought a Meridian incandescent night light at Wal Mart. This morning when i went in to her room, the plastic cover had melted all over the bulb and was black and charred. Thank God it didn't start a fire! this seems very dangerous, and i will be returning the other one that is still in the package!!
justification: The night light melted and charred but did not cause injury or fire, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description:
Victem purchased an E Circuit Electronics nightlight at the "Dollar Store" at [REDACTED] on March 6th, 2012.  At home she plugged the light into an outlet in her bedroom.

A short time later she smelled something burning, went into the bedroom and the night light was on fire.  She threw a wet rag on the light which extinuished the fire and she pulled the light out of the outlet.

She called the fire department who arrived and confirmed that the fire was limited to the light itself and there was no damage in the outlet box.

On March 12th (today) she called the fire department and told us we can now take posessiont of the light.


[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved a fire but no injuries or damage beyond the nightlight itself, and the fire was quickly contained.

incident_description: I have a Graco Lovin' Hug Plug-In Infant Swing. The frame moves with the swing, and makes creaking sounds. The baby keeps sliding down even when he's buckled in. The way the swing is positioned even when the chair is as far back as it can go his chin is resting on his chest. And most importantly the mobile falls off on top of the baby!
justification: The swing's issues pose a risk of injury due to the mobile falling on the baby and the baby sliding down, but no actual injury is reported.

incident_description: As far as I know there have been no reports of incidents with this product. But the product is very similar to other infant positioners that have been recalled and have been known to cause deaths.  Even the pictures of the infants go against all recommendations from the AAP regarding safe sleep.  Infants should be placed to sleep only on his/her back.  These positioners show infants sleeping on his/her side or stomach.  Both positions place the infant at great risk for SIDS or suffocation.
justification: The product is similar to recalled infant positioners linked to deaths, and its use goes against safe sleep recommendations, posing a high risk of SIDS or suffocation.

incident_description: I've owned a precious planet jumperoo for two years. My first son used it without a problem. It wasn't until my second son got his arm stuck that I saw the problem. My 6 month old son was jumping in this jumperoo having fun until I saw that he couldn't get his arm out. His arm was stuck in between two toys on the top. His arm was stuck in between the orange spinning toy and the yellow toy that is attached to the JUMP for lights and music toy. It didn't take much to remove his arm, just positioning it out the right way and he wasn't hurt that badly. I couldn't imagine what would have happend to my sons arm if he had turned the seat any more. I believe they have come out with a different version of this toy but I have not found a recall for this version. I bought this in November 2009. My husband had to use two butter knives and all of his strength to rip off this orange toy. They don't make it easily removable. Other than that issue the jumperoo has been fine. Thank goodness I am always in the room when he's in this toy.
justification: The child's arm got stuck but was not seriously injured, indicating a severity level of 2. The incident occurred once in two years of use, suggesting an occurrence likelihood of 2 (unlikely).

incident_description: My child has an imaginarium brand zoo animal bead maze activity cube. One side of the cube has an xylophone which is attached by wooden pegs and one wooden peg loosened and fell out. The peg is about 1/2 inch long and 1 centimeter wide whic is an obvious choking hazard.
justification: The loosened peg is a choking hazard, but no incident or injury has occurred yet.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that he was awaken by the an overwhelming odor of electrical fire and gas emitting from the night light.  He noticed that the bottom plastic housing had melted and it had a discoloration.  He unplugged the night light but the odor still lingered in the house.

2/22/12 The manufacturer was contacted and he was advised that someone will contact him.

The consumer feels that this product is a fire hazard and should be recalled.
justification: The incident involved a melted night light and lingering odor, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description: We have purchased 2 Fisher Price Newborn Rock n' Play Sleepers.  We frequently change out the top cover to wash it.  The top cover and the frame (with fabric on it) do not get saturated or stay wet.  With both of the sleepers that we purchased mold began to grow on the fabric that is covering the seat and helps to support the top cover.  Mold also began to appear on the safety straps near where they attach to the seat and come in contact with the fabric covering the plastic seat.  As I said the seat and the covers do not get wet and the top machine washable cover is frequently washed and completely dried prior to being put back onto the frame.  Since this fabric and the straps are not removable there is no way to safely wash the mold off and safely have an infant continue to use the seat.
justification: Mold growth on non-removable fabric and straps poses a hygiene issue but no immediate injury is reported.

incident_description:
Noticed some of the small "bristles" on baby's blue Born Free teether were missing. I brushed my hand over it and another one fell out. Baby loves chewing on this teether and has probably ingested missing bristles. I'm not sure whether or not that is safe (they are silicone) but I would assume this also could be a choking hazard.

This is a link to the product, which appears to have been discontinued:
http://www.diapers.com/p/born-free-teether-w-baby-toothbrush-80527

I contacted Born Free / Summer Infant who have not addressed the situation. This was the response:

Thank you for contacting Summer Infant, I have asked the appropriate manager about this situation and he has confirmed that the product has passed ASTM Child Safety tests and is safe for your child. Thank you for your time and patience and have a great day.

Sincerely,
[redacted] | Consumer Relations Representative : 8AM-6PM EST | Summer Infant, Inc.
1275 Park East Drive | Woonsocket RI, 02895 | ( 800-268-6237 )HRS: 8:00-6:00pm-est |
justification: The incident involves missing bristles that could pose a choking hazard, but there is no evidence of injury or death, and the product has passed safety tests.

incident_description: When my baby was 4 months old just after feeding him a bottle of formula and no success with burping I put him to bed in a sleep positioner, which is a piece of fabric with two wedges sewn onto it just far enough apart to fit a baby between them. This is to keep him from rolling to the side or onto his stomach, so the baby is forced to lay on his back. He also had one of those little snuggle bears kinda like a mini blankie with a little stuffed bear head in the center. I left him there in his crib to sleep while I was doing some work in my office. After about 20 minutes company arrived and I went down the hall to close my baby's door so our voices would not wake him. That is when I saw a most horrifying sight! My baby stuck in position from that sleep positioner and his favorite snuggle bear stuck to his face. I pulled the bear away and every orifice on his face was puddled white with spit up, a most awful image forever etched into my memory. I picked him up and his limbs and head seemed so heavy as they flopped downward, he was totally limp. I cleared the spit up from his face as I ran to the phone to call for help. While on the phone with the 911 operator I saw my baby's eyes roll into the back of his head and his body shuddered slightly as he appeared to be struggling for one last breath. In the calmest voice I could muster I repeatedly said to him "wake up for Mommy my sweet baby boy, please wake up, Mommy's here, I love you so very much" as I carried him quickly out the front door to the street (which is about 40 feet) and to my surprise the paramedics were just arriving, never could I have imagined a response time so quick! Medics placed me with my baby in my arms onto a stretcher and into the ambulance and off to Children's Hospital we rushed. On the way there they placed an oxygen mask on my baby's face then to the amazement of the medics and myself [REDACTED] regained consciousness and appeared completely normal before we had even traveled two miles. Once we arrived at Children's, doctors ran tests, scanned his brain, etc... No damage was detected. Thank you to God and to the Angel ([REDACTED]) who came to visit on that day, (had company not arrived, it could have been another 20 minutes before I checked on him) I am forever grateful.
justification: The baby experienced a life-threatening situation but ultimately recovered with no detected damage, indicating a severe incident with no lasting injury.

incident_description: The consumer says she laid her 6 month old down to sleep when he got his leg stuck in between the rail.  He could not get his leg out.  The consumer says he had flipped onto his stomach and was unable to turn back over.  The consumer was able to get his leg out.  She contacted the manufacturer who told her that the spacing between each bar meets regulations.  They told her that babies come in different sizes (fat, skinny etc).  The consumer told them that she can fit her entire arm in between the railing.
justification: The baby's leg got stuck but was freed without injury, and the manufacturer confirmed the rail spacing meets regulations.

incident_description:
The Learning Curve Baby Floating Stars Teething ring fluid is leaking from a seam.  My daughter does not have teeth yet so could not have punctured it.  I have seen similar comments made online about the product so it seems this is not an isolated problem.  For example see comments on amazon.com (click to view all comments beyond the first few that display). 

http://www.amazon.com/Learning-Curve-Floating-Stars-Teether/product-reviews/B000FZDIQ8/ref=cm_cr_dp_all_helpful?ie=UTF8&showViewpoints=1&sortBy=bySubmissionDateDescending
justification: The incident involves a product defect (fluid leakage) with no reported injury, and similar issues have been reported by others, indicating it's not isolated.

incident_description: My husband and I purchased the Cosco fold flat highchair when our son was 6 months old. We never had any problems with it then, but now that he is 13 months and more active he has gotten his leg stuck in the front of highchair numerous times. There is a section in the front of highchair that has a gap between the metal and the fabric that is about 2 inches. My son is capable of sticking his foot in this gap and then getting his ankle caught in it. He has not hurt himself seriously from this, yet, just a real panic in myself and husband trying to force his foot back through without hurting him. After looking at the highchair, I dont understand why they have it designed this way. Please address this matter.
justification: The child has gotten his leg stuck multiple times but has not been seriously injured, causing panic for the parents.

incident_description: My 13month old daughter (who weighs 25 lbs) was taking her morning nap this morning, I heard a crash and then screaming on the monitor. I  went upstairs and the back of the crib had collapsed and she was pinned imbetween the crib and the wall.  I was able to move the crib and get to her.  She is a little banged up, she has bruising on her lower back, left shoulder, and a small bump on the top of her head.  I immediately called my husband who called the Storkcraft company.  This is a brand new crib that supposedly met the safety standards.  We are waiting to hear back from the company but just did not want this to happen to another family.  It could have been devastating.
justification: The child suffered bruising and a bump, indicating injury, but no death or severe harm occurred.

incident_description: Hinge broke on the gate from normal use, the gate is meant to be mounted at the top of stairs. the parts are plastic and rather cheaply made. i run a state registered daycare center and can see this being a major compliance issue.  I have removed the gate until the replacement parts come which could be up to a month away.
justification: The gate broke but no injury occurred; however, the potential for injury is high given its location at the top of stairs in a daycare setting.

incident_description: Fisher Price Little Superstar, Step and Play piano:  The piano has "toys" attached with flexible semi-rigid plastic  - This plastic broke off when my daughter played with it.  On this toy, these toys are designed to be played with and moved around, however, the plastic "wore down" and eventually snapped.   It left a sharp piece at the end that scratched my daughter in the face and a sharp piece still attached to the toy
justification: The broken plastic caused a scratch injury to the child's face, indicating a severity level of 3. The likelihood is rated as 4 (likely) given the toy's design and the described wear and tear.

incident_description: This report concerns a safety gate, the Regalo Easy Open Extra Wide Gate.  The part of the gate that swings open and then when closed, latches onto the other side, has a tube on it.  There is a small grey plug that fits into the tube that was not secured.  It fell out and is a choking hazard. I found it on the ground by the gate.  Glad I found it before our dog or baby did!
justification: The incident involved a small part becoming detached, posing a potential choking hazard, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: As my client was carrying her four week old in the mi Swivel, made by First Years, the back of the chair broke apart causing the infant to fall through the back of the chair and land head first on the floor.  he suffered two subdurmal hemotomas, two fractures in his scull, brain bleeding and a black eye.
justification: The infant suffered severe injuries including skull fractures and brain bleeding, which constitutes a severity level of 4 (Death was not mentioned, but injuries are life-threatening).

incident_description:
My girlfriends daughter, her mother, my son, and I were present at my house.  This injured person is my girlfriends daughter.

IÃÂm trying to raise awareness about a product that was involved with a devastating critical injury to a toddler in Lacey WA.  

About a year ago, a little girl fell down the stairs of my home during the night while the adults were asleep.  She was found in the morning, unconscious.  Her baby gate that was on the doorway to her bedroom when she was put to bed, was lying flat on the carpet in the morning.  

She was rushed to the ER and has been in a coma for over a year.  She will never walk, talk, or be the same.  Most of her brain is non-functioning.

Shortly after her birth, a two pack of  Evenflo #202 baby gates were bought from Toys R Us in Olympia and used continuously.  After the accident, and upon examination, not just the one gate guarding her door exhibited a bent pressure pin, but the other did as well.

Evenflo claims that itÃÂs #202 is the largest selling baby gate.  They are sold virtually everywhere.  

I donÃÂt want this to happen to another child, ever.   There is an alternative to the this particular model it is in the same price range ( They are both the cheapest gates on the market).  The [REDACTED] gate is of the same exact design; except, the area that was bent on our Evenflo gates, allowing the little girl to get out during the night, has a re-enforced metal gusset to address this issueÃÂthereby eliminating this issue.

I am just trying to reach as many new parents. I have pictures to better understand what I'm talking about.
justification: The incident resulted in a toddler suffering severe, irreversible brain damage, which is considered a life-altering injury equivalent to death in terms of severity. The likelihood is rated as unlikely (2) because while the product defect is present, such severe outcomes are not common for every use of the product.

incident_description:
I am not usually a busybody or the type to cry "danger," but I have come across a product that seems so dangerous on its face that I needed to make sure you all knew about it.  I do not own this product; I was considering buying it for my baby until I read the reviews online and noted that many parents, who are using the product in the manner that it is advertised for, are ending up with babies with serious and lasting injuries.

The product is the Fisher Price Newborn Rock & Play sleeper.  It is billed as a safe, comfortable place for a newborn to sleep, built so it's height is level with a bed for easy nighttime care.  The literature advertising the sleepr states that it is meant for overnight sleep, nap time and even play time during the day.  

Unfortunately, it seems that many, many babies are ending up with Torticollis and flattened heads after using the sleeper.  In fact, i have a friend whose niece can no longer even turn her head after using this sleeper for some time.  There are literally dozens of reviews on amazon.com mentioning this problem.  

I know that, having decided against buying this sleeper, I have absolutely no standing to complain about the product.  But the thought that it is out there, still being sold when it harms kids whose parents are using it exactly as intended, really bothers me.  I needed to at least make sure you guys were aware of it.
justification: The product has caused serious and lasting injuries like Torticollis and flattened heads in many babies, as reported by numerous reviews and a personal account.

incident_description: On Dec. 23, 2011 we found our five-month-old son dead in his PeaPod Plus Portable Children's Travel Bed (Model P201). He was rolled three-quarters of the way onto his belly, face down and with his weight pressing him into in the non-breathable plastic sidingof the travel crib. As per manufacturer's instructions, we had not zippered the travel bed shut, so his legs were hanging out of the "door" of the travel bed. He may have suffocated, or he may have rolled there after/as he died from SIDS, or another cause. Regardless, though, I do not believe that this tent should be marketed as safe for infants. It is advertised as breathable, yet the area where a baby would put his face is wind-resistant and fire-resistant (according to a company spokesman who spoke with one of our friends after the incident), and is not breathable. In addition, the tent is malleable, and a baby can roll into the siding, molding his face and body into the non-breathable areas in a way that would not be possible in the more rigid siding of a [playpen].
justification: The incident resulted in the death of an infant due to suffocation or SIDS, with clear evidence of unsafe product design.

incident_description:
AmerTac nightlight 73174 shorted out and melted the lower portion of the plastic cover, the half of the duplex outlet to which it was attached, and destroyed the insulation on the wires connected to the outlet (12 gauge).  There is a large black streak on the wall above the wall outlet and the house reeked with the smell of melting plastic and insulation (probably not great stuff to breath...)  The 20 amp breaker in the sub-panel was tripped and a check with an ohm meter now shows 170 ohms between the grounded and ungrounded conductors supplying the outlet, which means that the wall will have to be opened and the wiring replaced.

The AmerTac 73174 unit has two electrical outlets in addition to the night light itself, but nothing was, nor ever had been, plugged into them.  The unit has been run continuously for well over a year (I don't remember exactly when it was purchased)
justification: The incident caused significant property damage and potential health hazards from fumes, but no reported injuries or deaths.

incident_description: I have been using pampers for about 2 years.  I noticed a diaper rash on my daughter from about 6 months of age that would not go away. I was told by my pediatrician that it ws a yeast infection and it will go away with cream.  Although the cream helped to a degree, the "burn like" appearance was always there.  About 4 weeks ago, my daughter got the worse "rash" i had ever seen on a baby.  I started doing research on the type of diaper I was using and came across a site that provided information about other parents who had trouble with rash's associated with pampers.  Upon reading this information, I read someone describe the rash as looking like a chemical burn.  That's exactly what my daughter has.  We changed diapers and within 2 days the redness was relieved and she was no longer in pain.  I am telling everyone who uses pampers to stop.  I firmly believe the issue with my daughter was caused by Pampers and I would like something to be done about it.
justification: The incident describes a persistent and severe diaper rash resembling a chemical burn, causing pain to the child, which qualifies as an injury. The likelihood is 'likely' (4) as multiple parents report similar issues with the product.
