incident_description:
The consumer has a set of fraternal twins that she believes may be experienced health and developmental issues to their neck and cranium, because of their sleep/rocker. The consumer stated that after her twins were born and brought them home they began sleeping in the rockers at times. The consumer purchased two identical products from an online retailer. The consumer stated that the product has a metallic frame with a hard plastic where a child would lay against. The hard plastic is covered by a fabric less than a quarter inch. 

Over time, the consumer has not noticed any damage to these products but has noticed anomalies in her childrenÃÂs development. The consumer first decided to take her children for a pediatric screening in June after noticing these abnormalities. The childrenÃÂs pediatrician noticed the twins were developing Torticollis, a stiffening of the neck and Plagiocephaly, a condition characterized by an asymmetrical distortion of the skull. The pediatrician decided it was best to begin physical therapy for the twins on July 12th.  

The children are seen for a physical therapy session 2 times a week for sessions 30-45 minutes each. The consumer was conducting independent research on Tuesday and found numerous comments and complaints from consumers whose children have developed the same symptoms. The consumerÃÂs insurance is paying for the childrenÃÂs physical therapy for Torticollis but the consumer is paying out of pocket for the treatment of plagiocephaly. The consumerÃÂs twins were given an orthotic of cranial molding helmets for the plagiocephaly by the childrenÃÂs cranial medical specialist. 

These Helmets were prescribed on October 28 2011. The children began wearing the helmets on November 15, 2011. The consumer called the firm on Wednesday to bring the issue to their attention.  The firm  seemed  knowledgeable about the situation and requested the consumer send medical documentation about her children, stating that the product caused and perpetuated these health issues. 

The firm also offered to refund her money once they can receive the products in question. The consumer stated that she does not feel comfortable in sending her childrenÃÂs medical records to the firm. The consumer has not notified the retailer. The consumer discussed the issue prior with consumer reports who referred the consumer to CPSC.
justification: The children have developed Torticollis and Plagiocephaly, requiring physical therapy and cranial molding helmets, indicating injury (severity 3). The occurrence likelihood is possible (3) as similar complaints from other consumers suggest a pattern.

incident_description: Two weeks ago I received a Summer Infant Extra tall baby gate for my baby shower. I installed it a few days later. The gate can be used for both regular doorways and top of stairs. Two days ago, my 4 year old daughter opened the gate to pass through and the plastic hinge just shattered causing the whole top of the gate to fall forward. She did not pull it hard and did not open it in any way I would not have. As the top of the gate broke, she stumbled forward. I am so thankful that we had not put this at the top of our stairs! Upon searching product reviews online I found that the exact same thing has happened to other consumers of Summer brand gates (other designs of their product in addition to the extra tall one we have). The quality of the plastic hinge is very poor for a heavy metal gate. When my 4 year old was born we had purchased 2 Summer Infant Extra Tall baby gates ((manuf. date 2003), but the design was a bit different and the product has stood up to it's purpose. They close automatically as the product described and the hinges have held up. The newer design claims to swing closed on it's own, but did not and hinge shattering is just dangerous. I worry about anyone who may place this gate at the top of the stairs. If the hinge failed upon opening, anyone could fall down the stairs. If a baby were to tug on the gate and it broke, the child could possibly die from the fall.
justification: The gate failure caused the child to stumble, indicating a potential for injury, and the product reviews suggest this is a recurring issue with the design.

The product literature included with the crib states that the crib must be at least 51 5/8 inches long.  I purchased a mattress that is 51 7/8 inches long.  Using this mattress with the Sundvik crib there is a 1.5 inch gap between the end of the mattress and the head of the crib (I have photos). incident_description: I bought a new crib for our baby expected in May 2012. We purchased the EUROPA BABY PALISADES CRIB. After purchasing a standard crib mattress (Serta Perfect Dream) and placing it in the crib, my 20 month old daughter wanted to "play night night" in her baby brother's crib. I let her sit (supervised) in the new crib for a few minutes, and when she stood up, her entire leg slipped between the mattress and the rail of the crib. After ensuring the crib was properly installed, we started taking measurements. The crib measures (from inside of rail to inside of rail) 28 1/2". This is supposedly within federal safety guidelines (28" +/- 5/8"). Our mattress measures 27 1/4", also within federal safety guidelines (28" +/- 3/4"). The crib/mattress combo did not pass the two finger test. I was easily able to slip 2 fingers between the mattress and the rail. In fact, I could slip my whole arm down there without much effort. I set out looking for a larger mattress, but the largest available is 27 1/2", which is still not wide enough to fit this crib. I called the crib maker to see if they had any suggestions, but all they kept telling me was "the crib meets federal safety guidelines." I understand the measurements are within the guidelines, but if a toddler's leg can slip between the mattress and the rail, then the measurements do not seem safe. incident_description:
I purchased a 10'' natural & organic crib bumper from Natura in 2009.  I used it with my daughter, who was born in 2009, for just a few weeks.  She didn't like having a bumper (she liked looking out of her crib) so I removed the bumper after just a few weeks of use.

In 2011 I had twins, and I used the crib bumper in my son's crib.  His crib is a standard crib from [REDACTED] that we bought in 2011.  The Natura crib bumper did not have enough ties placed in the right places for me to anchor it safely in each corner.  As a result, I found my son after a nap one afternoon with his head caught up under the un-anchored corner of the crib bumper.  I immediately removed the crib bumper.

I contacted Natura to inform them and ask them for a refund.  They told me that since I did not purchase the bumper directly from them (I bought it from a website called Pure Rest), they could not issue a refund.  They also told me it was the first time they had heard of this incident.

Before the scary incident with my son happened, I had tried to purchase a matching crib bumper online.  However, even though websites such as Amazon.com list this 10'' crib bumper, when I ordered the bumper I was sent a similar, but different, 6'' bumper that came in 4 pieces (not 2, like my 10'' one from 2009).  This 6'' bumper did seem to have more ties, and by having separate sections it is possible that it fits cribs better.

The problem I am reporting is specifically for the 10'' crib bumper that was sold in 2009.  It's got only two pieces, and not enough ties to be safe in a standard crib.  I am thankful my son did not strangle or suffocate.

I have since learned that crib bumpers are generally unsafe and I am no longer using them in any form.

Thank you.
justification: The incident involved a potential suffocation hazard but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description:
On November 26, 2008, I purchased The Rosado Sling at The Toy Box located in Brooklyn, New York.  The sling came in XS, S, M, ML, L and XL.  I purchased a Medium.  Sling had 2 silver rings and a padded shoulder.  The 2 silver rings are to help tighten and loosen the sling.  Sling was to sit on the shoulder and tuck underneath the arm.  On the actual sling is a label which say: The Rosado Sling, for Infants and Toddlers, Rosadosling.com and Julianne Rosado (maker of the sling).  Sling was blue with cotton fabric and polyester batting.  

On the packaging, it stated www.rosadosling.com, The Rosado Sling, for infants and toddlers, For a greater bond between caregiver & child.  Cotton Fabric, Polyester Batting. Fabric Care: Wash Cold, Hang dry.  With the sizes that I listed above.  No instructions nor warnings on both the packaging or on the sling itself. 

I placed my son in the sling shortly after his well baby visit where the pediatrician gave him a clean bill of health.  He was positioned near my breast with his head up.  I was able to look down and see his face.  During about a 4 hour time frame, I fed him, changed his diaper, family and some friends held him and went to some local stores.  However, as I was online at a local chain restaurant, I looked down and he was pale.  I immediately rushed him to the nearest ER where they ran all types of tests. He was in the hospital for 30 days due to lack of controlled body temperature but wasn't able to suck and placed him on seizure medication.  

My son is currently 3 years old and has been diagnosed with Cerebral Palsy.  He is not able to sit on his own, stand on his own, crawl, walk or talk.  He is receiving Physical Therapy, Occupational Therapy and Speech Therapy.  He is currently being seen by a neurologist, orthopedist as well as additional specialists.  

I hope that The Rosado Sling will not be used since it was a tragic incident that has caused my son's current injuries.
justification: The incident resulted in severe injuries leading to Cerebral Palsy, which is a significant and lasting impact on the child's health and development.

incident_description:
I purchased a Delta crib from Toys r us and received it the beginning of this month, January 2012.  While I was putting the crib together, I got to where you attach the mattress support part to the leg of the crib, I wasn't able to because there were no rivets in the leg to screw in the screws.  I right away called Delta and the girl that answered the phone didn't even let me fully explain the problem...she said it was a common problem and they would send out the part right away.  I was very concerned by this and asked to speak to a supervisor.  I was put on the line w/[REDACTED], a supervisor there at Delta.  He told me Oh well it happens and that he would send the leg out right away and that it was nothing to be concerned with.  
Well this morning, January 18, 2012, I went to get my grandson from his crib and found that he had pulled off several pieces of the veneer that goes over the wood on the leg of the crib.  He had pieces of all sizes, mostly in the crib and some of it in his mouth.  There were pieces that were small enough that he could have chocked on them.  Right away I called Delta and again got on the phone w/[REDACTED], the supervisor at Delta.  He said to me that my grandson could only have bit of parts from the top of the crib and he must be teething.  I said No, that it was from the side leg and he couldn't possible fit his head between the bars to be able to bite on the leg.  He asked that I send him pictures  and told me he would forward them on to be investigated.  I have sent the pictures he requested and will wait for Delta to reply.  But in the mean time, Once again I have a crib that I Can Not put my grand son into, and will have to put him in his pack and play, where I know he will be safe because he is Not safe in the Delta crib.  Please before a baby does choke to death on a piece of veneer from the crib, please do something to stop Delta from continuing to mass produce Unsafe cribs.  Thank you so much for taking the time to read this.  

Information regarding the crib:
Delta
Style No: 6023
Color: 607
SKN: 624 061
Lot #: QW11297
PO #: 254027
MFG Date: Sep 2011


If you need any further information please email me at [REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved a crib defect that led to a child ingesting small pieces of veneer, posing a choking hazard, but no actual injury was reported.

incident_description: VTECH Sit to Stand Learning Walker, Product Number 80-077000. This product states it is best for children ages 9-36 months.  My daughter is 9 months of age, has been crawling for over 2 months, has been pulling herself to a standing position for well over a month and can sit from a standing position without assistance.  She has a high desire to walk and we thought this would be a wonderful product to help assist her in her mobile desires.  She has been supervised 100% of the time during her use of this product.  My primary complaints are the this product has no speed control, no mechanism to slow the wheel speeds and without such feature, this product goes forward very quickly, causing my child to fall repeatedly every time she uses it.  Additionally, when she does pull herself up to a standing position from the designated standing area using the handle, the toy topples over backward and lands on top of my child.  This is not a one-time instance.  In my opinion, this product is a danger and hazard to children and should be recalled and restructured to include some kind of speed control mechanism on the wheels (perhaps a slow-click into place feature) and something to prevent this toy from tumbling backward onto children!  I no longer allow my daughter to use the walker and have unattached the play panel so she may have some enjoyment from the toy.  The company replied with a generic email to my complaint that they would keep the information on file.  Seriously?  This product poses a danger to children and they're simply going to keep the information on file?  These issues need to be addressed so no other children are hurt.

incident_description:
When I heard my 7 month old daughter choking over her baby monitor, I rushed into her room to find about 3 inches of pink fabric hanging from her mouth.  Another 6 inches were down her throat, obstructing her airway.  I am a former Paramedic, so believe me when I say that her airway was obstructed, and this would surely resulted in the death of my daughter had I not reached her in time.

The fabric was a tie strap from her crib bumper; one of the ties that holds the bumper in place on the crib.  Upon inspection, I noticed that the tie strap was not torn, nor was the knot untied.  The actual stitching that holds the strap to the bumper had come undone.  Upon even further inspection, I noticed that the stitching was coming undone on several other tie straps on this bumper, leading me to believe that there is an inherent issue with the combination of the fabric that makes up the bumper and straps, and the thread used to secure them together. 

The manufacturer has been contacted by my wife and myself, and they seem completely oblivious as to how dangerous this could be, and are not willing to help.  I do have photographs that I will be more than happy to provide.

The product is made by a company called Sleeping Partners, located in Bronx, NY.  Their website is sleepingparters.com  This product was under their line called "Tadpoles," and is the "Dimpled Velour" model, which came as part of a complete bedding set.
justification: The incident involved a life-threatening situation where the child's airway was obstructed, which could have resulted in death without immediate intervention.

I immediately drove to my pediatrician who recommended to make this case public as he had never seen this before. Her toes are still wound and have to be treated every 4 hours to avoid a serious infection. 
I still have the invoice of the bassinet as well as picures of the injured toes and the bassinet after the incident.
justification: The infant sustained injuries requiring medical treatment, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 2 (unlikely) since the pediatrician had never seen this before.

incident_description:
To whom it may concern:

I am writing in regard to a changing table I purchased of yours, from Babies R Us. I was
changing my two-year-old daughter on it when the board beneath just split wide open on her. I
immediately removed her and examined it, and found it to be as flimsy as cardboard. I called the
phone number on the sticker, immediately, and left a detailed and very concerned message. No one
ever bothered to respond to my call.

I called again last week. This time, I got a human being. Still, no apologies or even
sympathies, only excuses ("We don't know the condition you kept the changing table in," "It's no
longer still under warranty," "Maybe she was too heavy"--She wasn't; she was 25 lbs., and it's
supposed to hold up to 30--yaddie-yaddie-yaddah.). I'm sorry but a child falling through and being
injured from a changing table collapsing on her does not call for ANY excuses! And regardless of
WHEN the warranty expires, NO changing table should EVER be splitting open on ANY child!
The woman then non-chalantly instructed me to send pictures, I guess to prove I was telling
the truth. I explained to her that I had had to literally tape the changing table back together in order
to use it, but I would send pictures with the tape. So here they are (along with the model number,
etc.).

When you pay hundreds of dollars for a changing table to safely change your child in, you
do not expect to have to contend with having the table split wide open on your child due to this type
of shoddy workmanship. You should not have to worry about your child's safety--from the
furniture itself--when you lay her down to simply change a diaper. This is a disgrace and
completely unacceptable.

Sincerely,
[REDACTED]
justification: The child fell through the changing table but was not injured, indicating an incident without injury.

It's very easy to attach to the crib, which is nice for parents, but it turns out that it's just as easy for the infant to remove. Last week I heard a big thud and then she started screaming.  I came into her room and found the soother lying in the crib and she had a knot on her forehead and what would turn into a black eye.   I was horrified as I thought that I perhaps had put the toy on wrong or something.  Keep in mind that I'm a mom of 4, so these toys are not new to me and I am a college educated person as well.  I put the toy back on, and made sure it was snug tight.  The next naptime she was able to get it half off, but I came to her before it could fall off again completely.  Basically, all you have to do is push up on the soother and it comes undone.  

I attached the soother again last night and again she was able to get it off again this morning after only minutes.  She's no genius, just a typical 7 month old.

I'm concerned that given the weight of this item, (almost 4 pounds), a concussion could possibly result as the product is falling from above.  

Here's a link to it from walmart: http://www.walmart.com/catalog/product.do?product_id=12457971&sourceid=1500000000000003260330&ci_src=14110944&ci_sku=12457971

Thank you so much for your time, 
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident resulted in a knot on the forehead and a black eye, indicating an injury (severity 3). The toy was repeatedly dislodged by the infant, making the occurrence likely (4).

incident_description: My 3 year old was sitting in his Svan highchair Model USC002 and reached for something causing the highchair to tip. His head hit the corner of the table necessitating a trip to the pediatricians office, then the ER where he had a CT scan to determine if his skull was cracked. It also required a follow up hearing to test to determine if his hearing had been affected.
justification: The child suffered an injury requiring medical attention, including a CT scan and hearing test, indicating a severity level of 3.

incident_description: My son came home from pre-school with blue streaks on his inner thighs and a diaper rash.  I was able to use a little rubbing alcohol to remove the streaks.  After his bath his legs were streak free.  When I went to change his diaper before bed, I noticed the blue streaks were back.  I realized that the diapers lined up with the streaks.  I called Huggies the next morning and they confirmed that they had a problem with that Lot number.
justification: The incident involved a product defect causing visible streaks and diaper rash, but no serious injury was reported.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that her 24 month old daughter is contracting blisters from her diapers. The size of the diapers are size 4. The consumer has had her daughter using the diapers for a week before contracting the blisters on the bottom of her rear. The consumer purchased 2 packages  of these diapers. Each package has 160 diapers.  The consumer has only been through half of one package before she  stopped using the diapers. The consumer found that her daughter began contracting red bumps which became blisters. 

The consumer went back to her daughter's old diapers and saw her daughter's symptoms decrease over time. The consumer decided to use the trouble diapers again after a month removed from initially stopping usage of these diapers. Her daughter again began contracting the blisters only a day after she started to use these diapers. Her blisters have the diameter of a number two pencil eraser. The consumer insists that no other factors have changed in her daughter's diet or care patterns except for these diapers. 

The consumer was doing some independent research and found numberous complaints from other consumers about these diapers. The consumer called the firm today and was told that they would send her 50 dollars worth of coupons. The consumer has yet to call the retailer but intends to go back there today. The consumer has used [REDACTED] to assuage her daughter's blisters but has not taken her to a doctor. The consumer's daughter is not on any medication that may afflict or exacerbate her condition and normally does not contract rashes.
justification: The incident describes blisters and red bumps on the child, which constitute an injury, but there is no mention of death or severe harm.

incident_description:
We initially used pampers swaddlers up until my baby grew out of the sizes available.  We then switched to pampers baby dry and cruisers(more premium of the pampers brand).  After a week or so of using the diapers my son developed what we thought was usual diaper rash, but NOTHING cleared it up!  We have found a store that carries the Swaddlers (dye free) in a size 3 and have switched to those, with in a matter a of DAYS the rash has begun to heal.  It is a red, raised, and in some spots blistery.  We have had it checked by the Dr. to rule out any other possible causes (yeast, etc)  We have also used other brands of diapers ([REDACTED] brand...) without causing of this rash.

I have three other children, all of which we used pampers, and all without issue.  I prefer pampers over other brands.

Hopefully Pampers will do something about his issue, or we will be forced to switch brands.  Not sure what they changed, but it is definitely a pampers issue!  I have over $90 in diapers here that can not be used, due to buying in bulk at a local Sams club....maybe they will allow a return?

Thanks,
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident describes a baby developing a persistent and painful rash due to the use of specific diapers, which constitutes an injury.

incident_description: choking hazard on an attached toy.  The butterfly toy has long narrow wings that my child put all the way into the back of her mouth and chocked.
justification: The child choked on the toy's long narrow wings, indicating an injury occurred, and the design suggests a likely recurrence if not addressed.

incident_description: Our simplicity ellis 4 in 1the cribs bars on the frame have bent and one has come out of place. This can be dangerous to the baby or toddler who uses the bed.
justification: The bent crib bars pose a potential hazard to the baby or toddler, indicating an incident with no injury reported yet.

incident_description: I have a madison stork craft crib/changing table combo i bought a year ago. Two days ago i was changing my son on the changing table when i heard a snapping noise. Next thing i know is part of the changing table was in the top drawer along with my son.
justification: The incident involved a structural failure of the changing table, but there was no mention of injury to the child.

incident_description: Acyrlic night light melted and burnt blanket when blanket was kicked off bed and landed on night light.  Night light cover is a Steelers football player.
justification: The incident involved property damage (melted night light and burnt blanket) but no reported injury.

incident_description: My daughter developed a rash that turned into what looked like a burn. It got progressively worse until we changed diapers and after one day of a different diaper brand, it has healed considerably.
justification: The rash developed into a burn-like condition, indicating an injury that required intervention (changing diaper brands) to heal.

incident_description: I own the DwellStudioÃÂ® for TargetÃÂ®Silver Lake Convertible Crib 2nd Edition in Natural/White made by Foremost Groups. It was purchased on 9/4/2010. My son is 10 months old. The front and back rails of the crib are painted wood. My son was standing in his crib this morning. He put his mouth on the top of the rail while standing. I walked over the stop him and noticed a paint chunk taken out from the rail. He also had small flecks of paint on his mouth.
justification: The child ingested small flecks of paint, which is an incident but no injury was reported.

incident_description: Plastic piece holding gate door to gate side snapped, allowing gate door and child to push through to the stairs
justification: The incident involved a gate failure that allowed a child to pass through, but there is no mention of injury.

incident_description:
Recently purchased Safety First Lift, Lock and Swing baby gate.  Mounted gate, it shows that it is fully engaged but I noticed that the handle looked slightly off center.  I bumped the gate and the entire thing disengaged.  It seems that there may be a design flaw in the handle of the gate and even though it is pushed down fully, sounds like it clicks into place, shows the indicators are engaged, if the handle is not perfectly lined up, it could possibly disengage.  As this is advertised for the top of stairs, which is where we were thinking of installing it, it seems that it could become disengaged with a slight bump, allowing access to the stairs.

Luckily I caught this before installing all of the hardware at the top of the stairs.  I still think it is an ok gate for other areas but shouldn't be listed as safe for the tops of stairs until this issue is corrected.
justification: The gate disengaged with a slight bump, posing a potential fall hazard, but no injury occurred as it was caught before installation at the top of the stairs.

incident_description: My 7-month old son, [REDACTED], was sitting in the Fisher-Price Infant-To-Toddler Rocker when he fell forward and sustained a minor head injury. The chair was placed flat on the linoleum bathroom floor, with my son restrained with the safety belt fastened. I was standing about 4 feet away, with my baby within sight. [REDACTED] dropped the toy he was playing with and leaned forward to reach for it. When he did this, the chair tipped far forward and he fell face-first onto the bathroom rug, with the chair laying on top of him. He cried for approximately 5 minutes and sustained a bump with many small abrasions to the left side of his forehead, about 1 inch above his left eyebrow. I took him to the doctors office within a few hours to have him checked out. He did not sustain a concussion. My child is well within the weight limit of the product. [REDACTED] weighs 24.6 lbs, and the weight limit of said product  is stated to be 40 lbs. The product was being used properly, in accordance with the manufacturers' instructions.
justification: The child sustained a minor head injury with abrasions, indicating an injury (severity 3). The incident occurred despite proper use, suggesting a possible likelihood (3) of recurrence under similar conditions.

incident_description:
defective crib bracket. i put my daughter in her crib and the corner dropped to the floor wedging her foot in the corner.  upon inspection the bracket that holds the  crib mattress support to the wood cracked.
creations baby crib herritage collection model number 6021521.

incident_description: Once yesterday and twice today so far my son has gotten his leg stuck in his crib slats.  He seems to be fine now but when stuck he screams in pain like I have never heard him do before.  It is also incredibly difficult to get his leg unstuck.  I measures the slats and they have about 2 1/4 inches between them, within the guidelines.  This is unsafe, now I have to switch him to his pack-n-play to sleep in after spending a fortune on this crib.  The regulations need to be changed, this has got to be dangerous and is certainly painful for him.
justification: The child experienced significant pain and difficulty getting unstuck, indicating an injury level severity. The incident has occurred multiple times, suggesting a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: My niece and my son have both gotten their arm stuck in the side of my mom's Evenflo Envision high chair.  They got stuck in the space in between the seat and the leg.  They were able to slide their arm into the space and not back out.  It resulted in discomfort only.

incident_description:
My 4 month old baby was playing with the Woodours Baby Activity Rattle and Teether Bear (purchased at the baby store "Giggle")in his crib while under my supervision. A teether is attached to the bear with a string. My baby started screaming, and I found the teether underneath his head, the string tight against his neck deep under his chin, and the plush bear on his other side. The string was wrapped around the front of his neck. I didn't see the string at first because it was buried deep in his neck. I tried to move the bear and saw that the string was choking my son. As soon as removed the toy, he stopped screaming and seemed fine. 

The string is a hazard and should not be attached (sewn) on a toy that is sold as appropriate for newborns and older.
justification: The baby was choking but was unharmed after the toy was removed, indicating an incident with no injury.

incident_description: First, my good friend who has the mam air paifier had sent me a text image of her 8 month old little girls pacifier....broke in half...she ouldnt believe it!  I just thought maybe she stepped on it or ran it over...and dismissed it!  Just a couple days ago i was taking my son out of his carseat in the car to put him in my [REDACTED] carrier....i have the mam pacifier strap that you can pop onto the pacifier and hook to whatever....preventing it from falling!  I grabbed the pacifier from his mouth, was just about to put it in the loop and it snapped....i barely put any pressure on it at all, it was the same spot my friends broke, i asked her how it haopened and her baby....8 months snapped theirs off herself....right in half....not only is this a choking hazard but also very sharp!  I reported it to mam and they told me they would send me a new one??????NO way!  These are very thin...even an older toddler could very easly snap these in half!
justification: The pacifier broke in half, posing a choking hazard and sharp edges, but no injury was reported.

I turned around to wash out her bottle when I heard a HORRIBLE thud and turned around to see my baby on the tile floor!  She had hit the floor head first! She had fallen out b/c while in the recline position it allows child to easily slip through and lean over head first, then gravity takes over.  These high chairs shouldn't even have this position as an option!!!  And with the buckle, it gives parents a FALSE SENSE OF SECURITY.

incident_description: I purchased a value box of size 4 pampers cruiser from the local Target retail for my 22 month old. Within a few days she developed a severe reaction as a result from switching her from another brand to this pampers. The pain and discomfort was experienced immediately displayed by my daughter's behavior and irritability. I purchased several types of diaper rash cream as well as [REDACTED] ointment by the request of her pediatrician but it did not help at all. A week later, her genital and rectal area took on a more aggressive chemical burn with blisters and welts. That is when I eliminated any further use of this cruisers Pampers. I also informed her preschool to stop using it on her as we kept the supply there. It's nearly 3 weeks later, and the redness is just starting to fade but the itchiness and discomfort lingers. My husband and I feel we have been misled as consumers by P&G and want to make sure this is reported and documented. I have kept the remaining unused diapers in the event further investigation is needed.
justification: The child suffered a severe chemical burn with blisters and welts, indicating an injury, but such reactions are unlikely for most users.

incident_description:
We have had several incidents where our daughters feet are getting caught in the slats of the crib.  Here is a copy of a review we recently posted on the product.

Being a victim of the drop-side crib fiasco, we were given a voucher to purchase a new crib, even though we had never experienced any problems. Being diligent and desiring safety for our children we set out to find a new crib. We really liked the finish and the quality of materials of this crib, however...

Unfortunately about 6 months after we purchased the crib, we awoke to a terrible scream, not the normal type of scream. Rushing in we found our 6 month old daughter with her foot caught around the ankle between the slats, not a problem we ever had with our previous crib, the notorious drop-side crib, through 2 babies.
We have tried to weave the bedding bumper through the slats to help prevent recurrences but we still have occasional problems. As recent as last night, 10/30/2011, our now 18 month old daughter began screaming again. This time there was a noticeable indent on her ankle and swelling on her foot.

Other negatives are the customer support we received. The crib was shipped with the incorrect assembly directions and hardware. It took nearly a month to receive the parts and the correct directions.

This is a beautiful crib, but be warned of its dangers.
justification: The incident describes a child's foot getting caught in the crib slats, resulting in swelling and indentations, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description: I recieved a Vulli Sophie Giraffe  teether as a babyshower gift, and I would just like to report that my 4 month old daughter was chewing on the legs of her sophie when she rolled over & sophies two front legs became lodged in her throat, my mother heard her making choking noises and rushed to her aid, to discover her airway was completely occluded & she was almost blue within seconds. beware that this can happen & could have ended in tradegy. We will be disposing of her teether immediately. I have read many reviews of this product & found many other similar situations, had I only been aware I would have returned this gift & never allowed my daughter to use it.

My baby's foot and leg gets stuck in the slats of the Alma Mini crib.  The crib is small but the manufacture claims that is it safe for use up to twelve months.  My baby is four months and this is the 5th incident in the last week.  Although the company complies to federal regulation in regard to slat width, the crib is too small for a baby that is mobile. incident_description: Our baby [REDACTED] was born August 8, 2011 and I am her mother. We used Pampers Swaddler with Dry Max since she was brought home from the hospital. She began having a rash right away on her bum that persisted. Several visit to the doctor failed to clear the rash; we stopped using moist towelettes (opting instead for wet face cloths), we tried 3 different kind of medications (clotrimazole cream 1%, cortate ont 1%, nystatin), we dried her bum with a hair dryer every chance we got, changed her diapers very often...nothing worked! The rash persisted and got progressively worse. In the end she had open sores that bled - poor babe! Frustrated, I searched the internet determined to find a solution and finally stumbled upon articles about other parents who had went through the same problem and had traced it to the brand of diaper they were using: Pampers Swaddler with Dry Max. I went to [REDACTED] bedroom and confirmed that all her diapers since birth had been that brand/kind! We stopped using them and now [REDACTED] bum is 90% better after 1 week. This product should be discontinued OR come with a warning that the Dry Max component can be harmful to some babies.
justification: The baby suffered persistent and worsening rashes leading to open sores, indicating an injury. The issue was resolved only after discontinuing the product, suggesting a likely occurrence for similar cases.

incident_description:
Hello, 

My husband and I are both physicians and also parents.  Our son is 15 months old and never had any major issues with diaper rash.  We have used pamper diaper products since he was born.  It wasn't until we switched to the Dry max cruisers formula that he first began to develop severe rashes.  Initially we thought it was due to his diet.  So we began limiting certain food items.  When that didn't seem to work we started to be more aggressive with our diaper rash cream.  We were using maximum strength items and I even consulted the NICU team at our hospital for recommendations on what they use to treat their patients with severe rashes.  When those products also failed we suspected a possible fungal infection and used antifungal creams, although clinically it did not look fungal in origin, but in fact, more like a chemical burn with blistering.  It wasn't until a colleague of mine, who is also a pediatrician, mentioned the increased incidence of rashes associated with the diapers we were using.  I immediately went out and purchased a different brand of diapers and literally within only several hours I already began to see a difference and it was completely gone within a few days and now several weeks later he has not had another one since!  

I was very concerned with this rash, both by its appearance - chemical burn like in nature- and also by the significant amount of pain that it inflicted on my child.  I have no doubt in my mind that this was due to the Dry max formula diapers, and although i have no controlled studies to confirm this hypothesis, it is in my professional opinion that this formula of diapers should be taken off the market.
justification: The incident describes a severe rash resembling a chemical burn causing significant pain to the child, which qualifies as an injury. The likelihood is possible as it occurred after switching diaper brands.

incident_description: bad diaper rash from pampers diapers
justification: Bad diaper rash is an injury to the skin, indicating a severity level of 3.

incident_description: Within a couple of days of using a new brand of diaper (Pampers) my five month old developed the most terrible rash I have ever seen.  Once I realized it was a result of the diapers I threw them out.  I would have to say the rash is unlike any I have ever seen.  I would say the "rash" looks more  like a chemical burn.  She actually developed blisters which began to bleed. She was in obvious pain.  We have tried all kinds of remedies and nothing has helped. I have made an appointment with her Pediatrician.  I was discussing this with a co-worker of mine and it turns out he was having the same problem and using the same type of diaper (Pampers drymax).  I began to do some research so that I may notify Pampers.  I was appalled to learn that this has already been investigated and nothing came of it.   I do not wish to "get" anything out of this.  I just do not want another baby to have to suffer like my daughter is.  I have conducted many child abuse investigations in my line of work and again I can not stress enough to you how this looks like a chemical burn and not a rash.
justification: The description details a severe chemical burn-like rash with blisters and bleeding, indicating injury (severity 3). The occurrence likelihood is unlikely (2) as it is not a common reaction but has been reported by others.

incident_description:
Sam's Club Simply Right/Member's Mark Premium Diapers size 5 

My 2 year old daughter wore them for half of a day and formed a very severe skin irritation that looks ver similar to a chemical burn. She was brought to the hospital by suggestion of her family doctor. Dr at the hospital felt it was a reaction from the diapers recommended we switch to a different brand of diapers. We have used the Simply Right/Member's Mark Premium Diapers size 2-3-4 without incident.
justification: The child suffered a severe skin irritation requiring hospital visit, indicating an injury (severity 3). The issue is rare as previous use of similar diapers had no incidents.

incident_description: When my daughter was a young infant, I would place her in the nap nanny for naps.  I purchased the nap nanny perhaps in February 2010 at a boutique store after reading about the great benefits of the nap nanny in various parenting magazines.  She slept in the nap nanny just fine as a young infant (which was always placed on the floor or on the bed with supervision) for naps and bedtime without incident.  However, when she turned four or five months old, she began partially falling out of it.  While sleeping, she would shift and the top part of her body would fall out.  So, I began placing pillows on either side so she would not hit her head on the floor or injure her neck.  After a while of just becoming too anxious about placing her in the nap nanny, I stopped using it.  Althouth we used the harness correctly every time we placed her in the nap nanny, it did not secure her from falling.  I did not know what to think or do.  After all, according to many reviews, moms loved it.  I thought it was just happening to my daughter.  I kept it because I had paid $159.99 for it and I did not want to throw it away and waste my money.  About a year later, I decided to sell it to a kid's store.  I was told that they would not buy it due to a recall, but I could donate it.  Once I was told about the nature of the recall, I refused to donate it because it was clear that what happened to my daughter occurred to other infants with worse outcomes and I did not want to donate an item knowing it could cause harm.  So, instead I googled "nap nanny recall" and learned of this site to tell my story.  I would like a refund since the item put my daughter at lethal risk everytime she was placed in it.
justification: The infant partially fell out of the nap nanny multiple times, risking head and neck injury, and the product was later recalled due to similar incidents with worse outcomes.

incident_description: We bought a babymod fixed side crib in February of 2011 made by million dollar baby. Finally when we tried to convert the crib into a toddler bed the guard rail started splintering. I am very worried about my child's safety in this crib and feel that this crib should be looked into. This crib is the Cadence model, model number W5501.
justification: The crib's structural issues and splintering pose a potential hazard, but no injury or incident has been reported yet.

I left her for a minute and a half and she tried to get something on the floor and fell out of the walker onto a hardwood laminate floor. incident_description:
The problem is with a baby gate made by Regalo, the Regalo Easy Open Super Wide Walk Thru Gate (Amazon product page here: http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B001OC5UNK). The problem is a small part that can come loose that is a choking hazard for babies. 

The gate is constructed of metal tubes. The latching mechanism is a narrow tube that retracts inside the larger tube forming the top of the gate. There is a small circular plug, about 3/8 of an inch in diameter and 3/8 of an inch long, that fits inside the interior tube.

Last week, we discovered this plug in the hand by our 10-month old baby, who was sitting next to the gate. At first we did not understand what it was or where it had come from. Then we came to believe that it had come from the baby gate, specifically that it had popped out of the gate latch. We tried putting it back in and it fit very firmly; we then didn't understand how it had come out, since it would be beyond a baby's ability. After some experimentation, we found that when the latch is pulled open in a certain way, the edge of the plug can catch on the edge of the exterior tube, popping it out easily.

We have two of these gates, and did not find the plug in the other one. The plug is the same color and appears to be the same plastic from which the various other tube caps on the gate are made. The gates do not appear to have any other problems, and we are still using them both (with the plug removed, of course.)
justification: The incident involves a choking hazard for a baby, which could lead to injury if the small part is ingested.

incident_description: I own a Stokke Sleepi crib with a recalled mattress.  In 2009 I was sent a letter by Stokke stating that the mattress had been recalled.  I followed up with the company and ordered the replacement mattress.  When the replacement mattress arrived, I threw away the old ill fitting recalled mattress and began using the replacement mattress.  The replacement mattress however was still 4 inches short of the length of the crib (crib length is 48 inches long and the mattress is 43 inches long).  This was the REPLACEMENT mattress length, not the recalled mattress length.  In 2009, I reported my concern to Stokke that the replacement mattress did not fit the crib properly and received no meaningful response other than a 1 inch gap on either side of the mattress was acceptable.  My 2-3 month old daughter would roll to the edge of the bed and did get stuck in the gap between the mattress and the crib (no injury from this incident for my daughter).  I stopped using the crib as a crib and changed to using it as a toddler bed for my oldest daughter (which solved the problem of the ill fitting crib mattress since the toddler bed used a different mattress that had no fit issues).  This September 2011, I went to set up my Stokke crib again (in the crib size configuration) and the crib mattress length again became an issue for me.  This time, I sent Stokke an email detailing the crib mattress to crib length discrepancy with photos.  They sent me a new mattress which is a different material and is the appropriate length for the crib, so my problem is solved.  I am concerned, however, for all of the other owners of Stokke Sleepi cribs who were sent too short replacement crib mattresses to replace recalled mattresses.  It seems to me that another recall needs to be made for replacement crib mattresses that Stokke sent out in 2009.  I have the replacement mattress at my home presently.  Stokke sent a fed ex label so that I could send the old mattress back to their company.
justification: The incident involved a child getting stuck in the gap but no injury occurred, fitting severity level 2. The likelihood is rated as 4 (likely) due to the recurring issue with the mattress fit.

incident_description:
I put my 4 month old daughter down to sleep with her AVENT pacifier.  She seemed to be sucking on it rather vigorously before she fell asleep at 7pm. At 10:30pm, she woke up fussing.  My husband put her pacifier back in her mouth.  She spit it out within 2 minutes (thank God) and started fussing again.  I went in to check on her and noticed that the fat part of the nipple of her pacifier was about to rip off the rest of her pacifier.  It looked as if she had almost chewed through it.  My daughter has no teeth (not even any poking through).  The pacifier had been fully intact at 7pm.  Had the pacifier not been spit out, she would have swollened and choked on the nipple in the middle of the night.

The pacificer was bought new at Babies R Us.  We have been using it for about 3 months mostly when our daughter sleeps.  She usually spits it out within an hour or 2 of falling asleep.  In the past 3 months, I've boiled the pacifier twice (5 minutes each) and put it in a [REDACTED] microwave sterilizer bag once (for 1.5 minutes).  Otherwise, I've washed the pacifier in cold water.  I've never put it in a dishwasher or washing machine.

incident_description:
purchased a baby play mat from Ikea a year ago.  It is very unsafe.

the baby playmat, I used with one of the infants I watch in my daycare and noticed when I placed her on it, that the toys that were hanging down from the arches above her on the play mat, were down too far and thus stuck above her nose and she was having a hard time breathing.  It was actually blocking her breathing due to blocking her nostrils to breath.  All the other play mats that I have purchased from other stores, the toys dangling down are raised.  the object of the play mat is to get the infant to raise their hands and play and touch the hanging toys.  

I immediately took the mat away and returned it to Ikea.  Went to the return department and told them of the incident and the man stated we have not had any other incidents.  It was a new item to the store, so how could their of been any.  I do not know if they still carry the play mat with toys hanging from soft cloth arches above, but would hate any one to gert injuried or cause death.

The reason purchased the play mat from Ikea is that it was so much more cute than the others.  

With all that being said, I went to return as stated and did  not want it, especially if I saw harm being done to an infant, due to defect.  The return cashier, asked for my receipt and I did not have it at the time, so believe it or not , could not get a refund for a very dangerous item and said I could get another one.  NO THANK  YOU!@!!!!  so I had to get a store credit.  It was only around 20.00 but it was the principle of the dangerous item and the defect of the playmat.

Now that I know this web site exsists, I will make sure I report all to help someone else.  And maybe, just maybe the companies will have to be accountable and listen to the consumer more.  I am amazed how many products are defective and or are a hazard and to return brand new items is almost impossible.

incident_description:
This incident relates to the Anatex "Deluxe Mini Playcube", which is a wooden cube that has five panels with various games to assist with the motor skills of toddlers and young children.  My son (who is almost 14 months old) received this as a birthday gift and was sitting on the floor playing with the cube.  

The cube comes assembled with the exception of one panel that must be attached with four screws.  Otherwise, the cube is fully assembled.  

We had the cube for less than two weeks when the incident occurred.  My son was playing with the "wonder gears" which is located on the side of the cube, and has six interlocking gears.  If you push one gear, the others move in synchronicity.  The gears are attached to the cube with individual screws, and have a plastic screw in the middle which covers the metal component.  Again, this came assembled and there was no instruction to tell parents that they need to assemble these particular parts.

My son had pulled on one of the gears and was able to dislodge the screw component.  When I looked down he had already placed the plastic screw component (roughly one inch in size) into his mouth.  I was able to pry open his mouth and dislodge the component before he ingested it.  However, I have no doubt that without my supervision he would have choked on the part.

The cube is a comprised of beads, screws and small blocks, in total well over 100 small parts.  The lack of solid construction on the component parts could lead to choking very easily.  As the cube was purchased on Amazon, I saw several other postings where people complained about the same lack of construction and fear that it is a choking hazard.

The box indicates that the toy is for age 2 and up, and has a small warning lable indicating that the UNASSEMBLED parts could lead to a potential choking issue if not assembled correctly.  

While my son is a few months short of two years of age, this hazard exists with ASSEMBLED parts and I have no doubt that a two year old could potentially suffer the same fate.  Again, this toy was less than two weeks old, barely used and for my twenty three pound son to have the strength to pull off the assembled component parts means that this has shoddy construction.

Please protect other consumers from what I almost experienced with my son.
justification: The child nearly choked on a small part, indicating a clear hazard, but no actual injury occurred due to immediate intervention.

On another of the sides there are 3 columns of triangular blocks containing halves of different animals to be matched up.  There is enough room between the columns for my sons arm to fit in and again when he tried to remove his arm the blocks rotated and pinched and trapped his arm.

incident_description: Our 8 Month old was playing with the little sunshine wabble toy that came as an attachment to the Baby Einstein Musical Motion Jumper. incident_description: We just received this potty seat in the mail.  My 19 month old daughter was investigating it.  She was practicing sitting on and off of it, and occasionally she would turn it upside down.  I would then return it right side up. My daughter held on to the rim to sit down, and her middle finger on the right hand went into this gap.  When she sat down all her weight was pressed onto the finger that was stuck in the gap and she started screaming.  I had no idea what happened until I saw the tip of her finger turning purple.  We put ice on it and it is now okay.  I am afraid that had I not been right there, her fingertip could have been lacerated or amputated from her own weight. I know this is not a toy but part of potty training would require her familiarizing herself with and being comfortable with her potty seat, and now I have reservations about letting her use this one despite her infatuation with Elmo.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that her 13 month old grandchild consistently gets themselves caught in the slats of their full sized stationery crib. Usually when the child leg gets the stuck the consumer daughter in law will hear the child cry and remove the child's leg from the slat. The consumer stated that last month her daughter in law had to call a neighbor to use oil to get the infant's leg out of the slats. This has happened on 3 occasions. This occurred twice in August and in May. They only had to use the oil once in August. 

On the last occasion, her grandchild's right knee was caught in a fashion that was difficult for the consumer to remove but the child was not injured. The consumer did not call the ambulance to get her child leg from the slat at any time. The consumer has yet to call the off to make them aware of the entrapment hazard. The child sustained bruises on each occasion. The consumer has not called the retailer or the firm. 

The consumer's grandchild weighs 20 pounds roughly. The child does not have any scratches. The crib has no signs of structural damage. The crib has not damaged the consumer's home. The crib has a coil mattress. The consumer did not take her child to the doctor. The consumer was informed by an employee of the CPSC to call to register a report. The consumer has seen numerous recalls by this for other cribs no including this one in particular. Ordinarily, when the child gets his leg caught the consumer is alone in their crib.
justification: The child sustained bruises on each occasion, indicating minor injuries, and the incident has occurred multiple times.

incident_description:
My 8 month old son was using an Avent (Phillips) pacifier early that morning.  I suddenly heard him cough as if he had something in his mouth.  I turned to see if he was ok and noticed a small piece of plastic on his chest.  After taking a closer look, I determined that a piece of plastic had broken off his pacifier, and must have ended up in his mouth.  The broken piece was the center section of the handle.  There is a clean break in 2 locations, leading me to believe a manufacturing defect in this component.  Aside from the obvious CHOKING HAZARD GENERATED BY THE SMALL PART, the edges where the plastic severed is very sharp and could have cut his skin.  We now have numerous Avent products, including pacifiers, nipples, teethers, and bottles that we are uncomfortable using.  These goods cost us well over $100 and will need to be discarded and replaced for my wife and I to feel our child is safe during use.

My son could have been severely injured, or even worse could have died if were not close by.  I am concerned for other children using these products.  I feel they are unsafe; something needs to be done by the manufacturer to rectify this, and potentially many other situations.
justification: The incident involved a choking hazard and sharp edges, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: Last Friday on 9/16/11, My 4 month old daughter was playing on the floor. She had a rattle and her pacifier which she likes to play with also by pulling it out of her mouth and putting it back in. She has chewed on the sides of of the pacifier before and would put the pacifier in sideways but just enough to chew on the end of the mouth piece, the nipple and mouth piece are suppose to be not to able to allow it to go any further than that. I was on the couch and got up to change her diaper, she wasn't making any noise so I looked up at her as I often do anyways. When I looked up i saw my child's face bright red and the pacifier completely wedged/jammed into her mouth. There was not one part of this pacifier even remotely close to being out of her mouth, the whole entire thing completely wedged in there!! I panicked and attempted to remove the pacifier, to my shock it didn't budge. I then had to rip the pacifier with a good amount of force to get get it out of her mouth. She made no noise for about 8 seconds and began screaming crying hysterically. I held her close and wanted to see if her mouth was okay. The roof of her mouth was bright red, scratched, and swollen. My Daughter was not breathing while the pacifier was jammed in her mouth, she would have died had I not been there. She was using this pacifier the same way every other child does, teaching herself how to put it in and out of her mouth, sucking on it, nothing out of the ordinary. She should not have been able to do what she did.
justification: The child suffered a serious injury with the pacifier jammed in her mouth, causing swelling and scratches, and could have died without intervention.

incident_description:
On September 26, 2011, at approximately 7:45 p.m., our 15 year old daughter yelled from the basement, "There's a fire in the bathroom.".  My wife ran downstairs and saw that the plug in night light in our basement bathroom had an approximately three inch flame shooting up, there was smoke, and there were smoke marks on the walls.  My wife grabbed a hand towel and slapped the flames and then blew out the flame.  

I got downstairs to see the nightlight black, charred and slightly melted.  Black marks from the smoke were on the bathroom wall above the outlet.  The bathroom, and the basement smelled like smoke. The cap to the night light was on the bathroom floor, with the edges black.

We asked my daughter if she knew what happened. My daughter had been doing homework on our computer in the basement family room, when she said that she heard a "pop", which sounded like a light bulb had been dropped, so she looked in the bathroom, and she saw the flames coming from the night light.

After the excitement died down, I removed the night light from the outlet, and I took the cover plate off the outlet.  There was no sign of smoke or fire of any kind or type on the outlet or inside the box.

The night light is a plug in type AmerTac Model 71352.  We have the night light and cap in a plastic bag at home
justification: The incident involved a fire from a night light but was quickly extinguished without injury or significant damage.

incident_description: My 11 month old son has been using the "Sassy Buzz N Bite Gentle Vibrating Teether" for a few months. These bumps are not meant to come off and I'm glad I had noticed it before it had been bitten off and possibly swallowed or chocked on. I also sent an email to Sassy to report this problem.

incident_description: My daughter has always used Pampers diapers from birth swaddlers and then cruisers, she is now in a size 4 pampers cruisers.  About 4 months ago she started getting rashes on her bottom and above her private area.  Diaper rash creams would not work and it kept getting worse, It became big marks like burns and was red and she would try to scratch it constantly.  I took her to her dr who told me he didn't know what it was maybe just really dry skin and try not to bathe her as often because the water could irritate it.  Well I tried that and it still didn't work and the rash began to look like it was only where her diaper covered she even had burn like marks on the sides of her hips where the diaper wraps around.  At her one year check up in august I asked the dr again and he suggested [REDACTED], I put it on her and it would help clear it almost up and then it would flair up again worse.  Looking back now I think the [REDACTED] of working like a barrier between her skin and the diaper.  Finally this morning she didn't sleep well last night and when she got up this morning there was blood in her diaper....it was so bad she had scratched it so bad there were big bloody scratches on her butt along with all of the big whelps from the rash.  I researched it on the internet and saw there had been some problems with pampers because of a change they had made.  I am definately buying her some different diapers today but I am so glad we found out what the problem was finally.  Is there anyway I can reach Pampers to let them know how disaapointed I am?

incident_description: My daughter developed a severe diaper rash that very much resembled a chemical burn shortly after Pampers came out with their new Dry Max technology.  She was using the Swaddler's version at the time.  I typically don't use wipes, only water and dry thoroughly, so I knew it had nothing to do with that.  I never left her in wet/soiled diapers for prolonged periods, and her diet did not change at the time.  I reported this to Pampers, as some of my friends experienced similar problems with their children, and Pampers denied any correlation of their new product to my daughter's rash.  I stopped using the brand, but gave the company the benefit of a doubt.  However, recently, I purchased the Pampers Cruiser's version for her.  She is now 2 years old.  I experienced the same thing!  She has a horrible rash.  She scratched it until it bled.  Woke up in the middle of the night screaming in pain.  I am taking her to the pediatrician this afternoon.  I don't know what else could have caused the rash, other than chemical burn from the diaper "technology".

incident_description: i had followed the installation instructions to a "T". so when it came time for the baby and i to leave the hospital,([redacted]) i found my baby was scrunched and turned blue! because the support slid no matter what. i hurried and told my husband to turn back around ( we hadn't even left the parking lot) while i was giving infant CPR and he was quickly admitted to the E.R. where they called the NICU to handle the situation. after days in the NICU, after many grueling tests, in which they found nothing wrong. the nurses gave him what is called a "car seat challenge" they found that he did fine in his carseat, the neonatologist entered the room and quickly told us that it's sad that so many stores carry these items "which shouldn't even be in production" but if it is Not built into the carseat, DO NOT PUT ANYTHING IN IT! because of this product, our newborn son was admitted to the NICU for a week and racked up $22,000 in bills. all of you new parents heed the warning that Dr's told me "Steer clear of these products" for your child's safety and your emotional sake!

incident_description: I have used pampers baby dry diapers for nearly 10 months for my daughter and before that for two years for my son. I have occasionally tried a different brand or pampers line but always went back to baby dry. Just over a week ago my mother in law bought a box of diapers for us and she picked up the new pampers cruisers with dry max. I tried them out on my daughter later the next day and within the first diaper change she had a rash. She has only had a rash twice since she was born and not nearly as bad. At first I thought maybe it was food related, but I couldn't think of anything new she had eaten. By her next diaper change we were out of the house and it was getting worse but I had our usual pampers baby dry diapers in the diaper bag, I used that by the time we got home her rash was already looking better. I changed her again for bed with a baby dry diaper from her bag and by morning she was clear. Since then any time we used the pampers cruisers she had a rash by her next change so I switched back to the Pampers baby dry.  She was clear for a couple of days after that. Today my husband had her for several hours while I helped my friend look for her wedding gown. He used the pampers cruisers on her while I was gone and she has the worst rash ever. She hasn't had any new foods, drinks, medicine, etc, and she has never been prone to rashes. There is no doubt in my mind now that the new diapers are the cause, and we are officially switching back and throwing the rest of the cruisers out.

incident_description:
I have a new Eddie Bauer edition high chair purchased from Target in May 2011. 
http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B003A4CUZQ

My son is 9 months old as of this incident. There is a design flaw, the plastic piece that is a permanent, unmovable part has a gap just big enough for baby's foot to get jammed in and risk damage. Even while buckled in, baby can try to stand up and then when he sits back down, or even while trying to put the baby in seat initially, a foot can get wedged in, and the knee gets trapped under the tray and binds up the leg. I became very concerned that his leg might get broken or dislocated in the attempt to dislodge him after he got his foot stuck, it was all contorted in that space that really should not be there. It should not have a gap, the center crotch piece should go from the seat to the tray. This is dangerous!

On a side note, this rather expensive model features straps that do not buckle very well and are positioned ineffectively. Additionally, after less than six months use, the chair is wobbly and feels like it is coming apart. Attempts to tighten screws/bolt were unsuccessful in eliminating the instability of the chair.
justification: The description indicates a design flaw that could lead to injury, but no actual injury is reported.

incident_description: My son's Graco Pack n' Play caught on fire on September 12, 2011.  Thankfully he was NOT in it and no one was hurt!  A light bulb in the room blew and it appears that the shattered glass was hot enough to cause ignition and or maybe it sparked.  I contacted Graco and they informed me the following: "The foam in the mattress of all pack n' plays are fire retardant and meet the Federal Flammability Standards".  Then I asked about the Graco Playard Sheets, which we use to protect the mattress on the Pack'N Play, and Graco informed me that these sheet are NOT fire retardant.  It is my believe that the the Graco Playard Sheets are flammable.  There is a bed with sheets on it in the same room, next to the Pack'N Play, under the light bulb that blew, and it did not catch on fire.  The only thing in the room that caught on fire was the Pack'N Play.  Thankfully my son was not in it at the time the incident occurred.  The Graco Playard Sheets need to be inspected to prevent future recurrence and or a tragedy.
justification: The incident involved a fire but no injuries or deaths occurred, and the likelihood of recurrence is considered possible given the specific circumstances described.

incident_description:
I Purchased the Baby Eienstein Mucial Motion Activity Jumper.  I called the Baby Einstein in late July concerning the Musical Motion Activity Jumper that I have.  One of the anchors kept coming out of the unit and was a choking hazard for my son.  In addition, I later found when adjusting the level on the unit, very small plastic pieces from the red ball broke off and posed a potential ingestion hazard for my son.  

I was transferred from Baby Einstein to the manufacturer, who wanted to send me new parts.  I expressed my concern over the anchors and how exactly getting a new one would correct the problem as it seemed the anchor was just too small to lock into place.  I was then advised by the representative that this was a "known issue" and that they had redesigned them a few months back to correct the problem.  I was very upset by this and asked if there was a recall because I frequently check for recalls and never saw anything about this product.  She advised me it was "not" recalled.  I then became very upset and was crying and expressed to her that I felt this was extremly irresponsible of them and Disney for knowingly having a potential choking hazard with a product and not alerting consumers.  I found my son on 2 occassions with the anchor in his mouth before I took the anchor away completely.  What if he had choked on it before I saw him and then to know that Disney knew all along that it could happen?  I was just disgusted and saddened.  The representative asked me if I still wanted her to send the parts and I advised her that I did not want the parts as I had no way of knowing if there were other issues with this product and did not feel as though the company would be responsible enough in the future to properly recall items that are a potential danger to children.  I told her that I would probably just throw the whole thing out. She then advised me that she would speak to her supervisor and get back with me.  As of today, more than a month later I have heard nothing which only upsets me more.  

How could Disney, be so irresponsible?  It is the responsible of the manufactuer to take proper precautions when manufacturing a product.  It is their responsiblity to make the safety of toys for children a number one priority and by not being proactive when there is a known potential hazard, a potential "life threatening" hazard, that is just inexcusable to me.  

I hope that you consider administering a recall at this point as it would be truly heartbreaking to hear on the news one day of someone's child who is loved more than anything in the world by his/her parents and has not yet even learned to walk is taken from them due to choking on a piece of product that was known to be a hazard but felt that the company's bottom dollar was more important than the life of an innocent child who doesn't know yet to keep things out of his mouth.  
 
You may contact me via e-mail or you may call me at [redacted]
justification: The incident involves a known choking hazard with small plastic pieces breaking off, posing a potential ingestion risk, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description:

incident_description: My nephew who is 8 months old was swinging in the baby swing which is a Kolcraft Sesame Street Adjustable swing at my house when he leaned over because he dropped his toy and he flipped forward & the fabric which the seat belt is attached to unlatched it's self from the swing and the seatbelt was still attached to him but it caused him to and hit his face on the floor and he has a big knot & bruise on his head.

incident_description: We had two nightlights in our children's bedroom and one had a backpack that had accidently fallen down onto it. It became extremely hot and melted the plastic around the bulb as well as the backpack itself. We forgot we had another one in the room that was the same model and last night my daughter realized that her stuffed bear was up against it. Again, the bear was extremely hot and the plastic is molded around the bulb of the nighlight. The maker of the nightlight is AmerTac and the model # is 71055A. I am very concerned in both cases that a fire could have been started had we not found them when we did.
justification: The incident involved overheating and melting but no actual fire or injury occurred, indicating a moderate likelihood of recurrence with current usage.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that her daughter's crib poses a potential choking hazard to her daughter as the wood from the frame dethatches very easily. The consumer's daughter of 15 months has been removing the wooden frame the inside of her crib and ingesting the wooden segments. The consumer stated that she removed a segment as large as the size of her pinkie finger. The consumer made initial contact about this with retailer on July 11, 2011 and referred her to get in contact with the firm. 

The consumer made contact with the firm that same day but was told by the firm's rep that she needed to contact her via email and show her a picture of the crib. The consumer made email contact with the firm via email July 13th, 2011, who responded July 21, 2011 and was told that the wood was safe for lead ingestion and the finish was safe offered no further guidance.

 The consumer stated that the product has resulted in no injuries of lacerations to her daughter's mouth or gums. The consumer consulted with her daughter's pediatrician on the next day over the phone and told her the product was indeed not safe.
justification: The incident involves ingestion of wooden segments by a child, posing a choking hazard, but no injuries or lacerations were reported.

incident_description: My daughter was sitting in her Fisher-Price My Little Snug-a-bunny bouncer seat when I noticed her foot was bleeding, she was crying at this time.  She had been sitting, strapped into the seat, her feet were kicking, as normal 2 month old children do.  The bouncer seat was covered in blood as was her blankets and foot.  Upon investigation of the product I noticed a lip section that is right under the lining of the product on the vibrating controls housing unit.  It was bloody as well.  My daughter has a cut on the back of her heel that continued to bleed well into the evening.
justification: The incident resulted in a bleeding injury to the child's foot, which aligns with severity level 3.

incident_description: The consumer stated that her bassinet is a potential safety hazard as the locking mechanism on the bassinet does not function properly. The consumer stated that her 3 day old daughter was in the bassinet while the consumer was sleeping and woke to find her daughter was out of the bassinet as it had tipped over to the right. The consumer stated that her daughter was not injured by the product. The consumer did some research online and found that her product was not on recall. The consumer has yet to call the manufacturer or the firm. The product doesn't appear to show any signs of breaking but does still an issue with the locking mechanism located on the bottom of the bassinet towards the back. The locking mechanism is a lever.
justification: The bassinet tipped over but the infant was not injured, indicating an incident without injury.

incident_description: Child's arm became stuck between crib rails on side of crib.  I was able to remove arm from being stuck by pulling the child's skin taut and sliding out.
justification: The child's arm was stuck but was freed without injury, indicating an incident with no injury.

incident_description: I previously used Pampers Cruisers diapers for my 19 month old son.  I recently tried the New Pampers Cruisers and both times he ended up with a red, sore diaper rash after wearing the diapers.  I saw online that others had reported similar incidents.

incident_description:
Caller put her 23 month old baby boy down for his nap but heard him crying as if he was in pain.
She went to his room and found him with his left arm stuck at the elbow area.
Baby was standing up, at the head, his arm was stuck at the headboard where design of headboard is perpendicular to slats. 
She went to him and was able to wiggle his arm around and free him easily but his elbow was red and bruised at the bony area.

She called manufacturer June 14, no answer.
She called manufacture June 15,  spoke with [REDACTED] who told her the baby is too large to be sleeping in a crib.
23 month old baby weighs 22lb & is 32 inches tall.
She asked to speak with a manager who was not available at that time.

Supervisor named [REDACTED] representing manufacturer called her June 15, 2011 and demension are within regulation, that it was fairly common for them to receive reports of arms & legs stuck in slats but not in head board area.
Caller believes this to be a danger and would like this CPSC to be alerted to this issue.
justification: The baby suffered a bruised elbow, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The manufacturer indicated that limb entrapment is fairly common, suggesting a likelihood of 4 (likely).

incident_description: My two year old was standing next to her high chair and grabbed at the buckle/strap.  The buckle and a small piece of strap came off in her hand.
justification: The child was not injured, but a piece of the high chair broke off, which qualifies as an incident.

incident_description: A 3-month-old infant was placed in the bassinet attachment of a Graco Pack 'N' Play to sleep.  The attachment somehow became unhinged by 1 or 2 of the hooks and was at an angled decline.  The infant reportedly slid down the decline and her face was adjacent to the mesh webbing of the side wall.  The infant was found dead in this position.
justification: The incident resulted in the death of an infant, which is the highest severity level. The occurrence likelihood is rated as unlikely (2) based on the rarity of such fatal incidents.

Consumer feels that these cribs should be investigated and revised that the slats does not pose a risk for children getting their body parts stuck.

She says it came right off in several places.  The consumer says it is similar to the recalled dropside crib, but it does not have a dropside.

incident_description: My seven month old granddaughter was properly seated and buckled into the COSCO Flat Fold High Chair. She managed to get her left foot wedged under the bar beneath the tray and up against the fabric on the left side of the seat.  She was caught in this position for several minutes until I could remove the tray to see how to safely extricate her foot which was caught at the ankle.
