She sustained minor abrasions, redness and bruising to her ankle from struggling.
justification: The child sustained minor injuries (abrasions, redness, bruising) from being trapped, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is possible (3) as such incidents can occur with improper use or design flaws.

incident_description: I recently purchased Pampers Easy Ups for my 3 year old daughter. After wearing them for 1 day she has a very bad chemical burn on her buttocks and her genitals. I took her to her pediatrician today and she confirmed that it was a burn and not a diaper rash. I have tried diaper cremes, baking soda baths, and [REDACTED]. She has not worn the Easy ups in 2 days and still has a terrible burn.
justification: The child suffered a chemical burn confirmed by a pediatrician, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
My 11 month old son developed a rash all over his diaper area.  After having this rash for 10 days, we took him to our Pediatrician, [REDACTED] who runs a practice in Philadelphia, PA called [REDACTED].  Several of the Dr.'s in the practice came into the exam room to look at the rash and none of them could identify what the rash could have been caused by.  They suggested we try Triple Cream and bring him back if we saw no improvement.  A week later, we brought him back as there was no improvement.  The Dr. did a rapid strep test which came back negative.  Without a diagnosis, the Dr. suggested we try 1% cortisone cream.  We still saw no improvement.   Several days later, I recalled hearing about other children with a similar problem while using Pampers so I switched diapers.  Within 48 hours, the rash was almost gone.  We had a dermatology appointment scheduled for today and the Dermatologist suggested we report this problem to Pampers and the CPSC.

Please let me know if you have any questions.  It would be great to know you have read this report.
justification: The incident involved a rash that required medical attention but did not result in serious injury or death.

incident_description: My son was sitting in the Chicco D@nce Walker and Electronic Play Tray (listed on the registration card as the DJ Baby Walker, manufactured 2010-12-01). He was biting the edge of the Electronic Play Tray (only natural for a baby). I heard him cry out in pain, rushed over to him, and saw that his mouth had blood in it. I cleaned the blood out of his mouth and found a cut on his lower gum. The bleeding stopped after I applied pressure to the wound for approximately 30 seconds. My son did not require medical attention; however, he very well could have if I had not removed him from the walker immediately as he continued to bite the Electronic Play Tray even after crying out in pain. The wound appears to be causing him mild discomfort several hours after the incident. The walker was purchased at Buy Buy Baby in Downers Grove, IL, on August 20, 2011.
justification: The incident resulted in a cut on the baby's gum, causing pain and bleeding, which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is possible (3) as babies commonly bite objects, but injuries of this nature are not frequent.

incident_description: I have a 9month old baby and he was enjoying his Fisher Price "Luv U Zoo Jumperoo", product #V0206, as he always does since we bought this bouncer when he was 5months old. As any responsible parent, when I built this I did it following the instructions and making sure everything was right in its place. And today I found out that Fisher Price forgot to remind me to take out a small but very dangerous plastic sheet that was on the bouncer or that the piece that came off gets defective after being use. Thanks to God nothing major happened, but our baby scare me and my wife in a way I never thought would happen. This product has a mirror in it and that mirror had a very thin protective plastic sheet that until today it looked as part of the mirror. Of course my curious baby found out the wrong way that the plastic sheet did indeed was supposed to come off. All this in front of my wife, who didn't knew what was happening until she saw our boy coughing and putting his finger on his mouth like he was trying to get something out. We tried to figure out what's going on when he starts throwing up and we thought it was a natural reaction to putting his finger down his throat, but he kept coughing and throwing up more and that's when we realize there's something wrong. All this happens in less than 20 seconds, so we take him in our arms to see what's going on when I see a piece of plastic coming out of his mouth and quickly use my fingers to take it out. We couldn't believe what has just happened, our baby was on what we thought was one of the safest place he could be, but he had manage to grab something he shouldn't and almost choke with it. As we start asking ourselves how did that happened, I took a good look at what has just come out of my baby's mouth just to realize that it had always been there since day 1. The mirror on the bouncer had it all the time. I think I recall taking off a protective plastic from that mirror when I build the bouncer. That one I think had a red line indicating that there's was something there that needed to come off before a baby could use it. The one my baby almost swallow is a perfect circle, transparent, clear. That's why I'm reporting this. The bouncer's mirror is not safe and it's plastic coating comes off after being use for a while creating an extremely dangerous choking hazard for babies.
justification: The baby choked on a plastic sheet, causing vomiting and distress, but no lasting injury. The incident suggests a likely recurrence due to the product's design flaw.

incident_description:
Fisher Price Space Saver High Chair

My 11 month old son managed to get his arm stuck between the base of the high chair and the adjustable bar that holds the tray.  His arm was twisted so that it was pinned almost behind his back at a very awkward angle. It took two adults to remove him in a way that would not cause further injury.  We had to remove the tray, re-adjust the bar, and very carefully pull his arm out at the same time we pulled his entire body out of the chair.  We could not remove his arm with him still sitting because of the angle at which he was stuck.   Once removed he immediately calmed down and does not appear to have any visible lasting injuries. If he had thrashed more he could have caused himself more serious injuries. He was screaming and obviously in pain while stuck.  We made a report with Fisher-Price the same day  (8-19-11) and will be shipping the chair back to them for inspection.  They volunteered that no other accidents with this chair have been reported to them.  However, I found an almost identical report on this website from this past April.  Perhaps it was never filed with Fisher Price?
justification: The child was in pain and could have been injured more seriously if he had thrashed, but no lasting injuries were reported.

justification: The incident involved a toy being torn apart, but there was no injury reported.

incident_description: My daughter, born [REDACTED], was the first. From the time she was born, the hospital provided us with Pampers to use to diaper her. When she was about 2 weeks old she began to have persistent diaper rashes for which we took her to the doctor for. The doctor recommended ointment and more frequent diaper changes. The diaper rashes persisted for about 4 more weeks, with the doctor recommending everything from warm washclothes instead of wipes, letting her go diaperless for short periods during the day, formula changes, corn starch, etc. Painstakingly, it slowly cleared up. The doctor this time had us change diaper brands suspecting that our son was not adjusting to the diapers well. Neither child has any kind of allergies that would have cause these rashes.

justification: The incident resulted in slight bruising and has happened several times, indicating a likelihood of recurrence and potential for more serious injury.

incident_description:
Our 1 year old obtained a diaper rash after our testing of Huggies Snug and Dry. It would appear it has  "leak lock" a technology similar to the [REDACTED] that received similar complaints earlier this year. 

We have used 'original' [REDACTED]- since she was born. She has NEVER had a diaper rash. We were only 10 diapers into this first time trial of Huggies and found her ripping and pulling at her diaper. Clearly uncomfortable and upset by her diaper, we changed her to discover a horrible rash. We immediately switched back to [REDACTED] this afternoon and have been applying medication every hour. The rash appears to be improving - but is still bad enough to awaken her from her sleep. 

We searched online to see if anyone had a similar experience and were horrified to learn of many children experiencing the same.

While I understand the CPSC has not identified a root cause in the [REDACTED] case, I promise you that the only thing we've done differently with our daughter in the past 24 hours is change the brand of diapers. We bought it because the character on them is Mickey Mouse. Having just returned from a Disney trip, her brother thought they were 'cute'. 

I must repeat, this child has never had a diaper rash. We are diligent about changes and baths. Our first born was exactly the same. To see her in this level of discomfort as a result to a diaper is inexcusable. Huggies, and [REDACTED], are well aware that this 'leak lock" technology is generating a horrible reaction for many children. They should not be allowed to keep it on the market.

Please force these diaper brands to pull this technology from their products. They are hurting defenseless kids.
justification: The incident describes a diaper rash causing discomfort and sleep disruption, indicating an injury (severity 3). Online reports suggest this is a recurring issue, making occurrence likely (4).

incident_description:
My 16 MOnth old daughter has had a sevre Diaper rash since Christmas 2010..I had been to many physcians and they kept giving her cream after cream.. We all thought it was something she was eating or allergic to, or really just plain old teething... They dry max diapers were great. I would say the best however The quater size open sores and blood coming from these sores and the tears and pain she has endured is not a result of anything else than the chemcial BURNs she has recieved from using Pampers Dry Max... I just found out about this Monday June 13 2011 and It is now Wednesday June 15 and I already see results in healing...

To think that pampers would even do this to a small defenceless child is appauling! There better be some answers and some sort of compensations for all these children who have had to experience this!
justification: The description details severe diaper rash with open sores and bleeding, indicating injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is set to 4 (likely) based on the mention of multiple similar cases.

incident_description: This afternoon, my ten month old daughter's caretaker gave her a short (4 oz in a 5 oz bottle) glass Born-free bottle.  We've been  using both the Born-Free glass and plastic bottles sporadically since she was first born and exclusively since six months without problem.  My daughter took ahold of the top nipple part of the bottle because we are teaching her to feed herself and she gave the bottle a good clunk on the floor.  That glass bottle shattered right in front of her, not broke into large pieces, but shattered.  Fortunately her caretaker was quick enough to get her out of the way but not before her little foot was cut by the glass.  I am so angry.  Anything could have happened.  Those bottles should be built to withstand a baby playing with them.
justification: The incident resulted in a cut on the baby's foot, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). Given the nature of glass bottles and baby handling, such occurrences are possible (likelihood 3).

Recently we unpacked the box because we are a few weeks away from having a second baby. incident_description:
My daughter developed a burned look to her buttocks, genitals, and her hips.  Prior to that day, we had been using both Pampers and [REDACTED], as we had received both as gifts.  However, the day before I noticed the burned look, I had run out of [REDACTED] and only had Pampers on hand.

After doing some research on the advice of a friend, I quit using the Pampers and went exclusively to the [REDACTED].  Her burned looking skin cleared up within a couple hours.

incident_description: I purchased "Diego" Pamper pull-ups from Targe for my 2 year old.  After putting the first pull-up on him, I noticed his private was become swollen.  His private area turned bright read and appeared like it was rubbed raw and about to begin bleeding.  When I changed his first diaper I handed the diaper to my sister to throw away and she took it from me and threw it in the trash.  The next morning she complained to me that her fingers had become red and swollen.  After suspecting the diapers, my nanny ran two fingers on the inside of the pull-up to feel the material. incident_description: My son experienced blister-like burns in varying sizes on his bottom from the Pampers Swaddlers diapers with Dry Max.  I received many packages of diapers when my son was born because he is my second.  One afternoon a couple of weeks ago, my daycare phoned me to let me know my son had 'blisters' on his bottom. That incident happened near the end of a week and at home we were using a different brand of diapers.  His bottom healed.  However, this week, I sent him with another package of the Pampers Dry Max diapers to daycare.  And yesterday (Friday) the blisters appeared again.  The blisters are not like diaper rash.  I have been looking online to find what could cause the issue and was led to many individuals who have experienced the same incident when using these diapers.  No child should have to suffer blisters and it is a shame that parents trust in the Pampers brand.  And for Pampers to not see validity in the numbers of complaints is upsetting.  I will no longer purchase their products.

Safely concern:  Top of stair gate, Evenflo  Model 1556C  (Aug/08)

http://www.evenflo.com/product.aspx?id=75&pfid=114

The gate itself is sturdy wood, however the hinges and locking hardware are poor-quality plastic.  The hinges have been replaced once because they cracked, we were several day with out a gate, while waiting for parts, now we inspect them regularly & my husband just noticed they are sagging like they are going to break again soon.

My son, putting his feet under the gate, knocked it completely off; the gate crashed down the stairs. Luckily he somehow didn't fall with it.

Now we have found the locking mechanism is so poor that our dog opens it with its nose.  If a dog can open, certainly a toddler can.
justification: The gate has multiple safety issues, including broken hinges and a weak locking mechanism, which led to an incident where the gate fell down the stairs but luckily no one was injured.

incident_description:
To Whom It May Concern:

In June 2010, while 5 months pregnant, I purchased the Baby Trend Butterfly Nursery Center (item number PY8191). I intended to use the Nursery Center as a bassinet for the first four months of my childÃÂs life and then to use it as a playpen when my child started to crawl. I carefully looked the item over and was satisfied with how the product seemed to be made. I also understood at the time that there was a limited warranty on the item.
I gave birth to my child [REDACTED] and used the bassinet for the first four months as I originally intended. After the time frame mentioned I carefully put the item away in its carry case and stored it safely until I would use it again. In May I got rid of the receipt because I was not having any issues with the item and did not anticipate any occurring. In June my child started to crawl and I again pulled the item out to use it as a playpen. July 7th I noticed that the stitching on the item started to come undone. The enclosed pictures show the areas where the stitching was coming undone. Upon examination of the item it was clear that it had not been snagged on any other item nor was there anything but faulty stitching involved in the malfunction of the item.
I contacted the Baby Trend Company and after several conversations they were willing to fix the item and ship it back to me, but I would need to pay to send it to them. They re-iterated that there was a 6 month warranty on the item and told me that I should have carefully looked the item over when I purchased it.
I am writing this letter because I have several concerns with this item and with my interaction with the company. My first and greatest concern is, as you can see from the picture, that the hole along the stitching is large enough that my child could have fit her head through the hole and been unable to get it back through, thus choking to death. I do not want the company to re-stitch the item because I am concerned that this would happen again. I feel like this needs to be looked into because this could cause harm to a child. My second issue with this situation is the warranty on the item. There is only a 6 month warranty on the item but the only way that this issue would have been noticed is for something to be placed in the bottom of the playpen in order to put weight on the stitches to show how poorly made the item was. As in my case, most people would not put their child in the bottom of the playpen until the child is crawling, which is usually not until 6 or 7 months, thus the warranty is already void by the time this issue would arise. It seems as if the company wants to ensure that they would not have to replace an item not well made or to cause the customer to pay more money later on a faulty item. I am a mother that will not put my child back into a faulty playpen, but there are other mothers who would find the cost of fixing this item too great and would put their child back in playpen, thus endangering their child.
I am asking that CPSC look into the quality of this item to ensure that this item does not endanger a life of a child. This company needs to be held accountable for the items that they make.
justification: The incident describes a product defect that could potentially cause harm, but no actual injury or death occurred.

If a family had bought these and took them home to their kids like we did that didn't have smoke detectors that can detect carbon monoxide, I am afraid to think what damage these fumes might have done to them and their children in a closed environment. As grandparents who want to keep a toddler out of non-childproof areas, this product did not work for us and we would not recommend it to others.

By [REDACTED] "[REDACTED]" (ELMHURST, IL USA) - See all my reviews

WE USED TWO OF THESE GATES IN OUR HOME FOR APPROXIMATELY 2 WEEKS UNTIL ONE DAY MY NINE MONTH-OLD DAUGHTER SCOOTED OVER AND LIFTED THE FOOTPETAL - THUS ALLOWING THE GATE TO SWING WIDE OPEN. I CONTACTED THE MANUFACTURER VIA BOTH PHONE AND EMAIL AND THEIR ANSWER WAS "THE FOOT PEDAL SHOULD SNAP INTO PLACE...A NINE MONTH OLD SHOULD NOT BE ABLE TO OPEN IT". NO KIDDING! THE MANUFACTURER THEN TOLD US TO TAKE A HAMMER AND BREAK OFF THE BASE THAT THE PEDAL MOUNTS TO SO I CAN MAIL IT TO THEM (AT MY COST) FOR FURTHER INSPECTION. THAT IS THE MOST RIDICULOUS THING I'VE EVER HEARD IN MY LIFE! INSTEAD, I BROUGHT BOTH GATES TO THE RETAIL CHAIN THEY WERE PURCHASED FROM AND SHOWED THEM THE PROBLEM - THEY AGREED THAT THERE WAS A DEFECT AND GAVE ME TWO NEW GATES FROM A DIFFERENT MANUFACTURER THAT WE LOVE. I WOULD NOT RECOMMEND THIS PRODUCT TO ANYONE WITH CHILDREN. IT MIGHT BE GREAT FOR DOGS BUT I REGISTERED AT BABIES R US, NOT PETCO.

incident_description: On May 24th 2011 I purchased a Dream On Me 3-in-one portable crib off of amazon.com which shipped from CSN stores. It arrived damaged on June 4th and I contacted CSN stores who then shipped me a replacement crib. On June 17th 2011 I opened the box containing the new crib and it too had surface damage (nicks in the wood) but I decided to keep it as I needed a crib and wasn't going to keep waiting for new ones to ship! I pulled out the first piece, which is partially assembled, and it fell apart. The 2 pieces had been glued together but not enough glue was used apparently. So, I had wood glue and glued the pieces together myself. They fit together well so I wasn't concerned. I assembled the entire crib and used it for less than 1 week with a 13 mth old child who weighs less than 20 lbs. He is a typical baby and when he was awake from his nap he was holding onto the side of the crib and bouncing up and down. I entered the room to get him when suddenly the crib shifted and a corner of the crib sunk down. The locking caster in the front of the crib snapped! This compromised the safety of the crib and the child! I contacted the CSN store as well as the manufacturer. CSN ordered a new caster, Dream on Me has yet to reply. I am very concerned about the safety of this crib! I have read many disturbing reviews on line now about this crib and feel that it needs attention. This crib does not feel well-built. This caster breaking should never have happened and I am left wondering what is next! I do have photos if they are needed or desired.
justification: The crib's structural failure compromised safety but no injury occurred.

incident_description:

This happened to my 9 month old in 2009.  I contacted Ikea but was told there was nothing they could do. I bought 2 of these chairs and both had unsafe seatbelts.

incident_description: i purchased a Graco Lauren Classic Crib in Expresso (4 in 1 crib) last year at target. We just recently started putting our one year old son in his crib. we have noticed that this crib seems to have the wooden slats/ vertical bars too far apart and my son's extremities seem to get stuck in them while he is sleeping. incident_description: We purchased a crib from a consignment shop that I learned, upon returning home, had been recalled.  It is the Simplicity Ellis Crib, recalled for the structurally poor metal tubular mattress support railings.  The store owner wanted to argue that the crib was not included in the recall.  We showed her the information on the cpsc.gov website regarding the crib, but she still denied that the crib was included in the recall.  While she reluctantly refunded our money, her major concern was that she would lose money on this item.  I am concerned that this crib may be resold to another uninformed consumer, as we never removed the crib from the store and returned it; we paid for it were going to return to pick it up.  Instead we returned seeking our money back.  The owner made the comment that she did not have many cribs coming in due to the 'many crib recalls' as of late. The fact that a brand new mattress was included, though this is usually never done, per the salesperson, was also alarming b/c the rails were hidden from view.  I happened to lift the mattress out while examining the crib.  I would hope that something can be done to insure that this place of business not sell recalled items to parents for children.
justification: The crib was recalled but no injury or incident occurred, only a potential risk was identified.

incident_description: I bought this crib model #8676C from a yard sale and just found out it was one that was recalled. What can I do to make it safe I can't afford a new crib. Please Help
justification: The crib was recalled, indicating a potential safety hazard, but no incident or injury has occurred yet.

incident_description: My safety concern is with a new crib that I purchased on Sunday, July 3, 2011.  My understanding was that all cribs for sale in the US were to be updated to meet the new standards by this date.  I purchased the Europa Baby Geneva crib in white from walmart.com on the date above.  When I received the crib, the manufacture date on the seal read October 2010.  I was extremely disappointed in this, as I doubt that this crib meets the standards set in December 2010.  I purposely put off my crib purchase until after the June 28th date in order to purchase a safer product for my son.  In addition, while I was researching cribs in order to make this decision, I found that crib manufacturers were not willing to answer my questions about their products and how they comply to your standards.  I feel that I was shipped a crib from their stock that could not be sold before your June 28th deadline, which would be an illegal action.  I suggest that an investigation into these practices, by Wal-Mart or Europa Baby/LaJobi is in order, as well as other crib sellers or manufacturers.  It seems likely that these companies are trying to get rid of the products they have on hand that are now illegal to sell.  They are depending on consumers not being educated about these regulations and failing to notice the discrepancy in their dates.  I do fear that my child's is less safe in the crib that we purchased than in a crib meeting the new standards.
justification: The concern involves a potential safety issue with a crib not meeting updated standards, but no actual incident or injury has occurred.

incident_description: My baby boy who is 9 months keeps getting his leg all the way up to his thigh stuck in the bars when he rolls over to sleep at night.  He wakes up crying and then I have to go in there and wiggle his leg out.
justification: The baby's leg getting stuck causes distress but no injury, and it happens frequently during sleep.

incident_description: I have 9 month old twins girls. One was sitting in a maclaren rocker chair which has a bar over it  with velcro holders for toys. I noticed she was chewing on something, which given her age, not unusual, but luckily I took notice. She was able to take the small velcro toy holder off the toy bar and had it in her mouth. If I had not noticed she would have choked. This chair was given to me used but it is in good condition.  It also has a sticker from Jpma on it.
justification: The child was able to remove and chew on a small toy holder, posing a choking hazard, but no injury occurred due to timely intervention.

incident_description:
The baby was lying on her stomach on our bed.  She is 6.5 months old.  Her back was to us, and we were all watching TV.  Suddenly she began screaming.  I snatched her up and turned her around and to my horror the pacifier was lodged sideways in her mouth...Her mouth was forced open in a lock-jaw position and she was scared and in a lot of pain.  (Nipple toward one side of mouth, rear toward other side of mouth, 'laying down' so that the long part is horizontal with her gums and the short side was the part that was holding her mouth open.'

Instinctively I pulled it out, but I had to TWIST it and pull HARD to get it out.  She cried for 20 minutes, but her gums didn't seem to bleed.

I believe that if a baby was in their crib alone and this happened at a different angle, like with the rear of it inside the mouth as it was lodged in the gums sideways, that the baby could suffocate or die a crib death due to their airway mouth exit being blocked.  It's hard to get enough air to scream through your nose.

I hope they recall this product immediately.
justification: The baby experienced significant pain and distress, indicating an injury, though no bleeding was observed. The potential for suffocation suggests a possible risk of death in other scenarios.

incident_description: I bought a Da Vinci Kalani crib and started using it in the fall of last year. 8-9 months later I came in the room to find all the screws loose and some sticking out as far as 1inch. The front and back rails were ready to be swinging free. With all the sides loose and the rails, it raised a real concern that my child could have fallen and gotten stuck or just have fallen out of the crib. She is very small and could have easily gotten caught between the rails with them being as loose as they were. All the screws were tight as can be when built and there should have been no reason I had to go back and tighten EVERY SINGLE SCREW. I have not been able to find a place to contact the manufacturer directly so I am turning here as I may now have to buy a new crib and these cribs are supposed to be top of the line! Please help resolve this issue and look into this. I am sure I am not the only one who has run into this.
justification: The crib's structural failure posed a significant risk of injury to the child, though no actual injury occurred.

incident_description:
Item - Fisher Price product - Infant to Toddler Rocker model # W 2583 
I purchased this item for my granddaugher. Has a 3 point restraint listed in description. It only came with a hip restraint. It does not have a shoulder strap to keep baby from falling out. I was visiting my granddaughter during the holiday. Baby now at 9 months old with the seat in leaned back position,  she leaned forward and nearly tipped completely over if I had not stopped it. My understanding according to NHTSA definition of 3 point restraint is to include shoulder strap. They told me their definition of it is two from hip area and one between legs. This item along with several other bouncer/recliner infant seats they make DO NOT have shoulder straps included. I was told by Fisher Price who took my complaint that the reason for no shoulder straps is because it is a strangling issue. If that is the case then why do carriers, high chairs and car seats have shoulder straps?
I am very concerned about the safety of ANYONE using this product. We are returning the item for a full refund but this must be checked into please.
justification: The incident involved a near-tip-over of the infant, which was prevented by the grandparent, indicating no injury occurred but a safety concern was identified.

incident_description: Portable crib #625 seemed to be very loose with latches in place. side rail cracked in a short time of use. Matress did not fit well, very loose on all sides.
justification: The crib's loose latches and cracked side rail pose a potential hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description:
I have used pampers since my daughter's birth on [REDACTED] and never had a problem, in fact they were our favorite diaper to use until now. I unknowingly purchased a box of swaddlers new baby size 1 with dry max (the diapers did not have the wetness indicator, which was my first clue that these were different), got 4 diapers into the box without incident but I was alternating them with other brands of diapers left over from baby shower gifts. I had just put my little one in a fresh diaper when she suddenly started screaming and crying about 2 minutes later. The baby had peed and when I got the diaper off of her seconds later she had redness with small welts all over her genital area. I was able to wash the area with baby wash and water while she screamed and cried which she continued to do for about 15 minutes after the change and cleaning. Four days later my baby still has redness and cries when she urinates. Her doctor is having us coat the area with balmex zinc cream which appears to be protecting the skin until it can heal, but it does not appear as a normal diaper rash which in the past had  only occured occasionally between my child's butt cheeks. This redness and welts are where her legs meet her torso in the creases as well as her labia and inside her vaginal area which has never happened before, in fact since we switched to Seventh Generation diapers the day after this incident the baby hasn't even have a diaper rash between her butt cheeks.
After a quick internet search about dry max I have discovered that this is an unsafe  and poisonous product. I really cannot believe there has not been a recall and that this product is still on shelves! After all I have read including details of the class action lawsuit, I have decided that I will no longer purchase pampers. In fact I will probably eradicate my home of all P&G products because if P&G cannot make a safe product for babies, the most sensitive & vulnerable of us, how can I be assured that other P&G products are safe? 
So, I will be tossing 88 diapers into the dumpster and never buying pampers again. I sincerely hope that P&G will choose the health and safety of their customers over corporate profits!
justification: The baby suffered redness, welts, and pain for several days, indicating an injury from the diaper.

incident_description: In 2009, my infant child was using the Razberry teethers from Razbaby while my mom was watching him. He was able to turn the teether and get it lodged into his throat. I contacted the company and their response was only that they had tested them and that this had not happened before. This happened AGAIN to my son with a completely different teether (as I had thrown out the other one). Recently, which lead to this report, I found more reviews on sites such as amazon that children are still choking on this teether, as recent as February 2011. The company replied the same way, saying that this issue had not happened before. The handles are too soft for children that age. It is easy for them to get it lodged in their throat if they have a large mouth.
justification: The incident describes a choking hazard with the teether, which could lead to injury or death, but the specific incidents mentioned did not result in injury or death.

incident_description: I purchased a DaVinci crib, style name "Jamie", model number M7301W, at the beginning of 2010 for my son. He is now 14 months old. It was up to date with all of the recalls that I had done research on. On the early morning of July 1, 2011 my son woke me up screaming in pain. When I went to check on him he was laying on his stomach with his leg stuck between the vertical crib slats. His leg was stuck on the upper to mid part of his thigh on his left leg. It took me 5-10 minutes to slowly work his leg out without hurting him anymore than the crib had. I worked his leg out successfully. When I picked him up his leg was colder than the rest of his body and extremely sore to the touch. He has marks on the inner and outer part of his thigh, as well as the top of his thigh because he was sleeping on his stomach. After 24 hours the bruises got worse and were still very sore to the touch. I sent the company an e-mail right after that incident. They said they have 72 business hours to contact me. I have not yet heard from then. Then, today, July 5, 2011 my son woke up screaming again. When I went to check on him the same thing happened again. His left leg was stuck in the vertical slats on his crib. This time he was wearing long pants, where as on July 1st he was wearing shorts, and it wasn't as difficult to get his leg out. He has red marks on his legs from the 2nd incident. After 24hrs from July 1st I took pictures of his legs to have for proof. I regret not taking pictures of his leg actually stuck. My mind was 100% focused on getting his leg out and making sure he was okay. I do not feel safe with my son sleeping in his crib at all.
justification: The child suffered bruises and soreness from being stuck in the crib slats twice, indicating an injury (severity 3). The recurrence of the incident within days suggests it is likely to happen again (likelihood 4).

incident_description:
My 8-month old daughter has had a HABA pacifier chain ("Bear" model) attached to her carseat for about 6 months. In the past few months, she's started chewing on the pacifier chain sometimes. A couple weeks ago I noticed that there was a crack through one of the wooden pieces of the pacifier chain -- the one that has the embedded mirror. As I inspected it, it broke into two pieces. It was wet, so she had been chewing on it. This is a serious choking hazard!

I received this pacifier chain from HABA after I reported a similar incident with another of their pacifier chains (the Motley), in which the wood cracked after my son chewed on it. I emailed them, told them of the incident, and they sent me a variety of HABA products as replacements including the "Bear" pacifier chain. This was about 3 years ago.
justification: The incident involves a cracked wooden piece from a pacifier chain, posing a serious choking hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

The crotch strap pulled through the slot that was holding it there, causing my 18 month old to fall.  Though she was scared, she was relatively unharmed.

We are very sure that this crack was not there when we assembled. This is a safety issue. I am requesting a thorough testing of this product and a recall if possible.
justification: A cracked crib slate is a safety issue but no injury was reported, indicating a severity level of 2. The likelihood is possible as the defect was found after several months of use.

incident_description: My 9 month old son has on more than a few occassions gotten his leg stuck in the slats of the Graco Lauren crib. I have been awakened by him screaming because his upper thigh has gone through the slats and gotten stuck. On one occassion, I had a hard time getting him out of it and when I did, his leg was cold as if it had been in there for quite some time before it woke him up or it became uncomfortable.

incident_description:

incident_description: The bouncy seat we are using comes apart from the lets and the top.  To install the unit you must push down and twist to remove the legs and when the baby bounces on the seat the same things happen if he twists his body while jumping.  The enire unit fell to the ground seperating the legs from the top of the unit.  There is not locking device no snapping snug fit , its only twist and the legs come right off the top of the bouncy seat.  It is very unsafe and poor design and my son fell to the ground on Sunday becuase of the poor design.  He fits the required age and weight limit and it was accurately put together based on the directions in the box.
justification: The baby fell to the ground due to the bouncy seat's poor design, indicating an injury occurred.

incident_description: I ordered a Europe Geneva crib in white for my daughter through Amazon.com. It arrived about a week later. The large box was brought to my door and I placed it inside my living room. The box smelled really bad, like something toxic. I placed the box behind the couch to get it out of the way from my children. The next day my husband and I opened it and it continued to smell really bad. We brought the pieces upstairs to the room to where we wanted it. I cleaned each piece thinking I could "wash" the smell away; that didn't work. During the time it took my husband to put it together, he had to keep leaving the room, and at one point had to lay down because he was dizzy, nauseous, and light headed. The smell was not getting any better and now dissipating in the bedroom. We had to have my daughter sleep in another room and not in her new crib and open the windows (and it was not warm outside, it was rather cold and rainy) to prevent the odor from permeating the room. When we got close to the crib, it still smelled like toxic fumes. I called Amazon and they said to take it apart, and they would pick it up and send us another one. When the replacement crib arrived, the box had that same smell. I opened a corner of the box and the toxic smell again permeated the room. I immediately closed up the box and called to have it picked up. This is inexcusable and I feel like the safety of my daughter and my family were at risk!
justification: The toxic fumes caused dizziness, nausea, and lightheadedness, indicating injury (severity 3). The issue occurred with two separate cribs, but such incidents are unlikely to be widespread (likelihood 2).

incident_description: My 3 month old baby boy (that weighs nearly 15 pounds) was sleeping soundly on his back on the LifeNest Sleep System in his crib when I heard him crying. I went in to pick him up and was shocked to see that he had slid all the way down the LifeNest and was stuck at the bottom, unable to turn his head to catch his breath. The slide down the LifeNest had caused him to become face down, half  on the edge of the LifeNest wedge and half on his mattress. I feel this was a close call, and he easily could have been suffocated like this. He is unable to roll over on his own yet, and the LifeNest product states that the "mesh cradle" is supposed to keep the baby from sliding, but it definitely did not. I feel very lucky that this did not happen at night while I was sleeping, because my baby would have been stuck face down all night.
justification: The baby was stuck face down but was unharmed, indicating an incident with no injury. The product's failure suggests this could happen again if not addressed.

incident_description: This report is regarding the Babi Italia Pinehurst Convertible Crib. Both legs of my 18-month-old son were stuck between the slats earlier this evening. It was very difficult to remove them and once his legs were freed, they were swollen and bruised.
justification: The child's legs were swollen and bruised after being stuck, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
My husband and I just started using Pampers Swaddlers with Drymax for our daughter a few days ago, and this morning our 3-month old daughter woke up this morning with a blister on her thigh. Not knowing what could have caused her to get a blister on her thigh along with irritation like she had I googled it. That is how I found out about the chemical is Drymax diapers causing chemical burns. Refusing to recall the diapers and insisting that the many reports are just false allegations despite all the proof that has been posted online via photos of the burns (that is how I discovered that what she had on her leg was a chemical burn, I looked at photos of other children's diaper area), is just irresponsible and negligent and something needs to be done about their negligence!


Proctor and Gamble Pampers Swaddlers with DryMax!
justification: The incident describes a chemical burn on a 3-month-old baby, which constitutes an injury.

incident_description: I made numerous purchases of the Pampers Dry Max Diapers and the babies (x2) had diaper rashes unknown it was caused by this particular diaper until I recently heard about this diaper.  The rashes were so bad that it appeared to eat at the babies skin.  I had to buy expensive medication to get the rashes under control but it kept coming back.  I am extremely disturb about me just now hearing about this.
justification: The babies suffered severe diaper rashes requiring expensive medication, indicating injury (severity 3). The issue persisted despite treatment, suggesting a likely recurrence (likelihood 4).

incident_description: I wanted to let you know about a dangerous situation Infantino's Explore & Store Gym's can cause. Our daughter was pulling down the star shaped rings to her mouth, and one of the stars got stuck in her mouth between her gums. She could not get it out and her mouth was stuck open with the star lodged between her gums.
justification: The incident describes a child getting a star-shaped ring stuck in her mouth, causing distress and potential injury, warranting a severity level of 3. The likelihood is possible (3) as such incidents can occur with small children and toys.

incident_description:
Summer Infant "Summer Soothing spa and shower baby bath"

On third use, water seems to have infiltrated the pump housing and caused some kind of electrical arc, which created enough pressure to blast the lid off of the battery compartment and cover the device in some kind of black sludge.  It was enough pressure to mark the ceiling where the compartment lid hit.

The pump continued to run even after this event.  Thankfully it didn't shock my newborn son.  It hurt the heck out of my ear, though.
 
I've got a video and pictures of the failed pump if they're useful.

incident_description: My 9 month old was in her crib in her room  with the side up. Then the next thing I knew she had managed to get the side down I guess her weight pushed it down (she ways 21 lbs when she was at the doctor) and had fell to the floor,
justification: The infant fell from the crib to the floor, indicating an injury occurred, and such incidents are possible with improperly secured crib sides.

incident_description: The Tommee Tippee bottle warmer does not automatically shut off. I believe this can be a fire hazard. We went for a walk and around an hour later the warmer was still running and was without water at this time due to it being evaporated.

incident_description: The consumer says the slats are too far apart and her child's leg got stuck in between them and she did bruise a bit.  The consumer feels this is a design flaw.  The consumer says that she contacted the manufacturer and they told her that the crib meets safety standards.  The consumer feels that this is a problem that could be solved by just changing the design. The consumer says her child's leg was stuck for approximatley two minutes.

incident_description:
While the 18 month young 24 pound toddler was sleeping. She heard him screaming to the top of his lungs in the middle. She went into his room and noticed that the toddlers left leg up to his knee was caught in between the slats of the crib . 

In attempting to free his leg she pulled on the slats and attempted to push his leg back. The toddler has gotten his leg caught in between the slats on two occasions the first occasion was around February. The most recent occasion occurred on June 5, 2011 and he receive a minor bruise on both sides of his knee cap where his leg was wedged in between the slats. 

The firm was contacted when the first incident occurred and she spoke with a representative from the firm (name unknown) who indicated if the slats were a certain amount of inches apart (exact inches are unknown) then the crib was safe. 

The most recent incident the firm was not contacted she stated that they are taking her concerns with the cribs to lately. She currently allows the toddler to sleep with her in fear of his leg being wedged in between  the slats and breaking his leg.
justification: The toddler sustained a minor bruise from the incident, indicating an injury (severity 3). The recurrence of the incident suggests it is likely to happen again (likelihood 4).

incident_description: There is a headless nail sticking out of my gate. it appears that these nails are working their way out in several places. they are sharp and the exact height of my child's face.
justification: The sharp nails at child's face height pose a clear injury risk, but no incident has occurred yet.

incident_description: After only a few uses of the Baby Einstein Musical Motion Activity Jumper, our 6 month old discovered an issue with the yellow sunflower item attached to the activity center. She was able to bend it over which makes it catapult back towards her face. After it cracked her in the forehead (twice) resulting in tears, we removed this toy. I'm not sure how safe it is to have the holes exposed. This toy is a hazard. This yellow sunflower plastic piece is exceptionally hard, heavy, and springs back with too much force for little babies still developing coordination. An adult can recreate this by just bending back the sunflower piece with their hand.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (a hit to the forehead causing tears) and the issue is easily reproducible, indicating a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: I have a storkcraft Bradford 4-in-1 crib.  The wooden pieces that are lined along the sides back and front are very flimsy and can be broken very easily.  The matress is 2-3 inches away from the side of the crib and our daughter has got her arm and leg both caught in the matress support because of the gap.  There has been no serious injury.  But there is always a chance that she could get her head stuck and well.  We have quit using this crib and put her in her pack and play.  We did not notice these problems until we removed her bumpers and she is now bigger and can move around a little more.

incident_description: I purchased a package of Pampers Splasher swim pants for our daughter who just turned three.  I normally do not purchase Pampers products, but THOUGHT they were a reputable name and since there was more product for the same price, figured I would give them a try (and my daughter also like the character on the swimmers).  On June 17, 2011 I put the 1st pair of swim pants on our daughter.  She was only in them for approx. 1 1/2 hours before I brought her in to change.  Upon beginning to remove the swim pants she let out a scream and began crying.  I noticed that she had a very large red area with blisters where the swim pants had touched her leg (by the leg holes).  After tending to her, I immediately called Pampers.  Upon looking online I found there are several other people out there with similar situations regarding Pampers.  It is now over 7 1/2 hours later and the area is still very red and puffy and VERY uncomfortable for her.  I find this appalling and disturbing since Pampers is a company who makes products specifically for babies and young children.  I hope you can look into this before any other children get "injured".
justification: The child suffered blisters and discomfort, indicating an injury, but similar incidents appear uncommon based on the description.

incident_description:
The consumer was about to place her 10 month old, 28" tall, 17 lbs., baby in the crib when she discovered that it was broken.  While placing the child down, she found that the mattress was sagging and she stopped the use of the crib.

The wooden frame that surround the mattress (not the mattress support bars) cracked completely in half.  The consumer is not sure how the frame broke.  The child was not injured.

(5/30/11)  The consumer sent the manufacturer and e-mail describing the incident.
(5/31/11)  The consumer received an e-mail back from the manufacturer and their rep. indicated that they would replace the mattress base.  The e-mail stated that they would get the part to the consumer "right away".

NOTE:  The consumer said that she had placed her child in the crib in a lying position; the child would have been alright.  However, if her child was bigger and or more active, this may have created a situation when an incident could occur with the crib.
justification: The crib was broken but the child was not injured, and the manufacturer responded promptly to replace the part.

incident_description: The shoulder straps on my SpaceSaver High Chair have become a choking hazard. The buckle through which the length of the shoulder straps adjust is right by his face, so the extra four inches of length is hanging there for him to chew on. There is no way to move it or fasten it to prevent him from chewing on it, and I am concerned that he could push too much of it into his mouth and get it stuck in his throat. It has not yet gotten stuck, but he has gagged on it. The strap has a thickened end on it to prevent it from sliding through the buckle, so it's impossible to reverse the strap and have the extra against his body to make it less accessible. The thickened end of the strap could easily get stuck in his throat.
justification: The incident describes a choking hazard with potential for injury but no actual injury has occurred yet.

incident_description: My 14 month old baby has horrible red burns on her bottom and the pediatrician asked us what type of diapers we had been using.  We had been using Pampers with Dry Max technology.  When the doctor suggested switching, the rash/burns have almost cleared up in less than 48 hours.  I will never buy these diapers again.  I have found many reports online where other mothers have claimed the same type of reaction.  I can't imagine why these are still on the market.
justification: The baby suffered red burns, indicating an injury, and multiple similar reports suggest this is not an isolated incident.

incident_description:
Hello,

This complaint concerns the grasping/teething baby toy "SALTO" by "HABA".
It is a wooden toy made up of a ring 4 inches in diameter with a thin bar crossing it down the middle. On the bar are 5 colorful spinning pegs of varying lengths (1-2 inches).
I purchased this toy about 1 year and 4 months ago (February 2010) on Amazon.
My baby played with this toy, primarily clutching it and sucking on it.
About 1 month ago I gave my baby (13 months old at the time) this toy and stepped out of the room for a minute. When I came back into the room I noticed that this toy had broken apart and baby was holding one of the pegs near his mouth. After quickly grabbing this peg I realized that baby was sucking on another peg. I put my hand out to baby and got him to spit out the peg he was sucking on. I then counted all the pegs to make sure that they are all accounted for. 

I was very shaken by this incident. As a parent I strive to get good quality toys for my kids. Toys by reputable brands that name safety as being a top priority for them. Haba has earned such a reputation among parents, so how is it that this infant toy fell apart in my baby's mouth after as little as one year of use? When all my baby did was suck on it - which is exactly what he is supposed to do? 

Please look into this matter and keep me updated on your findings.

This incident also leads me to question the safety of all infant and baby toys containing small parts. There are many such toys on the market and as a parent you want to trust that these toys are safe and they will not break apart. However, incidences like this prove that some of these toys will break apart and pose choking hazards. So why even allow such toys to be considered safe for infants and small babies?

Thank you for providing an avenue for the reporting of unsafe products.
Please keep on working to make products safer for our children.
[REDACTED]
justification: The toy broke apart but no injury occurred, as the parent intervened before any harm could happen.

incident_description:
I purchased a Dream on Me 3 in 1 infant portable crib with the drop down sides.  When completing the company's online form for the current recall of this product, I found that though my model number (#625) was the same the manufacturing date was one month later (March 2009).  I understand that the recall only includes model #625 manufactured until February 2009.  After contacting the company they claimed there was a change in manufacturing plants.  

While I was going through my crib to collect the information for the recall, I found that the top rail on the drop side of the crib is split.  The wood has split at the contact point of the drop side hard ware.  I believe this is from when my daughter (1 year old and 20lbs) pulls herself up to a stand.  There must be pressure at the hardware point causing the wood to split.  I believe the reason for the current recall is this same issue, but for some reason did not include items manufactured later than February '09.  

We use this crib at a seasonal home, have never dropped down the side, and have only used the crib a dozen times.  I feel that the product is inferior, and should be included as part of the current Dream on Me recall.
justification: The crib's top rail is split, posing a potential hazard, but no injury has been reported.

incident_description: I received Pampers Dry Max size 1 (40 count) as a gift at my baby shower. After a month of using other diapers I opened this pack and began using them on her. After a few diapers she began to get a rash. I didn't think it was the diaper so I put some [REDACTED] on her and kept using them. Then after 3 days it became redder and puffy with raised bumps! Shes been crying and fussing all day and night and nothing seems to relieve her. I went online to see if others were having this problem and its all over message boards and parenting websites! There has been no change in her eating habits as shes breast fed only. I havent eaten anything unusual to make her break out and this rash is only on her private area and bottom.
justification: The baby developed a painful rash from the diapers, indicating an injury, and similar incidents are reported online, suggesting a possible occurrence.

incident_description:
Choking Hazard

Stainless steel water bottle distributed by iPlay under the Green Sprouts brand (see link below).  Product is marketed for use by infants and toddlers and is available from many retailers. 

Water bottle has a push/pull valve at the top like a traditional water bottle, however in this case it is actually a silicone rubber stopper that can be pulled all the way out with a slightly harder tug, e.g. for cleaning.  It's sufficiently easy to pull out that my 23 month old did so with his teeth almost immediately.

The stopper itself is clearly a choking hazard -- about 1-1/2" long, 1" around at it's widest part,  overall about 5/8" diameter, and made of a compressible material (silicone rubber).   Ironically it's also designed to be the part that a 1-3 year old is supposed to put in their mouths and pull on to open the bottle.

http://iplaybabywear.com/index.php/greensprouts/feeding/interchangeable-bottles/stainless-steel-bottle-468.html
justification: The silicone stopper is a choking hazard for infants and toddlers, and the description indicates it can be easily pulled out, increasing the likelihood of occurrence.

incident_description:
A year ago my daughter suffered from the worst "diaper rash" I've ever seen and there is no
doubt in any of our minds that her pampers cruisers are what caused it. I won't even call it a
diaper rash because that doesn't possibly convey it's severity. This is my 3rd child so trust me
when I say I've spent 7 years of my life changing lots of diapers. I was pampers swaddlers and
cruisers biggest fan until last May when this happened. I switched to [REDACTED] and the "rash"
cleared up quickly. Fast forward to one year later and my husband bought our daughter a
package of Luvs. A "rash" appeared almost instantly. We couldn't figure out why because even
though it presented just like the way she reacted to pampers, we knew none of them had
touched her. After some research, I became aware of the fact that Luvs and Pampers are both
made by Procter & Gamble. I also found a large number of other parents complaining of Luvs
now causing their babies a "rash" exactly like pampers had caused. Luvs are now very thin, a
purple hue, and the chemical odor is awful. I don't need anyone to confirm that P & G is now
using the dry max materials in Luvs now. You should be ready for thousands more complaints
and shame on you, CPSC, for "finding no link" between 5000 complaints in 2 months of severe
diaper rash with pampers diapers being what they all had in common. YOU, not even P & G,
should shoulder the blame of letting this continue. Allow me to send you a picture of my child's
rash. I don't have a lawyer, I don't want my money back, and please don't send me the robotic
message you've sent everyone else who has complained. Your actions most certainly prove you
are not sorry my child has a rash and I have no desire to call and tell you my "unique" experience.
I now know not to buy pampers or Luvs. But CPSC, you are allowing this to keep happening so I'll
have to keep vigilant myself for any rash that appears on my my daughter from a diaper. Because
you most certainly are not going to keep her from harm.
justification: The description details severe diaper rash caused by specific diaper brands, indicating an injury to the child.
