The drop side plastic piece broke off and now the drop side will no longer stay up or be held up.  This happened when my child first woke up and stood up (most likely pulling herself up on the bar of the drop side).  I heard her say, "Uh Oh" and when I got to her room, the left side of the drop side had completely detached from the side of the crib.  

From that date on, we moved my child to a toddler bed (at 1 year old) and have not used the crib.  We assumed it was just expected to happen since she was the second child to use the crib.  Now I am pregnant again and researching what I can do to fix it.  I thought maybe I could order a new plastic part to replace the broken piece.  It sounds like I need to return it for a refund?
justification: The crib's drop side failed but no injury occurred, and the child was moved to a toddler bed immediately.

incident_description: Consumer wanted to report a potential choking hazard with a Fisher-Price Linkadoo. Her son, who was 3 months at the time, was using the product for about a week when the consumer noticed some strange marking on the product. She stated that the products has plenty of perforations in the product and it appears that the white inner material and the inner plastic can chip off into the mouth of a child and result in choking. The consumer stated that the perforation are  the same size shape, and distance on the link. The consumer stated that there was no incident with the product and her son was not harmed by the product. The consumer has yet to call the manufacturer or the retailer about the product but felt that the CPSC should be notified about the product as there are similar products on the market.
justification: No incident or injury occurred, but the potential choking hazard is a concern. The likelihood is possible given the product's design.

incident_description:
I purchased Pampers with Dry Max technology for my 10 month old daughter. Within a week of beginning to use the diapers, she developed a bright red blistery rash on her buttocks that got progressively worse. Nothing else had changed...not any new foods, no new detergent, no new creams, no new soaps, etc. I stopped using the diapers and it cleared up within two days. I had a nurse look at it and she agreed that the rash was not yeast or common diaper rash. 

I contacted Pampers and they immediately sent me a refund.
justification: The child developed a severe rash requiring medical attention, indicating an injury, but the issue resolved quickly after discontinuing use.

incident_description:
My 1 year old son had been using Pampers Baby Dry diapers since he was born. Last week I began using Pampers Cruisers instead. Within 3 days, his anus was bright red, and he developed small bright red spots on and around his testicles. The folds between his legs are also bright red. I am quite positive that this rash is caused by the Cruisers diapers because this is the FIRST rash he has ever had and it developed within days of having begun to use them. 

I have since switched to another brand.
justification: The child developed a rash, which constitutes an injury, but there was no death or severe harm reported.

incident_description: My infant's arm is getting stuck in the Graco Contempo High Chair. I called Graco customer service and they were not concerned that this was a safety issue. Her arm was getting stuck between the sides of the highchair. We sent it back. I read online this is not the only instance of this happening to babies.
justification: The infant's arm getting stuck in the high chair poses a risk of injury, and similar incidents have been reported online.

incident_description:
I have a 28 month old toddler who has worn Pampers diapers from Birth. After puchasing a new box of Pampers Baby Dry, and using them overnight, my son woke up the next morning looking as if he were scalded from the testicle area back to the rectum. His skin was solid red and looked as if burning water had been poored on his bottom. Not realizing that it could be the diaper, I placed zinc cream on him and continued as usual. 

The next day, the rash was worse with oozing and weeping sores formed along the diaper line around the buttocks area. The pediatrician stated that this was an allergic reaction to the diaper. He was given a burn cream and I was instructed to discontinue the diapers. 

The incident began on a Thursday morning and continues one week later. He has open sores and a persistent rash. Although healing (since we no longer use diapers), the rash has lasted the week and is extremely painful. The skin has chaffed and peeled while healing and flares up any time a diaper is placed to the skin.

2 pediatricians looked at the affected area and stated this was due to the diaper, without a dought.
justification: The toddler suffered a severe allergic reaction with oozing sores and persistent pain, requiring medical attention, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description:
Phil & Ted's Me Too travel high chair

Our portable high chair is used exclusively as a high chair at every meal for my child, as a disclaimer, if that factors into the reliability of the high chair. 

On or about April 7th, my high chair slipped of the edge of my dining room table. only one side of the clamp released from the table despite routine checks of the clamps. My child swung downwards towards the ground, suffering only a bruised forearm. We rotate the Me Too with a lobster as each item becomes dirty from the child's eating habits so it is only on the table for an average of two to three weeks at a time. 

I did not think to report the incident until I noticed the CPSC recall/stop use advisory was released.
justification: The child suffered a bruised forearm due to the high chair slipping off the table, indicating an injury occurred.

incident_description: Last night at 11 pm in Navarre, Fl I heard my son crying after he had been asleep for about an hour. I went into his room and his leg was stuck in between 2 of the rails on his Nadia 3 in 1 crib. His foot had begun to turn purple and he had a small mark on his leg. We had to break one of the rails on the crib to get his leg out of it.
justification: The child's leg was stuck in the crib rails, causing a small mark and discoloration, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
I have just been given a Simplicity baby crib with changing table that attaches to the crib. One side of the crib has a broken plastic notch that slides up and down on the side of the crib. Upon researching this crib it has been recalled and no replacement parts are available.  This crib # is vendor #8994W
Date made  2204 CW.  Am I out of luck on a fix for this crib, or even getting a new crib? 
Thank you, please response quickly. Needing a crib for my newborn granddaughter.
[REDACTED]
justification: The crib has a broken part and is recalled, posing a potential hazard, but no injury has occurred yet.

incident_description:
My 2 year old son was taking a nap in his crib (Amy Convertible, manufacturer AFG International). When we got him up, one of the slats on the headboard piece was broken at the bottom and slid out of the top so the slat was in his bed and he was playing with it, leaving a big gap between 2 other slats. We contacted AFG March 28, 2011, and while they said they would look for a replacement part, they didn't believe one would be found and anyway it was out of warranty since it was purchased in 2008. I've also contacted USA Baby who sold us the crib but have not gotten any response. Multiple emails to AFG received responses that we needed to contact USABaby, and that AFG couldn't help us. 

The crib was purchased in October of 2008, the child born January 2009. He was not put into the crib until July of 2009 and the slat broke March 2011 so it was only used for about a year and a half and it's a crib intended to be used indefinitely since it's convertible. I can't personally think of anything a 30lb child could do in a crib that should damage it to that extent and think the slat had to have been defective or he wouldn't have been able to break it out of place like that, but AFG seems to think that it's not their fault since he's the one who broke it.  A missing slat is a huge saftey issue in my opinion no matter how it became that way.
justification: The incident involved a broken crib slat but no injury occurred, and similar incidents are unlikely based on the description.

incident_description: My daughter has been using the Fisher Price Rock and Play Sleeper for nighttime and naptime sleep for 6 months, since she came home from the hospital.  The product is marketed to parents as "meeting industry safety standards for bassinets" and the packaging includes a photo of a mom in bed with her infant beside her in this product.  After just 3 weeks of overnight use my daughter developed torticollis (a tightening of the neck muscles).  She was not diagnosed until 4 months (but it is visible in pictures at 3 weeks) and we did not make the connection to this product until she was 6 months old, at which time we ceased using the product.  Torticollis develops after use with this product because it forces the child to turn her head to one side.  I made the connection to this product after reading numerous reviews on Amazon.com of many other parents reporting the same condition after repeated nighttime use.  Treatment of this condition requires months of physical therapy and has delayed my daughter's physical development.  My daughter has also developed a flat head that has been shaped by the hard plastic backing of the product.  While hers is not severe, many of the Amazon.com reviewers report severe flat head problems.
justification: The incident describes a physical injury (torticollis and flat head) requiring treatment, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) due to multiple similar reports from other parents.

incident_description:
April 8, 2011at 10:00AM  22yr old father/caller while visiting his mother was sitting by his 6  month old son when the 6 month old while bounching hit his mouth on one of the toys on his bouncing activity exerciser.
Father looked at him, baby's mouth was bleeding and one of the two lower only teeth baby has was knocked out.
Father has tooth in zip lock bag, called pediatrician who normally sees baby, was informed that he is completely booked so is referring them to another office, however father states that it has been long time and he is planning to take baby to emergency room if doctor has not called back by the time this report is completed.
Callers have been waiting, called CPSC Hotline to report injury.
Baby was in distress when accident first occurred but is not at this time.
justification: The baby suffered a knocked-out tooth and bleeding, which constitutes an injury, but there was no death or life-threatening condition.

incident_description: Use of MeToo portable high chair.   My husband clamped it to the kitchen bar  - leaned on it to make sure it was sturdy to put our daughter in it -- she was in it for about 5 minutes before it gave way.  No indication that it was giving way (leaning, slipping, etc) - just a sudden drop practically straight down.    THANKFULLY no injury to my little girl (9 months), but traumatized her for a bit and definitely traumatized me (her mother).    We will definitely not use again, even if there is a repair kit.
justification: The high chair failed suddenly but no injury occurred, only emotional trauma.

incident_description:
Have purchased Phil and Ted's [metoo] attatched high chair to use when our grandson visits.
Purchase date 08/26/10. At age 8 months he was in the chair when it detached from the table
and he fell to the hard kitchen floor hitting his head. We just assumed we had done something 
incorrect. I went out and bought a regular highchair after that as I had no confidence in the chair.
We have only used the chair about 3 times.
justification: The child fell and hit his head, resulting in injury.

incident_description: My daughter has never had diaper rash in her 2 years of life...3 months ago we switched to Pamper Cruisers dry max and looking back this is when she got little pimple looking blisters here and there and diaper rash oftenly . I have used several differant ointments( [REDACTED]) visited the physician several time receiving many differant ointments ( including [REDACTED] etc) none seeming to giver her much relief. I was really beginning to thinbg there was something seriously wrong and began to question my mom & her father about changing her often enough....searching for some cause, never believing that Pampers could have put a product on the market that would harm my child, it seemed silly to me that something such as a diaper could cause my daughter all of this pain. The rash was so raw it literally would bleed and was almost purple in color along with this she had on her legs and belly and bottom fluid filled blisters. The last and final time I visited the pediatrician he suggested switching diapers....within a week it has began to taper off...some of the blisters still remain and there is scars from the severity of the diaper rash! My child is permanantly scarred from diapers? I am irrate...beyond irrate! Watching her scream while i simply tried to wipe her is something a mother can not get past especially when your baby's sking id practically sloughing off! I want something done about this...when i called pampers they offered to compensate my last box of diapers purchase .....NOT ENOUGH! These need to be off the shelf out of stores where not even one more child will have to go there what she has been throught!
justification: The child suffered severe diaper rash, bleeding, and permanent scarring, indicating an injury.

incident_description: My 7 month old son was in the Jenny Jump Up when I heard a gasping noise.  I turned to see his neck resting on the metal bar (which was covered by the cloth seat) and he was looking down and didn't lift his neck off of the metal bar and was choking.  I ran to get him out of the jump up and he caught his breath.
justification: The child was choking but recovered after intervention, indicating an injury was narrowly avoided.

incident_description: i own an evenflo ecersaucer triple fun jungle and there is an alligator as one of the toys and there is a ribbon attached to the alligator that attaches to a different part of the toy and the ribbon broke off from both parts of the toy and my son almost choked on it
justification: The ribbon broke off and the child almost choked, indicating a potential choking hazard but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: Wooden slat on Evenflo Top of Stairs Plus gate cracked.
justification: A cracked wooden slat on a stair gate poses a potential hazard but no injury is reported.

incident_description:
I own a Stanley Young America Contentment Sleigh crib with a dropside. Purchased in October 2008.  

We have several issues with this crib, and the manufacturer has refused to address them. While we have been fortunate to not have any accidents or injuries related to the crib, I do feel these are safety issues that could cause a problem in the future. 

First, the dropside gets stuck and jammed if lowered, for about a year now, so approximately 1 year after first use.  We do not use the dropside on a regular basis, so this has not been a major problem, but the only way to get it unjammed is to force it out of the track, which is clearly not safe. 

We recently contacted the manfacturer to recieve the dropside stabilization kit. We initially did this through the store we purchased the crib from. I heard the store manager talk to young america on the phone but we never received the kit. we contacted young america directly yesterday and they said they will only send them out through the retailers, not to the consumer directly. Since we already tried through the retailer, I feel as though they are just avoiding sending it. 

The third issue is not a safety issue as of yet, but it could become one in the future. The screws to raise and lower the mattress height have become stripped so at this point we can no longer use them to secure the mattress frame. We requested new hardware from them from Young America, but they refuse to provide it, stating it is our own fault that the screws stripped, even though we have only lowered the crib mattress twice ever in the life of the crib.  This will force us to use hardware that is not intended for the crib, which does not seem right to me.
justification: The dropside getting stuck and stripped screws pose potential safety risks, but no incidents or injuries have occurred yet.

incident_description:
My 2 year old son (whos bedroom is upstairs from us) started screaming after his nap (which is very unusual behavior) I ran into his nursery as he was trying to crawl over the  side of the crib the side callapsed down pinin his leg and  rear end between the matteress and the crib side, I tryed forcing it back up. But as it was completely uneven between left and ride triggers it wouldnt give in at all. My husband came runing and with full force Hit the side-bar of the crib upward untill the trigger plastic peace crashed appart and we removed the child. This was a very scarry incident aspecially for our 2 year old son [REDACTED]. He cried nonstop, pointing to crib saying Ouch..and hurts and no sleeping mommy.
My husband realized he just flat out broke the plastic part when he yanked it upward and off [REDACTED]. . The crib side was then lowered to its non-functionable position. ANd without hessitation we went to reordered the destroyed peace of assembly part. Pulling the waranty paperwork and sitting on the phone frustrated for phone numbers being DISCONECTED, we quickly logged on to the website provided. AND STUMBLED UPON CPSC's Warning of Recalls. This was especially chilling to us, we raised our now 5 year old daughter and now our 2 year old son in this crib and THANK GOD we had no Deaths! Or serious Injuries! Just a scarred little guy who has a fear of his crib now. Our heart goes out to the parents who lost their babies in their crib. Out of all places, that would be a safe haven for a child.
Now i am dealing with my Local Walmart giving me a hard time because our MODEL numbers were Rubbed off and faded with cleaning the milk-bottle-messes. Luckly i could make out the first 3 digits which fall in the category.  Sadly this is taking longer and alot more frustrating with our local store. I am advised that a Complience Officer is working with our case with the local retailer.
justification: The child was physically trapped and scared but no serious injuries were reported, aligning with severity level 2.

incident_description: We purchased a Graco play yard (model 1756464, manufactured 12/24/2009) a few months ago from Burlington Coat Factory. Once our baby was born on 4/7/11, we began using the changing table portion. There is a triangular cutout at each end of the plastic in the changing table. This area is dangerous - our son has caught and scraped hos toes in it. New designs in the store do not have this cutout. We have emailed Graco asking if this part been redesigned. While it appears that the worst that can happen is scraping of the toes/feet, it still shouldn't be designed so that a child can be injured.
justification: The incident describes a child scraping their toes on the play yard's changing table, which constitutes an injury.

incident_description: Started using Pampers Extra Protection with Dry Max and our 1 year old son started to get severe rashes. Our Doctor said these are not Diaper Rashes caused by his stool, but they are "Chemical Burns."
justification: The incident involves severe rashes diagnosed as chemical burns, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
I'm not sure how to go about this, so this is the first place where I am starting...

My son, [REDACTED], died in an Infantino Baby Sling. I now know that three other infants died in the sling. We thought it was SIDS because he was a healthy baby. But on October 11, 2008, I used the sling and when I checked on him, I knew something wasn't right and I knew he was already gone.

[REDACTED] was born [REDACTED].

It has been a very rough couple of years and I feel a lot of guilt because I was the one who put him in that sling. If I would have known the safety concerns, I would have never used it.
justification: The incident resulted in the death of an infant, which is the highest severity level. The occurrence likelihood is considered rare (1) as it is a tragic but uncommon event.

incident_description: My husband and I purchased the Leksvik crib from IKEA in Costa Mesa, CA in August 2010 for our baby who was due in the Fall. This crib gets good ratings through Consumer Reports. We didn't begin using the crib until March 2011, as our baby was in our room prior to that until she was 4 months old. I had noticed that the mattress didn't fit tightly into the crib and it worried me. We got the size mattress that went with the crib (purchased at IKEA when we bought the crib). A few times in the past 2 months my daughter got her arm or leg caught in the 1 to 2 inch gap between the mattress and the crib. She is an average sized baby for her age. She is also not super fussy so she didn't cry hard when this happened - thank goodness I went in to check on her, she was just making some fussing noises but not crying. After it happened a few times, I mentioned it to the instructor at Hoag Hospital's safety course I attended May 6 and the woman said the mattress needs to fit tightly into the crib and my daughter could break a limb. I went home and googled it and there are so many other parents experiencing this with this particular crib from IKEA. We exchanged the crib last friday evening, May 13th.
justification: The baby's limbs got caught multiple times in the crib gap, but no injury occurred, indicating a severity level of 2. The issue is common among other parents, suggesting a likelihood of 4.

incident_description:
We were given a ChildESIGNS Drop Side Crib in April of 2002 as a baby shower gift.  We used it until our son out grew it in 2004 and converted into a toddler bed and once he out grew that we stored it away.  Our youngest was born in October of 2009 and we are currently using it for him and just today the plastic part you lift to drop down the side cracked and broke.  We didnt hear about this recall until we got on and Googled replacement parts for this crib and are now looking into buying another crib because of the potential hazard.  Better safe than sorry.

Thank you.
[REDACTED]
justification: The crib's plastic part broke, posing a potential hazard, but no injury occurred as the parents are replacing the crib.

incident_description: I bought the Cosco Flat Fold HIgh Chair  Product number HC146 from Wal-Mart located in Lancaster, Ca 5/7/2011. I installed the high chair 5/12/2011. During the installation, my husband and I noticed there was a space (gap, if you will) from the tray and the bar set to sit the child legs.  We put our 9 month old in, we then noticed her leg was not in the leg area, it was located in the space we saw during the installation (not thinking that a baby would notice the area). once she couldnt get her foot out she began to cry. We removed her from the seat. We placed her back in 5/14/2011, thinking she would not remember the area, after being ther for 15 minutes, her foot was there again. I feel this item should be recalled because a child's foot should not be stuck in anything that is "safe". Had she tried taking her own foot out, there could have been more harm to her. Any child can occur brusing and their ankle being sprained to say the least. I went to their website to see if there was any safety notices, and non found. I feel this itme is not safe at all. Please call me if you need too, this item must be recalled for a baby's sake.  I have pictures if needed,. Thank you for your time.
justification: The incident describes a child's foot getting stuck in a gap, causing distress but no reported injury, indicating a severity level of 2. The likelihood is rated as 4 (likely) due to the repeated occurrence with the same child.

incident_description:
There have been two mornings this past week that my daughter has managed to get herself stuck between the bars in her crib rails. The first time it happened (earlier this week), her leg was sticking out the rails, and it was wedged all the way up to her high thigh. I was able to get her out okay, but her poor leg was very cold.

This morning was the second time this has happened. I woke up to her crying. I went into her room and saw that both her legs were sticking out of the rails stuck at the knees. I was able to get her out by gently adjusting her position. Her knees and legs had deep indents and purple lines where the bars were pressing on them and her legs were once again very cold.

She is ten and a half months old, about average in size for her age. I don't think she should be able to get herself stuck in the bars like that.
justification: The incident resulted in physical injury (deep indents and purple lines on legs), and it has occurred twice in a week, indicating a likely recurrence.

incident_description:
my daughter was 4 months old at time of incident i placed her in her 
walker and adjusted the setting to have her feet reach the ground. 
since then i have read the instructions which states do not adjust while
child is in unit, but i was unaware of that at the time and figured how would i know 
the approperiate setting for her if she was not in it to see?! so while i was adjusting 
the chair (turn red knob push in and the legs move up or down) the spring SNAPPED!
and pieces broke right off (the plastic) down went my baby, folded right up on her, 
her legs were bent and she had cuts and bruises and trouble moving them for a few minutes
i took pictures of her legs / wounds. i really could not believe what had happened 
almost like a freak accident but regardless the spring and hard plastic should not have snapped 
bc my 12lb baby was in the walker! it just doesn't make sense to me.
justification: The child suffered cuts, bruises, and temporary mobility issues, indicating an injury.

incident_description: My daughter was in a Graco Pack 'n Play that was empty and not positioned next to anything. She cannot climb yet, as she is only 9 mos old. She leaned over the rail and fell out, head first. She landed on the floor, and sustained bruising to her temple, along with the breath being knocked out of her. I don't feel that the rails are high enough to safely contain children, and should be looked into as a falling hazard.
justification: The child sustained bruising and had the breath knocked out of her, which constitutes an injury.

incident_description: I am writing this report about the Babyletto Newhaven 4 in 1 Crib with Toddler Rail. My daughter has been repeatedly getting her legs and arms stuck in teh slats of this crib every day and it has me very concerned. Since crib bumpers are not recommended I do not know what else to do, there are no solutions for this problem and I'm concerned my child will become injured. Her limbs were VERY stuck several times and I had to force the wood of the slats apart at one point to get her leg out. Crib manufacturers need to create something to prevent this issue, since it's such a common problem either by providing cribs that are completely mesh and breathable or by adding other safety features. Anyway, this crib does not feel safe. In addition to that the springs that the mattress rest on are very loud, creaking constantly and feel a tad shaky.
justification: The child's limbs getting stuck in the crib slats is a recurring incident with potential for injury, but no actual injury has been reported yet.

incident_description:
I have a night light and when I went to the bathroom this morning it was smoking. It is called a
"Lava Lite". It was to hot to touch and was smoking profusely.
justification: The night light was smoking and too hot to touch, indicating a potential fire hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: I was prompted to write because I watched your video about the Phil & Ted's Metoo recall. I never reported this incident because I figured it was "user error" - I assumed I had not tightened the clamps tight enough. About 2.5 years ago, my little boy, about age 1 and less than 20 pounds, kicked hard and one of the Metoo seat's clamps came loose from the countertop. The other clamp held, thank goodness, and he was strapped in; I saw him disappear from the other side of the counter! It took just a few seconds for me to get to him, he was unharmed and hanging upside-down from the seat straps. I set him upright and got him out of the seat, at which point he started crying - he was shocked but still had all his fingers!
justification: The child was unharmed but experienced a frightening incident where the seat came loose, indicating a potential safety issue without actual injury.

incident_description:
I was given a Dream on Me Happy Swing that is made by Dream on Me. My son is 6 weeks old, I placed him in the swing today and found that his head is able to slide under the should restraints because they are extremely high up on the seat. Both shoulder restraints sit next to his head but are lifted up off of the swing because it is a five point harness and clasp to the seat belt that fastens at the babies waist. I was concerned with the fact that the product does not give a minimum length a child should be to use this swing, it does say that it can be used on babies up to 25 lbs. 

I am worried that a baby could be seriously injured by this.
justification: The description indicates a potential safety hazard with the swing's restraints, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: I am responding to the announcement for the Phil&Ted clip on chair. Our chair failed when the screw used to tighten the chair to the table actually stripped out. No injuries occurred with the failed clamp.
justification: The chair failed due to a stripped screw, but no injuries occurred, making it an incident without injury.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that while her spouse was passing by the saucer his right foot was lacerated by the plastic underneath the unit, he was taken to the emergency center at Phorek Memorial hospital where he received 5 stitches and was released.  

Consumer is concern that this product is capable to harm an adult and she thinks that the injury would be worse had it been a child.

Consumer stated that this product has been recalled for end caps but this product has other saferty hazards and should be investigated.
justification: The incident resulted in a laceration requiring medical attention (5 stitches), which qualifies as an injury (severity 3). The consumer's concern about potential harm to children suggests a possible likelihood of recurrence (likelihood 3).

incident_description:
Sorellle City Lights Crib.
22-month old son got his leg stuck between the slats/bars of the crib.
Put his leg in past the knee and could not get it back.
My wife and I were able to pull on the slate in opposite directions and get his knee and leg out after a few  scary moments.
justification: The child got his leg stuck but was freed without injury, indicating an incident with no lasting harm.

incident_description: I used Pampers Cruisers w/ dry max on my almost 2-yr-old for 1-2 weeks and she had a severe rash on her genital area almost the entire time. I didn't think it was the diaper initially because I always use Pampers Baby Dry. I finally realized that I was using a different type of diaper so I stopped using it and the rash went away.
justification: The child suffered a severe rash, indicating an injury, but the issue resolved after discontinuing use of the product.

incident_description: Received an alarm to smoke smell in a residence. Upon investigation found that nite-light in bathroom had shorted out. The side housing of the light had ruptured and was blackened by smoke and heat. AmerTac LED model 71352.
justification: The incident involved a shorted nite-light causing smoke and heat damage, but no injuries or deaths were reported.

incident_description: The Simplicity 4 in 1 convertible crib that we purchased from Target in 2006 is very loose and wobbly now.  We have "converted" it many times through two children.  All of the screws and stripped and the side supports are wobbly.  Both children also chewed on the front, back, and side rails and most of the wood finish came off.  I'm sure they swallowed most of it.  At the time we were unaware of lead poisoning so I don't know if it harmed them or not.  I saw that all the cribs have been recalled due to failure of the bottom ring supports.  But this wobbly issue could be a good reason to recall them to.  If the cribs were meant to be converted, they should hold up through many conversions.
justification: The crib is wobbly and has stripped screws, posing a potential hazard, but there is no mention of actual injury or death.

incident_description:
I have a "high" chair that is to be used by placing it on a chair.  I do not use it this way, I use it while it is sitting on the floor.  My complaint and my concern is that on multiple occasions my grandson has had his arm lodged in between the seat and the arm rest.  This happens very quickly and while I am or my daughter is sitting right in front of him during a feeding.    His arm seems to slip into the rear of the arm rest and he pulls it forward causing his arm to become lodged between the arm rest and seat as previously stated.   My concern is that when this occurs, naturally his first instinct is to try to pull his arm out  causing the arm to become more lodged.   I can pull it out but not without him becoming upset.  
I am sitting right in front of him at all times but what if another caretaker leaves a child in this seat unattended?  This may cause much more injury before the situation is found.
justification: The incident describes a child's arm becoming lodged, causing distress and potential injury if unattended, indicating a moderate severity with a likely recurrence.

incident_description:
I have a Sassy teether that is in the shape of a butterfly. The body is two tones of green. It has a blue freezable wing (upper right); a red/white striped wing (bottom right); a hollow yellow ring with balls inside (bottom left); and a purple ring with blue polkadot nubs (top left). It is the latter 'wing' that is of gravest concern to me. The blue polkadot nubs are starting to come off as my daughter chews on them.
I saw that a similar item was recalled, so I thought it would be helpful to know that the same problem seems to be occurring on other items.

incident_description: 4 year old got arm stuck in ball tunnel. Had to use lotion to get it out. No injuries.

incident_description:
Purchased a night light for girls bedroom on Thursday April 14, 2011. 
Opened bubble pack and installed night light on Sunday evening April 17, 2011in 3 year old girls bedroom. Night light is a direct plug in to electrical socket and did not have any contact with furnature or clothing.
Within 30 to 35 minutes smelled smoke and hot plastic. Smoke alarm activated and mother saw smoke in daughters bedroom, removed daughter and extinguished fire. Notified County Fire Marshal of incident.

LED Night Light
Manufactured by GE
Modle 10937
justification: The incident involved a fire caused by a night light, but no injuries were reported as the child was safely removed.

incident_description: My daughter was in her crib when she slipped between the slats, I couldnt get her out and she was screaming, we ended up breaking the drop side apart to get her out. I filed a report with the consumer firm, to possibly recall the crib at that time and did not hear back, recently I found out it was recalled and I know there is a kit to repair the crib but in our case we had no choice but to break the crib, now I am pregnant again and feel they should send me a replacement.
justification: The child was trapped and screaming, indicating distress but no reported injury, hence severity level 2. The incident led to a recall, suggesting the likelihood is possible.

incident_description: Purchased a Munire Majestic Safeside Crib for my 18 month old toddler and within less than an hour of being in it, he got his right arm stuck in the side rails and he could not get it out by himself.  It took myself and my husband to get him free which took almost 5 minutes and I had to actually get in the crib myself to get his arm unstuck.  My son dropped his blanket from the top of the crib onto the floor, so he was just trying to pick it up.  We have another crib and we don't have this problem.
justification: The child got stuck but was freed without injury, indicating an incident with no harm.

incident_description: I have a Delta Luv Crib, model # 4520-1. It is a recalled drop side crib. I contacted the company for the fix a few months ago and installed it. They sent me 4 plastic red clips to attach to the bottom tracks to prevent the crib from dropping off the track. Last week on April 12, 2011, I was dropping the side of my sons crib and it completely came of the tracks and all the way to the floor smashing my foot. Upon contacting the company they said it shouldn't have happened because not only does this crib have the retrofit kit they sent me for the fix, but it also had safety pegs that are supposed to prevent the sides from dropping without them being engaged. They requested that i send them pictures of the crib and I did. A week later they got back to me and informed me that they will be sending me all new plastic pieces for my crib for me to install and that the bottom tracks will look different as they wont have the secondary safety pegs, just the red retrofit kit. The crib already failed with that kit and an additional safety mechanism. I am afraid to put my son in this crib because if his arm, leg or other body part had been in the rungs of the crib, it would have snapped his bone like a twig. If the retrofit kit didn't work the first time, I doubt it will prevent the same thing from happening again.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (foot smashed) and poses a significant risk of severe injury to a child, with a high likelihood of recurrence given the failure of safety mechanisms.

incident_description: The SpaceSaver High Chair by fisher-price has arms on it that are about an 1 1/2 inches away from the back part of the chair and within the couple of seconds it took me to get her dinner out of the refrigerator; she was able to slide her arm in between the arm and back of the chair and she got her arm stuck. We were able to get her arm unstuck and it didn't result in any injuries other than a red mark on her arm. As a consumer; I love this product but I would advise possibly; when making this chair; modifying it with the arms of the chair either closer (less than an inch) to the back of the chair or further away (whichever would make it less possible for a child to get their arm stuck)
justification: The incident resulted in a red mark on the child's arm but no serious injury, indicating a minor injury.

incident_description:
Medical personnel stated that she removed an Avent pacifier from a 11 month old child's throat,
she stated that the parent informed her that the child was attempting to place the pacifier in her mouth sideways when it flipped and got stuck in her throat, which the EMS had to use a forcep to remove. Rubber was in airway. With mouth open, back of pacifier was seen. 

Caller stated that she needed to report the safety hazard of this product.
justification: The child had a pacifier stuck in her throat requiring EMS intervention, indicating an injury occurred.

incident_description:
The round crib I purchased from little miss liberty round crib company (URL: www.crib.com) experienced a catastrophic failure of the latching side gate. The gate itself slides up and down and locks in place. It is wooden and has 2 horizontal supports on the top and bottom, separated by several round vertical wooden slats. As my daughter was grasping the slats, they fell out of the top horizontal piece and the bottom portion of the locking gate fell down. The vertical top piece remained locked. This happened after I put my daughter down for a nap. She fell into the exposed wooden ends, scraping her face and blackening her eye. The best way to describe the failure would be to send pictures, which I have. 

I contacted the company and they simply told me the crib was 2 months out of warranty. They gave no heed to the danger this could pose to my child or other children.
justification: The incident resulted in a child's injury (scraped face and blackened eye) due to crib failure, indicating a severity level of 3. The likelihood is rated as 4 (likely) given the described failure mechanism and lack of company response.

incident_description: The other day i bought my 13 month son a package of pampers cruisers with dry max. On the third diaper change i was going to do, i noticed a blister on the inside part his thigh. As I opened the diaper my son started screaming, his little butt, leg, butt cheeks, was raw! I couldn't even wipe his bottom with a diaper wipe. I rushed him upstairs to the bath tub. He couldn't even sit down in the lukewarm water! He was screaming pulling on me to get out, i took a washcloth and slowly rinsed his bottom and private part. I felt so bad for my son! I took pictures, kept some of the diapers. I immediatly stop use of the pampers dry max cruisers. This is the most terrible thing a company could do to your children! I called pampers, she told me " Well the cruisers don't work for all children." I will send you 4 $10 off coupons toyou for th inconvience. I don't want the coupons, because I will never by any of there products again.  I've told numerous people, about the situation, and plan to tell even more. I can't belive ths happend, they need to pull all of them off the shelves! Discontinue the dry max line.
justification: The incident describes a severe skin injury (raw skin, blister) caused by the diaper, which required immediate medical attention (bath and gentle cleaning). The likelihood is unlikely as it appears to be an isolated incident.

incident_description:
Re: Pampers Extra Protection diapers

The diapers contain absorbent balls of gel.  When my son urinated in the diaper at night, the gel balls swelled and "exploded" out of the diaper.  I found them everywhere inside my son's pajamas from his feet up to his neck.  They had escaped the pajamas through the neck hole and were piled on the sheet by his face, and a few had even left the crib (presumably through his movement in his sleep) and ended up on the floor.
I feel very lucky that my son is not prone to putting things in his mouth.  I have no idea what the absorbent material is, but I can't imagine that eating it would be very safe.
justification: The incident involved gel balls escaping the diaper but no injury occurred, though there was potential for harm if ingested.

incident_description: My 2 year old daughter, who had never had any significant rashes in her entire life, got horribly burned from the Pampers with Drimax.  We had started poty training, but were still having trouble at night  Pampers came out with this new product that was supposed to be super absorbant, so we thought it would be a great idea.  After using the diapers for only one day, she had the most horrible burns on her little bottom.  Bright red welts, all over the diaper area- she was in so much pain.  I didn't connect the dots at first, as she has been using pampers baby dry since she was born.  A few days laer, I heard the news report about the chemical burns/dri max connection.  I Immediatly stopped using the product and within a few days the burn gradually got better and went away.  I was amazed to find thousands of the same complaints on facebook pages and all over the web.  This product needs to be taken off the market.
justification: The child suffered bright red welts and significant pain, indicating an injury (severity 3). The widespread complaints suggest the issue is likely (occurrence 4).

incident_description: i have a bright star hybridrive baby swing. I put my five month old in it, buckled the seat belt, when i turned around from doing something because he was crying i found him upside down hanging in the seat! his head was very close to the floor and thank god did not hit the floor!! The cloth seat of the chair raised forward when he sat up in it but i think this seat it very unsafe!!! I will not put my baby in it and think everyone should be aware of this product. incident_description: On April 7th, I put my 8 and 1/2 month old daughter in her crib for a nap. About 2 weeks prior I purchased Summer Infant Breathable Bumpers. justification: The locking mechanism failed, posing a potential hazard, but no injury or incident occurred.

incident_description:
There has not been an accident with this item, but the problem is the construction and safety of the item. 

I bought a brand new wood play yard off eBay. It is similar to the plastic Super Yard you can buy in stores, but much larger. It is called BABY / PET WOODEN PLAYPEN ROOM DIVIDER WOOD OCTAGON by the seller id-rack on eBay. This item is imported from China and does not look safe to be used with infants or toddlers. 

I had a few minor problems in assembly not related to safety, such as the cheap construction of the shipping box so that it was damaged in shipment and one of the octagon "feet" was missing, which they replaced, and an allen-head bolt that the allen hole was defective so you could not tighten it with the wrench (I had to use pliers and turn the foot instead). 

The 1st thing regarding safety that concerned me was how lightweight the wood was. The instructions say not to lean on it, that even children shouldn't lean on it. You can hear it creak if you barely touch it. Part of the gate was damaged (the wood cracked and split open) in shipment because the wood was so light and you could see it was held together inside with small thin pieces of metal like staples. I repaired it with wood glue and tie wraps, but I do not trust removing the tie wraps as the sharp pieces of wood or the small wires like staples would be a choking hazard to a child if it did come apart again. The 2nd thing that bothered me is the bolts that are used to hold the gate segments (sides) together. The bolts along the bottom screw into wooden "feet", which don't concern me as much except that some donÃÂt tighten enough due to cheap materials, but the bolts that hold the top together are a male bolt that screws into a female bolt. Baby & toddler products sold in the US are not designed like this. Due to the lightweight wood and rickety construction, these bolts could come loose from shaking and a child could choke on them if they fall out (they do not even have any kind of thread locker). Most baby items like this have some sort of cap or cover to protect small children from bolts and other hardware so that they do not choke or get scratched. These bolts are all completely exposed. The 3rd thing that concerned me is that one of the bars was warped - like in the old cartoons where a character bends the jail bars to break out. Because this post is warped, it makes the rods or slats farther apart in that space and a small infant could possibly get their head or other body part stuck there, which is a choking hazard for a small baby or toddler. The 4th concern is that the light would can probably also come apart by a teething baby or toddler chewing on it as it is very soft. Most items that babies could chew on when bored, such as cribs and playpens, have hard wood or teething rails or are constructed of cloth or plastic. It is unfinished wood, and I'm not sure if that is a good thing or a bad thing (I probably don't have to worry about lead paint, but I do not know if it has chemicals like pressure treated wood, etc.).

I did write to the seller/importer that this item was unsafe and I'm surprised that it is allowed to be sold in the United States and they offered that I could return it, but they are still selling this on eBay and I feel this item has the potential to harm small children. It is sold as a playpen (even though it does not have a bottom) and a parent or babysitter could walk away into another room to take care of something else, thinking their child is in a safe place, and I can see them choking on a bolt or getting their head stuck in non-uniform rods/slats or leaning on it and cracking it and choking on shards of wood. I have not measured the bars (similar to slats, but round rods) as I am not sure if there is a regulation for wood playpens or play yards as there is for cribs.

I purchased this as item # [REDACTED] on eBay (if you can do a search, or I can print out the advertisement). I still have the shipping/item box and can take photos of any part of the box or the play yard that you wish. It is nice because it is large and my daughter has twins, but you cannot see from the stock auction photos taken too far away the cheap and unsafe construction of this product.  I bought this because I thought it would be better than the plastic Super Yard that the twins can push on and bend, but the light wood is more fragile than any plastic.

As a comparison, another seller [REDACTED] is selling a wood super yard (item [REDACTED]) and you can see that every place that a side is attached, there is a plastic cover so that fingers don't get pinched or hardware does not choke or scratch a child. It is made by a reputable brand and uses flat slats that are consistent in spacing.

But the China-imported item I purchased has the potential to be extremely unsafe and is a danger to small children and possibly even pets.
justification: The description highlights multiple safety concerns with the product that could lead to injury or choking hazards for children, though no actual incident has occurred yet.

Aspen Stages Crib with Drawer - Natural : Target

I know these have already been recalled because of bassinet safety concerns, but the rivet issue I'm having it causing the unit to be unsteady and not useable. And there is no way to fix it by just inserting screws, because the plastic holding the rivets is starting to break apart too.  Since my child is only 22 pounds, I doubt that this is caused by any strain of her laying in the play yard...  So right now I have a $130 playpen that is essentially a $0 piece of garbage.  I can't give it to anyone else or sell it because it would put THEIR child in danger too.

she been not watched closely it would have been possible to poke in her eye easily.

Carter's Tree Tops Mobile
