We bought 'Pampers Swaddlers New Baby' with Dry Max for our 3 week old baby at our local Walgreens. We had been using a different brand but they were sold out and decided to try these Pampers instead. Within 2 days our baby got a very bad nickle-sized blister just about his penis! 
I did some research and it turns out this has been happening to thousands of babies across the country. I'm extremely disappointed that these diapers are still on the shelves if they are hurting our children!!
justification: The baby suffered a significant injury (nickel-sized blister) due to the use of the diapers, which indicates a severity level of 3.

incident_description: When I left my 22 month old daughter alone in her crib to nap, she became stuck in her crib.  The front of the crib has a rail at the top of the bars, a gap, and then another rail.  The gap is the problem.  When my daughter stuck one leg in the horizontal gap, she was able to swing her other leg over.  The leg in the gap was pinned.   Then she was stuck straddling the crib.  She is not tall for her age.  We believe this is an unsafe crib design.  Luckily we heard her crying on the monitor and ran upstairs so she was only stuck for a minute or so.  She has a bad bruise on her leg from being stuck but otherwise is ok.  The back of the crib is much taller than the front or the sides and the entire crib should be this tall if the sleigh detail is going to be included.  If we had not heard her crying, I don't know how long she could have supported herself and may have fallen out of the crib or have been stuck hanging upside down.
justification: The child sustained a bad bruise from being stuck in the crib, indicating an injury. The incident could recur due to the unsafe crib design.

incident_description:
Caller is reporting that his nightlight burned up during the night and, singed wall in a square foot area then obviously extinguished itself while making a cracking noise but did not trip his breaker               Caller is glad that there was no fire but worried that there could have been.
Model numbers very near this one are recalled on number (11-123 ) but his is not.
Caller would like for CPSC to consider adding model# 71190A to this recall.
justification: The nightlight caused minor damage (singed wall) but no injury or fire, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: I was sitting on my couch with my boyfriend, eating a sandwich and watching our baby play in the floor on his blanket. He had his pacifier in his hand rubbing it on his gums. I took a bite of my sandwich and got a drink of my soda. I looked back at the baby and all I could see was the little end of the pacifier sticking out of his mouth. My boyfriend was sitting closest to him. I screamed at him and told him to get it out of his mouth, that he was choking. As soon as he pulled it out he threw up. He is okay. If we wasnt right there it could have been worse. It scared me to death.. I have stepped into another room to put up laundry or do dishes, without my eyes continuiously on him and he has had the pacifier. I just want others to know there babies can get choked to be careful.
justification: The baby choked on the pacifier but was quickly helped and is okay, indicating an incident with no lasting injury.

incident_description: My husband and I purchased the Munire Brighton Baby Furniture Collection for our son on 7/21/2007 from Norman's Furniture Store located at 1714-20 South 2nd Street, Phildelphia, PA 19148 (215) 334-0632. On July 5, 2008 he was taken to AI DuPont Hospital for Children as a result of falling out of his Munire Brighton crib. The out of pocket cost for us as a result of this incident was $737.85. This cost does not include the amount paid by our medical insurance company which was Blue Cross Blue Shield of DE. The only reason we are learning of this recall now is because we are researching cribs for our expected baby and came across on online article stating that our son's Munire Brighton crib was recalled.
justification: The child was injured and required hospital treatment, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is unlikely (2) as it is a specific incident tied to a recalled product.

incident_description: When using Pampers Cruisers Sizes 3 and 4 with Dry Max for our 16 month old daughter, she was suffering from diaper rashes that would not heal.  She had a rash for over one month, and she cried each time we tried to change her diaper.  We changed wipes, her diet, bath soap, etc, but she did not heal.  We then decided to change to a generic diaper from Walmart, and her rash healed within 3 days.
justification: The child suffered from persistent diaper rashes causing discomfort and crying, indicating an injury.

incident_description: My 7 month old son was playing with the Leapfrog Learn and Groove musical table, which we love!, when his thumb got smashed under the bookpage that flips back and forth on the top.    When his thumb from one hand is just slightly under he doesnt realize until he pushes down the page with the other hand bearing his weight on it and not understanding to lift up on it with that hand to free his thumb.  So he screams and I get it out.  But the first time this happened was last week around Wednesday April 6th. The second time was this morning Monday April 11.  I dont want to let him play with it anymore because he is bruised so bad from the first time and now he is just re-hurting himself with it.  It is such a great toy that we love so much though!  I just wish they would fix this problem some how.
justification: The child sustained bruises from the toy, indicating an injury (severity 3). The incident occurred twice within a short period, suggesting it is likely to happen again (likelihood 4).

incident_description: I recently bought a package of the Pampers Dry Max diapers.  I have used pampers brand diapers on both my babies before with no problems.  After the first use of the dry max diaper my son had a rash equal in severity to a normal rash for him that we are always able to cure within a day.  After one nights use of the diaper, despite the use of ointment, the rash had turned into a open bleeding and swolen sore about the size of an adult's thumb.  We discontinued use of the product and already the sore is healing over.  It is caused him great pain.  I have used many brands of diapers and although we see occasional redness we have never seen anything like this!  The dry max diapers were the only new thing introduced to his skin within the 24 hours of the rash going from bad to horrible.  He also has had nothing new added to his diet and is not sick.  It appears it is the diapers causing the rash and open sores.
justification: The incident describes an open bleeding and swollen sore caused by the diaper, indicating an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the unique reaction despite previous use of similar products.

incident_description: I bought the Safety 1st Comfort Care Fold-up Booster #21042 from T.J. Maxx. We intended to use it as an extra booster seat at my mother's house. The tray was very difficult to snap into place and when we finally got it, it pinched my 9 month old daughters side, breaking her skin.
justification: The incident resulted in injury (broken skin) to a child, and the difficulty with the tray suggests this could happen again under similar conditions.

incident_description: My infant was in the rocker with the kickstand up (so it can rock), she was properly strapped in and the rocker was sitting on a level carpeted surface. She cannot sit up by herself, she needs support. I left the room for approximately 2-3 minutes. I heard a quiet cough that didn't sound right so I ran back into the room to see if anything was wrong. She was dangling over the edge of the front of the rocker by one of her thighs, held in the strap. The rocker was not tipped over, but balancing on the front. She was bright red, turning blue and not breathing well because she was doubled over on herself. I quickly untangled her and checked her over. Her leg had red strap burns, but no bruising. I think I'm more traumatized emotionally, especially because she can't really move about yet and this happened. I just wanted to pass this along so others are aware that this could happen.
justification: The infant suffered red strap burns and was not breathing well, indicating an injury but no long-term harm.

incident_description: My 20lbs six month old child was jumping in this jumper and one of the four straps broke and he fell forward and hit his head, but did not fall out of the jumper seat.
justification: The child hit his head, indicating an injury, but the incident is unlikely to occur frequently under normal conditions.

incident_description: The sesame Street Chilly Teething Ring made by munchkin cut the sides of my son's mouth.  The edges i guess are sharp enough to cut into the skin so when he was chewing on it I looked down and the corners of his mouth were bleeding.
justification: The teething ring caused bleeding cuts on the child's mouth, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
My AmerTac night light, model 71194, is supposed to have an electric eye and turn on when it's dark.  However, the night light remained on all the time, even in normal room light (there are two large windows in the room where it was located).  Only shining a very bright light source (such as a flashlight) directly at the sensor would turn it off.  

While I did NOT experiencing any melting or burning, as reported in the recall info, that may be because I stopped using it.  It made me nervous to have this light burning when it clearly wasn't supposed to.
justification: The night light malfunctioned by staying on continuously, but no injury or damage occurred as described.

incident_description: I have a Delta  Tyson 2 in 1 crib white. I feel as though there is a defect in the wood making it to soft. The side rail at the top is cracked completley in half, and I have those rubber teething guards on there, and that is the only thing keeping it together( very dangerous where she could fall out of crib, or be pinched in between the broken wood. Also she has been teething on the two end boards of the crib,and not only have I found her countless times with big splinters in her hair and on floor, but now she has bitten a huge chunk off the one end of the crib,( I happen to come in the room before she spit it out of her mouth.. were talking about a piece of wood , a CHOKING HAZZARD..I have had to resort to wrapping the rails with sheets just to temp protect her until this is replaced.. PLEASE I wanted to bring this to your attention and I hope to be able to get my money back for the crib and buy another one. I did not just want to tell the company because I was afraid they might just sweep it under the rug and do nothing. God forbid any other baby happens to choke on the wood my baby has been able to bite off the crib. I can take pictures and send them, or you can have someone come look at the crib...     Also I have only been using this crib for 1 year( we bought it brand new  from Kmart in west seneca, ny. Prior to that she was sleeping in her travel bed.   Thank You [REDACTED]
justification: The crib has significant defects posing risks of injury (splinters, choking hazard) and potential falls, but no actual injury is reported yet.

incident_description: less than a yr ago a relative purchased an Eddie Bauer high chair from our target baby registry.  We have always associated Eddie Bauer with quality products and were surprised at how poor this product was constructed  Last night we finished feeding our 9 mo son and were taking him out of the chair, when the back of the chair departed the base.  I should point out that i put the chair together.  I am a former Navy helicopter mechanic and currently in USN Flight Engineer school.  So needless to say i am more than qualified to put a wooden, prefabricated high chair together.  I contacted Eddie Bauer and was informed that since they sell the rights to Target, they had no involvement with the warranty.  I contacted Target and was told there was nothing they could do because it had passed the 90 day warranty.
justification: The high chair broke but no injury occurred, indicating a severity level of 2. The likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the reported construction issues.

incident_description:
The nightlight  was plugged into a wall outlet in the living room  she noticed a burning smell and smoke comming fromt he side of the night light. SHe unplugged it immediately and layed it down to allow it to cool off. 

There was a dime size hole located on the seam of the night light (on the side). She contacted the firm two days after the incident and thye advised her that they would not be able to do anything about it and to contact the retailer.

She contacted the retailer and they advised her that she would not be able to return them with no receipt. 

SHe remembers purchasing about 15 of the night lights in which she also gave her daughter. They both decided to discontinue the use of the nightlights in fear of they would start a fire.

She noticed online that there was a recent recall (see Release #11-123) where her model number was not affect but she experienced the same hazard as listed in the recall.
justification: The incident involved a nightlight emitting smoke and a burning smell, but no injury or death occurred. The likelihood is rated as possible due to the recall notice and similar hazards reported.

incident_description:
Consumer stated her child 16 months old developed a very unusual skin rash on her bottom. She said the rash is exactly where the soft, mesh top sheet is located. The child had red, almost burnt skin in all areas of diaper area- they were open sores, little bumps and very red.  

The redness started after only 2 diapers from package, it got progressively worse as she continued to use the Dry Max Pampers Cruisers.  Once she realized it was the diaper and changed brands, the creams started to work and soothe and it started to clear up.  The biggest sores- over 1 inch in diameter- took 5-7 days to completely heal and even now have left scarring and discoloration of skin were sores were.
justification: The child developed open sores, bumps, and skin discoloration, indicating an injury that required healing time.

incident_description:
RE: VULLI SOPHIE GIRAFFE TEETHING TOY (http://www.sophiegiraffeusa.com/sophie.html)

While lying on her back playing with the teething toy, my 7 month old daughter began choking and was unable to breath. Luckily I was sitting next to her and immediately pulled the toy out of her mouth. She had pushed one of the legs to the back of her throat, it is just long enough and wide enough to completely block her airway. There are currently 67 1 star reviews on Amazon.com complaining of the same problem. Had I not in the immediate vicinity, she may have died.
justification: The child choked and was unable to breathe, which could have resulted in death if not for immediate intervention.

incident_description:
Recently I purchased Pampers Cruisers Overnight/Extra Protection diapers for my 15 month old son.  He was waking up in the morning having soaked through his diaper and I wanted to try a new diaper for the nighttime.
We began using them on Monday night and by Wednesday, there was a 3/4" blister on his right buttock.  I immediately put him in the bathtub in an effort to clean the area.  He was in so much pain he did not sit down.  

Per our routine, my husband was home with him on Friday (same week) and upon my return from work, he reported that my son's buttocks were bleeding.  I opened his diaper and saw specks of blood.  After a thorough check, I realized that the blisters (now on both buttocks) had burst and wiping after several bowel movements had irritated the area.  I again tried to put him in the tub to clean the area and this time, he cried when his buttocks contacted the water.  I let him stand to be rinsed and removed him immediately.

The only change in my son's routine has been the use of Pampers Overnight/Extra Protection Diapers.  My son has been allergy tested and I am certain that he does not have fish, milk, peanut butter or any other common food allergy known to cause skin irritation.  

I am livid to think that a diaper could cause my son such pain.  I have been a loyal user of Pampers Baby Dry for my daughter (now 4) and my son. You can check my "Gifts to Grow" rewards status!  I hope this matter gets resolved and Pampers recalls the product.
justification: The incident describes blisters and bleeding on the child's buttocks, which constitutes an injury.

incident_description: Baby appears to have a burn on inner thigs or the diaper line, slightly on his bottom, and testicles. We have not change detergents or baby wash, but rash appeared today.
justification: The description indicates a burn or rash affecting sensitive areas, which constitutes an injury.

incident_description: Last summer (I think it was late August) my son was in the SNIGLAR crib from Ikea and when he rolled over to the side of the crib the mattress came crashing down.  He was six months old at the time.  Fortunately, he wasn't hurt at all - it just scared him, so he cried and, of course, we came running.  We realized that we must have put the crib together wrong, and thought it was all our fault until we saw the recent recall.  I'm sure the new bolts will fix the problem (this is just a crib we use occasionally while visiting my mother, so he's not in any immediate danger anyway).  But I thought I should report it since apparently other people are having the same issue.
justification: The crib malfunctioned but the child was unharmed, indicating an incident without injury. The mention of a recall suggests the issue is possible but not certain to recur.

incident_description: We acquired a Safety 1st Winnie the Pooh Music & Lights Walker. Our 6mo old son is teething and was biting on one of the attached toys and bit off the paint and swallowed it.
justification: The child swallowed paint from a toy, which is an incident but there is no mention of injury.

incident_description: An AmerTac motion-activated LED nightlight, approximately 8 months old, stopped working - would not come on. When removed from the outlet, there were char marks around the holes in the outlet. I threw the light away and purchased a similar replacement AmerTac light. As I had disposed of the light before I knew of the recall, I have no idea of the model number of the defective light. The replacement model, #73092, is not on the recall list.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning nightlight causing char marks, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Little Playzone with Lights and Sounds for Kids

On two different occasions my 8 ÃÂ½ month old son has had his arm logged between the slats. He has been unable to free them himself resulting in screaming & him pulling his arm so hard it has left red marks and mild edema. This just after a few seconds. 

I have only been steps away to be able to free him. I imagine the potential for someone to leave their child in this ÃÂsafetyÃÂ yard and leave the room and this could result in further injury.
justification: The incident resulted in red marks and mild edema, indicating an injury (severity 3). The description suggests this has happened multiple times, making occurrence likely (4).

incident_description: I just went to get my daughter up from her nap and her leg was stuck in between the front slats of her Sorelle Princeton 4 in 1 Crib.  It took me a few minutes to remove her leg because it was swollen and she was very upset.  She now has a bruise and red marks from the crib slats.
justification: The child suffered a bruise and red marks, indicating an injury, but no long-term harm was reported.

incident_description: My son is 7 months old and was playing in the Evenflo exersaucer triple fun (the pond one) and he was playing with the frog part of the toy and somehow got the little yellow ring that attaches the frog to the purple flower completly off. He then was chewing on it and got it so far in his mouth he couldnt get it out. He started vomitting and crying hystirically. I removed the yellow ring from his mouth carefully and he seemed to be ok.
justification: The child vomited and was in distress, indicating physical harm, but recovered after the object was removed.

incident_description: Consumer wanted to report her daughter's Kids II baby swing is unsafe. She stated that the product doesnt seem to securely seat the child in the seat and when she tries to push the child the seat turns slightly. She noticed the product doing this 2 weeks after purchase. She stated her child has not been hurt using the product. She has discontinued use of the products. She feels that the product isn intended for children of 25 lbs as advertised as her child is 16 lbs and still feels that the swing is suitable for somebody of her size. She initially wanted to order a part to stabalize this hazard with a part from the manufacturer but feels it is more sufficient to notify the CPSC. She also stated that the food tray for the swing will periodically fall off.
justification: The product has a potential safety issue but no injury has occurred, and the consumer has discontinued use.

incident_description: I purchased two NUBY non-drip standard neck bottles with detachable handles (1098).  My infant daughter was able to remove the nipple completely from the bottle while assembled normally.  I assembled the bottle again and found that on both of the NUBY bottles, I was able to push the nipple out of place and into the bottle with only a small amount of pressure.  Once the nipple was in the bottle it slid out of the bottle easily when turned upside down.  These bottles are dangerous and a serious choking hazard.  Thank goodness my daughter chose to throw the nipple rather than put it back in her mouth.
justification: The nipple detachment poses a serious choking hazard, but no injury occurred in this instance.

incident_description: I purchased the Aosom 3in1 Baby Wood Superyard Playpen Combo from Amazon.com in June of 2010.  The wood, rather than being finished and smooth, is unfinished and splintery.  When I set up the superyard in my home, it was not sturdy at all - my son was able to push on one end of the superyard and the opposite end lifted up off the floor.  When I ran my hands up and down the vertical railings, little pieces of wood came off.  Since I purchased it, the superyard has broken twice, exposing sharp chunks of wood.  I complained to the manufacturer and was told that the gate is completely safe.  I just learned that the gate has been recalled.
justification: The description mentions splintery wood and structural instability, but no actual injury or death is reported.

incident_description:
This bath seat is excellent in every way for intended use. However, an injury occurred when not being used as intended...so I'm not sure if that qualifies it for recall but do want to report in case the company will consider a re-design as otherwise it is a fabulous product.
The Babycoon bath seat (made by Thermobaby of France) has a hole drilled into the plastic at the top. It is the size of a child's finger. My child inserted his thumb and swelling occurred so that he couldn't get his thumb out. Afraid the swelling would eventually reach the point of cutting off circulation I rushed him to the dr. and they (luckily) had cable cutters and were able to cut the tough plastic in two places so as to remove a piece allowing my son to get his finger out.
It was very traumatic for my son, though he has learned a lesson!
I hope they will consider making a larger hole, though no one is quite sure of the purpose of the hold so perhaps they would just go without.
Thank you!
justification: The child suffered swelling and required medical intervention to remove the thumb, indicating an injury.

incident_description: I purchased the Aosom wooden 8 panel playpen and was very happy with it -- until it broke.  I had stepped out of the room and  heard a loud thump and came out of the closet to find my baby lying on the floor and the broken pieces of the gate on the floor around him. The part of the gate that actually attaches to the wall had split.  The one of the screws had also come loose and was lying on the floor.  Thankfully no harm was done.
justification: The playpen broke, but no harm was done to the baby, making it an incident without injury.

incident_description:
My 2 year old developed a horrible, burn like rash after using the Pampers Cruisers with Dry Max. 

When both of my son's were infants we used Pampers brand until they switched to the Dry Max with my little guy.  The first box of diapers I used of the Dry Max my son (then about 1) got a horrible rash that took forever to go away. Thinking that it was probably something he ate, we kept using the diapers and he kept having a horrible rash. After 1 week of the rash not going away, I switched to REDACTED  thinking that the diapers were the reason. Sure enough, the rash went away and he hasn't had a rash since. After that incident, we have been using REDACTED brand diapers until my mother went to the store and picked up diapers for me and bought the huge box of Pampers. I decided to try the Cruisers again, thinking maybe the first round of rash was just a fluke or that maybe they changed the formula because they were brand new at the time. After ONE use of the pampers cruiser diaper, the horrible red rash was back. It was on my son's legs where the elastic part of the diaper hits and looked like a chemical burn with bumps. I treated it with REDACTED but it did not make it go away. The rash was more like a burn than a diaper rash that a food allergy or food related reaction would cause. After about a week and a half the rash faded and looked less painful. I donated the gigantic box of diapers after using that one diaper. We are back to REDACTED and no rashes are present.

I googled "rash and pampers" and discovered that thousands of other parents were having similar issues with the diapers since they switched to the Dry Max. Like I said before, we always used Pampers with no issues until they switched to the Dry Max formula. I know for a FACT that it was the diapers causing the rash with my son and do not think that it is coincidence that other parents are having the same issues. I believe the diapers are unsafe and should be investigated further.
justification: The child developed a severe burn-like rash, indicating an injury caused by the diapers.

incident_description: I was washing my son in the Safety 1st tubside bath seat when he spun himself around so he was facing backward. He was fine until he was ready to get out of the bath. At this point we could not get him out. He was stuck because when you pick up the baby the bottom lifts itself, thus leaving less room in the back for the babys legs to move so they could not move and in turn leaving them wedged in there. He had to be pulled out of the seat and when this happened his legs were forced to drag against the top of the seat and it left his legs red and bruised and him very upset.
justification: The baby suffered red and bruised legs from being stuck in the bath seat, indicating an injury.

incident_description: We just switched to Pampers Cruisers size 3 diapers. We always used Swaddlers with no problem. The first day we used the Cruisers I started to notice a rash. I just figured it was normal run of the mill diaper rash. By the next day, there were raised blisters especially by the legs where the diaper gathers to keep wetness in. We switched to Baby dry and it is now clearing up. I have photos of the rash if they are needed.
justification: The incident describes raised blisters, indicating an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is possible (3) as it occurred after switching diaper brands.

incident_description: I am a mother of 4 children and have used Pampers on and off for just shy of ten years now.  I have never experienced anything as scary as I did this evening!  I just started using Pampers Cruisers Size 4 with Dry Max about 3 days ago.  Last night when I put my son in his bath his bottom began to welt up with  oblong-shaped hives and he instantly started rubbing the area and showed me his bottom.  To my surprise his bottom was bright red with these oblong-shaped welts.  I called his dad upstairs to see and he instantly commented that the only thing I've changed is his diapers.  I just thought I'd watch it and see what happens.  After taking him out of the bath I put him back in the Pampers Cruisers with Dry Max diaper and made a mental note to check him again in a bit.  Before bedtime I changed him again and noticed that it had gotten better.  Then, just tonight, after he sat in the bath for just a minute or two, he got up and showed me his bum again.  To my SHOCK it was bright red and welted AGAIN!   I then decided it was in fact the diapers.  I have coated his poor bottom with aloe and put him back in his other brand of diaper.  After getting him off to bed tonight, I immediately got on the computer to do a little research.  TO MY DISMAY, I've discovered this has been an issue that P&G has been made aware of but, to the best of my knowledge, has done NOTHING to rectify the problem....THESE POOR BABIES!  I would like to know what is or can be done about this!  I am actually sick to my stomach after reading what so many babies and parents have gone through because of these diapers.  They really need to be pulled off the market!  I plan to contact P&G about this problem, too!  Please let me know the best way to get the word out so that this does not happen to another baby....PLEASE!  Thank you for your time.
justification: The child experienced bright red welts and discomfort, indicating an injury, and the issue recurred, suggesting a likely occurrence with these diapers.

incident_description: I have a 14 month old Daughter, who was taking a nap in her Delta Amber Baby Crib, When she woke up and starting screaming. I went in there and my daughter had her leg stuck in her bed rails. It took over 25 minutes to get her leg out. I had to use butter on her leg and crib to be able to release her. She has bruising on her leg where she was stuck. I contacted Delta Cribs about the issue and the Woman I spoke with seemed to not care at all that my child was hurt by her crib which is suppose to be a space place for my daughter to take a nap. I am worried/scared to put her back in her crib due to the fact what if next time it happens she gets hurt worse than some brusing. Broken bones ect... I have 2 other children and I have never had this happen so I dont know if this is something that happens often. I do not know what to do about it now. I contacted a lawyer who is the one who told me to report the Incident to you. Thanks [REDACTED]
justification: The child suffered bruising from being stuck in the crib rails, indicating an injury (severity 3). The parent's concern and lack of prior incidents suggest this is unlikely to happen frequently (likelihood 2).

incident_description:
Screws fall out too easily making this a choking and falling hazard.
Backrest falls back when child moves around too much.
Child able to kick off feeding tray. Yet, is difficult to take off as intended.
Anywhere the backrest and seat/arms come together can cause pinching.
justification: The description indicates potential hazards like choking, falling, and pinching, which could lead to injury.

incident_description:
We have and love the Selecta Musina Activity Gym, but we recently found one of the little dangling people's legs in our 4-month-old's bouncer.  He had removed it while playing but fortunately had not ingested it.  The leg seemed to have been attached by a dowel, which I suppose had gotten loose over time.

The part that fell off was spherical and slightly smaller than a marble.
justification: A small part came loose but was not ingested, indicating an incident without injury.

incident_description: I would like to report the Merry Muscles Baby Jumper as dangerous and defective since the bungee cord broke after only two uses and it is supposed to be safe for a child up to 40 lbs (and my daughter is only 28 lbs).  I purchased the jumper on Amazon.com and it is manufactured by a company in Canada (www.merrymuscles.com).  I would like to mail the product to you for testing and analysis although Merry Muscles, the manufacturer, wanted me to mail it back to them for a full refund including shipping.  The reason I am not mailing it back to Merry Muscles is that if I did, there would be no way for you to run tests on it and recall the product so that other infants and toddlers do not get harmed when the bungee cord snaps.  I paid $101.90 I paid for it on March 8th (Amazon Order #: 104-3695333-3216215).  I would appreciate it if an analyst would contact me so that I can mail the Merry Muscles Baby Bouncer to the Consumer Products Safety Board for testing that results in a recall until it is proven to be safe.  Amazon has already agreed to remove it from their Web site.
justification: The bungee cord broke but no injury was reported, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: My daughter's DaVinci Roxanne crib by Million Dollar Baby broke while she was in it.  The drop side came loose on one side and her arm got caught in it.  We are very lucky she wasn't hurt more than she was.  The peg that goes in the side broke in the middle allowing the side to push forward trapping her arm.  The skin is sliced and torn.  She is lucky it didn't break her arm or worse.
justification: The child's arm was caught and the skin was sliced and torn, indicating an injury.

incident_description: We bought this product for our 2 year old daughter when she started having some nighttime anxiety.  It was wonderful because it is a child friendly nightlight that she could keep right with her.  Then it broke so we bought another and that one broke and we bought a third.  It never occurred to me to report it until I saw another night light on a recall list that I check regularly.  All three broke in exactly the same spot.  The plastic around the screw holding on the battery cover snapped causing the battery cover to break off.  It could definitely pose a choking hazard with the battery cover,  the screw or the batteries.
justification: The incident describes a product defect that could pose a choking hazard, but no actual injury or death occurred.

incident_description: My daughter had a diaper "rash" that was being treated as both a yeast infection and sensitive skin, until after 4 months of having it and no medicine working, the doctor could not figure out what it was. I switched diapers and it started healing right away. My daughter had chemical burns, from Pampers DryMax technology that could not be treated with medications for fungual infections. Her entire bottom was opened sores, blisters, and bright red. As I researched, I found out this was not a diaper rash but looked like a chemical burn. It lasted 4months!
justification: The description details severe chemical burns and open sores, indicating an injury.

incident_description: My 8 month old was playing in his Baby Einstein jumper (just purchased in December 2010 from Target) and one of the purple hooks that are attached to it to hang toys off of came off. I didnt discover it until it was in his mouth and he was sucking on it. It was just the wrong shape and size that he could have swallowed it and choked on it. I removed the other one as well as a precaution. When I looked underneath, the hole that is supposed to hold that peg in place was shaped funny on that side, so it came out easier. The other one was solidly in place but I did not want to take a chance. A baby or small child could choke on this part, it is VERY unsafe!
justification: The incident involved a small part coming off a baby toy and ending up in the child's mouth, posing a choking hazard, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description:
Safety 1st Disney Serve N' Store High Chair - Sweet as Hunny
Model:  HC111ABV 
Manufacturing Date:  100317CB

High Chair's Adjustable Height locking mechanism on both front legs falls out of locking holes.  The chair itself either falls to the left, right, or both sides causing the seat of the chair to fall pass the height setting chosen. The INFANT OR SMALL CHILD is not not level in high chair when this occurs.  The Adjustable Height mechanism also falls pass locking dowels that attaches and locks the base of the front legs to the longer top portion of the front legs.  The plastic chair and movable parts are flimsy.  There is a pinching, bodily injury, and falling hazard to the INFANT OR SMALL CHILD in this chair.
justification: The high chair's locking mechanism failure poses a pinching, bodily injury, and falling hazard to infants or small children, indicating potential for injury.

incident_description: my son got a bad diaper rash from the pampers cruisers diapers... he screams everytime he pees and is very uncomfortable.
justification: The child is experiencing pain and discomfort from the diaper rash, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
danger product from BabiesRus 
http://www.toysrus.com/product/index.jsp?productId=3620292
Especially for Kids First Stages 3 in 1 Potty, make in USA.

It's a bit too easy to get the green seat off the base, and it is sharpe as a knife on the edge. It cut my 2 years old daughter small face in 2 area (about 2cm x 1 cm and 4 cm by 1.5cm) last Saturday.  I always watching them using this and within a few feet with kids, but when my daughter put it on the top of head and suddenly fall on the wall and floor, the green piece go down to her neck and cut her face. all this process finish within 5 seconds.  I am worry this hurt will keep track  on her face forever.  I don't want other kids has same accident, please take action to recall this unsafe product.

I have another similar product not purcahse from BabiesRus and all the edge is very smooth and did not causing problem.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries to a child due to sharp edges on the product, indicating a significant safety issue.

incident_description:
Tonight my 2 year old daughter pushed her feet against the dining room table and tipped her Stokke Tripp Trapp high chair with such force that she hit her head against the door and bent her neck forward, chin against chest as she banged to the ground. We were and are still terrified. The force and angle of incident, could have easily broken her neck. Luckily, she narrowly escaped with only a large bump on her head, bruised vertebrae, and bruises and scratches on her back. 

This of course is the first night that we've even thought it possible that she had the power to tip it over. Tonight I checked the Stokke site and we see that extended gliders are now available and that they warn against the possibility of tip over. These gliders should have come with our chair and should be STANDARD!  As ours was purchased for us as a gift in 2009, we did not even know that these existed. Given what we and our daughter experienced tonight, I truly believe that these should not be optional. 

My trust in Stokke has been shattered. I have written to Stokke to tell them what happened and have asked for a full refund. 

Sincerely, 
***
mother of ***, 2 years
justification: The child suffered a large bump, bruised vertebrae, and other injuries, indicating a severity level of 3. The incident was unexpected but possible given the circumstances.

incident_description: We were using a dropside crib for our child until I noticed the stationary side had worked loose. The screws on both sides (at the top) were loose and nearly falling out and the stationary side piece was coming apart from (head and foot) end pieces. If our child had put any pressure on that side of the crib it could have created the "V" effect described (which can cause strangulation). We are not using the crib at this time because even as we were able to tighten the screws down, we were not comfortable putting our child back in. We weren't sure how this even came loose as I periodically moved the crib to clean and change sheets and checked the hardware. Our daughter had been in the crib that day for a nap but no injury occured. We are currently using a playpen as our crib to avoid any possible injury.
justification: The crib's structural failure posed a potential strangulation hazard, but no injury occurred as the issue was detected and addressed in time.

incident_description: I bought the Carter's Sleep Haven Convertible Crib from Babies R Us for my 3 month old daughter. The third night sleeping in her bed she got both of her legs stuck in between the rails of the crib. I called babies r us to see if there was any kind of bumper that will help protect her and they were unable to find anything that would keep her from getting stuck again. The back of the crib is one solid piece so there are only rails on three sides of the bed, This bed is very dangerous for a baby of any age to be sleeping in, it can cause bodily harm to your baby.
justification: The baby got her legs stuck between the crib rails, indicating a potential for bodily harm, but no actual injury was reported.

incident_description: today i went in to my sons room after he was waking up from his nap screaming and found his leg caught in between the crib slats lodged in at the thigh. I had difficulties relasing and had to apply a&d ointment to slats and leg to release. his leg is brusied and red and sore from the accident. i feel this product is unsafe. i was about to cut the slats to relase my sons leg.it can cause problem and cut off circulation this was only a hr nap what if it was night time. please respond with actions to be taken. thanks so much ***
justification: The child's leg was bruised, red, and sore, indicating an injury, and the incident could have been more severe if not addressed promptly.

incident_description:
5 month old infant was using a Maclaren Techno Rocker (manufactured April 16 2010--purchased in November 2010 from Buy Buy Baby).  Infant was strapped in and kicked toy bar with legs.  Toy bar lifted from seat on her left side (only) and the end of the left toy bar landed in infant's mouth.  Baby was screaming and crying.  Inspected for injury, but appeared alright. 
Toy bar does not latch into seat.  My assumption is this is done to discourage parents/care givers from carrying the rocker; however, injury to child is likely if the child kicks the bar (e.g. mouth, eye, facial).
I have contacted the company today as well.
justification: The infant was not injured but experienced distress when the toy bar entered her mouth, indicating an incident without injury.

incident_description:
My 16 month old daughter was put into diapers she has never used before by her babysitter and she has broken out into about a 3 inch squareish type burn which is red, wet, hot, oozing a little bit of blood and pus on her inner upper right thigh that she did not have until after she started wearing the new brand of diapers.  

She has always worn Target brand Up and Up since she was born and this has been the only occasion that she has worn another brand and the only occasion she has experienced any kind of burn/rash like this.
justification: The child suffered a burn/rash with visible symptoms like redness, oozing blood and pus, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
i had this crib since my son was born. he is now 11 1/2 months old i am still using the crib because i dont have the money for a brand new one.
about a month ago in the middle of the night he started crying a looked in the crib he wasnt there and i turn the light on and he had fallen through and was underneath the crib!!! the crib even if you have it on its stilts so it doesnt rock the screws loosen and i have lost one on the bottom left side. i had tightened the screws a million times and they still come lose when he moves around in his sleep!
justification: The child fell through the crib but was not injured, indicating an incident without injury.

incident_description: A 5 month old african american infant was placed to sleep in a "Pack and Play" crib/basinette combo, face down. This sleeping position was normal for this infant. The infant was found unresponsive and pronounced dead the next morning. The infant had turned sideways in the bassinette and formed a bow in the bedding which prevented him from being able to turn over, this in turn caused him to suffocate in the mattress material. This infant weighed 18lbs and the unit was rated for a child that weighed no more thn 15lbs. However, this information is found no where on the unit itself. This information was found in the owners manual which was no longer in the household. ( Information was located on grayco website and was specific to this particular model )
justification: The infant died due to suffocation caused by improper sleeping conditions and exceeding the weight limit of the crib, which constitutes the highest severity level.

incident_description: The night light has potential to melt and cause fire.  The nightlight rear cover melted and was smelling when I very fortunately discovered and unplugged it. Base of night light where plugged into wall.  Made in China sticker on product as welll.
justification: The night light melted and emitted a smell, indicating a fire hazard, but no injury or death occurred.

incident_description:
Noticed a rash on the back of our 6 month old son.  it seemed to be irritating him, as he was constantly trying to scratch the area, and getting very fussy.  after a few days of this, we started thinking that it may be the diapers we were using (pampers dry max).  we switched diapers and the rash went away, and his scratches began to heal... 

a couple days later, we tried the pampers diapers again, and the rash immediately came back.  that's when we began to research the issue, and found numerous other similar cases...

worried for our son, and hope that he does not have any lasting damage from the experience.
justification: The rash caused irritation and required medical attention, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
I want to report an incident that happened with my son using the Jonti -Craft High Chairries product at a daycare that he attends. He was sitting in this product and the whole chair toppled over and he hit his head on a table and chipped off a piece of his front tooth. It appears that this product was too little for him to be in but when I called the manufacturer of the product at Jonti they informed me they don't issue weight limits on their products for legal reasons but do provide a guideline seating recommendation on their website at www.jonti-craft.com and click on seating it will pull up a chart guideline that they recommend. When I called this company and asked them where did they pull the recommended info from on the chart to compile this information to present to consumers all they could tell me was they got it from several sources and had to get back with me because they were not aware which sources it was. 
What regulations do children's furniture manufacturer's have to follow to make sure they fall within safety standards? 
My child had a horrible fall and chipped his tooth off because of this accident with this product but the accident could have been much worse depending on how he fell. As a consumer I would like to know if this particular company is falling within those guidelines as a manufacturer of children's furniture.
justification: The child suffered a chipped tooth from the chair toppling over, which constitutes an injury (severity 3). The likelihood is possible (3) as such incidents can occur with improper use or inadequate product guidelines.

incident_description: The slat on my daughter's crib was completely broken off and there is another slat that is loosening.  I called Jardine and all they want to do is replace the slat.  I'm very concerned for the safety of my child and I've decided to get rid of this horrible crib.
justification: A broken crib slat poses a potential hazard but no injury has occurred yet.

incident_description: My 7-month-old son was sitting in his bouncy chair, wiggling around making the seat bounce. There was a loud crack and the chair tilted all the way to the floor on one side. Now if I put him in it that side goes all the way to the floor. He banged his head a little bit, but thankfully it was minor. If he hadn't been strapped in, it could have been worse.
justification: The child suffered a minor head injury due to the chair malfunction, but no serious harm occurred.

incident_description: I bought this crib brand new and my sister bought one at the same time.Mine is a drop side crib and when my daughter went to get in her bed the bottomm fell and so did the stabilizer bar and she hit the floor.It seems like the stabilizer bar doesn't fit in the slots tight and they always fell loose.Then in the middle of the night while my daughter was kicking and turning in her sleep two of the poles poped right out and left a giant opening for her head.Then she leaned on the drop side rail and it slid down.This crib is made very poorly and falls apart easily my sisters is falling apart to.Now I have no toddler bed for her in fear this crib is not stable.
justification: The crib's structural failures led to the child falling but no injury was reported, indicating a severity level of 2. The repeated failures suggest a high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: I have a 5 month old baby and have been using Nuby pacifiers (0-6m).  I just recently bought 3 new packs of 2 pacifiers in each pack.  I have been using them for 1 week.  Last night, my son was sucking on the pacifier.  I pulled it out of his mouth and the ringed handle broke off.  I was left with two small, sharp pieces.  Had he have pulled it out himself, he would probably have placed one of the pieces in his mouth and choked.  After this happened, I inspected the other pacifiers I had bought.  Two of the other five were also weak in that area and broke easily.
justification: The pacifier broke into small, sharp pieces, posing a choking hazard, but no injury occurred.

incident_description:
We started using Pampers Cruisers Dry Max for my baby. We had been using Luvs with no problems (and previously used the old Papers Cruisers (not Dry Max) on my older daughter with no probelms). On two separate occasions while wearing a Pampers Cruisers Dry Max diaper, my daughter got horrible blisters (2 on one occasion- 1/26/11, 6 on the other- 3/12/11). She has no known allergies, never had any reaction to Luvs diapers, and the diapers were not that wet when we removed it and they were not left on her for an unusually long period. She did happen to be sick both times, once with a sinus infection and the other time with a virus, but I really don't know if that is related to the blisters. She never previously got blisters when wearing a Luvs diaper when ill. The blisters are extremely painful, are open and raw and take a long time to heal. 
For both incidents, she was using size 4 Pampers Cruises Dry Max. She did wear these diapers other times without a problem.
justification: The baby suffered painful blisters on two separate occasions, indicating an injury caused by the diapers.

incident_description: While feeding my daughter in the Evenflo highchair her foot has gotten stuck between the snack tray and the main tray on three occasions.  The most recent incident ocurred on 3/14.  Her foot was visibly red and she was crying.
justification: The child's foot was visibly red and she was crying, indicating injury, and the incident has occurred multiple times.

incident_description: I went to get my 18 month old from her nap in the Jardine crib (model # BC110-W; manf. date 02-2006) and saw a wooden slat from the drop down rail on the floor. She is 20# and was able to break the rail off, leaving a chunk of splintered wood attached to the rail that she could have cut herself on. It also left a large enough gap between the two slats where she could have been strangled or escaped from the crib and either been alone in her room or gotten out of her room and fallen down the stairs.
justification: The incident involved a broken crib rail with potential for injury or escape, but no actual harm occurred.

incident_description: My 6 month old son's leg was entrapped in the side rail of the crib.  It was wedged in there pretty good, and I was unable release it by simply pulling.  I had to remove his clothing and push up to squeeze his leg out.
justification: The child's leg was entrapped and required effort to free, indicating a potential for injury but none was reported.

incident_description:
My 3 year old toddler was playing with his silver teething rattle that he was given as an infant. It is circular in shape with a heart in the middle. He began coughing and choking when I realized that the heart from the middle had broken off and become stuck/lodged in his throat. I turned him upside down on my forearm and was able to easily thrust the "heart" from mouth. Fortunately there was no permanent injury, other than a scare as I was there to stop the choking from progressing into something more severe. I was upset that his teether/keepsake was broken, so I scoured the internet to see if I could replace it (not to let him play with since it was a choking hazard) but to keep for him later on in life. I came across a website saying that it had been recalled due to another incident! I unfortunately have no idea where it was purchased since this was a gift. Here is the website I came across:

http://www.cpsc.gov/cpscpub/prerel/prhtml08/08178.html

Again, it is the circular teether with the heart in the middle. I will contact the company first thing tomorrow (Monday) morning to alert them.
justification: The child choked on a broken teething rattle but was unharmed due to immediate intervention, indicating an incident with no injury.

incident_description: This is for the Evenflo triple jungle exersaucer.  My daughter encountered two seperate hazards.  Her arm became stuck between the band animals when she was 6 months old.  We removed that toy.  After converting it to an activity table, it constantly collapses under my 10 mo old where she has hurt herself without any evidence of injury. Very disappointed in this product
justification: The incident describes a child getting stuck and the product collapsing, causing harm but no evidence of injury, indicating a severity level of 2. The occurrence likelihood is high as it happened multiple times.

incident_description:
I purchased a box of 54 pampers easy ups in February 2011 for my 3 year old daughter who is totally potty trained. Upon opening the box, I immediately noticed a strong perfume fragrance on the product. Since this was my first time buying in about a year or two, I just figured they changed their scent.  I used the product for two (2) days on my potty trained daughter (product used just in case a potty accident occurs while commuting (1 1/2 hours each way) and overnight. After wearing the easy ups for approximately 3-4 hours in the day and overnight for two days, that evening she was in tears saying her bottom hurt, when I checked, her vaginal area had a horrible rash. I usually use Huggies pull ups for the exact time frame (1 1/2 hours in morning, 1 1/2 hours in the afternoon and overnight) without any problems or irritation.  I am so dissatisfied with this product, I tried with no success to contact Pampers to complain about the product but their customer service (by telephone) does not offer an opportunity to speak to a customer service representative.  I contacted Target to see if I can return the product, although I did use a few easy ups. 

Thank you
justification: The incident resulted in a severe rash, indicating an injury caused by the product.

incident_description:
After purchasing the jumperoo for almost $100, I quickly noticed that the poles that suspend the seat are very short which causes a jarring motion on the head and neck when the seat returns to the full upright position. 

He would jump for a moment and stop and grab his ear. As his weight neared 19 pounds his jumping became more vigorous and his head would whip from front to back. 
 I became concerned with the potential for serious head, neck and back injury and returned the toy to the store for a refund.

  *He was 7 months old when we purchased it, and we returned it (barely used) before he turned 9 months. At his 9 month check-up he weighed only 20 pounds, which is below the recommended limit.

As a side note: My son never enjoyed the toy and I think it was because of the immediate stop that occured as the seat came back up to a level position.
justification: The description indicates concern for potential injury but no actual injury occurred, and the product was returned before harm was done.

incident_description: I have a newborn suffering from a blistery, diaper rash that began when I started using Pampers Swaddlers with DryMax.  (Previously, I was using the Seventh Generation brand) I am changing her 15 times a day, using diaper cream, drying her bottom, all the things that are recommended...  The diapers are very fragrant and I thought that might be the problem.  I googled those specific diapers and diaper rash and was shocked to see all the complaints with these diapers.  We all have the same experience.  This many parents cannot be wrong!  It is sad that newborn babies have to suffer until parents figure out that a product designed for them is the problem.
justification: The newborn is suffering from a blistery diaper rash, indicating an injury, and multiple parents report similar issues with the product, suggesting it is likely to occur.

incident_description: On December 12th 1997, I found my son, [REDACTED], with his neck caught between the side rail and headboard of his ChildCraft drop side crib.  Sometime after his one am bottle, a single screw became loose creating a gap wide enough to entrap his neck. When this happened, the side of his crib became a spring-loaded vice, strangling him to death instantly.  [REDACTED] was ten months old. [REDACTED] crib was purchased new and used by his older sister for 18 months, then by [REDACTED]for ten months. The screw that loosened the night [REDACTED] died became loose twice before.  The screw was tightened with a screwdriver on both occasions. ChildCraft is no longer in business and sold its name to Foundations, Inc. The CPSC is aware of [REDACTED] death and has recently regulated crib standards in such a way that the drop side design will no longer meet CPSC regulations.  But I felt compelled to post on this database because ChildCraft drop side cribs are still in homes and daycares.  Cribs with drop-down sides are dangerous and the drop side feature is responsible for the death of my [REDACTED].
justification: The incident resulted in the death of a child due to a crib malfunction, which clearly meets the criteria for severity level 4. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 2 (unlikely) based on the rarity of such fatal incidents despite the known danger of drop-side cribs.

incident_description: My child was opening the safety gate (with supervision) when the plastic hinges broke and the whole gate fell down the stairs. The reason I purchased this particular gate was that it was could to be used on a staircase.
justification: The gate fell down the stairs but there was no mention of injury, only the incident itself.

incident_description: Since he was born two months ago, we have been using Pampers Sensitive diapers on our son with no problems (except they are a little pricier than other varieties). Now that he is a little older and up to a bigger size (size 1-2 or size 2), we started using Pampers Swaddlers with Dry Max last week (purchased 10 days ago). Just one week after the switch, he got a one inch welt on his bottom. This welt appeared within 45 minutes between normal diaper changes.  (Enfamil Gentlease formula diet, urine output, and bowel movements have not changed.) One diaper change he was perfectly fine with no diaper rash or redness; the next change had the huge welt. The welt was very red, but would turn white when he held his leg down, just like a burn. There was also redness all around the welt. He cried, screaming, for the next 20 minutes until he finally fell asleep. He woke up screaming crying as well and did not stop until I gave him Tylenol for the pain. I used petroleum jelly to block wetness from the burn, but the welt/redness/dry skin didn't go away until three days later and after a switch to a non-Dry Max variety of Pampers (Pampers Baby Dry).
justification: The incident describes a significant injury (a one-inch welt and severe pain) caused by the diaper, requiring pain medication and several days to heal.
